Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-A'raf

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

The discussion concerning the letters (huruf) at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, and its elaboration and the differences of people regarding it, has already preceded.

Ibn Jarir said: Sufyan ibn WakI' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad.﴾ "I am Allah, the One who distinguishes (afsil)." And Sa'id ibn Jubayr said likewise.

﴿A Book revealed to you﴾ means: this is a Book revealed to you, that is, from your Lord. ﴿So let there be no constriction in your breast concerning it﴾. Mujahid, Ata' and Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "It means doubt about it."

It was also said: "Do not be constrained by it in conveying it and warning with it, and be patient as the steadfast messengers (ulu al-azm) of the Messengers were patient." Therefore He said: ﴿That you may warn thereby﴾, that is, it was revealed to you so that you may warn the disbelievers thereby, ﴿and as a reminder for the believers﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, addressed all of mankind, saying: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, that is: follow the footsteps of the unlettered Prophet who has come to you with a Book revealed to you from the Lord and Sovereign of everything. ﴿And do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾, that is: do not turn away from what the Messenger has brought you to something else, lest you deviate from the judgment of Allah to the judgment of others.

﴿Little do you remember﴾, like His saying: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive eagerly, are not believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103], and His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [al-An'am: 116], and His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106].

He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed﴾, meaning: for opposing Our messengers and denying them. Their punishment was the disgrace of this world, linked with the humiliation of the Hereafter, as He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And messengers before you were mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock﴾ [al-An'am: 10]. And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So how many a town did We destroy while it was wrongdoing, so it lies in ruins upon its roofs, and [how many] a well abandoned and a lofty palace﴾ [al-Hajj: 45].[[In manuscript A: "wa-ka'ayyin" (وكأين).]]

And He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And how many a town We destroyed that exulted in its livelihood! Those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little. And We are the inheritors﴾ [al-Qasas: 58].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were taking their midday rest﴾, meaning: some of them were overtaken by the command of Allah, His might, and His vengeance. ﴿By night﴾ means at night. ﴿Or while they were taking their midday rest﴾ comes from al-qayluLah (الْقَيْلُولَة), which is resting in the middle of the day. Both times are times of heedlessness and amusement, as He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ [al-A'raf: 97-98]. And He says: ﴿Do those who devise evil schemes feel secure that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive? Or that He will seize them in their going back and forth, and they cannot escape? Or that He will seize them with gradual decline? Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 45-47].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So their claim was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers"﴾, meaning: their words when the punishment came were nothing but that they admitted their sins and that they deserved this. As He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And how many a town We shattered, which had been wrongdoing, and We produced after it another people. And when they perceived Our might, there they were fleeing from it. "Do not flee, but return to what you were made to live in luxury and your dwellings that you may be questioned." They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers." And that remained their claim until We made them as cut-down stubble, extinguished﴾ [al-Anbiya': 11-15].[[Ibn Kathir's text here cites the verses with the portion in brackets added from other manuscripts; in one manuscript the citation ends at "ila qawlihi" (إلى قوله), i.e., "up to His saying."]]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: In this verse there is clear evidence for the soundness of what has been reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "No people perish until they have been given an excuse from themselves." This was narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysara al-Zarrad, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people perish until they have been given an excuse from themselves." He said: I said to Abd al-Malik: How is that? He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿So their claim was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers"﴾.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/304).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent﴾, the verse [continues], like His saying: ﴿And on the day He calls them and says, "What did you answer the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65], and His saying: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. So the Lord, blessed and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection will question the nations about what they answered their messengers regarding what He sent them with, and He will also question the messengers about conveying His messages. For this reason Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, said regarding the tafsir of this verse: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent and We will surely question the messengers﴾: He said: Allah will question the people about what they answered the messengers, and He will question the messengers about what they conveyed.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us; Abu Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to us; al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The leader is questioned about the people [under him], the man is questioned about his family, the woman is questioned about her husband's house, and the servant is questioned about his master's property." Layth said: Ibn Tawus also narrated to me the same. Then he recited: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent and We will surely question the messengers﴾.[[Its chain contains Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi. Ibn Ma'in said: "He narrates the munkar reports from unknown narrators." However, it has been reported through another route, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, and in the two Sahihs.]]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs without this addition.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5188), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1829).]]

This was narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysara al-Zarrad, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people perish until they have been given an excuse from themselves." He said: I said to Abd al-Malik: How is that? He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿So their claim was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers"﴾.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/304).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent﴾, the verse [continues], like His saying: ﴿And on the day He calls them and says, "What did you answer the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65], and His saying: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. So the Lord, blessed and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection will question the nations about what they answered their messengers regarding what He sent them with, and He will also question the messengers about conveying His messages. For this reason Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, said regarding the tafsir of this verse: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent and We will surely question the messengers﴾: He said: Allah will question the people about what they answered the messengers, and He will question the messengers about what they conveyed.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us; Abu Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to us; al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The leader is questioned about the people [under him], the man is questioned about his family, the woman is questioned about her husband's house, and the servant is questioned about his master's property." Layth said: Ibn Tawus also narrated to me the same. Then he recited: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent and We will surely question the messengers﴾.[[Its chain contains Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi. Ibn Ma'in said: "He narrates the munkar reports from unknown narrators." However, it has been reported through another route, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, and in the two Sahihs.]]

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs without this addition.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5188), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1829).]]

Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿Then We will relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾: The Book will be placed on the Day of Resurrection, and it will speak of what they used to do. ﴿And We were not absent﴾ means: He, may He be exalted, informs His servants on the Day of Resurrection of what they said and what they did, whether small or great, minor or significant, because He, may He be exalted, is a witness over everything; nothing is hidden from Him, and He is not unaware of anything. Rather, He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal. ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry but it is in a clear Record﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: ﴿And the weighing﴾, i.e., of the deeds, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿is the truth﴾, i.e., Allah, exalted is He, does not wrong anyone at all, as He said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:40]. And He said: ﴿So as for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life. But as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss. And what can make you know what it is? [It is] a fire, intensely hot﴾ [al-Qari'ah 101:6-11]. And He said: ﴿And when the Horn is blown, there will be no relationships among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another. So he whose scales are heavy – it is those who will be successful. And he whose scales are light – those are the ones who have lost their souls, abiding eternally in Hell﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:101-103].

Section:

What is placed on the scale on the Day of Resurrection has been said to be the deeds themselves. Although deeds are accidents (a'rad), Allah, exalted is He, will transform them on the Day of Resurrection into bodies (ajsam).

Al-Baghawi said: This is related from Ibn 'Abbas, as in the Sahih regarding al-Baqarah and Ali 'Imran that they will come on the Day of Resurrection as if they were two clouds, or two shades, or two flocks of birds in ranks. Among this, in the Sahih, is the account of the Qur'an, that it will come to its companion in the form of a young man, pale of complexion, and he will say: "Who are you?" He will say: "I am the Qur'an, which kept you awake at night and made you thirsty during the day." [Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/348) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 3781, through Bashir ibn al-Muhajir, from 'Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him, as a marfu' report.] And in the hadith of al-Bara', in the account of the questioning in the grave: "The believer will be approached by a young man of good complexion and pleasant fragrance, who will say: 'Who are you?' He will say: 'I am your righteous deed.'" [Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/287).] And he mentioned the opposite concerning the disbeliever and the hypocrite.

It has also been said that the book of deeds is weighed, as in the hadith of the card (al-Bitaqah), concerning the man who will be brought forth, and for whom ninety-nine registers will be placed in one pan, each register as far as the eye can see. Then that card will be brought, in which is: "There is no god but Allah." He will say: "O Lord, what is this card with these registers?" Allah, exalted is He, will say: "Indeed, you will not be wronged." So that card will be placed in the pan of the scale. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The registers were made light, and the card was made heavy."

At-Tirmidhi related something similar to this, and authenticated it. [Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 2639; Ibn Majah related it in his Sunan, no. 4300, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/529) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound according to the conditions of both (Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it," and adh-Dhahabi agreed with him.]

It has also been said that the person who does the deed is weighed, as in the hadith: "On the Day of Resurrection a fat man will be brought, but he will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4729, in similar wording, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] Then he recited: ﴿So We will not assign them any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Kahf 18:105].

In the virtues of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud it is related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you wonder at the thinness of his calves? By the One in whose hand is my soul, they will weigh heavier in the scale than Uhud." [Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/420).]

It is possible to reconcile these reports by saying that all of them are sound: sometimes the deeds are weighed, sometimes their places (where they were done) are weighed, and sometimes their doer is weighed. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: ﴿And the weighing﴾, i.e., of the deeds, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿is the truth﴾, i.e., Allah, exalted is He, does not wrong anyone at all, as He said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:40]. And He said: ﴿So as for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life. But as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss. And what can make you know what it is? [It is] a fire, intensely hot﴾ [al-Qari'ah 101:6-11]. And He said: ﴿And when the Horn is blown, there will be no relationships among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another. So he whose scales are heavy – it is those who will be successful. And he whose scales are light – those are the ones who have lost their souls, abiding eternally in Hell﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:101-103].

Allah, exalted is He, says, bestowing favour upon His servants in what He has enabled for them: that He made the earth a resting-place (qarar), placed firm mountains (rawasi) and rivers in it, made for them dwellings and houses in it, permitted its benefits, subjected the clouds to them to bring forth their provision from it, and made for them in it ma'ayish (livelihoods), that is, means of gain and causes by which they trade and pursue all kinds of means. Yet most of them, despite this, are scarcely thankful for it, as He says: ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer, ungrateful.﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]

All the readers recited ﴿ma'ayish﴾ without a hamza, except ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz al-A'raj, who pronounced it with a hamza. The correct reading, which most scholars hold, is without a hamza, because ma'ayish is the plural of ma'ishah, derived from ʿaasha, ya'īshu, ʿayshan (to live). The root of ma'ishah was originally *ma'yisha*; the kasrah on the yā' was felt to be heavy, so it was moved to the ʿayn, becoming ma'ishah. When it was pluralised, the vowel returned to the yā' since the heaviness had disappeared, and it was said: ma'ayish. Its measure is mafa'il, because the yā' is radical (originally part of the root) in the word. This contrasts with madā'in, ṣaḥā'if and baṣā'ir, the plurals of madinah, ṣaḥīfah and baṣīrah, from madana, ṣaḥifa and abṣara, where the yā' is an added letter; for this reason they take the pattern fa'ā'il and are pronounced with a hamza. And Allah knows best.

Allah, exalted is He, here reminds the children of Adam of the honour of their father Adam, and makes clear to them the enmity of their enemy Iblis and the envy he harbours toward them and toward their father Adam, so that they may beware of him and not follow his ways. He says, exalted is He: ﴿And We did certainly create you and then give you form; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated﴾ [[Addition from K.]]. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create a human from clay, from black mud altered. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] spirit, then fall down to him in prostration." So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ [[Addition from M.]] [Al-Hijr: 28-30]. That is because, when Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, with His Hand from clay that sticks together, and fashioned him as a complete human being [[Addition from K, M, A.]] and breathed into him of His spirit, and commanded the angels to prostrate to him, glorifying the majesty of the Lord, exalted is He, they all heard and obeyed, except Iblis, who was not among those who prostrated. The discussion of Iblis has already been presented at the beginning of the tafsir of Surat al-Baqarah.

This which we have established is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir: that what is meant by all of this is Adam, peace be upon him.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And We did certainly create you and then give you form﴾: "They were created in the loins of men and fashioned in the wombs of women."

Al-Hakim narrated it and said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [Al-Mustadrak (2/319).]

Ibn Jarir also transmitted from some of the early generations (al-salaf) that what is meant by "We created you and then fashioned you" is the offspring.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said regarding this verse, ﴿And We did certainly create you and then give you form﴾: that means, "We created Adam, then We fashioned his descendants."

This view is open to question, because He said after it: ﴿Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾, which indicates that what is meant by that is Adam. The plural was used only because he is the father of mankind, just as Allah, exalted is He, says to the Children of Israel who lived at the time of the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And We shaded you with the clouds and sent down upon you manna and quail﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 57], while what is meant is their forefathers who lived at the time of Musa, peace be upon him [[Addition from A.]]. But since that was a favour upon the forefathers, who are the origin, it is as though it applied to the descendants. This is unlike His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging﴾ [[Addition from M, A; in H: "the verse".]] [Al-Mu'minun: 12-13], for what is meant there is Adam, created from the extract of clay, and his descendants are created from a sperm-drop. This is valid because what is meant by "We created man" is the species, not a specific individual. And Allah knows best.

Some grammarians, in explaining the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿What prevented you [from] [[addition from manuscript A.]] that you did not prostrate when I commanded you?﴾, said: the "lā" here is superfluous (zā'idah).

Others said: it was added to emphasize the negation, like the words of the poet:

"Mā in ra'aytu wa lā sami'tu bi-mithlihi"

So he placed "in" (which is for negation) upon the negating "mā," to emphasize the negation. They said: likewise here, ﴿What prevented you that you did not prostrate﴾, together with the preceding statement ﴿He was not among those who prostrated﴾.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related both opinions and rejected them. He chose that "manaʿaka" (prevented you) contains the meaning of another verb, its estimated sense being: "What made you need, obliged you, and compelled you that you did not prostrate when I commanded you," and similar. This opinion is strong and good, and Allah knows best.

As for the statement of Iblis, may Allah curse him: ﴿I am better than him﴾, it is from the excuse which is greater than the sin. It is as if he refused obedience because the superior is not commanded to prostrate to the inferior. That is, may Allah curse him: "And I am better than him, so how do You command me to prostrate to him?" Then he explained that he is better than him, because he was created from fire, and fire is nobler than what You created him from, which is clay. The accursed one looked at the origin of the element and did not look at the great honour, which is that Allah, the Exalted, created Adam with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and analogised a faulty analogy against the explicit text of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So fall down prostrate to him﴾ [Sad 72]. Thus he alone among the angels deviated by abandoning prostration; therefore he ﴿despaired of mercy﴾ [abalasa min al-rahmah], that is, he despaired of mercy. So he erred, may Allah disfigure him, in his analogy and in his claim that fire is also nobler than clay. For clay has the qualities of steadiness, forbearance, patience and deliberation, and clay is the place of plants, growth, increase and improvement. Fire, by its nature, is burning, recklessness and haste. Therefore the element of Iblis betrayed him, while the element of Adam benefited him in returning, turning back in repentance, humility, submission, yielding and surrender to the command of Allah, and acknowledgement and seeking of repentance and forgiveness.

In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The angels were created from light, the jinn (Iblis) was created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you." Thus Muslim narrated it.

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of 'Urwah, on the authority of 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah created the angels from the light of the Throne, and created the jinn from [a smokeless flame of] [[addition from manuscript A.]] fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you." I said to Nu'aym ibn Hammad: Where did you hear this from 'Abd al-Razzaq? He said: In Yemen. [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. 20904.] In some wordings of this hadith outside the Sahih: "And the wide-eyed houris were created from saffron." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/237) by way of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him. In its chain is 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr. Ibn Hibban said in al-Majruhin: "He narrates fabrications from reliable narrators, and when he narrates from 'Ali ibn Yazid he brings calamities, and when a report's chain contains 'Ubayd Allah, 'Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, that report is nothing but what their hands have fabricated."]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Mattar al-Warraq, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾, he said: Iblis analogised, and he was the first to analogise. Its chain is sound.

He also said: 'Amr ibn Malik narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi narrated to me, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: The first to analogise was Iblis, and the sun and moon were only worshipped through analogies. Its chain is also sound.

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing Iblis with a decree of destiny and creation: ﴿Then get down from it﴾, meaning: because of your disobedience to My command and your departure from My obedience, so it is not for you to act arrogantly therein.

Many of the commentators (mufassirun) said: the pronoun refers to Paradise. It is also possible that it refers to the station in which he was in the Highest Kingdom (al-malakut al-a'la).

﴿So go out, for you are among the debased﴾, that is, among the humiliated and despised. This is a treatment of him in the opposite of his intention, a recompense for his aim with its opposite. Thereupon the accursed one recovered himself and asked for respite until the Day of Resurrection. He said: ﴿Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, you are among those reprieved.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, granted him what he asked, because of the wisdom, will, and purpose He has in that, which cannot be opposed or prevented, and there is no one who can repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing Iblis with a decree of destiny and creation: ﴿Then get down from it﴾, meaning: because of your disobedience to My command and your departure from My obedience, so it is not for you to act arrogantly therein.

He said: ﴿Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, you are among those reprieved.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, granted him what he asked, because of the wisdom, will, and purpose He has in that, which cannot be opposed or prevented, and there is no one who can repel His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.

Ibn Kathir said, "Allah the Exalted informs that when Iblis was granted respite (ﷺ) until the day they are raised [in the manuscript: "al-din", which is an error], and Iblis was assured of this, he persisted in opposition and rebellion, and said: ﴿Because You have sent me astray, I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾, meaning: as You have led me astray."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "as You have misguided me." Others said: "as You have destroyed me. I will surely sit in ambush for Your servants — those whom You will create from the offspring of this one whom You have banished me because of — ﴿on Your straight path﴾, that is, the path of truth and the way of salvation. And I will certainly lead them astray from it, so that they will not worship You or affirm Your oneness, because of Your leading me astray."

Some grammarians said: the letter bāʾ (ba, "by") here is an oath particle, as if he were saying: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path."

Mujahid said: ﴿Your straight path﴾ means: the truth.

Muhammad ibn Suqah reported from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah: it means the road to Makkah.

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view is that al-sirat al-mustaqim is more general than all of that."

I say: This is because Imam Ahmad narrated:

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil — meaning al-Thaqafi, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil — narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us, Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd informed me, from Sabrah ibn Abi Fakih, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Shaytan sat in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat in wait for him on the path of Islam, and said: "Will you embrace Islam and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers?" He disobeyed him and embraced Islam. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of migration (hijrah), and said: "Will you migrate and leave your land and your sky? The likeness of the emigrant is like a horse on a tether?" He disobeyed him and migrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of jihad, which is the jihad of the self and wealth, and said: "Will you fight and be killed, so that your wife is married and your wealth is divided?" He disobeyed him and strove." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever of them does that and dies, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise; or if he is killed, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to admit him into Paradise; and if he drowns, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise; or if an animal throws him, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾ — I will cast doubt upon them about their Hereafter; ﴿and from behind them﴾ — I will make them desire their worldly life; ﴿and from their right﴾ — I will confuse for them the matter of their religion; ﴿and from their left﴾ — I will make sins appealing to them.

Also Ibn Talhah, in one narration, and al-'Awfi, both from Ibn 'Abbas: As for ﴿from before them﴾, it is from the direction of their worldly life; as for ﴿from behind them﴾, it is the matter of their Hereafter; as for ﴿from their right﴾, it is from the direction of their good deeds; and as for ﴿from their left﴾, it is from the direction of their evil deeds.

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah: He comes to them ﴿from before them﴾, informing them that there is no resurrection, no Paradise and no Fire; ﴿and from behind them﴾, concerning worldly matters, adorning them for them and calling them to it; ﴿and from their right﴾, from the direction of their good deeds, holding them back from them; ﴿and from their left﴾, adorning evil deeds and sins for them, calling them to them and commanding them with them. "He comes to you, O son of Adam, from every direction, except that he does not come to you from above; he cannot come between you and the mercy of Allah."

Similar has been related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj, except that they said: ﴿from before them﴾ is the world, and ﴿from behind them﴾ is the Hereafter.

Mujahid said: "from before them and from their right": where they can see; "and from behind them and from their left": where they cannot see.

Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant is all the paths of good and evil: good turns them away from it, and evil makes it appealing to them.

al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left﴾, and He did not say "from above them", because mercy descends from above them.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ — he said: "monotheists."

This saying of Iblis is only an assumption and a delusion on his part, and it coincided with reality in this, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of the believers. And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from one who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾ [Saba': 20–21].

For this reason, it has come in the hadith to seek refuge from Satan's domination over the human being from all his directions. As the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad:

Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Mujammi' narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, from Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im — meaning Nafi' ibn Jubayr — from Ibn 'Abbas. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab — meaning al-Sijistani — narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Yunus ibn Khabbab, from Ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion and my worldly life, and my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and calm my fears, and guard me from before me and behind me, and on my right and on my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge in You, O Allah, from being seized from beneath me." Al-Bazzar alone narrated it, and he graded it hasan.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, 'Ubadah ibn Muslim al-Fazari narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Abi Sulayman ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im narrated to me, I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not omit these supplications in the morning and in the evening: "O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from before me and behind me, and on my right and on my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being seized from beneath me." Waki' said: "That means being swallowed up by the earth."

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim also narrated it from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn Muslim, with it. Al-Hakim said: its isnad is sahih.

Ibn Kathir said, "Allah the Exalted informs that when Iblis was granted respite (ﷺ) until the day they are raised [in the manuscript: "al-din", which is an error], and Iblis was assured of this, he persisted in opposition and rebellion, and said: ﴿Because You have sent me astray, I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾, meaning: as You have led me astray."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "as You have misguided me." Others said: "as You have destroyed me. I will surely sit in ambush for Your servants — those whom You will create from the offspring of this one whom You have banished me because of — ﴿on Your straight path﴾, that is, the path of truth and the way of salvation. And I will certainly lead them astray from it, so that they will not worship You or affirm Your oneness, because of Your leading me astray."

Some grammarians said: the letter bāʾ (ba, "by") here is an oath particle, as if he were saying: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path."

Mujahid said: ﴿Your straight path﴾ means: the truth.

Muhammad ibn Suqah reported from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah: it means the road to Makkah.

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view is that al-sirat al-mustaqim is more general than all of that."

I say: This is because Imam Ahmad narrated:

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil — meaning al-Thaqafi, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Aqil — narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Musayyab narrated to us, Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd informed me, from Sabrah ibn Abi Fakih, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Shaytan sat in wait for the son of Adam on his paths. He sat in wait for him on the path of Islam, and said: "Will you embrace Islam and abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers?" He disobeyed him and embraced Islam. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of migration (hijrah), and said: "Will you migrate and leave your land and your sky? The likeness of the emigrant is like a horse on a tether?" He disobeyed him and migrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the path of jihad, which is the jihad of the self and wealth, and said: "Will you fight and be killed, so that your wife is married and your wealth is divided?" He disobeyed him and strove." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever of them does that and dies, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise; or if he is killed, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to admit him into Paradise; and if he drowns, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise; or if an animal throws him, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾ — I will cast doubt upon them about their Hereafter; ﴿and from behind them﴾ — I will make them desire their worldly life; ﴿and from their right﴾ — I will confuse for them the matter of their religion; ﴿and from their left﴾ — I will make sins appealing to them.

Allah, exalted is He, emphasized upon him the curse, the expulsion, the removal, and the banishment from the place of the Exalted Assembly by His saying: ﴿Get out of it, disgraced and expelled.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: As for "al-madhu'um" (مَذْءُومًا), it means the blamed, censured one. "Al-dhaam" (الذَّأْم), without shaddah, means blame. It is said: "dha'amahu yadh'amuhu dha'man, fahuwa madhu'um" (ذَأَمَهُ يَذْأَمُهُ ذَأْمًا فَهُوَ مَذْءُومٌ). Some drop the hamzah and say: "dhamtahu adhimuhu dhaymān wa dhaaman" (ذمْته أَذِيمُهُ ذَيْمًا وذَاما), and "al-dhaamm" and "al-dhaym" are more emphatic in blame than "al-dhamm" (الذَّمّ).

He said: "Al-madhhur" (الْمَدْحُورُ) means the one driven away, the one who is distanced and expelled.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: We do not know "al-madhu'um" (الْمَذْءُومَ) and "al-madhmum" (الْمَذْمُومَ) to mean anything other than one thing.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿Get out of it, disgraced and expelled﴾ that he said: "Maqitan" (hated, detested).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "Saghiran maqitan" (diminished and detested). Al-Suddi said: "Maqitan madhrudan" (detested and driven away). Qatadah said: "La'inan maqitan" (cursed and detested). Mujahid said: "Manfiyyan madhrudan" (exiled and driven away). Al-Rabi ibn Anas said: "Madhu'uman": exiled; and "al-madhhur": the diminished one (al-musaghghar).

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever among them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with you all﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense. And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and launch against them your horses and your foot soldiers, and share with them in wealth and children, and promise them." And Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, and sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-Isra: 63-65].

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 7, verses 19–21:

He, may He be exalted, mentions that He permitted Adam, peace be upon him, and his wife [Hawwa' (Eve)] [[addition from A.]] to eat from all the fruits of the Garden except one tree. The discussion of this has already preceded in "Surat al-Baqarah." Thereupon, Satan envied them both, and strove through deception, trickery and whispering, that they might be stripped of the blessing and the fine clothing they were in. He said, falsely and fabricating: "Your Lord has only forbidden you from eating of this tree lest you become angels [[malakayn]], or become immortal here." That is, lest you become angels, and had you eaten from it you would have obtained that (the same), like His saying: ﴿"O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 120], meaning: lest you become angels. Like His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [an-Nisa: 176], meaning: lest you go astray; and ﴿He cast firm mountains upon the earth lest it shake with you﴾ [an-Nahl: 15], meaning: lest it shake with you.

Ibn 'Abbas and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir used to read: ﴿illa an takunaa malakayn﴾ with a kasrah on the lam (malikayn). The majority read it with a fathah (malakayn).

﴿And he swore to them both﴾, meaning he swore to them by Allah: ﴿"Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisors"﴾, for I am from before you here and know this place better. This is of the form of mufa'alah, though only one side is meant, as Khalid ibn Zuhayr, the cousin of Abu Dhu'ayb, said:

*And he swore to her by Allah with full effort that you are / sweeter than the salwa when its shoots are cut* [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (12/350), and the editor attributed it to Ash'ar al-Hudhaliyyin (1/158).]]

That is: he swore to them by Allah [on that] [[addition from D, K, M, A.]] until he deceived them. Indeed, a believer in Allah may be deceived. He said: "I was created before you both, and I know more than you both, so follow me and I will guide you." Some of the scholars used to say: "Whoever deceives us by Allah, we are deceived by him."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 22–23:

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah said, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Adam was a tall man, as if he were a towering palm tree, with abundant hair on his head. When he committed the sin that he committed, his private parts became visible to him at that moment, though he had not seen them before. He fled running through the Garden, and a tree from the trees of the Garden caught his head. He said to it, 'Let me go.' It said, 'I will not let you go.' Then his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said, 'My Lord, I was ashamed before You.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/354).]]

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through several chains (turuq), from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ). However, the mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not traced to the Prophet) is sounder in its isnad. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/352). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/345) through Yazid ibn al-Had, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with similar wording, and said: "This does not weaken the hadith of Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, for he knows al-Hasan's hadith better than the people of Madinah and Egypt, and Allah knows best." Al-Hakim meant by this what he narrated in al-Mustadrak (1/344) through Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from 'Utayy, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with similar wording. He gave a reason for the defect at its end: that al-Hasan had narrated it from Ubayy without mentioning 'Utayy. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf (3/400), from Ibn Jurayj: "I was told from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," and he mentioned it with similar wording.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Imarah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The tree that Allah forbade to Adam and his wife was the ear of wheat (al-sunbulah). When they both ate from it, their private parts became visible to them. What covered their private parts was their nails. They began to stick together leaves of the Garden, the leaves of the fig tree, over themselves. Adam, peace be upon him, then ran away, turning back in the Garden, and a tree from the Garden caught his head. It called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, but I am ashamed before You, O Lord.' He said: 'Did you not have in what I granted you of the Garden and permitted you from it a wide choice, apart from what I forbade you?' He said: 'Yes, my Lord, but by Your might, I did not think that anyone would swear by You falsely.' He said: That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And he swore to them both, 'Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers.'﴾ He said: 'By My might, I will surely bring you down to the earth, and you will not obtain a living except with hardship.' He said: So he was brought down from the Garden. They had been eating from it in abundance (raghadan), and now he was brought down to a place without abundance of food or drink. He was taught the craft of iron, and was commanded to till the land. He tilled, sowed, and irrigated, and when it reached harvest he reaped it, then threshed it, then winnowed it, then ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate it. He did not reach that point until he reached what Allah willed him to reach."

[[This was narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (12/352) through the chain of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]]

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿and they began to stick together over themselves leaves of the Garden﴾: "It was the leaves of the fig tree." Sahih, traced to him (sahih ilayhi).

Mujahid said: "They began to stick over themselves leaves of the Garden in the manner of a garment."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said, concerning His saying ﴿stripping them of their clothing﴾: "The clothing of Adam and Eve was light upon their private parts, so that this one did not see the private parts of that one, nor that one the private parts of this one. When they both ate from the tree, their private parts became visible to them." Ibn Jarir narrated it with a sahih isnad to him.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Adam said: "My Lord, what do You think if I repent and seek forgiveness?" He said: "Then I will admit you into the Garden." As for Iblis, he did not ask for repentance; he asked for respite (al-nazrah), and so each of them was given what he asked for.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it was said to him: 'Why did you eat from the tree that I forbade you?' He said: 'Hawwa'. She commanded me.' He said: 'Then I have decreed for her that she will bear only with hardship, and give birth only with hardship.' Then Hawwa' cried out, and it was said to her: 'The crying out is upon you and upon your offspring.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/356).]]

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, concerning His saying ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾: "These are the words that Adam received from his Lord, [Mighty and Majestic]." [[An addition from manuscript A.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 22–23:

Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah said, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Adam was a tall man, as if he were a towering palm tree, with abundant hair on his head. When he committed the sin that he committed, his private parts became visible to him at that moment, though he had not seen them before. He fled running through the Garden, and a tree from the trees of the Garden caught his head. He said to it, 'Let me go.' It said, 'I will not let you go.' Then his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said, 'My Lord, I was ashamed before You.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/354).]]

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through several chains (turuq), from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ). However, the mawquf (a report ending with a Companion, not traced to the Prophet) is sounder in its isnad. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/352). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/345) through Yazid ibn al-Had, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with similar wording, and said: "This does not weaken the hadith of Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, for he knows al-Hasan's hadith better than the people of Madinah and Egypt, and Allah knows best." Al-Hakim meant by this what he narrated in al-Mustadrak (1/344) through Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from 'Utayy, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with similar wording. He gave a reason for the defect at its end: that al-Hasan had narrated it from Ubayy without mentioning 'Utayy. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf (3/400), from Ibn Jurayj: "I was told from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," and he mentioned it with similar wording.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan ibn 'Imarah, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The tree that Allah forbade to Adam and his wife was the ear of wheat (al-sunbulah). When they both ate from it, their private parts became visible to them. What covered their private parts was their nails. They began to stick together leaves of the Garden, the leaves of the fig tree, over themselves. Adam, peace be upon him, then ran away, turning back in the Garden, and a tree from the Garden caught his head. It called out to him: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, but I am ashamed before You, O Lord.' He said: 'Did you not have in what I granted you of the Garden and permitted you from it a wide choice, apart from what I forbade you?' He said: 'Yes, my Lord, but by Your might, I did not think that anyone would swear by You falsely.' He said: That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And he swore to them both, 'Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers.'﴾ He said: 'By My might, I will surely bring you down to the earth, and you will not obtain a living except with hardship.' He said: So he was brought down from the Garden. They had been eating from it in abundance (raghadan), and now he was brought down to a place without abundance of food or drink. He was taught the craft of iron, and was commanded to till the land. He tilled, sowed, and irrigated, and when it reached harvest he reaped it, then threshed it, then winnowed it, then ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate it. He did not reach that point until he reached what Allah willed him to reach."

[[This was narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (12/352) through the chain of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]]

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿and they began to stick together over themselves leaves of the Garden﴾: "It was the leaves of the fig tree." Sahih, traced to him (sahih ilayhi).

Mujahid said: "They began to stick over themselves leaves of the Garden in the manner of a garment."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said, concerning His saying ﴿stripping them of their clothing﴾: "The clothing of Adam and Eve was light upon their private parts, so that this one did not see the private parts of that one, nor that one the private parts of this one. When they both ate from the tree, their private parts became visible to them." Ibn Jarir narrated it with a sahih isnad to him.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Adam said: "My Lord, what do You think if I repent and seek forgiveness?" He said: "Then I will admit you into the Garden." As for Iblis, he did not ask for repentance; he asked for respite (al-nazrah), and so each of them was given what he asked for.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When Adam ate from the tree, it was said to him: 'Why did you eat from the tree that I forbade you?' He said: 'Hawwa'. She commanded me.' He said: 'Then I have decreed for her that she will bear only with hardship, and give birth only with hardship.' Then Hawwa' cried out, and it was said to her: 'The crying out is upon you and upon your offspring.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/356).]]

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, concerning His saying ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾: "These are the words that Adam received from his Lord, [Mighty and Majestic]." [[An addition from manuscript A.]]

It was said: the address in "Descend" (ihbitu) is to Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent. Some of them did not mention the serpent, and Allah knows best.

The principal enmity is between Adam and Iblis; for this reason the Exalted said in Surah Ta-Ha: "He said: Descend, both of you, from it all together" [the verse, 123]. Eve follows Adam, and the serpent, if its mention is authentic, follows Iblis.

The commentators have mentioned the places where each of them descended, and the sum of those reports returns to the Isra'iliyyat (narrations from the Children of Israel), and Allah knows best their authenticity. Had there been any benefit in specifying those places that returns to the accountable in matters of their religion or their worldly affairs, Allah the Exalted would have mentioned it in His Book or His Messenger (ﷺ) would have.

* *

His saying: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time" [7:24] means: a residence and lifespans set to determined terms, for which the Pen has run, which the Decree has counted, and which were inscribed in the First Book. Ibn 'Abbas said: "dwelling place" means the graves. And from him: the surface of the earth and what is beneath it. Ibn Abi Hatim related both.

* *

His saying: "He said: In it you will live, and in it you will die, and from it you will be brought forth" [7:25] is like His saying: "From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth a second time" [Ta-Ha: 55]. The Exalted informs that He makes the earth a home for the children of Adam for the duration of the worldly life: in it is their living, in it is their dying and their graves, and from it is their resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, the Return, on which Allah gathers the first and the last and recompenses each for his deeds.
