His saying: ﴿Then a caller will call out among them﴾ means: an announcer will announce and a caller will call: ﴿That the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: lasting upon them.

Then He described them with His saying: ﴿who avert [people] from the way of God and seek to make it crooked﴾, meaning: they prevent people from following the way of God, His law, and what the prophets brought, and they desire that the way be crooked and not straight, so that no one will follow it. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾, meaning: they deny the meeting with God in the Hereafter, that is, they reject and deny it, not affirming it or believing in it. For this reason they do not care what evil they commit in word and deed, because they do not fear reckoning for it or punishment. So they are the worst of people in deeds and words.

Ibn Kathir said: God informs us of what the people of Paradise say to the people of the Fire when they have settled in their abodes, in the manner of rebuke and reproach: ﴿That we have found what our Lord promised us to be true [so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?]﴾ [the bracketed addition is from manuscripts K and M]. The "an" (that) here is explanatory (mufassira) of an omitted saying, and "qad" is for emphasis. That is, they say to them: ﴿We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true; so have you found what your Lord promised to be true?" They say, "Yes."﴾ As God mentioned in Surat al-Saffat about the one who had a companion among the disbelievers: ﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire. He said, "By God, you were nearly to destroy me! Had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth [to punishment]. Is it that we will not die, except our first death, and we will not be punished?"﴾ [37:55–59]. That is, he denies to his companion the statement he used to make in the world, and rebukes him with what he has come to of punishment and torment. Likewise, the angels rebuke them, saying to them: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or is it that you do not see? Burn therein; so be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ [52:14–16]

And likewise the Messenger of God (ﷺ) rebuked the slain of the well (al-qalib) on the day of Badr. He called out: "O Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, O Utba ibn Rabi'a, O Shayba ibn Rabi'a," and he named their leaders: "Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." 'Umar said: "O Messenger of God, do you address people who have decomposed?" He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you are not more able to hear what I say than they are, but they cannot answer."

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (3980), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (932), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both.]

* *

His saying: ﴿Then a caller will call out among them﴾ means: an announcer will announce and a caller will call: ﴿That the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: lasting upon them.

Then He described them with His saying: ﴿who avert [people] from the way of God and seek to make it crooked﴾, meaning: they prevent people from following the way of God, His law, and what the prophets brought, and they desire that the way be crooked and not straight, so that no one will follow it. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾, meaning: they deny the meeting with God in the Hereafter, that is, they reject and deny it, not affirming it or believing in it. For this reason they do not care what evil they commit in word and deed, because they do not fear reckoning for it or punishment. So they are the worst of people in deeds and words.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 46–47 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the conversation between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, He pointed out that between Paradise and the Fire there is a *hijab* (barrier), which is the partition that prevents the people of the Fire from reaching Paradise.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: It is the wall about which Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them, with a gate. Within it is mercy, and facing it from without is punishment﴾ [al-Hadid 57:13]. It is the *al-A'raf* (the Heights) about which Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And upon the A'raf will be men﴾.

Then he related with his chain of narration from al-Suddi that he said concerning His words, [the Exalted] [[Addition from K.]] ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾: it is "the wall", and it is "al-A'raf".

Mujahid said: Al-A'raf is a barrier between Paradise and the Fire, a wall with a gate. Ibn Jarir said: Al-A'raf is the plural of *'urf*, and among the Arabs every elevated part of the ground is called *'urf*. The crest of a rooster is called *'urf* only because of its height.

Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us: Ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Al-A'raf is the elevated thing.

Al-Thawri said, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Al-A'raf is a wall like the crest of a rooster.

In another narration from Ibn 'Abbas: Al-A'raf is a hill between Paradise and the Fire, on which some people of the sins are detained between Paradise and the Fire. In another narration from him: It is a wall between Paradise and the Fire. Likewise al-Dahhak and more than one of the scholars of tafsir said.

Al-Suddi said: Al-A'raf was only so named because its companions "recognise" (ya'rifun) people.

The expressions of the mufassirun differ concerning who the people of al-A'raf are, but all of them are close and return to one meaning: they are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. This was stated explicitly by Hudhayfah, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, and more than one of the early and later generations, may Allah have mercy on them.

A marfu' (attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ)) hadith has also come, which al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related:

Abd Allah ibn Isma'il related to us, 'Ubayd ibn al-Husayn related to us, Sulayman ibn Dawud related to us, al-Nu'man ibn Abd al-Salam related to us, a shaykh of ours called Abu 'Abbad related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the one whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, and he said: "Those are the companions of al-A'raf. They did not enter it, while they aspire (to enter)."

This is a gharib (single-channel) hadith from this route. [[Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn 'Asakir in his History, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/463).]] It was also related by another route, from Sa'id ibn Salamah, from Abu al-Husam, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from a man of Muzaynah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf, and he said: "They are a people who went out disobedient, without the permission of their fathers, and were killed in the way of Allah." [[Abu al-Shaykh, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/465). Sa'id ibn Salamah was declared weak by al-Nasa'i, but Muslim included narrations from him in his Sahih.]]

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Abu Ma'shar related to us, Yahya ibn Shibl related to us, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani [[In the manuscripts it reads "Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani", and in the tafsir of al-Tabari "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani", and in Musnad al-Harith and Masawi' al-Akhlaq "Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani". I did not find anyone who gives his biography, except that Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil in the biography of Yahya ibn Shibl that he narrated from "Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani".]] from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about "the companions of al-A'raf", and he said: "They are men [[In A: "qawm" (a people).]] who were killed in the way of Allah on account of the disobedience of their fathers. The disobedience of their fathers prevented them from entering Paradise, and their being killed in the way of Allah prevented them from entering the Fire."

Thus it was related by Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim, through various routes, from Abu Ma'shar with it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/458). Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah related it in his Musnad, no. 711 (Bughyat al-Basith), and al-Khara'iti in Masawi' al-Akhlaq, no. 252, both through Abu Ma'shar. Abu Ma'shar is Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman, and al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected).]] Likewise Ibn Majah related it as marfu', from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [[I did not find them in the Sunan of Ibn Majah. Rather, Ibn Mardawayh related them in his tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/465). The hadith of Abu Sa'id was also related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 3322 (Majma' al-Bahrayn), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Ata', from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/23): "In it is Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-Ru'ayni, who is weak." I say: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is also weak.]] [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]] . And Allah knows best the soundness of these marfu' reports. At best they are mawquf (ending with a Companion), and in that is an indication of what has been mentioned.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Hushaym related to us, Husayn informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Hudhayfah, that he was asked about the companions of al-A'raf, and he said: "They are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal. Their bad deeds held them back from Paradise, and their good deeds kept them away from the Fire." He said: "So they stood there on the walls until Allah judges concerning them." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/453).]]

He also related it by another route, more detailed than this, saying:

Ibn Humayd related to us, Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, who said: Al-Sha'bi said: Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman sent for me, and with him was Abu al-Zinad Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan, mawla of Quraysh, and they had mentioned something about the companions of al-A'raf that was not as they had said. So I said to them: "If you wish, I will inform you of what Hudhayfah mentioned." They said: "Go on." I said: "Hudhayfah mentioned the companions of al-A'raf and said: They are a people whose good deeds carried them beyond the Fire, and whose bad deeds held them back from Paradise. When their gaze is turned towards the companions of the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾. While they are like that, your Lord looks down upon them and says to them: 'Go, enter Paradise, for I have forgiven you.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/452).]]

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, while narrating this from Ibn Mas'ud: "People will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one, enters Paradise, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one, enters the Fire." Then he recited Allah's words: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful. And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, abiding forever in Hell﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:102–103] [[Addition from K, M, A. In H: "the two verses."]]. Then he said: "The scale is tipped by the weight of a mustard seed, and it inclines." He said: "And whoever's good deeds and bad deeds are equal is among the companions of al-A'raf. They stop on the Sirat, then they recognise the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. When they look at the people of Paradise, they call out: 'Peace be upon you.' And when they turn their gaze to their left and look at the companions of the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾, and they seek refuge in Allah from their dwelling-place." He said: "As for the people of good deeds, they are given light, and they walk by it before them and to their right. Every servant on that day is given light, and every community is given light. When they reach the Sirat, Allah strips the light of every male hypocrite and female hypocrite. When the people of Paradise see what the hypocrites have suffered, they say: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:8]. As for the companions of al-A'raf, the light was in their hands and was not taken away. At that point Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They have not entered it, while they aspire to﴾, so their aspiring was (considered as) entering." He said: "And Ibn Mas'ud said: Indeed, when the servant does a good deed, ten (rewards) are recorded for him for it, and when he does a bad deed, only one is recorded. Then he says: 'Destroyed is the one whose single (bad deed) outweighs his tenths.'" [[Ibn Jarir related it (12/454).]]

Ibn Jarir also said:

Ibn Waki' and Ibn Humayd related to me, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is the wall between Paradise and the Fire, and the companions of al-A'raf are in that place, until when Allah decides to grant them well-being, they are taken to a river called "al-Hayah" (Life), its banks are reeds of gold, adorned with pearls, its soil is musk. They are cast into it until their complexions become good, and white marks appear on their necks by which they are recognised. When their complexions are good, the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted, brings them and says: "Wish for whatever you want," and they wish, until their wishes run out. Then He says to them: "For you is what you have wished, and its like seventy times over." So they enter Paradise, with a white mark on their necks by which they are recognised; they are called "the poor of the people of Paradise" (masakin ahl al-Jannah).

Ibn Abi Hatim related it likewise, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mughirah, from Jarir, with it. Sufyan al-Thawri related it from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, as his own saying (mawquf), and this is more sound, and Allah knows best. It has been related in this way from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and more than one other. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/455).]]

Sunayd ibn Dawud said: Jarir related to me, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Amr ibn Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf, and he said: "They are the last of the servants to be judged between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished judging between the servants, He says: 'You are a people whose good deeds brought you out of the Fire, and you did not enter Paradise. So you are My freed ones, graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'" This is a mursal hasan (a report omitting a Companion in its chain, yet sound). [[Al-Tabari related it (12/461) from al-Qasim, from Sunayd, with its chain.]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related, in the biography of al-Walid ibn Musa, from Munabbih ibn 'Uthman [[In the manuscripts it reads "Shaybah ibn 'Uthman", and the correction is from Tarikh Dimashq and al-Ba'th of al-Bayhaqi.]], from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that the believers among the jinn have reward and they have punishment. We asked him about their reward, and he said: "On the A'raf, and they are not in Paradise with the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)." We asked him: "And what is al-A'raf?" He said: "The wall of Paradise, through which rivers flow, and in which trees and fruits grow." [[In the manuscripts: "concerning their reward and their believers." The text here is from al-Durr al-Manthur (3/88), as noted in the margin of the Shu'ayb edition.]]

Al-Bayhaqi related it from Ibn Bishran, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri, from Yusuf ibn Yazid, from al-Walid ibn Musa, with it. [[Tarikh Dimashq (17/910), the manuscript section, and al-Ba'th of al-Bayhaqi, no. 117, and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat).]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: "The companions of al-A'raf are a righteous people, jurists and scholars."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And between them is a barrier, and upon the heights (al-A'raf) are men who recognize each by his mark﴾. He said: They are men from among the angels, who recognize the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. He said: ﴿And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, but they are hoping [to]. And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people." And the companions of the heights call out to men [in the Fire] whom they recognize by their marks, saying, "Your gathering did not avail you, nor did what you were arrogant about. Are these the ones you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?"﴾ He said: This is when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, [and it is said to them]: ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve.﴾

This chain is sound up to Abu Mijlaz Lahiq ibn Humayd, one of the Successors (tabi'un), but it is a strange statement from him and contrary to the apparent context. The view of the majority takes precedence over his, by the indication of the verse toward what they held. Likewise the saying of Mujahid: that they are a righteous people, scholars and jurists [in the manuscripts K, M, A: "fuqaha' 'ulama'"], is also strange. And Allah knows best.

Al-Qurtubi and others have related twelve opinions concerning them, among which: that they are people of righteousness who testified that they were righteous, who branched off from the branch of the Hereafter, [and in M: "and they were made"; in A: "and they were created"] to observe the news of the people. It was also said: they are prophets. And it was said: they are angels.

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿who recognize each by his mark﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They recognize the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces, and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces. Al-Dahhak also related it from him in the same way.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah placed them in that station so that they might recognize those in Paradise and in the Fire, and so that they might recognize the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and seek refuge in Allah that He not place them with the wrongdoing people. In that state they greet the people of Paradise with peace; they have not entered it, but they hope to enter it, and they will enter it, if Allah wills.

Likewise said Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Ma'mar related from al-Hasan that he recited this verse: ﴿They have not entered it, but they are hoping﴾ and said: By Allah, He did not put that hope in their hearts except as an honor He intends for them.

Qatadah said: Allah informed you of their place in hope.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: When the companions of the heights look at the people of the Fire and recognize them, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Suddi said: "And when they pass by them" — meaning the companions of the heights — "a group being led away to the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾"

'Ikrimah said: Their faces will be darkened in the Fire, and when they see the companions of Paradise, that will leave them.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying: ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾: they saw their faces blackened and their eyes blue-grey, ﴿and they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾

Ibn Humayd related to us, Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq related to us, who said: Al-Sha'bi said: Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman sent for me, and with him was Abu al-Zinad Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan, mawla of Quraysh, and they had mentioned something about the companions of al-A'raf that was not as they had said. So I said to them: "If you wish, I will inform you of what Hudhayfah mentioned." They said: "Go on." I said: "Hudhayfah mentioned the companions of al-A'raf and said: They are a people whose good deeds carried them beyond the Fire, and whose bad deeds held them back from Paradise. When their gaze is turned towards the companions of the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾. While they are like that, your Lord looks down upon them and says to them: 'Go, enter Paradise, for I have forgiven you.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/452).]]

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, while narrating this from Ibn Mas'ud: "People will be reckoned on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one, enters Paradise, and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one, enters the Fire." Then he recited Allah's words: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful. And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, abiding forever in Hell﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:102–103] [[Addition from K, M, A. In H: "the two verses."]]. Then he said: "The scale is tipped by the weight of a mustard seed, and it inclines." He said: "And whoever's good deeds and bad deeds are equal is among the companions of al-A'raf. They stop on the Sirat, then they recognise the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. When they look at the people of Paradise, they call out: 'Peace be upon you.' And when they turn their gaze to their left and look at the companions of the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾, and they seek refuge in Allah from their dwelling-place." He said: "As for the people of good deeds, they are given light, and they walk by it before them and to their right. Every servant on that day is given light, and every community is given light. When they reach the Sirat, Allah strips the light of every male hypocrite and female hypocrite. When the people of Paradise see what the hypocrites have suffered, they say: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:8]. As for the companions of al-A'raf, the light was in their hands and was not taken away. At that point Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They have not entered it, while they aspire to﴾, so their aspiring was (considered as) entering." He said: "And Ibn Mas'ud said: Indeed, when the servant does a good deed, ten (rewards) are recorded for him for it, and when he does a bad deed, only one is recorded. Then he says: 'Destroyed is the one whose single (bad deed) outweighs his tenths.'" [[Ibn Jarir related it (12/454).]]

Ibn Jarir also said:

Ibn Waki' and Ibn Humayd related to me, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-A'raf" is the wall between Paradise and the Fire, and the companions of al-A'raf are in that place, until when Allah decides to grant them well-being, they are taken to a river called "al-Hayah" (Life), its banks are reeds of gold, adorned with pearls, its soil is musk. They are cast into it until their complexions become good, and white marks appear on their necks by which they are recognised. When their complexions are good, the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted, brings them and says: "Wish for whatever you want," and they wish, until their wishes run out. Then He says to them: "For you is what you have wished, and its like seventy times over." So they enter Paradise, with a white mark on their necks by which they are recognised; they are called "the poor of the people of Paradise" (masakin ahl al-Jannah).

Ibn Abi Hatim related it likewise, from his father, from Yahya ibn al-Mughirah, from Jarir, with it. Sufyan al-Thawri related it from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, as his own saying (mawquf), and this is more sound, and Allah knows best. It has been related in this way from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and more than one other. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/455).]]

Sunayd ibn Dawud said: Jarir related to me, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Amr ibn Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the companions of al-A'raf, and he said: "They are the last of the servants to be judged between. When the Lord of the worlds has finished judging between the servants, He says: 'You are a people whose good deeds brought you out of the Fire, and you did not enter Paradise. So you are My freed ones, graze in Paradise wherever you wish.'" This is a mursal hasan (a report omitting a Companion in its chain, yet sound). [[Al-Tabari related it (12/461) from al-Qasim, from Sunayd, with its chain.]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related, in the biography of al-Walid ibn Musa, from Munabbih ibn 'Uthman [[In the manuscripts it reads "Shaybah ibn 'Uthman", and the correction is from Tarikh Dimashq and al-Ba'th of al-Bayhaqi.]], from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that the believers among the jinn have reward and they have punishment. We asked him about their reward, and he said: "On the A'raf, and they are not in Paradise with the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)." We asked him: "And what is al-A'raf?" He said: "The wall of Paradise, through which rivers flow, and in which trees and fruits grow." [[In the manuscripts: "concerning their reward and their believers." The text here is from al-Durr al-Manthur (3/88), as noted in the margin of the Shu'ayb edition.]]

Al-Bayhaqi related it from Ibn Bishran, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri, from Yusuf ibn Yazid, from al-Walid ibn Musa, with it. [[Tarikh Dimashq (17/910), the manuscript section, and al-Ba'th of al-Bayhaqi, no. 117, and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat).]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: "The companions of al-A'raf are a righteous people, jurists and scholars."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And between them is a barrier, and upon the heights (al-A'raf) are men who recognize each by his mark﴾. He said: They are men from among the angels, who recognize the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. He said: ﴿And they call out to the companions of Paradise, "Peace be upon you." They have not entered it, but they are hoping [to]. And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people." And the companions of the heights call out to men [in the Fire] whom they recognize by their marks, saying, "Your gathering did not avail you, nor did what you were arrogant about. Are these the ones you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?"﴾ He said: This is when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, [and it is said to them]: ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve.﴾

This chain is sound up to Abu Mijlaz Lahiq ibn Humayd, one of the Successors (tabi'un), but it is a strange statement from him and contrary to the apparent context. The view of the majority takes precedence over his, by the indication of the verse toward what they held. Likewise the saying of Mujahid: that they are a righteous people, scholars and jurists [in the manuscripts K, M, A: "fuqaha' 'ulama'"], is also strange. And Allah knows best.

Al-Qurtubi and others have related twelve opinions concerning them, among which: that they are people of righteousness who testified that they were righteous, who branched off from the branch of the Hereafter, [and in M: "and they were made"; in A: "and they were created"] to observe the news of the people. It was also said: they are prophets. And it was said: they are angels.

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿who recognize each by his mark﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They recognize the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces, and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces. Al-Dahhak also related it from him in the same way.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah placed them in that station so that they might recognize those in Paradise and in the Fire, and so that they might recognize the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces, and seek refuge in Allah that He not place them with the wrongdoing people. In that state they greet the people of Paradise with peace; they have not entered it, but they hope to enter it, and they will enter it, if Allah wills.

Likewise said Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Ma'mar related from al-Hasan that he recited this verse: ﴿They have not entered it, but they are hoping﴾ and said: By Allah, He did not put that hope in their hearts except as an honor He intends for them.

Qatadah said: Allah informed you of their place in hope.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: When the companions of the heights look at the people of the Fire and recognize them, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Suddi said: "And when they pass by them" — meaning the companions of the heights — "a group being led away to the Fire, they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.﴾"

'Ikrimah said: Their faces will be darkened in the Fire, and when they see the companions of Paradise, that will leave them.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying: ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾: they saw their faces blackened and their eyes blue-grey, ﴿and they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾

Allah the Exalted says, reporting (إخبارا [[In K, M, A: "reporting"]]) the rebuke of the people of al-A'raf (the Heights) to men among the chiefs and leaders of the polytheists, whom they recognise in the Fire by their marks: ﴿What your multitude (jam'ukum) availed you, nor your arrogance (mā kuntum tastakbirūn)﴾. That is, your great numbers (katharatukum). ﴿And what you used to be arrogant about﴾. That is, your great numbers and your hosts did not benefit you (in-yanfa'ukum [[In A: "yamna'ukum"]]) against the punishment of Allah. Rather, you have come to what you are in of punishment and torment. ﴿Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy?﴾ 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: they mean the people of al-A'raf. ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, my father narrated to me, my paternal uncle narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They will say, "What your multitude availed you [and what you used to be arrogant about]"﴾ [[Addition from D, K, M, A.]] and so on. He said: When they said to them what Allah had decreed they should say—meaning the people of al-A'raf to the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire—Allah said to the people of arrogance and wealth: ﴿Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy? Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.﴾

Hudhayfah said: The people of al-A'raf are a folk whose deeds were balanced; their good deeds fell short of bringing them to Paradise, and their bad deeds fell short of bringing them to the Fire. So they were placed on al-A'raf, recognising people by their marks. When Allah had judged between the servants, they were permitted to seek intercession. So they came to Adam and said: "O Adam, you are our father, so intercede for us with your Lord." He said: "Do you know that Allah created someone with His hand, breathed into him from His spirit, whose mercy preceded His anger, and whom the angels prostrated to, other than me?" They say: "No." [He said] [[Addition from K, M.]] He says: "I do not know its (his) reality; I cannot intercede for you. But go to my son Ibrahim."

They come to Ibrahim (ﷺ) and ask him to intercede for them with their Lord. He says: "Do you know anyone whom Allah took as a close friend (khalil)? Do you know that anyone was burned in the Fire by his people for the sake of Allah other than me?" They say: "No." He says: "I do not know its reality; I cannot intercede for you. But go to my son Musa."

They come to Musa (peace be upon him), and they say: "Intercede for us with your Lord." He says: "Do you know anyone whom Allah spoke to directly and brought near as a confidant (najiyyan) other than me?" They say: "No." He says: "I do not know its reality; I cannot intercede for you. But go to Isa."

They come to Isa (peace be upon him) and say to him: "Intercede for us with your Lord." He says: "Do you know anyone whom Allah created without a father other than me?" They say: "No." He says: "Do you know anyone who healed the blind and the leper and raised the dead by Allah's permission other than me?" He said: They say: "No." He says: "I am a disputant for myself. I do not know its reality; I cannot intercede for you. But go to Muhammad (ﷺ)."

They come to me, and I strike my hand upon my chest and say: "I am for it (ana laha)." Then I walk until I stand before the Throne, and I come to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and He opens for me of praise what no hearer has ever heard the like of. Then I prostrate, and it is said to me: "O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted." So I raise my head and say: "My Lord, my community (ummati)!" He says: "They are yours." Then no prophet sent, nor any near angel, remains but he envies me for that station, and it is the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud). I bring them to Paradise, I ask for it to be opened, and it is opened for me and for them. They are taken to a river called the River of Life (nahr al-hayawan), its banks are reeds encrusted with pearls, its dust is musk, and its pebbles are rubies. They bathe in it, and the colours of the people of Paradise return to them, and the fragrance of the people of Paradise [[Addition from K, M, A.]], so they become like shining stars, and white marks remain on their chests by which they are recognised; it is said of them: "the Poor (masakin) of the people of Paradise."

[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (12/469).]]

[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (12/469).]]

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, the Exalted, informs us of the humiliation of the people of the Fire, of their request to the people of Paradise for some of their drink and food, and that they will not be granted it.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿The companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided for you."﴾ He meant food.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: they ask them for food and ask them for drink.

Al-Thawri related, from 'Uthman al-Thaqafi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning this verse, that he said: A man calls out to his father or his brother, saying, "I am burning, so pour water on me." It will be said to them, "Answer them." They will say: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers.﴾

It is also related by another chain, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same (1).

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers﴾ means the food of Paradise and its drink.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, Musa ibn al-Mughirah informed us, Abu Musa al-Saffar related to us in the house of 'Amr ibn Muslim, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas, or he was asked: "Which charity is best?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is water. Have you not heard how the people of the Fire, when they cried out to the people of Paradise, said: ﴿Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided for you﴾?" (2)

He also said: Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, al-A'mash related to us, from Abu Salih, who said: When Abu Talib fell ill, they said to him, "If only you would send to this nephew of yours, so that he might send you a cluster from Paradise; perhaps he would cure you with it." The messenger came while Abu Bakr was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr said: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers." (3)

Then Allah, the Exalted, described the disbelievers by what they relied upon in the world: taking their religion as amusement and play, and being deceived by the world, its adornment and its ornaments, away from what they were commanded to do, which is working for the Hereafter.

His saying: ﴿This Day, We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs﴾ means: We will treat them as one who has forgotten them, because Allah, the Exalted, nothing of His knowledge strays from Him, and He does not forget. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:52].

Allah, the Exalted, said this by way of recompense, as He said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], and He said: ﴿Likewise, Our signs came to you, but you neglected them; and likewise today you are neglected﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:126], and the Exalted said: ﴿It will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours"﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:34].

Al-Awfi related, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿This Day, We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs﴾, he said: Allah forgets them from good, but He does not forget them from evil.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "We will leave them, just as they left the meeting of this Day of theirs." Mujahid said: "We will leave them in the Fire." Al-Suddi said: "We will leave them without mercy, just as they left off working for the meeting of this Day of theirs."

It is in the Sahih that Allah, the Exalted, says to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: "Did I not marry you? Did I not honour you? Did I not subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to enjoy?" He will say: "Yes." He will say: "Did you think that you would meet Me?" He will say: "No." Allah will say: "Then today I forget you as you forgot Me." (4)

The Exalted says, informing about His establishing proof against the polytheists by sending the Messenger to them with the Book that the Messenger brought, and that it is a detailed and clear Book, as He said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses have been perfected and then presented in detail from [the One who is] Wise and Acquainted [with all things]﴾ [Hud 11:1] and so on.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We have detailed it with knowledge﴾ [[In K: "knowledge for the worlds," which is an error.]], meaning: with knowledge from Us of what We have detailed it with, as He said: ﴿He sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [An-Nisa 4:166].

Ibn Jarir said: This verse refers back to His saying: ﴿A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no discomfort in your breast concerning it [so that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers]﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:2], and [the verse] ﴿And We have certainly brought them a Book [which We have detailed with knowledge]﴾ [[Added from K and M.]] and so on.

However, what he said is open to question, for the separation is long, and there is no evidence for it. Rather, when He informed about what they had come to of loss in the Hereafter, He mentioned that He had removed their excuses in the worldly life by sending the Messengers and sending down the Books, as in His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra 17:15]. For this reason He said: ﴿Do they await anything but its fulfillment?﴾, meaning: what was promised of punishment, torment, Paradise and Hellfire. This was said by Mujahid and others.

Malik said: its reward. Al-Rabi' said: its fulfillment continues to come as a matter until the Day of Reckoning is complete, until the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire; then its fulfillment is completed on that Day.

﴿The Day its fulfillment comes﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas. ﴿Those who had forgotten it before will say﴾, meaning: those who abandoned acting upon it and neglected it in the worldly life: ﴿The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. Then are there for us any intercessors who will intercede for us?﴾, meaning: for our deliverance from what we are in, ﴿or could we be sent back﴾ to the worldly life ﴿so that we might do other than what we used to do﴾, as He said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire and say, "Oh, if only we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." Rather, there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [Al-An'am 6:27-28]. As He said here: ﴿They have lost themselves, and what they used to fabricate has departed from them﴾, meaning: they have lost themselves by entering the Fire and abiding in it, ﴿and what they used to fabricate has departed from them﴾, meaning: what they used to worship besides Allah has gone from them, so they do not help them, nor do they intercede for them, nor do they rescue them from what they are in.

Allah, exalted is He, informs us that He created this world, its heavens and its earth, and what lies between them, in six days, as He stated in more than one verse of the Qur'an. The six days are: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. On Friday all of creation was gathered together, and on it Adam (peace be upon him) was created.

Scholars differed about these days. Is each of them like these days we know, as is the common understanding that comes to minds? Or is each day like a thousand years, as Mujahid and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal stated explicitly? This is also related through al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas. As for Saturday, no creation took place on it, because it is the seventh day, and it was named al-Sabt (Saturday) from *al-qat'* (cutting off, rest), which is its meaning.

As for the hadith that Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' (the freed slave of Umm Salamah), from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "Allah created the clay on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, created the trees in it on Monday, created the disliked thing on Tuesday, created light on Wednesday, scattered the creatures in it on Thursday, and created Adam after 'Asr on Friday, the last of creation, in the last hour of the hours of Friday, between 'Asr and night."

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated it in his Sahih, and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several chains, from Hajjaj, who is Ibn Muhammad al-A'war, from Ibn Jurayj, with it. In it, all seven days are mentioned, whereas Allah, exalted is He, said "in six days." For this reason al-Bukhari and other hadith memorizers (huffaz) criticized this hadith and considered it to be from the narration of Abu Hurairah from Ka'b al-Ahbar, not a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne﴾, people have made a great many statements on this matter, and this is not the place to expand upon them. Rather, in this matter the path of the pious predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) is followed: Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Thawri, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and others from the imams of the Muslims, past and present. It consists of affirming these attributes as they came, without modality (takyif), without likening (tashbih), and without negation (ta'til). The apparent meaning that comes to the minds of those who liken Allah to creation is negated from Allah, for none of His creation resembles Him, and ﴿There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. Rather, the matter is as the imams said, among them Nu'aym ibn Hammad al-Khuza'i, the teacher of al-Bukhari: "Whoever likens Allah to His creation has disbelieved, and whoever denies what Allah has described Himself with has disbelieved." There is no likening in what Allah described Himself with, nor what His Messenger described Him with. Whoever affirms for Allah, exalted is He, what the clear verses and authentic reports have mentioned, in the manner that befits the majesty of Allah, exalted is He, and negates from Allah, exalted is He, all deficiencies, has taken the path of guidance.

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He covers the night over the day, which pursues it swiftly﴾, meaning: the darkness of this (night) goes away by the light of that (day), and the light of that (day) goes away by the darkness of this (night). Each of them pursues the other swiftly, that is, quickly, without delay from it. Rather, when this one goes, that one comes, and when that one comes, this one goes. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs on to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing. And for the moon We have appointed stations until it returns like the old dried palm stalk. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each is floating in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 37-40]. His saying ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ means that it does not escape from it at any time so as to fall behind it; rather, it follows directly after it, with no interval between them. For this reason He said: ﴿pursuing it swiftly, and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command﴾. Some read (the words) in the accusative, and some in the nominative, and both readings are close in meaning. That is: all of them are under His dominion, subjugation, and will. For this reason He said, as an alert: ﴿Surely, His is the creation and the command﴾, that is, His is the sovereignty and the disposal of affairs. ﴿Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, as He said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed constellations in the sky, and placed in it a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ [al-Furqan: 61].

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to us, Hisham Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Ansari narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Shami, from his father, who had companionship (with the Prophet), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not praise Allah for the righteous deed he has done, and praises himself, has disbelieved and his deed has been nullified. And whoever claims that Allah has given His servants a share in the command, has disbelieved in what Allah sent down to His prophets, because of His saying: ﴿Surely, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾."

In the transmitted supplication, from Abu al-Darda' (and it is also reported as marfu'): "O Allah, to You belongs all sovereignty, to You belongs all praise, to You all affairs return. I ask You for all good, and I seek refuge in You from all evil."

The Exalted [and Glorified] guided His servants to supplicate to Him, which is their welfare in this world and the next. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾. It was said that its meaning is: with humility and submissiveness. And ﴿secretly﴾ is as He said: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and fearfully, and without loudness in speech, in the mornings and evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf 205] [[Added from K, M, A. In H: "the verse".]]

In the Two Sahihs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Added from A.]], who said: The people raised their voices in supplication, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. Indeed, the One you call upon is All-Hearing, Near..." [[In M, K: "All-Hearing, Near"; in D: "Near, All-Hearing".]] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4205); Sahih Muslim, no. (2704).]] The hadith continues.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿humbly and secretly﴾: "Secretly" means "privately."

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿humbly﴾ means with humility and submission to His obedience. ﴿Secretly﴾ means: with the humility of your hearts and the soundness of certainty in His oneness and lordship between you and Him, not openly and ostentatiously.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan, who said: "A man would have memorized the Qur'an while people did not perceive it. A man would have acquired much jurisprudence while people did not perceive it. A man would pray a long prayer in his house while those around him did not perceive it. We have indeed encountered people who had no deed on earth that they could do in private which would ever become public. The Muslims would strive in supplication while no voice of theirs was heard, except a whisper between them and their Lord. That is because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly [Indeed, He does not like transgressors]﴾ [[Added from K.]]. Allah mentioned a righteous servant whose action He approved, saying: ﴿When he called out to his Lord in a secret call﴾ [Maryam 3]."

Ibn Jurayj said: Raising the voice, calling out, and shouting in supplication is disliked, and humility and submissiveness are commanded. Then it was related from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, He does not like transgressors﴾, that it refers to transgression in supplication and in other than it.

Abu Mijlaz said: ﴿Indeed, He does not like transgressors﴾ means: one should not ask for the ranks of the prophets.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, Shu'bah related to us, from Ziyad ibn Mikhraq, I heard Abu Na'amah [[In M, K, A: "Abu 'Ayyaba".]] from a client of Sa'd: that Sa'd heard his son supplicating, saying: "O Allah, I ask You for Paradise, its bliss, its brocade, and similar things, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire, its chains and its shackles." Sa'd said: "You have asked Allah for much good, and sought refuge in Allah from much evil. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'There will indeed be a people who will transgress in supplication.'" And he recited this verse: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly [Indeed, He does not like transgressors]﴾ [[Added from K, M, A. In H: "the verse".]]. It is sufficient for you to say: "O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings me closer to it of speech or deed, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire and whatever brings me closer to it of speech or deed." [[Al-Musnad (1/172).]]

Abu Dawud also related it, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Ziyad ibn Mikhraq, from Abu Na'amah, from a son of Sa'd, from Sa'd, and mentioned it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1480).]] And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Affan related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu Na'amah: that Abdullah ibn Mughaffal [[In A: "Ma'qil".]] heard his son saying: "O Allah, I ask You for the white palace on the right side of Paradise when I enter it." He said: "My son, ask Allah for Paradise, and seek refuge in Him from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'There will be a people who will transgress in supplication and in purification.'"

Thus Ibn Majah related it, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Affan with it. Abu Dawud also narrated it, from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Jurayri, from Abu Na'amah [[Al-Musnad (5/55), Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (3864), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (96).]]. His name is Qays ibn Abayah al-Hanafi al-Basri, and it is a good chain with no defect. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾ forbid, the Exalted, corruption on the earth. How harmful it is after reformation! For when affairs are proceeding upon rectitude, and then corruption occurs after that, it is the most harmful thing for the servants. So Allah, the Exalted [[Added from A.]], forbade that, and commanded worship of Him, supplication to Him, humble entreaty to Him, and abasement before Him, saying: ﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope﴾, meaning: in fear of what is with Him of severe punishment, and in hope of what is with Him of abundant reward.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾, meaning: His mercy is prepared for the doers of good, who follow His commands and abandon His prohibitions, as the Exalted said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things; so I will decree it for those who fear Me [and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses. Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet]﴾ [al-A'raf 156-157] [[Added from K, M, A.]].

And He said ﴿near﴾ and did not say "near" in the feminine, because He treated mercy as having the meaning of reward, or because it is attributed to Allah. Therefore He said: "near to the doers of good."

Mattar al-Warraq said: "Hasten to the promise of Allah through obedience to Him, for He has decreed that His mercy is near to the doers of good." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 57–58:

When the Exalted mentioned that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and that He is the One who disposes, judges, arranges and subjects all things, and He directed the believers to call upon Him, because He is capable of whatever He wills, He drew attention to the fact that He is the Provider, and that He will restore the dead on the Day of Resurrection. So He said: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings﴾. That is, spreading ahead of the clouds that carry the rain. Some of them read ﴿bushran﴾ (as glad tidings), like His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news﴾ [al-Rum: 46].

* *

His saying: ﴿before His mercy﴾ means before the rain, as He said: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Shura: 28]. And He said: ﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the Giver of life to the dead, and He is over all things Competent﴾ [al-Rum: 50].[[In manuscript A: "āthār" (traces).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿until, when they have carried heavy clouds﴾ means the winds carry heavy clouds, heavy because of the abundance of water in them, hanging low near the earth, dark. As Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"And I have submitted my face to Him to whom the clouds submit,
bearing sweet, pure water;
And I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth submits,
bearing heavy rocks."[[The two verses are in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/231).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿We drive it to a dead land﴾ means to a dead land, barren, with no vegetation in it, as the Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead land; We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33]. For this reason He said: ﴿Then We produce by it all kinds of fruits. Thus We bring forth the dead﴾. That is, just as We gave life to this earth after its death, so We will bring the bodies back to life after they have become dust on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sends down water from the sky, and the earth is rained upon for forty days, and the bodies sprout from it in their graves, just as grain sprouts in the earth. This meaning occurs often in the Qur'an, where Allah makes the revival of the earth after its death an example of the Resurrection. For this reason He said: ﴿So that you may remember﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the good land, its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾ means the good land brings forth its plants quickly and beautifully, as He said: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and made her grow a good growth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37].

﴿And that which is wretched, it comes forth only meagerly﴾. Mujahid and others said: like salt-marsh land and the like.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the verse: This is a parable that Allah struck for the believer and the disbeliever.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Hammad ibn Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain that fell on a land. Part of it was pure and absorbed the water, and it produced abundant grass and herbage. Part of it was hard ground that held the water, and Allah benefited people with it; they drank, gave drink, and cultivated. And it fell upon another part, which was barren flat ground that holds no water and grows no plants. That is the likeness of the one who has understanding of the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah has sent me with, so he learns and teaches; and the likeness of the one who does not raise his head to it and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I have been sent."

Related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i through various routes, from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, with it.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (79); Sahih Muslim, no. (2282); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (5843).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 57–58:

When the Exalted mentioned that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and that He is the One who disposes, judges, arranges and subjects all things, and He directed the believers to call upon Him, because He is capable of whatever He wills, He drew attention to the fact that He is the Provider, and that He will restore the dead on the Day of Resurrection. So He said: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings﴾. That is, spreading ahead of the clouds that carry the rain. Some of them read ﴿bushran﴾ (as glad tidings), like His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good news﴾ [al-Rum: 46].

* *

His saying: ﴿before His mercy﴾ means before the rain, as He said: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Shura: 28]. And He said: ﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the Giver of life to the dead, and He is over all things Competent﴾ [al-Rum: 50].[[In manuscript A: "āthār" (traces).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿until, when they have carried heavy clouds﴾ means the winds carry heavy clouds, heavy because of the abundance of water in them, hanging low near the earth, dark. As Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"And I have submitted my face to Him to whom the clouds submit,
bearing sweet, pure water;
And I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth submits,
bearing heavy rocks."[[The two verses are in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/231).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿We drive it to a dead land﴾ means to a dead land, barren, with no vegetation in it, as the Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead land; We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33]. For this reason He said: ﴿Then We produce by it all kinds of fruits. Thus We bring forth the dead﴾. That is, just as We gave life to this earth after its death, so We will bring the bodies back to life after they have become dust on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sends down water from the sky, and the earth is rained upon for forty days, and the bodies sprout from it in their graves, just as grain sprouts in the earth. This meaning occurs often in the Qur'an, where Allah makes the revival of the earth after its death an example of the Resurrection. For this reason He said: ﴿So that you may remember﴾.

The Qur'an's mention of Adam's story at the beginning of the surah is concluded, along with what relates to it. Then Allah, the Exalted, began to mention the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, in order, starting with the earliest. He began with Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, because he was the first messenger sent to the people of the earth after Adam, peace be upon him. He is Nuh son of Lamak, son of Mutawshalikh, son of Khanukh, who is Idris [the Prophet] [[Addition from A.]], peace be upon him, according to what they claim, and he was the first to write with the pen. He is the son of Barad, son of Muhlil, son of Qaynan, son of Yanish, son of Shith, son of Adam, upon [[In A: "upon them."]] him be peace.

Thus did Muhammad [[Addition from K, M, A.]] ibn Ishaq and many other genealogists trace his lineage. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: No prophet suffered harm from his people as much as Nuh did, except a prophet who was killed.

Yazid al-Raqqashi said: He was only named Nuh because of how much he lamented (naha) over himself.

Between Adam and the time of Nuh, peace be upon them both, there were ten generations, all of them upon Islam [this was said by Abdullah ibn Abbas [Addition from M, A.]].

Abdullah ibn Abbas and many other scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) said: The first form of idol worship came about when righteous people died, and their folk built places of worship over their graves and made images of those righteous people in them, so that they would remember their condition and worship and emulate them. When time passed, they made those images into bodies in the likeness of those figures. As time went on, they worshipped those idols and named them after the names of those righteous people: "Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr." When the matter grew severe, Allah, glorified and exalted, to Whom belong all praise and grace, sent His messenger Nuh to command them to worship Allah alone, with no partner. He said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ That is, the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, if you meet Allah while associating others with Him. ﴿The eminent among his people said⦆ That is, the majority, the leaders, the commanders and the chiefs among them: ﴿Indeed, we see you in clear error.﴾ That is, in your calling us to abandon the worship of these idols that we found our fathers devoted to. This is also the attitude of the wicked, who see the righteous as being in misguidance, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿When they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are surely astray."﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 32] And: ﴿Those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they are not guided by it, they will say, 'This is an ancient falsehood.'"﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 11], and other verses to that effect.

﴿He said, "O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: I am not astray, but I am a messenger from the Lord and Sovereign of everything. ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord and advise you, and I know from Allah what you do not know.﴾ This is the way of a messenger: he is to be eloquent, articulate, and a sincere advisor on behalf of Allah, and none of Allah's creation attains these qualities as he does. As it came in Sahih Muslim: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the Day of Arafah, when they were at their most numerous and their gathering was greatest: "O people, you will be questioned about me, so what will you say?" They said: "We testify that you have conveyed, fulfilled and advised." He then began raising his finger toward the sky and pointing it at them, saying: "O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness. O Allah, bear witness." [["O Allah, bear witness" appears three times in A.]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1218), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

The passage is from Ibn Kathir's commentary. Translating it now.

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about Nuh (peace be upon him), that he said to his people: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, so that he may warn you and that you may fear Allah, and that perhaps you may receive mercy?﴾ That is, do not be astonished at this. There is nothing astonishing in Allah revealing to a man from among you, out of mercy, kindness and benevolence towards you, in order to warn you and so that you may guard against the punishment of Allah and not associate anything with Him, ﴿and that perhaps you may receive mercy﴾.

Allah says: ﴿But they denied him﴾, meaning they persisted in denying and opposing him, and none believed with him from among them except a few, as stated elsewhere: ﴿Then We saved him and those with him in the ship﴾, which is the Ark (al-Fulk), as He said: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15]. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾, as He said: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned, then they were made to enter the Fire, and they found for themselves no helpers besides Allah﴾ [Nuh: 25].

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were a blind people﴾, meaning blind to the truth: they neither perceive it nor are they guided to it.

In this story, Allah has made clear that He avenged His allies against their enemies, saved His messenger and the believers, and destroyed their enemies among the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses will stand, the day when the excuse of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51-52].

This is the way of Allah with His servants in this world and the Hereafter: that the final outcome is for the righteous, and victory and triumph belong to them, just as the people of Nuh were destroyed by drowning and Nuh and his believing companions were saved.

Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam: The people of Nuh were so crowded that the plain and the mountain were too narrow for them.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Allah did not punish the people of Nuh except when the earth was full of them, and there was not a plot of land on earth except that it had an owner and a possessor.

Ibn Wahb said: It reached me from Ibn 'Abbas that eighty men were saved with Nuh in the ship, one of them being "Jurhum," and his tongue was Arabic.

Ibn Abi Hatim related these reports. This last report has also been narrated through another, connected chain from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Allah the Exalted says: Just as We sent Noah to his people, so too We sent to 'Ad their brother Hud.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They were [from] [[addition from M.]] the descendants of 'Ad ibn Iram ibn 'Aws ibn Sam ibn Noah.

I say: These are the first 'Ad, whom Allah mentioned [the Exalted] [[addition from A.]]. They are the sons of 'Ad ibn Iram, who used to take refuge in pillars in the open country, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [the people of] Iram of the pillars, the likes of whom were not created in the lands?﴾ [Al-Fajr: 6-8]. That was because of their great might and strength, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were arrogant in the earth without right and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they were rejecting Our signs.﴾ [Fussilat: 15].

Their dwellings were in Yemen, in al-Ahqaf, which are mountains of sand.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khuza'i, from Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila, who said: I heard 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] [[addition from A.]] say to a man from Hadramawt: "Have you seen a red sand dune mixed with red clay, with arak trees and abundant lote trees, in such-and-such a region of the land of Hadramawt? Have you seen it?" He said: "Yes, O Commander of the Faithful. By Allah, you describe it as one who has seen it." He said: "No, but I have been told about it." The Hadrami said: "What is its matter, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "In it is the grave of Hud, peace be upon him."

Ibn Jarir narrated it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (12/507).]]. This report contains the benefit that their dwellings were in Yemen, and that Hud, peace be upon him, was buried there. He was among the most noble of his people in lineage, because Allah sends the Messengers [may the blessings of Allah be upon them] [[addition from A.]] only from the best and most noble tribes.
