There was also another woman called Sadduf, daughter of al-Muhayya ibn Dahr ibn al-Muhayya, who had lineage, wealth and beauty, and who had been married to a Muslim man of Thamud, but she separated from him. These two women would offer rewards to whoever would undertake to kill the she-camel. Sadduf summoned a man called al-Hubab and offered herself to him if he would hamstring the she-camel, but he refused her. So she summoned a paternal cousin of hers called Mis'da' ibn Mihraj ibn al-Muhayya, and he agreed to that. 'Unayzah daughter of Ghanm summoned Qidar ibn Salif ibn Jundu', who was a reddish-blue, short man. They claimed that he was the son of an illegitimate union, and that he was not the son of his supposed father Salif; rather he was from a man called Sihyad, but he was born on the bed of Salif. She said to him: "I will give you whichever of my daughters you wish, on condition that you hamstring the she-camel!" At that, Qidar ibn Salif and Mis'da' ibn Mihraj set out and stirred up some of the deviants of Thamud. Seven men followed them, making nine men, and they are the ones about whom Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there were in the city nine people who spread corruption in the land and did not amend﴾ [Al-Naml 27:48]. They were chiefs among their people, and they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, which obeyed them in this. So they set out and lay in wait for the she-camel when she came back from the water. Qidar hid at the base of a rock on her path, and Mis'da' hid at the base of another. She passed by Mis'da', who shot her with an arrow, which struck the muscle of her leg. Then Umm Ghanam 'Unayzah came out and ordered her daughter, who was among the most beautiful of people, to uncover her face to Qidar and urge him on. He rushed at the she-camel with the sword and cut her hamstring, so she fell down to the ground. She let out a single cry, warning her young, then he stabbed her in the throat and slaughtered her. Her young, which was her foal, ran off until it reached a fortified mountain, climbed to the top of the highest rock on it, and cried out. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from someone who heard al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "O Lord, where is my mother?" It is also said that it cried out three times, and that it entered a rock and disappeared into it. It is also said that they pursued it and hamstrung it along with its mother. And Allah knows best. [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/536)]

When they had done that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the news reached Salih, peace be upon him, and he came to them while they were gathered together. When he saw the she-camel he wept and said: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied﴾ [Hud 11:65]. The killing of the she-camel had taken place on Wednesday. When evening came, those nine men of the group resolved to kill Salih, peace be upon him, and said: "If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will send him to join his she-camel!" ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah that we will attack him and his family by night, and then we will say to his guardian: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'" And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people all together. Those are their houses, empty because of what they did wrong﴾ [An-Naml 27:49-52], and the rest of the verse.

When they had resolved upon this and agreed on it, and came at night to slay the Prophet of Allah Salih, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and to Him belongs might, and to His Messenger, sent down upon them stones which crushed them, in advance and by hastening, before their people. Thamud awoke on Thursday, which was the first day of the respite, and their faces were yellow, as Salih, peace be upon him, had promised them. They awoke on the second day of the delay, which was Friday, and their faces were red. They awoke on the third day of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. When they awoke on Sunday, having perfumed themselves with camphor and sat waiting for the vengeance and punishment of Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from that, not knowing what would be done to them or how the punishment would come upon them, and when the sun rose, there came upon them a blast from the heavens and a severe quaking from beneath them. Their souls departed and their lives were taken in a single moment, ﴿so they were in their homes lying prostrate﴾, that is, corpses with no life in them. None of them escaped, neither small nor great, neither male nor female. They said: except for a girl who was paralysed, named "Kalba bint al-Saluq", also called "al-Zuraygah", and she was an unbeliever, extremely hostile to Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, her legs were freed, and she got up running as fast as anything, and came to one of the tribes and informed them of what she had seen and what had befallen her people. Then she asked them for water, and when she drank it, she died.

The scholars of tafsir said: No one remained of the offspring of Thamud except Salih, peace be upon him, and those who followed him, may Allah be pleased with them, except that a man called "Abu Righal" was, when the punishment fell on his people, residing in the Sacred Precinct (Haram), so nothing befell him. When he went out one day to the non-sacred area (al-Hill), a stone from the sky came to him and killed him.

The hadith of "Jabir ibn Abdullah" about this has already been mentioned at the beginning of the story, and they mention that this Abu Righal was the father of Thaqif, who used to live in Ta'if [See: the discussion on Abu Righal, and the preference that he was the guide of Abraha, in the tafsir of Surat an-Nisa', verse 4].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me that the Prophet ﷺ passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "Do you know who this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud, who was in the Sanctuary of Allah, and the Sanctuary of Allah protected him from the punishment of Allah. When he went out, he was struck by what struck his people, and he was buried here, and buried with him was a branch of gold. The people descended and rushed at it with their swords, searching for him, and they extracted the branch."

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is the father of Thaqif.

[Al-Musannaf, no. (20989), and Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/119, 220).]

This is a mursal report by this route, but it has been narrated connected by another route, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, when we went out with him to Ta'if, and we passed by a grave, "This is the grave of Abu Righal, and he is the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this Sanctuary, and it protected him. When he went out from it, the punishment that struck his people struck him in this place, and he was buried here. The sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him; if you dig for it, you will find it with him." So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.

Abu Dawud related it in this manner, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, with it.

[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3088).]

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a hasan gharib hadith.

I say: Only Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr narrated it connected, and he is an unknown shaykh who is known only through this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Isma'il ibn Umayyah.

I say: In light of this, it is feared that he erred in raising this hadith, and it may be only a statement of Abdullah ibn Amr, which he took from the two books (al-Zamilatayn).

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj said, after I presented this to him: This is possible, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His, the Exalted's, saying:

The scholars of tafsir and genealogy say: Thamud was the son of 'Athir ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh (Noah). He was the brother of Jadis ibn 'Athir, and the tribe of Tasm was likewise. All of these were living tribes of the Arabs of al-'Ariba before Ibrahim al-Khalil (Abraham the Friend of God) (peace be upon him). Thamud came after 'Ad, and their dwellings were well known between the Hijaz and al-Sham (Syria), extending to Wadi al-Qura and its surroundings. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by their villages and dwellings in the ninth year (AH), on his way to Tabuk.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) camped with the people at Tabuk, he camped with them at al-Hijr, near the dwellings of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they kneaded dough with it and set their cooking pots with it. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them, so they poured out the pots and fed the dough to the camels. Then he moved on with them until he camped with them at the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them to enter upon the people who had been punished, and said: "I fear that what befell them will befall you, so do not enter upon them." [Al-Musnad (2/117)]

Imam Ahmad also said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said while he was at al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you." [Al-Musnad (2/74)]

The origin of this hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) through more than one chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3381), and Sahih Muslim no. (298)]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-Mas'udi informed us, from Isma'il ibn Awsat, from Muhammad ibn Abi Kabshah al-Anmari, from his father, who said: During the expedition of Tabuk, the people rushed to the people of al-Hijr, entering upon them. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he called out among the people: "Gather for prayer!" He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was holding his camel's [staff/stick], and he was saying: "Why do you enter upon a people with whom Allah is angry?" A man among them called out: "We are amazed at them, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Shall I not inform you of something more amazing than that? A man from among yourselves who informs you of what came before you and what will come after you. So be upright and steadfast, for Allah does not regard your punishment at all, and there will come a people who will not repel anything from themselves." [Al-Musnad (4/231). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/194): "In it is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mas'udi, and he had become confused (in his memory)."]

None of the authors of the Sunan collections recorded it. Abu Kabshah's name is Umar ibn Sa'd, and it is said: Amir ibn Sa'd. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by al-Hijr, he said: "Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them. The she-camel used to come through this mountain pass and leave through that mountain pass. But they transgressed the command of their Lord and slaughtered her. She used to drink their water one day, and they used to drink her milk one day. Then they slaughtered her, so a blast seized them, and Allah extinguished every one of them beneath the vault of the sky, except one man who was in the sanctuary of Allah." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Abu Righal. When he left the sanctuary, what had befallen his people befell him." [Al-Musnad (3/296). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/194): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih."]

This hadith is not in any of the Six Books, but it meets the conditions of Muslim.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih﴾, meaning: And We certainly sent to the tribe of Thamud their brother Salih. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾. All the Messengers called to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, as the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:25]. And He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:36].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you﴾, meaning: There has certainly come to you a proof from Allah confirming the truth of what I have brought you. It was they who had asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they proposed to him that she should emerge for them from a solid rock which they themselves had specified. It was a single rock in a region of al-Hijr, called al-Katibah. They asked him to bring out from it a pregnant she-camel in her final months, about to give birth. So Salih took from them covenants and firm pledges that if Allah answered their request and granted their demand, they would believe in him and follow him. When they had given him their covenants and firm pledges on this, Salih (peace be upon him) stood up to his prayer and called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That rock moved, then split open, and out came a she-camel, large and hairy, her unborn young moving between her sides, just as they had asked. At that point the chief of the people, Jundu' ibn Amr, and those with him in his affair (in his religion), believed. The remaining nobles of Thamud wanted to believe, but Dhu'ab ibn Amr ibn Labid and al-Hubab, the keeper of their idols, and Rabab ibn Sam'ar ibn Jalhas prevented them. Jundu' ibn Amr had a paternal cousin called Shihab ibn Khalifah ibn Muhallah ibn Labid ibn Harras, who was one of the nobles and best men of Thamud. He wanted to become Muslim as well, but that group forbade him, and he obeyed them. A man among the believers of Thamud, called Mihwas ibn 'Anmah ibn al-Dumayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said about this:

A band of the family of 'Amr called upon Shihab
to the religion of the Prophet, all of them together,
the mighty one of Thamud. He was resolved to answer, and had he answered,
Salih would have become mighty among us,
and they would not have deviated from their leader, Dhu'ab.
But the deviants of the family of Hujr,
after their rightness, turned into wolves.

The she-camel and her young remained among them for a period after she had given birth amid them. She drank the water of their well one day, and left it for them one day. They used to drink her milk on the day she drank, milking her and filling whatever vessels and containers they wished, just as He said in another verse: ﴿And inform them that the water is divided between them; each share is attended﴾ [Al-Qamar 54:28]. And He said: ﴿This is a she-camel; she has a drink, and you have a drink on a known day﴾ [Al-Shu'ara 26:155]. She used to graze in some of those valleys, entering by one mountain pass and leaving by another, so that there would be room for her, because she would drink her fill of the water. According to what has been mentioned, she was a fearsome creature and a magnificent sight; when she passed by their livestock, they would scatter away from her. When their denial of Salih the Prophet (peace be upon him) grew long and intense, they resolved to kill her, so that they could monopolize the water every day. It is said that they all agreed together on killing her.

Qatadah said: It has reached me that the one who killed the she-camel went around among all of them, and they all consented to her killing, even the women in their litters and the boys as well.

I say: This is the apparent meaning, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled them﴾ [Al-Shams 91:14]. And He says: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her﴾ [Al-Isra 17:59]. And He says: ﴿But they hamstrung the she-camel﴾. He attributed it to the whole tribe collectively, which indicates the consent of all of them to it. And Allah knows best.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, and other scholars of tafsir mentioned regarding the cause of the killing of the she-camel: that a woman among them, called 'Unayzah, daughter of Ghanm ibn Mijlaz, whose kunyah was Umm Ghanam, was an old disbelieving woman, and she was among the people most hostile to Salih (peace be upon him). She had beautiful daughters and abundant wealth. Her husband was Dhu'ab ibn Amr, one of the chiefs of Thamud. There was also another woman called Sadduf, daughter of al-Muhayya ibn Dahr ibn al-Muhayya, who had lineage, wealth and beauty, and who had been married to a Muslim man of Thamud, but she separated from him. These two women would offer rewards to whoever would undertake to kill the she-camel. Sadduf summoned a man called al-Hubab and offered herself to him if he would hamstring the she-camel, but he refused her. So she summoned a paternal cousin of hers called Mis'da' ibn Mihraj ibn al-Muhayya, and he agreed to that. 'Unayzah daughter of Ghanm summoned Qidar ibn Salif ibn Jundu', who was a reddish-blue, short man. They claimed that he was the son of an illegitimate union, and that he was not the son of his supposed father Salif; rather he was from a man called Sihyad, but he was born on the bed of Salif. She said to him: "I will give you whichever of my daughters you wish, on condition that you hamstring the she-camel!" At that, Qidar ibn Salif and Mis'da' ibn Mihraj set out and stirred up some of the deviants of Thamud. Seven men followed them, making nine men, and they are the ones about whom Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there were in the city nine people who spread corruption in the land and did not amend﴾ [Al-Naml 27:48]. They were chiefs among their people, and they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, which obeyed them in this. So they set out and lay in wait for the she-camel when she came back from the water. Qidar hid at the base of a rock on her path, and Mis'da' hid at the base of another. She passed by Mis'da', who shot her with an arrow, which struck the muscle of her leg. Then Umm Ghanam 'Unayzah came out and ordered her daughter, who was among the most beautiful of people, to uncover her face to Qidar and urge him on. He rushed at the she-camel with the sword and cut her hamstring, so she fell down to the ground. She let out a single cry, warning her young, then he stabbed her in the throat and slaughtered her. Her young, which was her foal, ran off until it reached a fortified mountain, climbed to the top of the highest rock on it, and cried out. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from someone who heard al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "O Lord, where is my mother?" It is also said that it cried out three times, and that it entered a rock and disappeared into it. It is also said that they pursued it and hamstrung it along with its mother. And Allah knows best. [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/536)]

When they had done that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the news reached Salih, peace be upon him, and he came to them while they were gathered together. When he saw the she-camel he wept and said: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied﴾ [Hud 11:65]. The killing of the she-camel had taken place on Wednesday. When evening came, those nine men of the group resolved to kill Salih, peace be upon him, and said: "If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will send him to join his she-camel!" ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah that we will attack him and his family by night, and then we will say to his guardian: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'" And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people all together. Those are their houses, empty because of what they did wrong﴾ [An-Naml 27:49-52], and the rest of the verse.

When they had resolved upon this and agreed on it, and came at night to slay the Prophet of Allah Salih, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and to Him belongs might, and to His Messenger, sent down upon them stones which crushed them, in advance and by hastening, before their people. Thamud awoke on Thursday, which was the first day of the respite, and their faces were yellow, as Salih, peace be upon him, had promised them. They awoke on the second day of the delay, which was Friday, and their faces were red. They awoke on the third day of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. When they awoke on Sunday, having perfumed themselves with camphor and sat waiting for the vengeance and punishment of Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from that, not knowing what would be done to them or how the punishment would come upon them, and when the sun rose, there came upon them a blast from the heavens and a severe quaking from beneath them. Their souls departed and their lives were taken in a single moment, ﴿so they were in their homes lying prostrate﴾, that is, corpses with no life in them. None of them escaped, neither small nor great, neither male nor female. They said: except for a girl who was paralysed, named "Kalba bint al-Saluq", also called "al-Zuraygah", and she was an unbeliever, extremely hostile to Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, her legs were freed, and she got up running as fast as anything, and came to one of the tribes and informed them of what she had seen and what had befallen her people. Then she asked them for water, and when she drank it, she died.

The scholars of tafsir said: No one remained of the offspring of Thamud except Salih, peace be upon him, and those who followed him, may Allah be pleased with them, except that a man called "Abu Righal" was, when the punishment fell on his people, residing in the Sacred Precinct (Haram), so nothing befell him. When he went out one day to the non-sacred area (al-Hill), a stone from the sky came to him and killed him.

The hadith of "Jabir ibn Abdullah" about this has already been mentioned at the beginning of the story, and they mention that this Abu Righal was the father of Thaqif, who used to live in Ta'if [See: the discussion on Abu Righal, and the preference that he was the guide of Abraha, in the tafsir of Surat an-Nisa', verse 4].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me that the Prophet ﷺ passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "Do you know who this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud, who was in the Sanctuary of Allah, and the Sanctuary of Allah protected him from the punishment of Allah. When he went out, he was struck by what struck his people, and he was buried here, and buried with him was a branch of gold. The people descended and rushed at it with their swords, searching for him, and they extracted the branch."

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is the father of Thaqif.

[Al-Musannaf, no. (20989), and Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/119, 220).]

This is a mursal report by this route, but it has been narrated connected by another route, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, when we went out with him to Ta'if, and we passed by a grave, "This is the grave of Abu Righal, and he is the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this Sanctuary, and it protected him. When he went out from it, the punishment that struck his people struck him in this place, and he was buried here. The sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him; if you dig for it, you will find it with him." So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.

Abu Dawud related it in this manner, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, with it.

[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3088).]

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a hasan gharib hadith.

I say: Only Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr narrated it connected, and he is an unknown shaykh who is known only through this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Isma'il ibn Umayyah.

I say: In light of this, it is feared that he erred in raising this hadith, and it may be only a statement of Abdullah ibn Amr, which he took from the two books (al-Zamilatayn).

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj said, after I presented this to him: This is possible, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His, the Exalted's, saying:

The scholars of tafsir and genealogy say: Thamud was the son of 'Athir ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh (Noah). He was the brother of Jadis ibn 'Athir, and the tribe of Tasm was likewise. All of these were living tribes of the Arabs of al-'Ariba before Ibrahim al-Khalil (Abraham the Friend of God) (peace be upon him). Thamud came after 'Ad, and their dwellings were well known between the Hijaz and al-Sham (Syria), extending to Wadi al-Qura and its surroundings. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by their villages and dwellings in the ninth year (AH), on his way to Tabuk.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) camped with the people at Tabuk, he camped with them at al-Hijr, near the dwellings of Thamud. The people drew water from the wells from which Thamud used to drink, and they kneaded dough with it and set their cooking pots with it. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them, so they poured out the pots and fed the dough to the camels. Then he moved on with them until he camped with them at the well from which the she-camel used to drink. He forbade them to enter upon the people who had been punished, and said: "I fear that what befell them will befall you, so do not enter upon them." [Al-Musnad (2/117)]

Imam Ahmad also said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said while he was at al-Hijr: "Do not enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping; if you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you." [Al-Musnad (2/74)]

The origin of this hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) through more than one chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3381), and Sahih Muslim no. (298)]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-Mas'udi informed us, from Isma'il ibn Awsat, from Muhammad ibn Abi Kabshah al-Anmari, from his father, who said: During the expedition of Tabuk, the people rushed to the people of al-Hijr, entering upon them. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he called out among the people: "Gather for prayer!" He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was holding his camel's [staff/stick], and he was saying: "Why do you enter upon a people with whom Allah is angry?" A man among them called out: "We are amazed at them, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Shall I not inform you of something more amazing than that? A man from among yourselves who informs you of what came before you and what will come after you. So be upright and steadfast, for Allah does not regard your punishment at all, and there will come a people who will not repel anything from themselves." [Al-Musnad (4/231). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/194): "In it is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mas'udi, and he had become confused (in his memory)."]

None of the authors of the Sunan collections recorded it. Abu Kabshah's name is Umar ibn Sa'd, and it is said: Amir ibn Sa'd. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by al-Hijr, he said: "Do not ask for signs, for the people of Salih asked for them. The she-camel used to come through this mountain pass and leave through that mountain pass. But they transgressed the command of their Lord and slaughtered her. She used to drink their water one day, and they used to drink her milk one day. Then they slaughtered her, so a blast seized them, and Allah extinguished every one of them beneath the vault of the sky, except one man who was in the sanctuary of Allah." They said: "Who is he, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Abu Righal. When he left the sanctuary, what had befallen his people befell him." [Al-Musnad (3/296). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/194): "The narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih."]

This hadith is not in any of the Six Books, but it meets the conditions of Muslim.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih﴾, meaning: And We certainly sent to the tribe of Thamud their brother Salih. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾. All the Messengers called to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, as the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya 21:25]. And He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [Al-Nahl 16:36].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you﴾, meaning: There has certainly come to you a proof from Allah confirming the truth of what I have brought you. It was they who had asked Salih to bring them a sign, and they proposed to him that she should emerge for them from a solid rock which they themselves had specified. It was a single rock in a region of al-Hijr, called al-Katibah. They asked him to bring out from it a pregnant she-camel in her final months, about to give birth. So Salih took from them covenants and firm pledges that if Allah answered their request and granted their demand, they would believe in him and follow him. When they had given him their covenants and firm pledges on this, Salih (peace be upon him) stood up to his prayer and called upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That rock moved, then split open, and out came a she-camel, large and hairy, her unborn young moving between her sides, just as they had asked. At that point the chief of the people, Jundu' ibn Amr, and those with him in his affair (in his religion), believed. The remaining nobles of Thamud wanted to believe, but Dhu'ab ibn Amr ibn Labid and al-Hubab, the keeper of their idols, and Rabab ibn Sam'ar ibn Jalhas prevented them. Jundu' ibn Amr had a paternal cousin called Shihab ibn Khalifah ibn Muhallah ibn Labid ibn Harras, who was one of the nobles and best men of Thamud. He wanted to become Muslim as well, but that group forbade him, and he obeyed them. A man among the believers of Thamud, called Mihwas ibn 'Anmah ibn al-Dumayl, may Allah have mercy on him, said about this:

A band of the family of 'Amr called upon Shihab
to the religion of the Prophet, all of them together,
the mighty one of Thamud. He was resolved to answer, and had he answered,
Salih would have become mighty among us,
and they would not have deviated from their leader, Dhu'ab.
But the deviants of the family of Hujr,
after their rightness, turned into wolves.

The she-camel and her young remained among them for a period after she had given birth amid them. She drank the water of their well one day, and left it for them one day. They used to drink her milk on the day she drank, milking her and filling whatever vessels and containers they wished, just as He said in another verse: ﴿And inform them that the water is divided between them; each share is attended﴾ [Al-Qamar 54:28]. And He said: ﴿This is a she-camel; she has a drink, and you have a drink on a known day﴾ [Al-Shu'ara 26:155]. She used to graze in some of those valleys, entering by one mountain pass and leaving by another, so that there would be room for her, because she would drink her fill of the water. According to what has been mentioned, she was a fearsome creature and a magnificent sight; when she passed by their livestock, they would scatter away from her. When their denial of Salih the Prophet (peace be upon him) grew long and intense, they resolved to kill her, so that they could monopolize the water every day. It is said that they all agreed together on killing her.

Qatadah said: It has reached me that the one who killed the she-camel went around among all of them, and they all consented to her killing, even the women in their litters and the boys as well.

I say: This is the apparent meaning, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled them﴾ [Al-Shams 91:14]. And He says: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her﴾ [Al-Isra 17:59]. And He says: ﴿But they hamstrung the she-camel﴾. He attributed it to the whole tribe collectively, which indicates the consent of all of them to it. And Allah knows best.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, and other scholars of tafsir mentioned regarding the cause of the killing of the she-camel: that a woman among them, called 'Unayzah, daughter of Ghanm ibn Mijlaz, whose kunyah was Umm Ghanam, was an old disbelieving woman, and she was among the people most hostile to Salih (peace be upon him). She had beautiful daughters and abundant wealth. Her husband was Dhu'ab ibn Amr, one of the chiefs of Thamud. There was also another woman called Sadduf, daughter of al-Muhayya ibn Dahr ibn al-Muhayya, who had lineage, wealth and beauty, and who had been married to a Muslim man of Thamud, but she separated from him. These two women would offer rewards to whoever would undertake to kill the she-camel. Sadduf summoned a man called al-Hubab and offered herself to him if he would hamstring the she-camel, but he refused her. So she summoned a paternal cousin of hers called Mis'da' ibn Mihraj ibn al-Muhayya, and he agreed to that. 'Unayzah daughter of Ghanm summoned Qidar ibn Salif ibn Jundu', who was a reddish-blue, short man. They claimed that he was the son of an illegitimate union, and that he was not the son of his supposed father Salif; rather he was from a man called Sihyad, but he was born on the bed of Salif. She said to him: "I will give you whichever of my daughters you wish, on condition that you hamstring the she-camel!" At that, Qidar ibn Salif and Mis'da' ibn Mihraj set out and stirred up some of the deviants of Thamud. Seven men followed them, making nine men, and they are the ones about whom Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there were in the city nine people who spread corruption in the land and did not amend﴾ [Al-Naml 27:48]. They were chiefs among their people, and they won over the entire disbelieving tribe, which obeyed them in this. So they set out and lay in wait for the she-camel when she came back from the water. Qidar hid at the base of a rock on her path, and Mis'da' hid at the base of another. She passed by Mis'da', who shot her with an arrow, which struck the muscle of her leg. Then Umm Ghanam 'Unayzah came out and ordered her daughter, who was among the most beautiful of people, to uncover her face to Qidar and urge him on. He rushed at the she-camel with the sword and cut her hamstring, so she fell down to the ground. She let out a single cry, warning her young, then he stabbed her in the throat and slaughtered her. Her young, which was her foal, ran off until it reached a fortified mountain, climbed to the top of the highest rock on it, and cried out. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from someone who heard al-Hasan al-Basri, that he said: "O Lord, where is my mother?" It is also said that it cried out three times, and that it entered a rock and disappeared into it. It is also said that they pursued it and hamstrung it along with its mother. And Allah knows best. [Tafsir al-Tabari (12/536)]

When they had done that and finished hamstringing the she-camel, the news reached Salih, peace be upon him, and he came to them while they were gathered together. When he saw the she-camel he wept and said: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied﴾ [Hud 11:65]. The killing of the she-camel had taken place on Wednesday. When evening came, those nine men of the group resolved to kill Salih, peace be upon him, and said: "If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will send him to join his she-camel!" ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah that we will attack him and his family by night, and then we will say to his guardian: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'" And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive. So see how was the end of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people all together. Those are their houses, empty because of what they did wrong﴾ [An-Naml 27:49-52], and the rest of the verse.

When they had resolved upon this and agreed on it, and came at night to slay the Prophet of Allah Salih, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and to Him belongs might, and to His Messenger, sent down upon them stones which crushed them, in advance and by hastening, before their people. Thamud awoke on Thursday, which was the first day of the respite, and their faces were yellow, as Salih, peace be upon him, had promised them. They awoke on the second day of the delay, which was Friday, and their faces were red. They awoke on the third day of enjoyment, which was Saturday, and their faces were black. When they awoke on Sunday, having perfumed themselves with camphor and sat waiting for the vengeance and punishment of Allah, we seek refuge in Allah from that, not knowing what would be done to them or how the punishment would come upon them, and when the sun rose, there came upon them a blast from the heavens and a severe quaking from beneath them. Their souls departed and their lives were taken in a single moment, ﴿so they were in their homes lying prostrate﴾, that is, corpses with no life in them. None of them escaped, neither small nor great, neither male nor female. They said: except for a girl who was paralysed, named "Kalba bint al-Saluq", also called "al-Zuraygah", and she was an unbeliever, extremely hostile to Salih, peace be upon him. When she saw what she saw of the punishment, her legs were freed, and she got up running as fast as anything, and came to one of the tribes and informed them of what she had seen and what had befallen her people. Then she asked them for water, and when she drank it, she died.

The scholars of tafsir said: No one remained of the offspring of Thamud except Salih, peace be upon him, and those who followed him, may Allah be pleased with them, except that a man called "Abu Righal" was, when the punishment fell on his people, residing in the Sacred Precinct (Haram), so nothing befell him. When he went out one day to the non-sacred area (al-Hill), a stone from the sky came to him and killed him.

The hadith of "Jabir ibn Abdullah" about this has already been mentioned at the beginning of the story, and they mention that this Abu Righal was the father of Thaqif, who used to live in Ta'if [See: the discussion on Abu Righal, and the preference that he was the guide of Abraha, in the tafsir of Surat an-Nisa', verse 4].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar said: Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me that the Prophet ﷺ passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "Do you know who this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, a man from Thamud, who was in the Sanctuary of Allah, and the Sanctuary of Allah protected him from the punishment of Allah. When he went out, he was struck by what struck his people, and he was buried here, and buried with him was a branch of gold. The people descended and rushed at it with their swords, searching for him, and they extracted the branch."

Abd al-Razzaq also said: Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Righal is the father of Thaqif.

[Al-Musannaf, no. (20989), and Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/119, 220).]

This is a mursal report by this route, but it has been narrated connected by another route, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, when we went out with him to Ta'if, and we passed by a grave, "This is the grave of Abu Righal, and he is the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this Sanctuary, and it protected him. When he went out from it, the punishment that struck his people struck him in this place, and he was buried here. The sign of that is that a branch of gold was buried with him; if you dig for it, you will find it with him." So the people rushed to it and extracted the branch from it.

Abu Dawud related it in this manner, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Wahb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, with it.

[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (3088).]

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is a hasan gharib hadith.

I say: Only Bujayr ibn Abi Bujayr narrated it connected, and he is an unknown shaykh who is known only through this hadith. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: I did not hear anyone narrate from him except Isma'il ibn Umayyah.

I say: In light of this, it is feared that he erred in raising this hadith, and it may be only a statement of Abdullah ibn Amr, which he took from the two books (al-Zamilatayn).

Our shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj said, after I presented this to him: This is possible, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His, the Exalted's, saying:

This is a reproof from Salih, peace be upon him, to his people, after Allah destroyed them for opposing him, rebelling against Allah, refusing to accept the truth, and turning away from guidance toward blindness. Salih said this to them after their destruction, as a reproach and rebuke while they could hear it, just as it is established in the *Sahihayn* (the two authentic collections of Bukhari and Muslim): when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gained victory over the people of Badr, he stayed there for three days. Then he ordered his mount to be saddled, and after three days, at the end of the night, he rode it and set out until he stopped at the well of Badr. He began to say: "O Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, O Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, O Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, and O so-and-so, son of so-and-so: Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? For I have found what my Lord promised me to be true." Then Umar said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you speak to bodies that have become putrid?" He said: "By the One in whose hand my soul is, you are no more able to hear what I say than they are, but they cannot answer."

In the *Sirah* (the biography of the Prophet), it is related that he, peace be upon him, said to them: "Evil is the clan of the Prophet you have been to your Prophet. You denied me while people affirmed me; you expelled me while people sheltered me; you fought me while people helped me. Evil is the clan of the Prophet you have been to your Prophet." [Ibn Hisham, *al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah*, (1/639)]

Likewise Salih, peace be upon him, said to his people: ﴿I had conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you﴾, meaning: yet you did not benefit from that, because you do not love the truth and do not follow a counsellor. Therefore He said: ﴿but you do not love those who give counsel﴾.

Some exegetes have mentioned that every prophet whose people were destroyed would go and stay in the Sacred Precinct, the Haram of Makkah. But Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih related to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by the valley of Usfan during his pilgrimage, he said: "O Abu Bakr, what valley is this?" He said: "This is the valley of Usfan." He said: "Hud and Salih, peace be upon them both, passed through it on red young she-camels whose halters were of palm fibre, their waist-wraps were cloaks, and their mantles were striped woollen garments, chanting the talbiyah, making pilgrimage to the Ancient House."

This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route; none of the compilers of the six books has narrated it. [Musnad, (1/232). Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma'* (3/220): "In its chain is Zam'ah ibn Salih, about whom there is criticism, but he has been declared reliable."]

The commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 80–81:

Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And﴾ We sent ﴿Lot﴾. Or its implied meaning is: ﴿And﴾ mention ﴿Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in?"﴾

Lot is the son of Haran ibn Azar, and he is the nephew of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), upon them both [[In manuscripts ك and أ: "عليه" (upon him).]] be peace. He had believed along with Abraham, peace be upon him, and emigrated with him to the land of Syria (al-Sham). Allah [Exalted] [[Addition from manuscript أ.]] sent him to the people of Sodom (Sadum) and the villages around it, calling them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and commanding them to do what is right and forbidding them from the sins, the prohibited acts, and the abominations that they had invented and that no one from the children of Adam or others had preceded them in. That abomination was intercourse with males. This is something the children of Adam were not accustomed to, did not become familiar with, and did not even occur to their minds, until the people of Sodom did it, may the curses of Allah be upon them.

Amr ibn Dinar said: Regarding His saying, ﴿no one among the worlds has preceded you in﴾, he said: "No male mounted another male until the people of Lot did."

Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, the Umayyad caliph, builder of the Mosque of Damascus, said: "Were it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had related to us the story of Lot, I would not have thought that a male could mount a male."

For this reason Lot, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿Do you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in? Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women﴾. That is: you turned away from women, although your Lord had created for you wives from them to satisfy you. This is extravagance and ignorance on your part, because it is placing a thing in other than its proper place. For this reason he said to them in another verse: ﴿"These are my daughters, if you must act."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 71]. So he guided them to their wives, but they excused themselves by saying that they had no desire for them: ﴿They said, "You know well that we have no right to your daughters, and you know what we want."﴾ [Hud: 79]. That is: "You know that we have no need for women and no desire for them, and you know what we want from your guests."

The exegetes mentioned that the men had become self-sufficient with one another, and likewise their women had become self-sufficient with one another as well.

Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And﴾ We sent ﴿Lot﴾. Or its implied meaning is: ﴿And﴾ mention ﴿Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in?"﴾

Meaning: they gave Lut no answer except that they resolved to expel him and those with him from among the believers from their midst. So Allah brought him out safe, and destroyed them in their land, humbled and disgraced.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾. Qatadah said: they found fault with them without any fault.

Mujahid said: ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ from the anuses of men and the anuses of women. The same was narrated from Ibn Abbas as well.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: "So We saved Lot and his family," and none of his people believed in him except his own household alone, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We found not in it except one house of Muslims﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 51:35-36], "except his wife; she did not believe in him, but rather she was upon the religion of her people, colluding with them against him and informing them of whoever came to him of his guests, through signals between her and them. For this reason, when Lot, peace be upon him, was commanded to travel by night with his family, he was commanded not to inform his wife and not to bring her out of the city."

Some of them say: "Rather, she followed them, and when the punishment came, she turned around, and what befell them befell her." The more apparent view is that she did not leave the city, and Lot did not inform her; rather, she remained with them. For this reason Allah says here: ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾, meaning: those who stayed behind. Some of them interpreted ﴿among those who remained behind﴾ as "those who perished," and this is an interpretation by necessary consequence (tafsir bil-lazim).

* *

His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ is explained by His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of baked clay, layered, marked from your Lord. And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 11:82-83]. For this reason He said: ﴿So see how was the end of the criminals﴾, meaning: look, O Muhammad, at how was the end of those who openly defied the prohibitions of Allah and denied His messengers.

Imam Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the active partner in sodomy (al-lati) is thrown from a high place and stones are pelted after him, as was done to the people of Lot.

Others among the scholars held that he is stoned whether he was married (muhsan) or not. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. Their proof is what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of al-Darawardi, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one it is done to."

Others said: "It is like adultery: if he is muhsan he is stoned, and if he is not muhsan he is flogged one hundred lashes." This is the other opinion of al-Shafi'i.

As for anal intercourse with women, it is the "lesser Lut-practice" (al-lutiyyah al-sughra), and it is forbidden by the consensus of the scholars, except for a single anomalous opinion attributed to some of the earlier generation. Numerous hadiths forbidding it have been related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the discussion of them has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: "So We saved Lot and his family," and none of his people believed in him except his own household alone, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We found not in it except one house of Muslims﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 51:35-36], "except his wife; she did not believe in him, but rather she was upon the religion of her people, colluding with them against him and informing them of whoever came to him of his guests, through signals between her and them. For this reason, when Lot, peace be upon him, was commanded to travel by night with his family, he was commanded not to inform his wife and not to bring her out of the city."

Some of them say: "Rather, she followed them, and when the punishment came, she turned around, and what befell them befell her." The more apparent view is that she did not leave the city, and Lot did not inform her; rather, she remained with them. For this reason Allah says here: ﴿except his wife; she was among those who remained behind﴾, meaning: those who stayed behind. Some of them interpreted ﴿among those who remained behind﴾ as "those who perished," and this is an interpretation by necessary consequence (tafsir bil-lazim).

* *

His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ is explained by His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of baked clay, layered, marked from your Lord. And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 11:82-83]. For this reason He said: ﴿So see how was the end of the criminals﴾, meaning: look, O Muhammad, at how was the end of those who openly defied the prohibitions of Allah and denied His messengers.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 85:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "They were of the lineage of Madyan ibn Ibrahim. Shu'ayb is the son of Mikil ibn Yashjur." He said: "His name in Syriac is Yathrun."

I say: Madyan is used to refer to the tribe and also to the town, which is near Ma'an on the Hijaz road. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community of people watering [their flocks]﴾ [Al-Qasas: 23]. They are the People of the Thicket (Ashab al-Aykah), as we will mention, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust.

﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him.﴾ This is the call of all the messengers. ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ That is: Allah has established the proofs and clear signs confirming the truth of what I have brought you. Then he admonished them regarding their dealings with people, that they should give full measure and full weight, and not deprive people of their things, meaning: do not cheat people in their wealth by taking it through deprivation (bakhs), which is the diminishing of the measure and the scale secretly and by deception, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Woe to those who give less [than due], who, when they take a measure from people, take in full, but when they give by measure or weight to them, give less. Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 1-6]. This is a severe threat and a binding warning; we ask Allah for protection from it.

Then Allah the Exalted said, reporting about Shu'ayb, who is called "the orator of the prophets" for the eloquence of his expression and the forcefulness of his admonition.

Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, forbade them from blocking the road, both the physical and the figurative, by his saying: ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening [people] and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked.﴾ That is, you threaten people with killing if they do not give you their wealth. Al-Suddi and others said: "They were ʿashshārīn (tax collectors)." It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], Mujahid and others that ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening﴾ means: you threaten the believers who come to Shu'ayb in order to follow him. The first interpretation is more apparent, because He said ﴿on every path﴾, and the paths are the roads. The second is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked﴾, that is, you wish that the way of Allah were crooked and deviated. ﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you﴾, that is, you were weak because of your small number, then you became mighty through the multitude of your numbers. So remember the favor of Allah upon you in that. ﴿And look at how was the end of the corrupters﴾, that is, of the earlier nations and the past generations, what punishment and retribution befell them because of their audacity in disobeying Allah and denying His messengers [[In A: "and denying them."]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who have not believed﴾, that is, you have [[Addition from D, K, M.]] disagreed concerning me. ﴿So be patient﴾, that is, wait, ﴿until Allah judges between us﴾, that is, decides between us, ﴿and He is the best of judges.﴾ For He will surely make the final outcome to be for the righteous, and destruction upon the disbelievers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who have not believed﴾, that is, you have [[Addition from D, K, M.]] disagreed concerning me. ﴿So be patient﴾, that is, wait, ﴿until Allah judges between us﴾, that is, decides between us, ﴿and He is the best of judges.﴾ For He will surely make the final outcome to be for the righteous, and destruction upon the disbelievers.

This is an announcement from Allah, [Exalted is He], about what the disbelievers confronted the Prophet of Allah, Shu'ayb, and those believers who were with him with, in their threat to him and those with him, to expel them from the town or to compel them to return to their creed and enter with them into what they were engaged in. This address is directed at the Messenger, while what is meant is his followers who were with him upon the creed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Even though we were averse?﴾ It means: Would you compel us to do that even though we are averse to what you call us to? For if we were to return to your creed and enter with you into what you are in, we would have greatly fabricated lies against Allah by making partners with Him as equals. This is an expression from him about his followers. ﴿It would not be for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will.﴾ This is a referral to the Will [of Allah], for He knows all things, and He has encompassed all things in knowledge. ﴿In Allah we have put our trust.﴾ That is, in our affairs, regarding what we do and what we leave undone. ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth,﴾ that is, judge between us and our people, and grant us victory over them. ﴿And You are the best of those who give decision.﴾ That is, the best of judges, for You are the Just who never oppresses at all.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the intensity of the disbelief of the people of Shu'ayb, their defiance and their obstinacy, and of the misguidance they were in, and of the opposition to the truth to which their hearts were disposed. For this reason they swore and said: ﴿Indeed, if you follow Shu'ayb, then you will surely be losers.﴾ Therefore, Allah followed this with His saying: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home prostrate corpses.﴾

Here Allah informs us that the earthquake (al-rajfah) seized them because they had threatened Shu'ayb and his companions and warned them with expulsion, as He mentioned about them in Surah Hud, where He said: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the blast seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes prostrate corpses.﴾ [Hud: 94]. The connection in this, and Allah knows best, is that when they mocked the Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb in their saying: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped or that we do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning.﴾ [Hud: 87], then the blast came and silenced them.

And Allah, exalted is He, said, reporting about them in Surah ash-Shu'ara': ﴿So they denied him, and the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 189]. That was only because they had said to him in the course of the story: ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are of the truthful.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 187]. So He informed that the punishment of the Day of the Shade afflicted them, and all of that came together upon them: the punishment of the Day of the Shade, which was a cloud that shaded them, in which there were sparks of fire, flame and great blaze; then there came upon them a cry from the sky and a severe quaking from the earth beneath them, so the souls expired, the spirits departed, and the bodies became still, ﴿and they became within their home prostrate corpses.﴾

Then Allah said: ﴿as if they had never prospered therein﴾, meaning: as if, when the retribution befell them, they had never dwelt in their homes from which they had intended to expel the Messenger and his companions.

Then He said, in response to their saying: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were the ones who were the losers.﴾

Then He said, in response to their saying: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were the ones who were the losers.﴾

Meaning: Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) turned away from them after what had befallen them of punishment, vengeance and retribution. He addressed them with rebuke and reproach, saying: "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you sincerely." That is, I have delivered to you what I was sent with, so I should not grieve over you, since you have disbelieved in what I brought. For this reason He said: "So how could I grieve over a disbelieving people?"

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the test He subjected the earlier nations to, those to whom He sent the prophets, with hardship and adversity. That is, ﴿al-ba'sa'﴾ (hardship) refers to what befalls them in their bodies of illnesses and ailments, and ﴿al-darra'﴾ (adversity) refers to what befalls them of poverty, need, and the like. ﴿So that they might humble themselves﴾ means they would call upon Allah, be humbly submissive, and supplicate to Allah, the Exalted, for the removal of what had descended upon them.

The sense of the statement is: He tested them with distress so that they would humble themselves, but they did none of what Allah wanted from them. So He turned their condition to ease in order to test them therein. For this reason He said: ﴿Then We substituted good in place of evil﴾, that is, We changed their condition from hardship to ease, from sickness and ailment to health and well-being, and from poverty to wealth, so that they would give thanks for that, but they did not.

* *

His saying ﴿until they multiplied﴾ means they increased in number and their wealth and children grew. It is said: "'afā al-shay'" when a thing increased. ﴿And they said: "Indeed, adversity and ease touched our forefathers as well, so We seized them suddenly while they were unaware."﴾ The Exalted says: He tested them with this and with that so that they would humble themselves and turn in repentance to Allah, but nothing took effect on them, neither this nor that, and they did not desist through this or through that. Rather they said: "Hardship and adversity have touched us, and then after it ease, just as it befell our forefathers in ancient times. It is merely time with its alternating phases," and they did not perceive Allah's purpose concerning them, nor did they sense Allah's testing of them in either state. This is contrary to the condition of the believers, who give thanks to Allah in ease and are patient in adversity, as is established in the Two Sahihs: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer: Allah does not decree any decree for him except that it is good for him. If ease befalls him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb ibn Sinan, may Allah be pleased with him. I did not find it in Sahih al-Bukhari with this wording.] So the believer is one who perceives what Allah has tested him with of ease and adversity. For this reason it has come in a hadith: "Affliction does not cease to befall the believer until he leaves the world purified of his sins, whereas the hypocrite is like a donkey: he does not know why his people tied him up, nor why they released him," or as he said. For this reason He follows this description with His saying: ﴿So We seized them suddenly while they were unaware﴾, that is, We seized them with punishment suddenly, by surprise from them and without their awareness, meaning We seized them unexpectedly, as in the hadith: "Sudden death is a mercy for the believer and a grip of regret for the disbeliever." [It has come from the hadiths of 'A'ishah, 'Ubayd ibn Khalid al-Sulami, and Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them.

As for the hadith of 'A'ishah: al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (1207) "Majma' al-Bahrayn," and Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (2/894), by way of Salih ibn Musa, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Musa ibn Talhah, from 'A'ishah, with the wording: "Sudden death is an alleviation for the believer and wrath for the disbeliever." In its chain is Salih ibn Musa, who is abandoned (matruk).

As for the hadith of 'Ubayd ibn Khalid: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (3/424) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (3110), by way of Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Tamim ibn Salamah or Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, from 'Ubayd ibn Khalid, with the wording: "Sudden death is a grip of regret."

As for the hadith of Anas: Ibn al-Jawzi narrated it in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (2/893), by way of Muhammad ibn Muqatil, from Ja'far ibn Harun, from Sam'an ibn al-Mahdi, from Anas, with the wording: "Sudden death is a mercy for the believers and a punishment for the disbelievers." Ibn al-Jawzi said: "Sam'an is unknown (majhul), and his hadith is munkar."]]

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said regarding His words: ﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its former people?﴾ Did We not make clear to them... [And similarly said Mujahid and as-Suddi, and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Did We not make clear] to them that, if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (at-Tabari) said in his tafsir: The Most High says: Did We not make clear to those who are made successors in the earth after the destruction of others before them, who were its people, so that they followed their course, did their deeds, and transgressed against their Lord: ﴿that if We willed, We could afflict them for their sins﴾, meaning: if We willed, We would do to them as We did to those before them. ﴿And seal their hearts﴾, meaning: and We seal their hearts, ﴿so they do not hear﴾ admonition or reminder.

I say: Likewise the Most High said: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:128]. And the Most High said: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs. Will they not then listen?﴾ [As-Sajdah 32:26]. And He said: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be no decline for you? And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth parables for you﴾ [Ibrahim 14:44-45]. And the Most High said: ﴿How many generations have We destroyed before them? Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a whisper?﴾ [Maryam 19:98], meaning: Do you see any figure of them, or hear any sound from them? And the Most High said: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established in the earth as We have not established you, and sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain, and made rivers flow beneath them? Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them other generations﴾ [Al-An'am 6:6]. And the Most High said, after mentioning the destruction of 'Ad: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen but their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you, and We gave them hearing, sight, and hearts, but their hearing, their sight, and their hearts did not avail them anything, since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them what they used to mock. And We destroyed the towns around you and varied the signs that they might return﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 46:25-27]. And the Most High said: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach a tenth of what We had given them, yet they denied My messengers, so how was My rejection?﴾ [Saba' 34:45]. And the Most High said: ﴿And those before them had denied, so how was My rejection?﴾ [Al-Mulk 67:18]. And the Most High said: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy while it was wrongdoing, so it lies fallen upon its roofs, and [many] a well abandoned and a lofty palace. Have they not traveled through the earth so that they would have hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 22:45-46]. And the Most High said: ﴿And messengers were certainly mocked before you, but those who ridiculed them were enveloped by what they used to mock﴾ [Al-An'am 6:10]. And beyond these verses that indicate the descent of His vengeance upon His enemies and the attainment of His favor by His allies; therefore He followed that with His words, and He is the most truthful of speakers and Lord of the worlds:

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 101–102:

When Allah the Exalted related to His Prophet (ﷺ) the report of the people of Nuh (Noah), Hud, Salih, Lut (Lot) and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all, and what He did in destroying the disbelievers and saving the believers, and that He established the proof against them by making the truth clear to them through evidence, via the tongues of the Messengers, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all, He said: ﴿Those are the cities; We relate to you some of their news﴾, meaning, O Muhammad, ﴿some of their news﴾, meaning some of their reports. ﴿And their Messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with evidence for the truth of what they told them, as He said: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a Messenger﴾ [Al-Isra': 15]. And He said: ﴿That is from the news of the cities which We relate to you; of them some are still standing and some are harvested. And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101, 102].

* *

His saying, ﴿So they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾: the particle "bi" (ba' sababiyyah, the causal "ba'") is causal, meaning: they were not going to believe in what the Messengers brought them, because of their denial of the truth at the very first time it reached them. This was related by Ibn 'Atiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is a sound and good interpretation, like His saying: ﴿And what will make you perceive that when it comes, they will not believe? And We will turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110, 111]. For this reason He says here: ﴿Thus Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers. And We did not find in most of them any covenant; and indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: for most of the past nations; ﴿any covenant﴾, meaning that they were defiantly disobedient, departing from obedience and compliance. The covenant which He took from them is what He created them upon and made them to be by nature (fitrah). He took from them in the loins of their fathers that He is their Lord and Sovereign, and that there is no god but Him. They affirmed this and bore witness against themselves to it, but they violated it, cast it behind their backs, and worshipped other than Allah without any proof or evidence, neither rational nor legislated, while sound natural disposition is contrary to that. The noble Messengers, from the first of them to the last, came with the prohibition of this, as is related in Sahih Muslim, where Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, I created My servants as hanif (upright in monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them." And in the two Sahihs: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian," and the hadith continues. And He, the Mighty, says in His Book: ﴿And We did not send before you any Messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 25]. And He says: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 45]. Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 101–102:

When Allah the Exalted related to His Prophet (ﷺ) the report of the people of Nuh (Noah), Hud, Salih, Lut (Lot) and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all, and what He did in destroying the disbelievers and saving the believers, and that He established the proof against them by making the truth clear to them through evidence, via the tongues of the Messengers, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all, He said: ﴿Those are the cities; We relate to you some of their news﴾, meaning, O Muhammad, ﴿some of their news﴾, meaning some of their reports. ﴿And their Messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with evidence for the truth of what they told them, as He said: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a Messenger﴾ [Al-Isra': 15]. And He said: ﴿That is from the news of the cities which We relate to you; of them some are still standing and some are harvested. And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101, 102].

* *

His saying, ﴿So they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾: the particle "bi" (ba' sababiyyah, the causal "ba'") is causal, meaning: they were not going to believe in what the Messengers brought them, because of their denial of the truth at the very first time it reached them. This was related by Ibn 'Atiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is a sound and good interpretation, like His saying: ﴿And what will make you perceive that when it comes, they will not believe? And We will turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110, 111]. For this reason He says here: ﴿Thus Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers. And We did not find in most of them any covenant; and indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: for most of the past nations; ﴿any covenant﴾, meaning that they were defiantly disobedient, departing from obedience and compliance. The covenant which He took from them is what He created them upon and made them to be by nature (fitrah). He took from them in the loins of their fathers that He is their Lord and Sovereign, and that there is no god but Him. They affirmed this and bore witness against themselves to it, but they violated it, cast it behind their backs, and worshipped other than Allah without any proof or evidence, neither rational nor legislated, while sound natural disposition is contrary to that. The noble Messengers, from the first of them to the last, came with the prohibition of this, as is related in Sahih Muslim, where Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, I created My servants as hanif (upright in monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them." And in the two Sahihs: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian," and the hadith continues. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then after them We sent﴾, that is, the messengers mentioned earlier, such as Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot and Shu'ayb, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them and upon all of Allah's prophets. ﴿Moses with Our signs﴾, that is, with Our proofs and clear evidences, to ﴿Pharaoh﴾, who was the king of Egypt in the time of Moses, ﴿and his chiefs﴾, that is, his people. ﴿But they wronged them﴾, that is, they denied and disbelieved in them out of injustice and obstinacy, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ [An-Naml: 14], that is, those who averted people from the way of Allah and denied His messengers. The meaning is: look, O Muhammad, at how We dealt with them, and We drowned them all to the last one, in full view of Moses and his people. This is more forceful as a punishment for Pharaoh and his people, and more healing for the hearts of the friends of Allah, Moses and his people, from among the believers in him.

Allah, the Exalted, relates the debate between Moses and Pharaoh, how Moses silenced him with proof, and how he displayed the clear signs in the presence of Pharaoh and his people, the Copts of Egypt. He said, ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds,"﴾ meaning: the One who sent me is the Creator of everything, its Lord and its Sovereign.

﴿It is fitting for me that I should not say about Allah except the truth.﴾ Some of them said: its meaning is, "It is worthy and proper that I should not say about Allah except the truth," that is, I am deserving of this and it is right for me.

They also said that "al-ba'" (بِ) and "'ala" (عَلَى) are interchangeable, so one says "ramaytu bil-qaws" (I shot with the bow) and "ramaytu 'ala al-qaws" (I shot at the bow), and "ja'a 'ala hal hasanah" and "ja'a bihal hasanah" (he came in a good state).

Some of the exegetes said: its meaning is, "I am eager that I should not say about Allah except the truth."

Others, from the people of Madinah, read it as ﴿It is binding upon me (haqiq 'alayya)﴾, meaning: it is obligatory and binding upon me that I should not report about Him except what is true and right, because of what I know of the might of His majesty and the greatness of His dominion.

﴿I have certainly come to you with a clear proof from your Lord﴾, that is, with a decisive argument from Allah, which He has given me as evidence of my truthfulness in what I have brought you. ﴿So send with me the Children of Israel﴾, that is, release them from your captivity and oppression, and leave them to worship their Lord and your Lord. For they are descended from a noble prophet, Israel, who is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, the friend of the Most Merciful [upon them be the blessings of the Most Merciful].

﴿He said, "If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ That is, Pharaoh said: "I will not believe you in what you have said, nor will I obey you in what you have asked. If you have a proof with you, then show it so that we may see it, if you are truthful in what you claim."
