Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 107–108:

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿a manifest serpent﴾: "The ḥayyah (serpent), the male." The same was said by al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

And in the ḥadīth of "al-Futūn" (the Trials), from the narration of Yazīd ibn Hārūn, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Zayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Ayyūb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿So he cast down his staff﴾, and it turned into a great serpent, gaping its mouth, rushing toward Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it, that it was heading straight for him, he leapt down from his throne and cried out to Mūsā to restrain it from him, and he did so.

Qatādah said: "It turned into a great serpent, like a city."

al-Suddī said regarding His saying ﴿then behold, it was a manifest serpent﴾: "al-Thuʿbān is the male of the serpents, opening its mouth, placing its lower jaw on the ground and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, then it turned toward Pharaoh to seize him. When he saw it, he was terrified of it, leapt up and defecated, which he had not done before that, and he cried out: 'O Mūsā, take it, and I will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you.' So Mūsā, peace be upon him, took it, and it returned to being a staff."

It was also narrated from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, something similar to this.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When Mūsā entered upon Pharaoh, Pharaoh said to him: "Do I know you?" He said: "Yes." He said: ﴿Did we not raise you among us as a child?﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 18]. He said: Mūsā returned to him what he had returned, and Pharaoh said: "Seize him!" But Mūsā rushed at him, ﴿and cast down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent﴾. It charged at the people, and they fled from it, and twenty-five thousand of them died; some of them killed others, and Pharaoh got up in flight until he entered the house.

Ibn Jarīr, Imam Aḥmad in his book "al-Zuhd" (Asceticism), and Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated it. In its context there is strangeness (gharābah). And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers﴾: meaning, he drew out his hand: he took it out of his garment after he had put it into it, and it came out white, gleaming, without leprosy or illness, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without harm﴾ [al-Naml: 12] [another verse].

Ibn ʿAbbās said in the ḥadīth of al-Futūn: [He took his hand out of his bosom and saw it white] ﴿without harm﴾, meaning: without leprosy. Then he returned it to his sleeve, and it returned to its original color. Likewise said Mujāhid and others.

The Chief (al-Mala') of his people, that is, the majority and the nobles of Pharaoh's people, who agreed with Pharaoh's statement about him after his fright had left him and he had settled on the throne of his kingdom, said to those around him: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer.﴾ They agreed with him and spoke as he had spoken. They consulted about his matter, what they should do concerning him, and how their scheme might be to extinguish his light, quell his word, and make manifest his lying and fabrication. They feared that he might win people over with his sorcery, in what they believed, so that this would become a cause for his prevailing over them and driving them out of their land. But what they feared, they fell into, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We showed Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts what they were wary of.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 6] So when they consulted about his affair and conspired concerning it, their opinion agreed upon what Allah the Exalted related of them in His saying, the Exalted:

"And send" (﴿وَأَرْسِلْ﴾) means: dispatch (ابْعَثْ) "into the cities" (﴿فِي الْمَدَائِنِ﴾), meaning: into the provinces and the administrative districts of your kingdom; "gatherers" (﴿حَاشِرِينَ﴾) means: those who will bring together for you the sorcerers from all the lands and assemble them.

Sorcery was widespread and prevalent in their time. Some of them believed, and some of them were led to believe, that what Musa (peace be upon him) had brought was of the same kind as what their sorcerers perform through trickery. This is a contest from the magicians against Musa (peace be upon him), in their words: ﴿Either you throw first, or we will be the first to throw﴾, meaning: before you. As He said in another verse: ﴿Or we will be the first to throw﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:65]. So Musa (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿Throw﴾, meaning: you first, before me. The wisdom in this, Allah knows best, is that people would see their performance and reflect upon it. When they were finished with their display and their tricks, the clear and manifest truth would come to them after they had sought it and awaited its arrival, so it would have a stronger effect on souls. And so it was. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them﴾, meaning: they made the sights imagine that what they did was real in external existence, when it was only mere craft and illusion. As the Exalted said: ﴿Then their ropes and their staffs seemed to him, because of their magic, to be moving. So Musa sensed fear within himself. We said: Do not fear, indeed you are the superior. And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a magician, and the magician does not succeed wherever he goes﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:66–69].

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: They threw thick ropes and tall sticks. He said: Then they came, and it seemed to him, because of their magic, that they were moving.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Fifteen thousand magicians lined up, each with his ropes and his staffs. Musa (peace be upon him) went out with his brother, leaning on his staff, until he came to the assembly, while Pharaoh was in his council with the nobles of his kingdom. Then the magicians said: ﴿O Musa, either you throw, or we will be the first to throw. He said: Rather, you throw.﴾ Then their ropes and staffs [appeared] [Ta-Ha 20:65–66]. The first thing their magic seized was the sight of Musa and the sight of Pharaoh, then the sight of the people after them. Then each man among them threw what was in his hand of ropes and staffs, and suddenly there were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, one riding over another.

Al-Suddi said: They were some thirty-odd thousand men, and each one of them had a rope and a staff. ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them﴾ means: they frightened them, that is, they caused them to flee in terror.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, who said: Pharaoh gathered seventy thousand magicians, and they threw seventy thousand ropes and seventy thousand staffs, until it seemed to him, because of their magic, that they were moving. [Note: Tafsir al-Tabari (13/28). This is one of the reports from the People of the Book, whose knowledge has no benefit.]

Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And they came with a great magic﴾.

This is a contest from the magicians against Musa (peace be upon him), in their words: ﴿Either you throw first, or we will be the first to throw﴾, meaning: before you. As He said in another verse: ﴿Or we will be the first to throw﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:65]. So Musa (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿Throw﴾, meaning: you first, before me. The wisdom in this, Allah knows best, is that people would see their performance and reflect upon it. When they were finished with their display and their tricks, the clear and manifest truth would come to them after they had sought it and awaited its arrival, so it would have a stronger effect on souls. And so it was. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them﴾, meaning: they made the sights imagine that what they did was real in external existence, when it was only mere craft and illusion. As the Exalted said: ﴿Then their ropes and their staffs seemed to him, because of their magic, to be moving. So Musa sensed fear within himself. We said: Do not fear, indeed you are the superior. And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the trickery of a magician, and the magician does not succeed wherever he goes﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:66–69].

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: They threw thick ropes and tall sticks. He said: Then they came, and it seemed to him, because of their magic, that they were moving.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Fifteen thousand magicians lined up, each with his ropes and his staffs. Musa (peace be upon him) went out with his brother, leaning on his staff, until he came to the assembly, while Pharaoh was in his council with the nobles of his kingdom. Then the magicians said: ﴿O Musa, either you throw, or we will be the first to throw. He said: Rather, you throw.﴾ Then their ropes and staffs [appeared] [Ta-Ha 20:65–66]. The first thing their magic seized was the sight of Musa and the sight of Pharaoh, then the sight of the people after them. Then each man among them threw what was in his hand of ropes and staffs, and suddenly there were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, one riding over another.

Al-Suddi said: They were some thirty-odd thousand men, and each one of them had a rope and a staff. ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them﴾ means: they frightened them, that is, they caused them to flee in terror.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, who said: Pharaoh gathered seventy thousand magicians, and they threw seventy thousand ropes and seventy thousand staffs, until it seemed to him, because of their magic, that they were moving. [Note: Tafsir al-Tabari (13/28). This is one of the reports from the People of the Book, whose knowledge has no benefit.]

Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And they came with a great magic﴾.

The Most High informs that He revealed to His servant and messenger Musa (peace be upon him), at that great station in which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood, commanding him to throw down what was in his right hand, which was his staff. ﴿And behold, it swallowed﴾, meaning it devoured, ﴿what they were falsely fabricating﴾, meaning what they were throwing down and making it appear to be real, when it was false.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It did not pass over anything of their ropes or their staffs [in A: "upon anything"] without swallowing it up. So the sorcerers knew that this was a matter from the heavens and that it was not sorcery. So they fell down prostrating and said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It kept swallowing those ropes and staffs one by one, until not a trace of what they had cast could be seen in the valley, neither little nor much. Then Musa took it, and behold, it was a staff in his hand as it had been before. The sorcerers fell down prostrating, [saying]: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ "If this were a sorcerer, we would not have been overcome."

Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza said: Allah revealed to him: "Throw your staff," so he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent with its mouth wide open, swallowing their ropes and their staffs. The sorcerers were then cast down prostrate [in M: "they were made to fall"], and they did not lift their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their respective people.

He (Exalted is He) reports what Pharaoh, may Allah curse him, threatened the sorcerers with when they believed in Musa, peace be upon him, and the deceit and scheming he displayed to the people in His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot that you have plotted in the city, to drive its people out of it﴾ [7:123]. That is: their defeat by him on this day of yours came only from your consultation and your consent to it, as in His other saying: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾ [Ta-Ha: 70]. He knows, and every person of intellect knows, that what he said is among the most false of falsehoods. When Musa, peace be upon him, came from Madyan, he called Pharaoh to Allah and displayed dazzling miracles and decisive proofs of the truth of what he brought. At that, Pharaoh sent into the cities of his kingdom and the provinces of his realm and gathered sorcerers scattered throughout all the regions of the land of Egypt, those chosen by him and the chiefs of his people, and brought them before him and promised them lavish rewards. They were among the most eager of people for this, and for display in that position and for advancement before Pharaoh. Musa, peace be upon him, did not know any of them, had not seen them, and had not met them, and Pharaoh knew this. He said this only as concealment and deception toward the rabble of his state and its ignorant ones, as He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him﴾ [43:54]. Indeed, a people who believed him when he said: ﴿I am your lord, the Most High﴾ [79:24] were among the most ignorant and misguided of Allah's creatures.

As-Suddi said in his tafsir, with his well-known chain of narration from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and others among the Companions, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot that you have plotted in the city﴾: They said: Musa, peace be upon him, met the chief of the sorcerers, and Musa said to him: "Tell me, if I defeat you, will you believe in me and testify that what I brought is true?" The sorcerer said: "I will surely bring tomorrow a magic that no magic can overcome. By Allah, if you defeat me, I will surely believe in you and testify that you are right." Pharaoh was watching them both. They said: So this is why he said what he said.

* *

His saying: ﴿so that you may drive out its people﴾ means: that you and he may unite, and you may have dominion and power, and you may expel from it the nobles and the leaders, and the authority and command will be yours. ﴿Then you will come to know﴾ means: what I will do to you.

Then he explained this threat with His saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, meaning he will cut off the right hand and the left foot of a man, or the reverse. And ﴿I will surely crucify you all﴾. In the other verse He said: ﴿on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [20:71], meaning upon the trunks.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh was the first to crucify and the first to cut off hands and feet on alternate sides.

As for the words of the sorcerers: ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾, meaning: we have become certain that we will return to Him. His punishment is more severe than your punishment, and His retribution is greater than your retribution for what you call us to and what you have compelled us to do of magic. So we will be patient today under your punishment in order to be saved from the punishment of Allah. When they said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, meaning: overwhelm us with patience upon Your religion and steadfastness in it, ﴿and let us die as Muslims﴾, meaning: following Your prophet Musa, peace be upon him. And they said to Pharaoh: ﴿So decree what you will decree. You only decree concerning this worldly life. * Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and the magic you compelled us to do. And Allah is better and more enduring. * Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. * But whoever comes to Him as a believer who has done righteous deeds, for those are the high ranks﴾ [20:72–75]. So they were sorcerers at the beginning of the day, and by its end they became righteous martyrs.

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: They were sorcerers at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at its end.

Allah, the Exalted, informs us of what Pharaoh and his chiefs conspired together, and of the harm and hatred they harboured and displayed toward Moses, peace be upon him, and his people. [[In K, M, A: "absorbed" (aḍmarūhu); in D: "absorbed" (aḍmarū). The variant is a grammatical one.]]

﴿And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said﴾, meaning to Pharaoh, ﴿"Will you leave Moses and his people?"﴾, meaning: will you let them be, so that they may spread corruption in the land, that is, corrupt the subjects of your realm and call them to worship their Lord instead of you? How astonishing! These people are concerned about Moses and his people corrupting others! Indeed, Pharaoh and his people are the ones who spread corruption, but they do not perceive it. For this reason they said: ﴿"and abandon you and your gods"﴾.

Some scholars said: the *wāw* (and) here is *ḥāliyyah* (circumstantial), meaning: "Will you let him and his people corrupt while he has abandoned your worship?" Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited this verse as: "and he has abandoned you, [so that] they worship you and your gods." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related this.

Others said: the *wāw* is *ʿāṭifah* (conjunctive), meaning: "Do not let Moses and his people do the corruption they are doing, which you have permitted them, along with their abandonment of your gods."

Some read *"ilāhatak"* (your worship), meaning your worship [of yourself]. This reading is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid.

On the first reading (*"wa-ilāhataka"*), some said: Pharaoh had a god that he worshipped. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Pharaoh had a god that he worshipped in secret. In another narration he said: he had a pendant (*jumānah*) around his neck, to which he would prostrate.

As for al-Suddi, concerning Allah's words ﴿"and abandon you and your gods"﴾, he said: his gods, as Ibn ʿAbbas claimed, were cows. Whenever they saw a beautiful cow, Pharaoh would order them to worship it. For this reason he produced for them a calf with a body (that lowed).

Pharaoh answered their request with his words: ﴿"We will kill their sons and spare their women"﴾. This was a second command of this kind, for he had already inflicted this on them before Moses' birth, out of fear of his existence. Thus it turned out contrary to what he intended and opposite to his aim. Likewise, he was treated in the same way in this action too: he only wanted to subdue and humiliate the Children of Israel, but the matter came out contrary to what he intended. Allah granted them victory over him, humiliated him, abased him, and drowned him and his armies.

When Pharaoh insisted on what he had mentioned of harming the Children of Israel, ﴿Moses said to his people: "Seek help in Allah and be patient"﴾, and promised them the good outcome, and that the land would eventually be theirs, in his words: ﴿"Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the good outcome is for the righteous."﴾ ﴿They said: "We were harmed before you came to us and after you came."﴾ That is: what we have experienced of humiliation and degradation has befallen us both before you came, O Moses, and after that. Then he admonished them about their present condition and what they would come to in the end, saying: ﴿"It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you will act."﴾ This is an exhortation to them to resolve to be grateful when blessings arrive and hardships depart.

Allah granted them victory over him, humiliated him, abased him, and drowned him and his armies.
