Then he admonished them about their present condition and what they would come to in the end, saying: ﴿"It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you will act."﴾ This is an exhortation to them to resolve to be grateful when blessings arrive and hardships depart.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning We tested them, examined them, and afflicted them ﴿with years [of drought]﴾, which are the years of hunger caused by the scarcity of crops [[In d, k, m: "al-zar'" (the crops).]] ﴿and a loss of fruits﴾. Mujahid said: "And it was less than that."

Abu Ishaq, citing Raja ibn Haywa, said: "The palm tree would bear only one fruit."

﴿So that they might take heed.* But when good came to them﴾, meaning fertility and provision, ﴿they said, "This is ours by right"﴾, meaning, "This is ours because we deserve it." ﴿And if an evil befell them﴾, meaning barrenness and famine, ﴿they would ascribe their misfortune to Moses and those with him﴾, meaning, "This is because of them and what they brought."

﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talha, citing Ibn Abbas, said regarding ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾: "Their calamities are with Allah." Allah said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

Ibn Juraij, citing Ibn Abbas, said: "[The meaning of] ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾ is: only from the side of Allah."

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh﴾, meaning We tested them, examined them, and afflicted them ﴿with years [of drought]﴾, which are the years of hunger caused by the scarcity of crops [[In d, k, m: "al-zar'" (the crops).]] ﴿and a loss of fruits﴾. Mujahid said: "And it was less than that."

Abu Ishaq, citing Raja ibn Haywa, said: "The palm tree would bear only one fruit."

﴿So that they might take heed.* But when good came to them﴾, meaning fertility and provision, ﴿they said, "This is ours by right"﴾, meaning, "This is ours because we deserve it." ﴿And if an evil befell them﴾, meaning barrenness and famine, ﴿they would ascribe their misfortune to Moses and those with him﴾, meaning, "This is because of them and what they brought."

﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talha, citing Ibn Abbas, said regarding ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾: "Their calamities are with Allah." Allah said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

Ibn Juraij, citing Ibn Abbas, said: "[The meaning of] ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾ is: only from the side of Allah."

This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, about the rebellion and arrogance of Pharaoh's people, their obstinacy toward the truth, and their persistence in falsehood, in their words: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you.﴾ They mean: whatever sign or proof you bring us and whatever argument you establish, we will reject it. We will not accept it from you, nor believe in you or in what you have brought. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾.

They differed about its meaning. From Ibn Abbas, in one narration: it is the abundance of rain that drowns and destroys crops and fruits. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also said this.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is the abundance of death. Ata also said this.

Mujahid said: ﴿al-tufan﴾ is water, and it is also plague in every case.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam ibn Mina, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The tufan is death."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the hadith of Yahya ibn Yaman, with this chain, and it is a gharib (strange) hadith.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is a command from Allah that circled around them. Then he recited: ﴿Then a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep, and it became like the reaped crops﴾ [al-Qalam: 19–20]. As for the locust, it is well known and famous, and it is lawful to eat, because it is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa about locusts, and he said: We fought seven battles with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we ate locusts.

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Two dead animals and two bloods have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen." [Musnad al-Shafi'i (1734), Musnad Ahmad (2/97), Sunan Ibn Majah (3218).] Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak, and Abu Zur'a and al-Daraqutni preferred that it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn Umar only, not to the Prophet).

Al-Baghawi (Abu al-Qasim) also narrated it from Dawud ibn Rushayd, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Tamam al-Ayli, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Umar, marfu' (traced to the Prophet), similarly. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i (4/202), through Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Dawud ibn Rashid, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Hisham al-Ayli: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam narrate from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it.
Note: here it says "Abu Tamam al-Ayli", while in Nasb al-Raya it says "Abu Hisham al-Ayli." This is an error; the correct reading is "Abu Hashim al-Ayli," who is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Ayli, weak. See Talkhis al-Habir by Ibn Hajar (1/26).]

Abu Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan al-Ahwazi, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about locusts, and he said: "They are the greatest of Allah's armies. I do not eat them, nor do I forbid them." [Sunan Abi Dawud (3913).]

He (ﷺ) left them only because he found them repellent, just as his noble soul disliked eating the dhabb (lizard), though he permitted it.

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in a juz' (part) he compiled on locusts, narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi, who said: Nasr ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not eat locusts, nor the kulwatayn (two kidneys), nor the dhabb, without forbidding them. As for the locust, it is a rijz (plague) and a punishment. As for the two kidneys, it is because they are close to urine. As for the dhabb, he said: "I fear it may be a transformation (maskh)." Then he said: gharib; I have not written it except from this route. [Also narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (18185); its chain is broken, for Ata did not hear from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jurayj is a mudallis (one who conceals defects) who narrated with 'an 'an (ambiguous wording).]

Umar ibn al-Khattab, Amir al-Mu'minin, may Allah be pleased with him, was fond of locusts and loved them. Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated, from Ibn Umar, that Umar was asked about locusts and said: "I wish we had a basket or two of them to eat." [Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' (2/933).]

Ibn Majah narrated: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send locusts to one another on platters. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3220). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/64): "This isnad is weak."]

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Numayr ibn Yazid al-Qayni, who said: My father narrated to me, from Sudayy ibn Ajlan, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Maryam daughter of Imran, peace be upon her, asked her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to feed her meat without blood, so He fed her locusts. She said: O Allah, let it live without suckling, and let it follow one another without a cry." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/166) through Baqiyya ibn al-Walid. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/39): "It contains Baqiyya, who is trustworthy but a mudallis, and Yazid al-Qayni, whom I do not know, while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."] Numayr said: "al-shiyah" means the sound.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Abu Taqi Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Yazani narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'a, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Zuhayr al-Numayri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not fight locusts, for they are Allah's greatest army." Very gharib. [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/297), and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani in al-'Azamah (1293), through Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Damdam ibn Zur'a.]

Ibn Abi Najih narrated, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts﴾, that he said: they would eat the nails of their doors and leave the wood.

Ibn Asakir narrated from the hadith of Ali ibn Zayd al-Kharaiti, from Muhammad ibn Kathir, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: I went out into the desert, and behold, there was a multitude of locusts in the sky, and behold, a man was riding on one of the locusts, wearing iron armour. Whenever he gestured with his hand like this, the locusts inclined with his hand, and he was saying: "The world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Faraj al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Hariri narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, who told us, from Amir, who said: Shurayh the judge was asked about locusts, and he said: "May Allah disfigure the locust. In it is the form of seven tyrants: its head is a horse's head, its neck is a bull's neck, its chest is a lion's chest, its wing is an eagle's wing, its two legs are a camel's legs, its tail is a serpent's tail, and its belly is a scorpion's belly."

We mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu al-Muhazzam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a pilgrimage or an 'umrah, and we came across a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with sticks while we were in ihram. We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." [Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 96.]

Ibn Majah narrated, from Harun al-Hammal, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Anas and Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that when he invoked against locusts, he would say: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihoods and our provisions. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." Jabir said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you invoke against one of the armies of Allah, asking that its offspring be cut off?" He said: "It is only a sneeze of a fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad informed me that someone who saw it told him that the fish sneezes it out. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3221). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/65): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. Ibn al-Jawzi included it among the fabricated (mawdu'at) hadiths through the route of Harun ibn Abd Allah and said: It is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); Musa ibn Muhammad, mentioned above, fabricated it."]

He said: Whoever verifies this should know that when a fish lays its eggs on the seashore, and the water recedes from them and they are exposed to the sun, they all hatch into flying locusts.

We also mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Except that they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38], the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Allah created a thousand communities: six hundred in the sea and four hundred on land, and the first of them to perish will be the locusts." [Surah al-An'am, verse 38. Muhammad ibn Isa alone narrated this hadith. Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: Amr ibn Ali said: Muhammad ibn Isa is a Basri, a companion of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, weak and munkar al-hadith (unreliable in narration). He narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, from Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning locusts.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Yazid ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated to us, Salim ibn Salim narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Jawzajani Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no plague with the sword, and no escape with the locust." A gharib hadith. [Narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (30871), and in al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti (6/439), where he marked it as weak, and al-Munawi and al-Albani affirmed this.]

As for ﴿al-qummal﴾ (the lice): from Ibn Abbas, it is the weevil that emerges from wheat. And from him, it is the dabba (small locust without wings). Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah also said this.

From al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are small black creatures.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are fleas.

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ is a plural whose singular is "qummalah," an insect resembling lice, which camels eat, as I have been informed. It is what al-A'sha meant by his saying:

A people whose children treat lice, and chains, and a solid door.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (13/56) and Lisan al-Arab, root q-m-l.]

He said: Some scholars of Arabic among the people of Basra claimed that among the Arabs, al-qummal is "al-hamnan," its singular being "hamnanah," which are small ticks above the qamqama (a large species of tick).

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Musa (peace be upon him) came to Fir'awn, he said to him: "Send the Children of Israel with me." So Allah sent upon them the tufan, which is the rain, and it poured down upon them some of it. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the rain from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. Then in that year He caused to grow for them something that had not grown before of crops, fruits and herbage, and they said: "This is what we used to wish for." Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, and it overcame the herbage. When they saw its effect on the herbage, they knew that it would leave no crops standing, so they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift the locusts from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. They trampled (the crops) and took shelter in their houses, and said: "We have become secure." So Allah sent upon them the qummal, which is the weevil that emerges from grain. A man would take out ten sacks to the millstone, and would bring back only three qafiz from them. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the qummal from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. Then, while he was sitting with Fir'awn, he heard the croaking of a frog, and he said to Fir'awn: "What do you and your people suffer from this?" He said: "And what could the trickery of this be?" Before evening came, a man would be sitting with the frogs up to his chin, and when he intended to speak, a frog would leap into his mouth. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift these frogs from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted them from them, but they did not believe. Allah then sent upon them blood. Whatever they drew from the rivers and wells, and whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be fresh blood. They complained to Fir'awn, saying: "We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink." He said: "Indeed, he has bewitched you!" They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find in our vessels nothing but water that has turned into fresh blood?" They came to him and said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

It has been narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatadah and other than them from the scholars of the early generations.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When the magicians believed, the enemy of Allah Fir'awn returned defeated and bound, but he refused except to persist in disbelief and to continue in evil. So Allah sent successive signs upon him and afflicted him with years of drought. He sent upon him the tufan, then the locusts, then the qummal, then the frogs, then the blood, as distinct signs. The tufan was water: it overflowed the face of the earth and then stood still, so they could not plough or do any work, until they were overcome with hunger. When this reached them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord by what He has promised you: if you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and surely send the Children of Israel with you." Musa prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. So Allah sent upon them the locusts, which ate the trees, so I have been told, to the extent that they would eat the iron nails of the doors, until their houses and dwellings fell. They said the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the qummal. It was mentioned to me that Musa, peace be upon him, was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. He walked to a great heap of white sand and struck it with it, and it poured out upon them as qummal, until it overwhelmed the houses and the food, and prevented them from sleep and rest. When it had exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled the houses, the food and the vessels, so that no one could uncover a garment or food without finding frogs overwhelming it. When this exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he asked his Lord and He removed them from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them blood, so the water of the family of Fir'awn turned to blood. They could not drink from a well or river, nor scoop from a vessel, without it turning into fresh blood.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Nadr informed us, Isra'il informed us, Jabir ibn Yazid informed us, from Ikrimah, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Do not kill frogs, for when they were sent upon the people of Fir'awn, a frog went and fell into an oven with fire, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah. So Allah replaced them with the coldest water he knows, and made their croaking glorification (tasbih)." It was also narrated through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, something similar.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: By "blood" is meant nosebleeds (ru'af). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, about the rebellion and arrogance of Pharaoh's people, their obstinacy toward the truth, and their persistence in falsehood, in their words: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you.﴾ They mean: whatever sign or proof you bring us and whatever argument you establish, we will reject it. We will not accept it from you, nor believe in you or in what you have brought. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾.

They differed about its meaning. From Ibn Abbas, in one narration: it is the abundance of rain that drowns and destroys crops and fruits. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also said this.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is the abundance of death. Ata also said this.

Mujahid said: ﴿al-tufan﴾ is water, and it is also plague in every case.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam ibn Mina, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The tufan is death."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the hadith of Yahya ibn Yaman, with this chain, and it is a gharib (strange) hadith.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is a command from Allah that circled around them. Then he recited: ﴿Then a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep, and it became like the reaped crops﴾ [al-Qalam: 19–20]. As for the locust, it is well known and famous, and it is lawful to eat, because it is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa about locusts, and he said: We fought seven battles with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we ate locusts.

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Two dead animals and two bloods have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen." [Musnad al-Shafi'i (1734), Musnad Ahmad (2/97), Sunan Ibn Majah (3218).] Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak, and Abu Zur'a and al-Daraqutni preferred that it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn Umar only, not to the Prophet).

Al-Baghawi (Abu al-Qasim) also narrated it from Dawud ibn Rushayd, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Tamam al-Ayli, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Umar, marfu' (traced to the Prophet), similarly. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i (4/202), through Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Dawud ibn Rashid, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Hisham al-Ayli: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam narrate from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it.
Note: here it says "Abu Tamam al-Ayli", while in Nasb al-Raya it says "Abu Hisham al-Ayli." This is an error; the correct reading is "Abu Hashim al-Ayli," who is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Ayli, weak. See Talkhis al-Habir by Ibn Hajar (1/26).]

Abu Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan al-Ahwazi, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about locusts, and he said: "They are the greatest of Allah's armies. I do not eat them, nor do I forbid them." [Sunan Abi Dawud (3913).]

He (ﷺ) left them only because he found them repellent, just as his noble soul disliked eating the dhabb (lizard), though he permitted it.

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in a juz' (part) he compiled on locusts, narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi, who said: Nasr ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not eat locusts, nor the kulwatayn (two kidneys), nor the dhabb, without forbidding them. As for the locust, it is a rijz (plague) and a punishment. As for the two kidneys, it is because they are close to urine. As for the dhabb, he said: "I fear it may be a transformation (maskh)." Then he said: gharib; I have not written it except from this route. [Also narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (18185); its chain is broken, for Ata did not hear from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jurayj is a mudallis (one who conceals defects) who narrated with 'an 'an (ambiguous wording).]

Umar ibn al-Khattab, Amir al-Mu'minin, may Allah be pleased with him, was fond of locusts and loved them. Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated, from Ibn Umar, that Umar was asked about locusts and said: "I wish we had a basket or two of them to eat." [Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' (2/933).]

Ibn Majah narrated: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send locusts to one another on platters. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3220). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/64): "This isnad is weak."]

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Numayr ibn Yazid al-Qayni, who said: My father narrated to me, from Sudayy ibn Ajlan, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Maryam daughter of Imran, peace be upon her, asked her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to feed her meat without blood, so He fed her locusts. She said: O Allah, let it live without suckling, and let it follow one another without a cry." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/166) through Baqiyya ibn al-Walid. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/39): "It contains Baqiyya, who is trustworthy but a mudallis, and Yazid al-Qayni, whom I do not know, while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."] Numayr said: "al-shiyah" means the sound.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Abu Taqi Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Yazani narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'a, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Zuhayr al-Numayri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not fight locusts, for they are Allah's greatest army." Very gharib. [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/297), and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani in al-'Azamah (1293), through Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Damdam ibn Zur'a.]

Ibn Abi Najih narrated, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts﴾, that he said: they would eat the nails of their doors and leave the wood.

Ibn Asakir narrated from the hadith of Ali ibn Zayd al-Kharaiti, from Muhammad ibn Kathir, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: I went out into the desert, and behold, there was a multitude of locusts in the sky, and behold, a man was riding on one of the locusts, wearing iron armour. Whenever he gestured with his hand like this, the locusts inclined with his hand, and he was saying: "The world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Faraj al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Hariri narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, who told us, from Amir, who said: Shurayh the judge was asked about locusts, and he said: "May Allah disfigure the locust. In it is the form of seven tyrants: its head is a horse's head, its neck is a bull's neck, its chest is a lion's chest, its wing is an eagle's wing, its two legs are a camel's legs, its tail is a serpent's tail, and its belly is a scorpion's belly."

We mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu al-Muhazzam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a pilgrimage or an 'umrah, and we came across a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with sticks while we were in ihram. We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." [Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 96.]

Ibn Majah narrated, from Harun al-Hammal, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Anas and Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that when he invoked against locusts, he would say: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihoods and our provisions. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." Jabir said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you invoke against one of the armies of Allah, asking that its offspring be cut off?" He said: "It is only a sneeze of a fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad informed me that someone who saw it told him that the fish sneezes it out. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3221). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/65): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. Ibn al-Jawzi included it among the fabricated (mawdu'at) hadiths through the route of Harun ibn Abd Allah and said: It is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); Musa ibn Muhammad, mentioned above, fabricated it."]

He said: Whoever verifies this should know that when a fish lays its eggs on the seashore, and the water recedes from them and they are exposed to the sun, they all hatch into flying locusts.

We also mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Except that they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38], the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Allah created a thousand communities: six hundred in the sea and four hundred on land, and the first of them to perish will be the locusts." [Surah al-An'am, verse 38. Muhammad ibn Isa alone narrated this hadith. Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: Amr ibn Ali said: Muhammad ibn Isa is a Basri, a companion of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, weak and munkar al-hadith (unreliable in narration). He narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, from Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning locusts.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Yazid ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated to us, Salim ibn Salim narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Jawzajani Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no plague with the sword, and no escape with the locust." A gharib hadith. [Narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (30871), and in al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti (6/439), where he marked it as weak, and al-Munawi and al-Albani affirmed this.]

As for ﴿al-qummal﴾ (the lice): from Ibn Abbas, it is the weevil that emerges from wheat. And from him, it is the dabba (small locust without wings). Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah also said this.

From al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are small black creatures.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are fleas.

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ is a plural whose singular is "qummalah," an insect resembling lice, which camels eat, as I have been informed. It is what al-A'sha meant by his saying:

A people whose children treat lice, and chains, and a solid door.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (13/56) and Lisan al-Arab, root q-m-l.]

He said: Some scholars of Arabic among the people of Basra claimed that among the Arabs, al-qummal is "al-hamnan," its singular being "hamnanah," which are small ticks above the qamqama (a large species of tick).

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Musa (peace be upon him) came to Fir'awn, he said to him: "Send the Children of Israel with me." So Allah sent upon them the tufan, which is the rain, and it poured down upon them some of it. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the rain from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. Then in that year He caused to grow for them something that had not grown before of crops, fruits and herbage, and they said: "This is what we used to wish for." Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, and it overcame the herbage. When they saw its effect on the herbage, they knew that it would leave no crops standing, so they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift the locusts from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. They trampled (the crops) and took shelter in their houses, and said: "We have become secure." So Allah sent upon them the qummal, which is the weevil that emerges from grain. A man would take out ten sacks to the millstone, and would bring back only three qafiz from them. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the qummal from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. Then, while he was sitting with Fir'awn, he heard the croaking of a frog, and he said to Fir'awn: "What do you and your people suffer from this?" He said: "And what could the trickery of this be?" Before evening came, a man would be sitting with the frogs up to his chin, and when he intended to speak, a frog would leap into his mouth. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift these frogs from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted them from them, but they did not believe. Allah then sent upon them blood. Whatever they drew from the rivers and wells, and whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be fresh blood. They complained to Fir'awn, saying: "We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink." He said: "Indeed, he has bewitched you!" They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find in our vessels nothing but water that has turned into fresh blood?" They came to him and said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

It has been narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatadah and other than them from the scholars of the early generations.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When the magicians believed, the enemy of Allah Fir'awn returned defeated and bound, but he refused except to persist in disbelief and to continue in evil. So Allah sent successive signs upon him and afflicted him with years of drought. He sent upon him the tufan, then the locusts, then the qummal, then the frogs, then the blood, as distinct signs. The tufan was water: it overflowed the face of the earth and then stood still, so they could not plough or do any work, until they were overcome with hunger. When this reached them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord by what He has promised you: if you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and surely send the Children of Israel with you." Musa prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. So Allah sent upon them the locusts, which ate the trees, so I have been told, to the extent that they would eat the iron nails of the doors, until their houses and dwellings fell. They said the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the qummal. It was mentioned to me that Musa, peace be upon him, was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. He walked to a great heap of white sand and struck it with it, and it poured out upon them as qummal, until it overwhelmed the houses and the food, and prevented them from sleep and rest. When it had exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled the houses, the food and the vessels, so that no one could uncover a garment or food without finding frogs overwhelming it. When this exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he asked his Lord and He removed them from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them blood, so the water of the family of Fir'awn turned to blood. They could not drink from a well or river, nor scoop from a vessel, without it turning into fresh blood.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Nadr informed us, Isra'il informed us, Jabir ibn Yazid informed us, from Ikrimah, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Do not kill frogs, for when they were sent upon the people of Fir'awn, a frog went and fell into an oven with fire, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah. So Allah replaced them with the coldest water he knows, and made their croaking glorification (tasbih)." It was also narrated through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, something similar.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: By "blood" is meant nosebleeds (ru'af). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, about the rebellion and arrogance of Pharaoh's people, their obstinacy toward the truth, and their persistence in falsehood, in their words: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you.﴾ They mean: whatever sign or proof you bring us and whatever argument you establish, we will reject it. We will not accept it from you, nor believe in you or in what you have brought. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾.

They differed about its meaning. From Ibn Abbas, in one narration: it is the abundance of rain that drowns and destroys crops and fruits. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also said this.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is the abundance of death. Ata also said this.

Mujahid said: ﴿al-tufan﴾ is water, and it is also plague in every case.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam ibn Mina, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The tufan is death."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the hadith of Yahya ibn Yaman, with this chain, and it is a gharib (strange) hadith.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is a command from Allah that circled around them. Then he recited: ﴿Then a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep, and it became like the reaped crops﴾ [al-Qalam: 19–20]. As for the locust, it is well known and famous, and it is lawful to eat, because it is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa about locusts, and he said: We fought seven battles with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we ate locusts.

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Two dead animals and two bloods have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen." [Musnad al-Shafi'i (1734), Musnad Ahmad (2/97), Sunan Ibn Majah (3218).] Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak, and Abu Zur'a and al-Daraqutni preferred that it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn Umar only, not to the Prophet).

Al-Baghawi (Abu al-Qasim) also narrated it from Dawud ibn Rushayd, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Tamam al-Ayli, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Umar, marfu' (traced to the Prophet), similarly. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i (4/202), through Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Dawud ibn Rashid, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Hisham al-Ayli: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam narrate from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it.
Note: here it says "Abu Tamam al-Ayli", while in Nasb al-Raya it says "Abu Hisham al-Ayli." This is an error; the correct reading is "Abu Hashim al-Ayli," who is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Ayli, weak. See Talkhis al-Habir by Ibn Hajar (1/26).]

Abu Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan al-Ahwazi, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about locusts, and he said: "They are the greatest of Allah's armies. I do not eat them, nor do I forbid them." [Sunan Abi Dawud (3913).]

He (ﷺ) left them only because he found them repellent, just as his noble soul disliked eating the dhabb (lizard), though he permitted it.

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in a juz' (part) he compiled on locusts, narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi, who said: Nasr ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not eat locusts, nor the kulwatayn (two kidneys), nor the dhabb, without forbidding them. As for the locust, it is a rijz (plague) and a punishment. As for the two kidneys, it is because they are close to urine. As for the dhabb, he said: "I fear it may be a transformation (maskh)." Then he said: gharib; I have not written it except from this route. [Also narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (18185); its chain is broken, for Ata did not hear from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jurayj is a mudallis (one who conceals defects) who narrated with 'an 'an (ambiguous wording).]

Umar ibn al-Khattab, Amir al-Mu'minin, may Allah be pleased with him, was fond of locusts and loved them. Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated, from Ibn Umar, that Umar was asked about locusts and said: "I wish we had a basket or two of them to eat." [Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' (2/933).]

Ibn Majah narrated: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send locusts to one another on platters. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3220). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/64): "This isnad is weak."]

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Numayr ibn Yazid al-Qayni, who said: My father narrated to me, from Sudayy ibn Ajlan, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Maryam daughter of Imran, peace be upon her, asked her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to feed her meat without blood, so He fed her locusts. She said: O Allah, let it live without suckling, and let it follow one another without a cry." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/166) through Baqiyya ibn al-Walid. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/39): "It contains Baqiyya, who is trustworthy but a mudallis, and Yazid al-Qayni, whom I do not know, while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."] Numayr said: "al-shiyah" means the sound.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Abu Taqi Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Yazani narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'a, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Zuhayr al-Numayri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not fight locusts, for they are Allah's greatest army." Very gharib. [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/297), and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani in al-'Azamah (1293), through Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Damdam ibn Zur'a.]

Ibn Abi Najih narrated, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts﴾, that he said: they would eat the nails of their doors and leave the wood.

Ibn Asakir narrated from the hadith of Ali ibn Zayd al-Kharaiti, from Muhammad ibn Kathir, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: I went out into the desert, and behold, there was a multitude of locusts in the sky, and behold, a man was riding on one of the locusts, wearing iron armour. Whenever he gestured with his hand like this, the locusts inclined with his hand, and he was saying: "The world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Faraj al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Hariri narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, who told us, from Amir, who said: Shurayh the judge was asked about locusts, and he said: "May Allah disfigure the locust. In it is the form of seven tyrants: its head is a horse's head, its neck is a bull's neck, its chest is a lion's chest, its wing is an eagle's wing, its two legs are a camel's legs, its tail is a serpent's tail, and its belly is a scorpion's belly."

We mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu al-Muhazzam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a pilgrimage or an 'umrah, and we came across a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with sticks while we were in ihram. We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." [Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 96.]

Ibn Majah narrated, from Harun al-Hammal, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Anas and Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that when he invoked against locusts, he would say: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihoods and our provisions. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." Jabir said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you invoke against one of the armies of Allah, asking that its offspring be cut off?" He said: "It is only a sneeze of a fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad informed me that someone who saw it told him that the fish sneezes it out. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3221). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/65): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. Ibn al-Jawzi included it among the fabricated (mawdu'at) hadiths through the route of Harun ibn Abd Allah and said: It is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); Musa ibn Muhammad, mentioned above, fabricated it."]

He said: Whoever verifies this should know that when a fish lays its eggs on the seashore, and the water recedes from them and they are exposed to the sun, they all hatch into flying locusts.

We also mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Except that they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38], the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Allah created a thousand communities: six hundred in the sea and four hundred on land, and the first of them to perish will be the locusts." [Surah al-An'am, verse 38. Muhammad ibn Isa alone narrated this hadith. Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: Amr ibn Ali said: Muhammad ibn Isa is a Basri, a companion of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, weak and munkar al-hadith (unreliable in narration). He narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, from Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning locusts.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Yazid ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated to us, Salim ibn Salim narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Jawzajani Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no plague with the sword, and no escape with the locust." A gharib hadith. [Narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (30871), and in al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti (6/439), where he marked it as weak, and al-Munawi and al-Albani affirmed this.]

As for ﴿al-qummal﴾ (the lice): from Ibn Abbas, it is the weevil that emerges from wheat. And from him, it is the dabba (small locust without wings). Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah also said this.

From al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are small black creatures.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are fleas.

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ is a plural whose singular is "qummalah," an insect resembling lice, which camels eat, as I have been informed. It is what al-A'sha meant by his saying:

A people whose children treat lice, and chains, and a solid door.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (13/56) and Lisan al-Arab, root q-m-l.]

He said: Some scholars of Arabic among the people of Basra claimed that among the Arabs, al-qummal is "al-hamnan," its singular being "hamnanah," which are small ticks above the qamqama (a large species of tick).

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Musa (peace be upon him) came to Fir'awn, he said to him: "Send the Children of Israel with me." So Allah sent upon them the tufan, which is the rain, and it poured down upon them some of it. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the rain from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. Then in that year He caused to grow for them something that had not grown before of crops, fruits and herbage, and they said: "This is what we used to wish for." Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, and it overcame the herbage. When they saw its effect on the herbage, they knew that it would leave no crops standing, so they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift the locusts from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. They trampled (the crops) and took shelter in their houses, and said: "We have become secure." So Allah sent upon them the qummal, which is the weevil that emerges from grain. A man would take out ten sacks to the millstone, and would bring back only three qafiz from them. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the qummal from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. Then, while he was sitting with Fir'awn, he heard the croaking of a frog, and he said to Fir'awn: "What do you and your people suffer from this?" He said: "And what could the trickery of this be?" Before evening came, a man would be sitting with the frogs up to his chin, and when he intended to speak, a frog would leap into his mouth. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift these frogs from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted them from them, but they did not believe. Allah then sent upon them blood. Whatever they drew from the rivers and wells, and whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be fresh blood. They complained to Fir'awn, saying: "We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink." He said: "Indeed, he has bewitched you!" They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find in our vessels nothing but water that has turned into fresh blood?" They came to him and said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

It has been narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatadah and other than them from the scholars of the early generations.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When the magicians believed, the enemy of Allah Fir'awn returned defeated and bound, but he refused except to persist in disbelief and to continue in evil. So Allah sent successive signs upon him and afflicted him with years of drought. He sent upon him the tufan, then the locusts, then the qummal, then the frogs, then the blood, as distinct signs. The tufan was water: it overflowed the face of the earth and then stood still, so they could not plough or do any work, until they were overcome with hunger. When this reached them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord by what He has promised you: if you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and surely send the Children of Israel with you." Musa prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. So Allah sent upon them the locusts, which ate the trees, so I have been told, to the extent that they would eat the iron nails of the doors, until their houses and dwellings fell. They said the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the qummal. It was mentioned to me that Musa, peace be upon him, was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. He walked to a great heap of white sand and struck it with it, and it poured out upon them as qummal, until it overwhelmed the houses and the food, and prevented them from sleep and rest. When it had exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled the houses, the food and the vessels, so that no one could uncover a garment or food without finding frogs overwhelming it. When this exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he asked his Lord and He removed them from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them blood, so the water of the family of Fir'awn turned to blood. They could not drink from a well or river, nor scoop from a vessel, without it turning into fresh blood.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Nadr informed us, Isra'il informed us, Jabir ibn Yazid informed us, from Ikrimah, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Do not kill frogs, for when they were sent upon the people of Fir'awn, a frog went and fell into an oven with fire, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah. So Allah replaced them with the coldest water he knows, and made their croaking glorification (tasbih)." It was also narrated through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, something similar.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: By "blood" is meant nosebleeds (ru'af). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, about the rebellion and arrogance of Pharaoh's people, their obstinacy toward the truth, and their persistence in falsehood, in their words: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with, we will not believe you.﴾ They mean: whatever sign or proof you bring us and whatever argument you establish, we will reject it. We will not accept it from you, nor believe in you or in what you have brought. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾.

They differed about its meaning. From Ibn Abbas, in one narration: it is the abundance of rain that drowns and destroys crops and fruits. Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also said this.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is the abundance of death. Ata also said this.

Mujahid said: ﴿al-tufan﴾ is water, and it is also plague in every case.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, al-Minhal ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam ibn Mina, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The tufan is death."

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the hadith of Yahya ibn Yaman, with this chain, and it is a gharib (strange) hadith.

Ibn Abbas said in another narration: it is a command from Allah that circled around them. Then he recited: ﴿Then a visitation from your Lord came upon it while they were asleep, and it became like the reaped crops﴾ [al-Qalam: 19–20]. As for the locust, it is well known and famous, and it is lawful to eat, because it is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Ya'fur, who said: I asked Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa about locusts, and he said: We fought seven battles with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and we ate locusts.

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Majah narrated, through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Two dead animals and two bloods have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and liver and spleen." [Musnad al-Shafi'i (1734), Musnad Ahmad (2/97), Sunan Ibn Majah (3218).] Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak, and Abu Zur'a and al-Daraqutni preferred that it is mawquf (attributed to Ibn Umar only, not to the Prophet).

Al-Baghawi (Abu al-Qasim) also narrated it from Dawud ibn Rushayd, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Tamam al-Ayli, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn Umar, marfu' (traced to the Prophet), similarly. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i (4/202), through Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Dawud ibn Rashid, from Suwayd ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Hisham al-Ayli: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam narrate from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it.
Note: here it says "Abu Tamam al-Ayli", while in Nasb al-Raya it says "Abu Hisham al-Ayli." This is an error; the correct reading is "Abu Hashim al-Ayli," who is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Ayli, weak. See Talkhis al-Habir by Ibn Hajar (1/26).]

Abu Dawud narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, from Muhammad ibn al-Zibriqan al-Ahwazi, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about locusts, and he said: "They are the greatest of Allah's armies. I do not eat them, nor do I forbid them." [Sunan Abi Dawud (3913).]

He (ﷺ) left them only because he found them repellent, just as his noble soul disliked eating the dhabb (lizard), though he permitted it.

The Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in a juz' (part) he compiled on locusts, narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Adawi, who said: Nasr ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not eat locusts, nor the kulwatayn (two kidneys), nor the dhabb, without forbidding them. As for the locust, it is a rijz (plague) and a punishment. As for the two kidneys, it is because they are close to urine. As for the dhabb, he said: "I fear it may be a transformation (maskh)." Then he said: gharib; I have not written it except from this route. [Also narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (18185); its chain is broken, for Ata did not hear from Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jurayj is a mudallis (one who conceals defects) who narrated with 'an 'an (ambiguous wording).]

Umar ibn al-Khattab, Amir al-Mu'minin, may Allah be pleased with him, was fond of locusts and loved them. Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated, from Ibn Umar, that Umar was asked about locusts and said: "I wish we had a basket or two of them to eat." [Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' (2/933).]

Ibn Majah narrated: Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Sa'd Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send locusts to one another on platters. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3220). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/64): "This isnad is weak."]

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Numayr ibn Yazid al-Qayni, who said: My father narrated to me, from Sudayy ibn Ajlan, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Maryam daughter of Imran, peace be upon her, asked her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to feed her meat without blood, so He fed her locusts. She said: O Allah, let it live without suckling, and let it follow one another without a cry." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/166) through Baqiyya ibn al-Walid. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/39): "It contains Baqiyya, who is trustworthy but a mudallis, and Yazid al-Qayni, whom I do not know, while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."] Numayr said: "al-shiyah" means the sound.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Abu Taqi Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Yazani narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Zur'a, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Zuhayr al-Numayri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not fight locusts, for they are Allah's greatest army." Very gharib. [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/297), and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani in al-'Azamah (1293), through Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Damdam ibn Zur'a.]

Ibn Abi Najih narrated, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts﴾, that he said: they would eat the nails of their doors and leave the wood.

Ibn Asakir narrated from the hadith of Ali ibn Zayd al-Kharaiti, from Muhammad ibn Kathir, who said: I heard al-Awza'i say: I went out into the desert, and behold, there was a multitude of locusts in the sky, and behold, a man was riding on one of the locusts, wearing iron armour. Whenever he gestured with his hand like this, the locusts inclined with his hand, and he was saying: "The world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood; the world is falsehood, falsehood, and whatever is in it is falsehood."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Faraj al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Hariri narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, who told us, from Amir, who said: Shurayh the judge was asked about locusts, and he said: "May Allah disfigure the locust. In it is the form of seven tyrants: its head is a horse's head, its neck is a bull's neck, its chest is a lion's chest, its wing is an eagle's wing, its two legs are a camel's legs, its tail is a serpent's tail, and its belly is a scorpion's belly."

We mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], the hadith of Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu al-Muhazzam, from Abu Hurayra, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a pilgrimage or an 'umrah, and we came across a swarm of locusts, and we began striking them with sticks while we were in ihram. We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: "There is no harm in the game of the sea." [Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 96.]

Ibn Majah narrated, from Harun al-Hammal, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ulatha, from Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Anas and Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that when he invoked against locusts, he would say: "O Allah, destroy their large ones, kill their small ones, spoil their eggs, cut off their offspring, and seize them by their mouths away from our livelihoods and our provisions. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." Jabir said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you invoke against one of the armies of Allah, asking that its offspring be cut off?" He said: "It is only a sneeze of a fish in the sea." Hashim said: Ziyad informed me that someone who saw it told him that the fish sneezes it out. [Sunan Ibn Majah (3221). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/65): "This isnad is weak because of the weakness of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim. Ibn al-Jawzi included it among the fabricated (mawdu'at) hadiths through the route of Harun ibn Abd Allah and said: It is not authentic from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); Musa ibn Muhammad, mentioned above, fabricated it."]

He said: Whoever verifies this should know that when a fish lays its eggs on the seashore, and the water recedes from them and they are exposed to the sun, they all hatch into flying locusts.

We also mentioned earlier, at His saying: ﴿Except that they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am: 38], the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Allah created a thousand communities: six hundred in the sea and four hundred on land, and the first of them to perish will be the locusts." [Surah al-An'am, verse 38. Muhammad ibn Isa alone narrated this hadith. Ibn Adi said in al-Kamil: Amr ibn Ali said: Muhammad ibn Isa is a Basri, a companion of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, weak and munkar al-hadith (unreliable in narration). He narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, from Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning locusts.]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Yazid ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated to us, Salim ibn Salim narrated to us, Abu al-Mughira al-Jawzajani Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no plague with the sword, and no escape with the locust." A gharib hadith. [Narrated by Ibn Sasri in his Amali, as in al-Kanz (30871), and in al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti (6/439), where he marked it as weak, and al-Munawi and al-Albani affirmed this.]

As for ﴿al-qummal﴾ (the lice): from Ibn Abbas, it is the weevil that emerges from wheat. And from him, it is the dabba (small locust without wings). Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah also said this.

From al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are small black creatures.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ are fleas.

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿al-qummal﴾ is a plural whose singular is "qummalah," an insect resembling lice, which camels eat, as I have been informed. It is what al-A'sha meant by his saying:

A people whose children treat lice, and chains, and a solid door.

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (13/56) and Lisan al-Arab, root q-m-l.]

He said: Some scholars of Arabic among the people of Basra claimed that among the Arabs, al-qummal is "al-hamnan," its singular being "hamnanah," which are small ticks above the qamqama (a large species of tick).

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When Musa (peace be upon him) came to Fir'awn, he said to him: "Send the Children of Israel with me." So Allah sent upon them the tufan, which is the rain, and it poured down upon them some of it. They feared that it was a punishment, so they said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the rain from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. Then in that year He caused to grow for them something that had not grown before of crops, fruits and herbage, and they said: "This is what we used to wish for." Then Allah sent upon them the locusts, and it overcame the herbage. When they saw its effect on the herbage, they knew that it would leave no crops standing, so they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift the locusts from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted the locusts from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him. They trampled (the crops) and took shelter in their houses, and said: "We have become secure." So Allah sent upon them the qummal, which is the weevil that emerges from grain. A man would take out ten sacks to the millstone, and would bring back only three qafiz from them. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift the qummal from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. Then, while he was sitting with Fir'awn, he heard the croaking of a frog, and he said to Fir'awn: "What do you and your people suffer from this?" He said: "And what could the trickery of this be?" Before evening came, a man would be sitting with the frogs up to his chin, and when he intended to speak, a frog would leap into his mouth. They said to Musa: "Pray to your Lord to lift these frogs from us, and we will believe you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted them from them, but they did not believe. Allah then sent upon them blood. Whatever they drew from the rivers and wells, and whatever was in their vessels, they found it to be fresh blood. They complained to Fir'awn, saying: "We have been afflicted with blood, and we have no drink." He said: "Indeed, he has bewitched you!" They said: "How has he bewitched us, when we find in our vessels nothing but water that has turned into fresh blood?" They came to him and said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord to lift this blood from us, and we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you." He prayed to his Lord, and He lifted it from them, but they did not believe, and they did not send the Children of Israel with him.

It has been narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatadah and other than them from the scholars of the early generations.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When the magicians believed, the enemy of Allah Fir'awn returned defeated and bound, but he refused except to persist in disbelief and to continue in evil. So Allah sent successive signs upon him and afflicted him with years of drought. He sent upon him the tufan, then the locusts, then the qummal, then the frogs, then the blood, as distinct signs. The tufan was water: it overflowed the face of the earth and then stood still, so they could not plough or do any work, until they were overcome with hunger. When this reached them, they said: "O Musa, pray to your Lord by what He has promised you: if you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you and surely send the Children of Israel with you." Musa prayed to his Lord, and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. So Allah sent upon them the locusts, which ate the trees, so I have been told, to the extent that they would eat the iron nails of the doors, until their houses and dwellings fell. They said the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the qummal. It was mentioned to me that Musa, peace be upon him, was commanded to walk to a sand dune and strike it with his staff. He walked to a great heap of white sand and struck it with it, and it poured out upon them as qummal, until it overwhelmed the houses and the food, and prevented them from sleep and rest. When it had exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he prayed to his Lord and He removed it from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them the frogs, which filled the houses, the food and the vessels, so that no one could uncover a garment or food without finding frogs overwhelming it. When this exhausted them, they said to him the same as they had said, so he asked his Lord and He removed them from them, but they did not fulfil anything of what they had said. Then Allah sent upon them blood, so the water of the family of Fir'awn turned to blood. They could not drink from a well or river, nor scoop from a vessel, without it turning into fresh blood.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Nadr informed us, Isra'il informed us, Jabir ibn Yazid informed us, from Ikrimah, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Do not kill frogs, for when they were sent upon the people of Fir'awn, a frog went and fell into an oven with fire, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah. So Allah replaced them with the coldest water he knows, and made their croaking glorification (tasbih)." It was also narrated through the route of Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, something similar.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: By "blood" is meant nosebleeds (ru'af). Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted informs that when they (the people of Pharaoh) transgressed and rebelled, despite Him testing them with the successive, repeated signs one after another, [that] He took vengeance upon them by drowning them in the sea (al-Yamm), which is the sea that He split for Musa. Musa and the Children of Israel crossed it, then Pharaoh and his hosts followed in their tracks. When they had entered fully into it, it closed over them, and they drowned to the last one of them. That was because of their denial of the signs of Allah and their heedlessness toward them.

Allah the Exalted also informed that He caused the people who had been oppressed, namely the Children of Israel, to inherit ﴿the easts and wests of the earth﴾, as He said: ﴿And We wished to confer favour upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas 28:5-6]. And He said: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and noble dwellings and bounty in which they had been delighting. Thus did We make them inherit it, another people﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:25-28].

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿the easts and wests of the earth which We had blessed﴾, that it means ash-Sham (Greater Syria).

* *

As for His saying ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience﴾, Mujahid and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: It is His saying: ﴿And We wished to confer favour upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they feared﴾.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 138–139:

He, exalted is He, tells of what the ignorant among the Children of Israel said to Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, when they crossed the sea, after they had seen the signs of Allah and His great authority that they had seen. ﴿They came upon﴾, meaning they passed by, ﴿a people devoting themselves to idols of their own﴾. Some of the mufassirun (commentators on the Qur'an) said: they were from the Kan'anites. It was also said: they were from Lakhm.

Ibn Jurayj said: They worshipped idols in the form of cows. This is why that incident stirred up in them a doubt that led to their worship of the calf afterwards. They said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant.﴾ That is, you are ignorant of the greatness and majesty of Allah, and of what must be exalted above having a partner or an equal.

﴿Indeed, these – what they are in is doomed, and worthless is what they have been doing.﴾ That is, destroyed.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir [may Allah have mercy on him] transmitted the tafsir of this verse from the narrations of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, 'Aqil, and Ma'mar, all of them from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, that they went out from Makkah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward Hunayn. He said: The disbelievers had a lote tree (sidrah) where they would devote themselves and hang their weapons. It was called "Dhat Anwat" (the one with hanging places). He said: We passed by a large green lote tree. He said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, make for us a Dhat Anwat just as they have a Dhat Anwat." He said: "You have said – by Him in whose hand my soul is – just as the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods. He said, 'Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant. Indeed, these – what they are in is doomed, and worthless is what they have been doing.'﴾" [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/81, 82).]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Dili, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before Hunayn. We passed by a lote tree, and I said: "O Prophet of Allah, make for us this one a Dhat Anwat, just as the disbelievers have a Dhat Anwat." The disbelievers used to hang their weapons on a lote tree and devote themselves around it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah is greatest! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods [He said, 'Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant']﴾. Indeed, you will follow the ways of those before you." [Al-Musnad (5/218). It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11185), through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq; and by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (2180), through the chain of Sufyan from al-Zuhri with similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from the hadith of Kathir ibn Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Awf al-Muzani, from his father, from his grandfather, in a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) form. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/21), through Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Kathir ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, from his father, from his grandfather, in marfu' form. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/24): "In its chain is Kathir ibn Abdullah, whom the majority have declared weak, though al-Tirmidhi graded his hadith as hasan."]
