Moses, peace be upon him, reminds them of Allah's blessing upon them: their deliverance from the captivity and oppression of Pharaoh, the humiliation and abasement they had been under, and what they came to attain of honour and of avenging themselves upon their enemy, witnessing him in his state of humiliation and destruction, and his drowning and annihilation. The explanation of these (verses) has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah.

Moses, peace be upon him, reminds them of Allah's blessing upon them: their deliverance from the captivity and oppression of Pharaoh, the humiliation and abasement they had been under, and what they came to attain of honour and of avenging themselves upon their enemy, witnessing him in his state of humiliation and destruction, and his drowning and annihilation. The explanation of these (verses) has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah.

Allah, exalted is He, says, bestowing favor upon the Children of Israel for the guidance they attained through His speaking to Musa, peace be upon him, and His giving him the Torah, in which were their rulings and the details of their law. He, exalted, mentions that He promised Musa thirty nights.

The exegetes said: Musa, peace be upon him, fasted them. When the appointed time was complete, he used the siwak (tooth-stick) made from the bark of a tree, so Allah, exalted is He, commanded him to complete them with ten more, making forty.[[In A: "the ten."]]

The exegetes differed about what these ten were. The majority hold that the thirty were Dhu al-Qa'dah and the ten were the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. This was said by Mujahid, Masruq and Ibn Jurayj, and it is related from Ibn 'Abbas. On this view, he completed the appointed time on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), and on it the speaking to Musa took place, and on it Allah perfected the religion for Muhammad ﷺ, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

When the appointed time was complete, Musa resolved to go to the Mount (al-Tur), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Children of Israel, We had delivered you from your enemy and made a appointment with you at the right side of the Mount﴾ [Ta-Ha: 80], and so on. At that point Musa appointed his brother Harun over the Children of Israel as successor and instructed him to act righteously and not to cause corruption. This was a reminder and an admonition; otherwise Harun, peace be upon him, is a noble prophet, honored and esteemed by Allah, possessing standing and dignity, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all the prophets.[[In D, K, M: "and he resolved."]] [[In K, A: "the prophets of Allah."]]

Ibn Kathir says, concerning Musa (peace be upon him): when he came to the appointed time of Allah, and he had been addressed directly by Allah [Most High] [[added from manuscripts K and A]], he asked Allah Most High to let him see Him, saying: ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look at You. He said: You will not see Me﴾.

The particle "lan" (لن) has been problematic here for many scholars, because it is laid down to negate permanence (التأبيد). The Mu'tazila (the rationalist school) used it as evidence for denying the vision of Allah both in this world and in the Hereafter. This is the weakest of the opinions, because the hadiths have been transmitted by tawatur (mass transmission, so that they are certain) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the believers will see Allah in the Hereafter, as we shall cite them at His words: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:22-23].

* *

And His words, reporting about the disbelievers: ﴿No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 83:15].

It has been said: the particle is for negating permanence in this world, in order to reconcile this verse with the decisive evidence for the validity of the vision in the Hereafter.

It has also been said: this statement in this context is like His statement: ﴿Vision does not encompass Him, but He encompasses vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-An'am 6:103], and this has already been discussed in Surat al-An'am [at verse 103].

In the earlier scriptures it is related that Allah Most High said to Musa, peace be upon him: "O Musa, no living being sees Me but dies, and no dry thing but crumbles." Therefore Allah Most High said: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious﴾.

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his tafsir of this verse: Ahmad ibn Suhayl al-Wasiti narrated to us, Qurrah ibn 'Isa narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from a man, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He pointed with His finger and made it crumble," and Abu Isma'il showed us with his index finger.

In this isnad there is an unnamed man who was not identified. Then he said [in A: "and said"]: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Layth, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, and said: "Like this, with His finger," and the Prophet ﷺ placed his thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, "and the mountain sank."

Thus in this narration appears "Hammad ibn Salamah, from Layth, from Anas." The well-known version is "Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas," as Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hudbah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble﴾, and said: He placed the thumb close to the tip of his little finger, and said: "the mountain sank." Humayd said to Thabit: Do you say this? Thabit raised his hand and struck Humayd's chest and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says it, and Anas says it, and I would conceal it?

Imam Ahmad related it likewise in his Musnad: Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning His words: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain [He made it crumble]﴾ [added from A], he said: He did like this, meaning he extended the tip of the little finger. Ahmad said: Mu'adh showed us, and Humayd al-Tawil said to him: What do you intend by this, Abu Muhammad? He said: Then he struck his chest a severe blow and said: Who are you, O Humayd?! And what are you, O Humayd?! It is narrated to me by Anas ibn Malik from the Prophet ﷺ, and you say: What do you intend by it?!

Likewise al-Tirmidhi related it in his tafsir of this verse, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Hakam al-Warraq, from Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh with it; and from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad [ibn Salamah] [added from A] with it [[al-Musnad 3/125; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3074; Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in al-Tawhid no. 113 via Mu'adh ibn Jabal]]. Then he said: This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Hammad.

Likewise al-Hakim related it in his Mustadrak through several routes, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with it, and said: This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it [in A: "he did not record it"] [[al-Mustadrak 2/320; Ibn Khuzaymah no. 114; Ibn al-A'rabi in his Mu'jam no. 405, via 'Affan ibn Muslim from Hammad ibn Salamah]].

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Khallal also related it, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Suwayd, from Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, and he mentioned it and said: This is a sahih isnad with no defect.

Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar related it from Shu'bah, from Thabit, from Anas, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report [This is worthless, because Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar is a liar; al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani and Abu Bakr [...] also related it in similar wording] [[added from A]] [[Ibn Mandah in al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah no. 59, via Shu'bah]].

Ibn Mardawayh traced it by two routes, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas as a marfu' report, in similar wording [[Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil 1/350 via Ayyub ibn Khawt from Qatadah from Anas, marfu'; Ayyub ibn Khawt is abandoned in hadith]]. And Ibn Mardawayh traced it by a route from Ibn al-Baylamani, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, as a marfu' report, and this too is not sound.

al-Suddi said, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning Allah's words: ﴿When His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾: "Only the measure of the little finger manifested of Him." ﴿He made it crumble﴾: "into dust." ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious﴾: "he was struck senseless." Ibn Jarir related it.

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious﴾: "dead."

Sufyan al-Thawri said: the mountain sank into the earth until it fell into the sea, and it keeps going along with it.

Sunayd said, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali: ﴿He made it crumble﴾: it was uprooted, entered beneath the earth, and does not appear until the Day of Resurrection.

It has come in some reports that it sank into the earth, and it keeps sinking in it until the Day of Resurrection; Ibn Mardawayh related it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya Abu Ghassan al-Kinani narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Jald ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When Allah manifested Himself to the mountains [in A: "to the mountain"], six mountains flew away out of His greatness; three fell in Madinah and three in Makkah. In Madinah: Uhud, Warqan, and Radwa. And in Makkah fell: Hira', Thabir, and Thawr."

This is a gharib (singular) hadith, rather munkar (rejected) [[Ibn al-A'rabi, Mu'jam 2/166; al-Muhamili, Amali 1/172/1; al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, Tarikh Baghdad 10/441, all via 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Imran from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Abd Allah. Al-Khatib said: "This hadith is very gharib; I have written it only with this isnad." Ibn al-Jawzi included it in al-Mawdu'at 1/120 and said: "Ibn Hibban said: fabricated; 'Abd al-'Aziz is abandoned, narrating rejected reports from well-known narrators."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Thalj, Al-Haytham ibn Kharijah narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Husayn ibn 'Allaq narrated to us, from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, who said: The mountains, before Allah manifested Himself to Musa on Mount Tur, were solid and smooth; when Allah manifested Himself to Musa on Tur, it was [in A: "became"] crumbled, the mountains split, and there came to be cracks and caves.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious﴾. That is because when the veil was lifted and the mountain saw the light, it became like a crumbled heap of dust. Some of them said: ﴿He made it crumble﴾ means: He pulverized it.

Mujahid said concerning His words: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me﴾ [al-A'raf 7:143]: "for it is greater than you and stronger in creation." ﴿When His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾: he looked at the mountain, unable to hold himself; the mountain came and crumbled from its first part, and Musa saw what the mountain was doing, and fell down senseless.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿He made it crumble﴾: Allah looked at the mountain, and it became a desert, dust.

Some readers recited it with this reading, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and a marfu' hadith has been reported about it, related by Ibn Mardawayh.

What is known is that "al-sa'q" (الصعق) here means fainting (الغشي), as Ibn 'Abbas and others explained, not as Qatadah explained it, death; although that is correct in the language, as in His words: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾ [al-Zumar 39:68]. For there is an indication there that points to death, just as here there is an indication that points to fainting, and it is His words: ﴿Then when he recovered﴾, and recovery only comes from a faint.

﴿He said: Glory be to You﴾: in glorification, exaltation, and reverence, that anyone in this world should see Him and not die.

* *

His words: ﴿I have turned to You in repentance﴾. Mujahid said: [that is,] "that I ask You for the vision."

﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: "among the Children of Israel." Ibn Jarir chose this. In another report from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾: that no one sees You. Likewise Abu al-'Aliyah said: There were believers before him, but he meant: "I am the first to believe in You, that no one of Your creation will see You until the Day of Resurrection."

This is a good opinion with a valid line of argument. Muhammad ibn Jarir mentioned here in his tafsir a lengthy report full of strange and wondrous things, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar [may Allah have mercy on him] [[added from A]], and it seems he received it from the Israiliyyat (narrations from Israelite sources) [[see Tafsir al-Tabari 13/91]]. And Allah [Most High] [[added from M]] knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious﴾. Concerning it, there are reports from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. As for the hadith of Abu Sa'id, al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih at this point, saying:

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man from the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ, his face having been slapped, and said: "O Muhammad, a man from your Companions, from the Ansar, slapped my face." He said: "Call him." They called him. He said: "Why did you slap his face?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I passed by a Jew and heard him say: By Him who chose Musa above mankind." I said: "And above Muhammad?" Anger seized me, so I slapped him. He said: "Do not make me superior among the Prophets, for people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to recover, and behold, Musa will be holding one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he recovered before me, or was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Tur."

Al-Bukhari related it in many places in his Sahih, and Muslim in the chapter on the stories of the Prophets in his Sahih, and Abu Dawud in the Book of the Sunnah in his Sunan, by various routes, from 'Amr ibn Yahya ibn 'Umarah ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Mazini al-Ansari al-Madani, from his father, from Abu Sa'id Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Khudri, with it [[Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 4638, 2412, 6917, 3398, 7427, 6518; Sahih Muslim no. 2374; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4668]].

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad:

Abu Kamil narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Two men reviled each other: a man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews. The Muslim said: "By He who chose Muhammad above the worlds." The Jew said: "By He who chose Musa above the worlds." The Muslim became angry at the Jew and slapped him. The Jew came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what had happened. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the Muslim, and he admitted to it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not make me superior to Musa, for the people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness, and I will find Musa holding onto the side of the Throne. So I do not know whether he was among those who swooned and regained consciousness before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepted." Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same chain.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated that the one who slapped the Jew in this incident was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. [Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (6/443): "As for the claim that the slapper in this story was al-Siddiq, it is explicitly stated in what Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah recorded in his Jami' and Ibn Abi al-Dunya recorded in Kitab al-Ba'th through his chain, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata' and Ibn Jad'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: there was a dispute between a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and a man from the Jews over something. Amr ibn Dinar said: it was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq."] However, it was previously established in the Two Sahihs that he was a man from the Ansar, and this is more authentic and more explicit. And Allah knows best.

The discussion regarding his saying, peace be upon him, "Do not make me superior to Musa," is like the discussion regarding his saying: "Do not prefer me over the prophets, nor over Yunus ibn Matta." It was said: it is from the category of humility. It was said: it was before he knew of that. It was said: he forbade that they be preferred among themselves in a manner of anger and partisanship. It was said: he forbade it in the manner of speaking by mere opinion and whim. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for his saying, "for the people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection": the apparent meaning is that this swooning will occur in the open plains of the Resurrection, when a matter happens from which people swoon. Allah knows best about it. It may also be when the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, comes to decide the judgment, and the Sovereign, the Judge, manifests Himself to the creation, just as Musa swooned from the manifestation of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This is why he, peace be upon him, said: "So I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me, or whether he was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Sinai?"

Al-Qadi 'Iyad narrated at the beginning of his book "al-Shifa'," with his chain, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq: Qatadah narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Yahya ibn Wassab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When Allah manifested Himself to Musa, peace be upon him, he could see an ant on the rock in a dark night from a distance of ten farsakh." [Al-Shifa' (1/165).] Then he said: "It is not far, in light of this, that a prophet be specially granted what we have mentioned in this category, after the Night Journey and the favor of what he saw of the greatest signs of his Lord."

That is the end of what he said. It seems he deemed this hadith authentic, but its authenticity is questionable, and the narrators of its chain include unknown, unidentified persons. Such a report is only accepted when transmitted by a trustworthy, precise narrator from a similar one, until it reaches its end. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 144–145:

He, exalted is He, mentions that He addressed Musa (peace be upon him) [addition from A.], saying that He had chosen him above the people of his time with His messages and with His speech [in K, M: "and His speech"]. There is no doubt that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the master of the children of Adam among the first and the last. For this reason, Allah singled him out by making him the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, whose law continues until the Hour is established, and his followers are more numerous than the followers of all the other prophets and messengers. After him, in nobility and excellence, comes Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, then Musa [ibn 'Imran] [addition from M, A.], the one who spoke with the Most Merciful (Kalim al-Rahman), peace be upon him. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said to him: ﴿So take what I have given you﴾, meaning: of the speech [and revelation] [addition from M.] and the intimate communication, ﴿and be among the grateful﴾, meaning: for that, and do not seek what you have no capacity for.

Then Allah, exalted is He, informed that He wrote for him on the Tablets, of everything, an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything. It was said: the Tablets were of jewel, and that Allah, exalted is He, wrote for him in them admonitions and detailed rulings clarifying the lawful and the unlawful. These Tablets contained the Torah, concerning which Allah [exalted is He] [addition from K, M, A.] said: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations, as insights for the people﴾ [al-Qasas: 43].

It was also said: the Tablets were given to Musa before the Torah, but Allah knows best. In every case, they were like a compensation for him for what he asked of the vision and was refused, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So take it with strength﴾, meaning: with resolve to obey, ﴿and enjoin your people to take the best of it﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: Abu Sa'd narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa (peace be upon him) was commanded to take with the strictest of what he commanded his people.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: you will see the outcome of those who opposed My command and departed from My obedience, how they come to destruction, ruin and perdition.

Ibn Jarir said: He only said ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾ as one says to someone he is addressing: "Tomorrow I will show you where the state of one who opposed my command will end," in the manner of threat and warning to whoever disobeys him and opposes his command.

He then transmitted this meaning from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri.

It was also said: its meaning is ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., from the people of Syria, and I will give it to you. And it was said: it refers to the dwellings of the people of Pharaoh. The first view is more preferable, and Allah knows best, because this was after Musa and his people had separated from the land of Egypt, and it is an address to the Children of Israel before they entered the wilderness (al-Tih), and Allah knows best.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on the earth without right﴾. That is, I will prevent the hearts of the arrogant from comprehending the proofs and evidences of My greatness, My law, and My rulings, so that they do not obey Me. As the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. And the Exalted said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5].

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "Knowledge is not attained by the shy or the arrogant."

Another said: "Whoever does not endure the humiliation of learning for an hour will remain in the humiliation of ignorance forever."

I say: This does not necessarily follow, because Ibn 'Uyaynah meant that this applies universally to every nation, and there is no difference between one person and another in this matter. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96-97].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way﴾. That is, even if the way of right guidance becomes clear to them, that is, the path of salvation, they will not follow it. And if the path of destruction and misguidance becomes clear to them, they will take it as their way.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have failed﴾. That is, whoever among them did that and persisted in it until death, his deeds have failed.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about the misguidance of those among the Children of Israel who went astray by worshipping the calf. As-Samiri (the Samaritan) fashioned it for them from the ornaments of the Copts, which they had borrowed from them. He shaped for them a calf from it, then cast into it a handful of dust that he had taken from the footprint of Jibril's horse (peace be upon him). It became a calf with a body that had a lowing sound. "Khuwar" (the lowing) is the sound of cattle.

This happened among them after Musa (peace be upon him) [[addition from A.]] had gone to the appointed time with his Lord, exalted is He. Allah informed him of this while he was on the Mount, as He says, reporting about His noble Self: ﴿He said: "Indeed We have tested your people after you, and As-Samiri has led them astray."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 85]

The scholars of tafsir have differed regarding this calf: did it become flesh and blood with a lowing sound, or did it remain of gold, except that air entered it so that it made a sound like a cow? There are two opinions on this, and Allah knows best. It is said that when the calf made a sound for them, they danced around it and were seduced by it, and ﴿they said: "This is your god and the god of Musa, but he has forgotten."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88] Then Allah said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them any speech, and does not possess for them any harm or benefit?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 89]

In this noble verse, He says: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them nor guide them to a way?﴾ He rebukes them for their misguidance through the calf and their heedlessness of the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Lord and Sovereign of everything, that they worshipped alongside Him a calf with a body and a lowing sound, which does not speak to them nor guides them to any good. Rather, the blindness of ignorance and misguidance covered the eyes of their insight [[in M: "their eyes"]], as has preceded in the report of Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud from Abu ad-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your love for a thing makes you blind and deaf."

[[Al-Musnad (5/194) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5130); Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (6/450) as a mawquf (companion's statement). Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in his answers concerning the hadiths of al-Masabih: "The mawquf is more likely."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when they were overcome with regret﴾, meaning: they repented for what they had done, ﴿and saw that they had indeed gone astray, they said: "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ Some of them read: "If You do not have mercy upon us," with the letter ta' at the beginning, "Rabbana" as a vocative, and "wataghfir lana" (and forgive us). ﴿We will surely be among the losers﴾, meaning: among the ruined. This is their acknowledgment of their sin and their turning to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 150–151:

He, exalted is He, informs that Musa, peace be upon him, returned to his people from his intimate conversation with his Lord, angry and grieved (ghadban asif).

Abu al-Darda' said: "Al-asaf" is the most intense anger.

﴿He said: "Evil is what you did as my successors after me."﴾ Meaning: how evil is what you did in worshipping the calf after I left and left you behind.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Did you hasten the command of your Lord?﴾ Meaning: you hastened my coming to you, though it was decreed by Allah, exalted is He.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself.﴾ It was said: the tablets were of emerald. It was also said: of ruby. And it was said: of crystal. In this there is an indication of what has come in the hadith: "Hearsay is not like seeing with one's own eyes" [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/271) from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hearsay is not like seeing with one's own eyes. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed Musa of what his people had done with the calf, so he did not throw the tablets; but when he saw what they had done, he threw the tablets and they broke."]].

Then, the apparent context indicates that he threw the tablets only out of anger at his people, and this is the view of the majority of scholars, earlier and later. Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah a strange view on this, whose chain does not validly reach Qatadah's report; Ibn Atiyyah and many other scholars rejected it, and it deserves rejection. It seems Qatadah received it from some of the People of the Book, among whom are liars, forgers, fabricators and heretics.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself.﴾ Out of fear that he might have been negligent in forbidding them, as He said in another verse: ﴿He said: "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Have you then disobeyed my order?" He said: "O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.'"﴾ [Ta-Ha 92–94]. And here He said: ﴿"O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me with the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is: do not drive me in their direction, and do not mix me with them. He said "son of my mother" so that it would be more tender and effective with him; otherwise he was his full brother, of the same father and mother. When Musa, peace be upon him, became certain of Harun's innocence, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Harun had already said to them before: "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."﴾ [Ta-Ha 90], then Musa said: ﴿"My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa. The one who sees is not like the one who is informed. His Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, informed him that his people had been tested after him, but he did not throw the tablets; when he saw them and witnessed them, he threw the tablets." [[Narrated also by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/380) through Abu Bishr, with the same chain. He said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." In al-Dhahabi's Talkhis: "Two trustworthy narrators heard it from Abu Bishr."]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 150–151:

He, exalted is He, informs that Musa, peace be upon him, returned to his people from his intimate conversation with his Lord, angry and grieved (ghadban asif).

Abu al-Darda' said: "Al-asaf" is the most intense anger.

﴿He said: "Evil is what you did as my successors after me."﴾ Meaning: how evil is what you did in worshipping the calf after I left and left you behind.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Did you hasten the command of your Lord?﴾ Meaning: you hastened my coming to you, though it was decreed by Allah, exalted is He.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself.﴾ It was said: the tablets were of emerald. It was also said: of ruby. And it was said: of crystal. In this there is an indication of what has come in the hadith: "Hearsay is not like seeing with one's own eyes" [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/271) from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hearsay is not like seeing with one's own eyes. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed Musa of what his people had done with the calf, so he did not throw the tablets; but when he saw what they had done, he threw the tablets and they broke."]].

Then, the apparent context indicates that he threw the tablets only out of anger at his people, and this is the view of the majority of scholars, earlier and later. Ibn Jarir narrated from Qatadah a strange view on this, whose chain does not validly reach Qatadah's report; Ibn Atiyyah and many other scholars rejected it, and it deserves rejection. It seems Qatadah received it from some of the People of the Book, among whom are liars, forgers, fabricators and heretics.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And he seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself.﴾ Out of fear that he might have been negligent in forbidding them, as He said in another verse: ﴿He said: "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Have you then disobeyed my order?" He said: "O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.'"﴾ [Ta-Ha 92–94]. And here He said: ﴿"O son of my mother, indeed the people oppressed me and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me with the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is: do not drive me in their direction, and do not mix me with them. He said "son of my mother" so that it would be more tender and effective with him; otherwise he was his full brother, of the same father and mother. When Musa, peace be upon him, became certain of Harun's innocence, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Harun had already said to them before: "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."﴾ [Ta-Ha 90], then Musa said: ﴿"My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa. The one who sees is not like the one who is informed. His Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, informed him that his people had been tested after him, but he did not throw the tablets; when he saw them and witnessed them, he threw the tablets." [[Narrated also by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/380) through Abu Bishr, with the same chain. He said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." In al-Dhahabi's Talkhis: "Two trustworthy narrators heard it from Abu Bishr."]]

The anger that befell the Children of Israel over the worship of the calf was that God, exalted is He, did not accept their repentance until some of them killed others, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves; that is better for you in the sight of your Creator. Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:54]

As for the humiliation, it followed them as abasement and disgrace in the life of this world. His words, ﴿And thus We recompense the fabricators﴾, apply to everyone who invents an innovation (bid'ah, a newly invented practice in religion). The humiliation of innovation and opposition to the Messenger is attached from the heart to the shoulders. As al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The humiliation of innovation is upon their shoulders, even if mules amble with them and horses clatter with them."

Likewise, Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani narrated from Abu Qilabah al-Jarmi that he recited this verse, ﴿And thus We recompense the fabricators﴾, and said: "By God, it applies to every fabricator until the Day of Resurrection."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Every possessor of an innovation is humiliated."

Then God, exalted is He, reminded His servants and guided them to the fact that He accepts the repentance of His servants for any sin whatsoever, even if it is disbelief (kufr), polytheism (shirk), hypocrisy (nifaq), or schism (shiqaq). For this reason He followed this story with His words: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ That is, O Muhammad, O Messenger of mercy and Prophet of light, ﴿after them﴾, meaning after that deed, ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Aban narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Azrah, from al-Hasan al-'Urafi, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), that he was asked about that, meaning about a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her. He recited this verse: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Abdullah recited it ten times, and he neither commanded them with it nor forbade them from it.

The anger that befell the Children of Israel over the worship of the calf was that God, exalted is He, did not accept their repentance until some of them killed others, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves; that is better for you in the sight of your Creator. Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:54]

As for the humiliation, it followed them as abasement and disgrace in the life of this world. His words, ﴿And thus We recompense the fabricators﴾, apply to everyone who invents an innovation (bid'ah, a newly invented practice in religion). The humiliation of innovation and opposition to the Messenger is attached from the heart to the shoulders. As al-Hasan al-Basri said: "The humiliation of innovation is upon their shoulders, even if mules amble with them and horses clatter with them."

Likewise, Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani narrated from Abu Qilabah al-Jarmi that he recited this verse, ﴿And thus We recompense the fabricators﴾, and said: "By God, it applies to every fabricator until the Day of Resurrection."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Every possessor of an innovation is humiliated."

Then God, exalted is He, reminded His servants and guided them to the fact that He accepts the repentance of His servants for any sin whatsoever, even if it is disbelief (kufr), polytheism (shirk), hypocrisy (nifaq), or schism (shiqaq). For this reason He followed this story with His words: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ That is, O Muhammad, O Messenger of mercy and Prophet of light, ﴿after them﴾, meaning after that deed, ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Aban narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Azrah, from al-Hasan al-'Urafi, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), that he was asked about that, meaning about a man who commits adultery with a woman and then marries her. He recited this verse: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Abdullah recited it ten times, and he neither commanded them with it nor forbade them from it.

He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the anger subsided﴾, meaning it calmed, ﴿from Moses﴾, meaning his anger at his people, ﴿he picked up the tablets﴾, meaning those he had thrown down out of intense anger at their worship of the calf, out of zeal for God and anger on His behalf. ﴿And in their inscription was guidance and mercy﴾.

Many of the exegetes say that when he threw them, they broke, and that he then gathered them up afterwards. For this reason some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "He found in them guidance and mercy." As for the detailed text, it is gone. They claimed that its fragments (rudaḍ) remained in the treasuries of the kings of the Children of Israel until the Islamic state, but God knows best whether this is correct. The conclusive proof that they broke when he threw them, though they were made of the essence of Paradise, is that God, may He be exalted, informed us that when he took them after throwing them, he found in them guidance and mercy.

﴿For those who fear their Lord﴾. He made the fear (al-rahba) imply the meaning of humility (al-khuḍū'), and for this reason it takes the preposition lam (lil-) [i.e., it is followed by lam, not by a direct object].

Qatadah said concerning God's words ﴿he picked up the tablets﴾: He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community, the best community brought forth for mankind, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, so make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community who are the last ones (al-ākhirūn) – meaning last in creation – and the first (al-sābiqūn) to enter Paradise. My Lord, make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community whose gospels are in their chests; they recite their scripture from memory, whereas those before them used to read their scripture by looking at it, and when they set it down they retained nothing of it and did not know it." Qatadah said: "God gave that community a capacity for memorization that He had given to no other nation." He said: "My Lord, make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community who believe in the first Book and the last Book, and who fight the remnants of error until they fight the one-eyed liar (al-A'war al-Kadhdhab). Make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community whose charities they eat within their bellies and are rewarded for them. Those before them among the nations, when someone gave a charity and it was accepted from him, God sent a fire upon it and it consumed it; and if it was rejected from him, it was left, and the beasts and birds ate it. God has taken your charities from your rich to your poor." He said: "My Lord, make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community that, when one of them intends a good deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him; and if he does it, ten times its like is written for him up to seven hundred fold. My Lord, make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community that, when one of them intends an evil deed, it is not written against him until he does it; and if he does it, one evil deed is written against him. Make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community who are those who respond and those to whom response is given. Make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad." He said: "My Lord, I find in the tablets a community who are the intercessors and those for whom intercession is made. Make them my community." He said: "That is the community of Aḥmad."

Qatadah said: It was related to us that the prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, threw down the tablets and said: "O God, make me of the community of Aḥmad."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/124).]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse: God had commanded Musa to choose seventy men from his people, and he chose seventy men and went out with them to supplicate their Lord. Among what they asked God was: "O Allah, give us what You have not given anyone before us, and do not give it to anyone after us." God disliked this request, so the earthquake (al-Rajfah) seized them. Musa said: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Al-Suddi said: God commanded Musa to come to Him with some men of the Children of Israel, who would apologise to Him for the worship of the calf, and He set them an appointed time. Musa chose seventy men from his people by his own eye, then went with them so that they might apologise. When they reached that place they said: "We will not believe you, O Musa, until we see Allah openly, for you have spoken to Him, so show Him to us." Then the thunderbolt (al-Sa'iqah) seized them and they died. Musa stood weeping and supplicating to Allah, saying: "My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I meet them, after You have destroyed their best?" ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Musa chose from the Children of Israel seventy men, the best of the best, and said: "Go to Allah and repent to Him for what you have done, and ask Him to accept the repentance of those you have left behind among your people. Fast, purify yourselves, and purify your garments." He went out with them to Mount Sinai, at the appointed time his Lord had set for him, and he would not come to Him except by His permission and knowledge. The seventy said to him, as it is related to me, when they had done what he commanded them and set out with him to meet their Lord: "Ask for us, so that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." When Musa approached the mountain, a column of cloud descended upon it until it covered the whole mountain. Musa drew near and entered into it, and he said to the people: "Come near." Whenever Allah spoke to Musa, a bright light would fall upon Musa's forehead, such that no son of Adam could look at it, so a veil was placed between them. The people drew near until, when they entered, they fell prostrate and heard Him speaking to Musa, commanding and forbidding him: "Do this, and do not do that." When the matter was finished, the cloud withdrew from Musa and he came to them. They said to Musa: "We will not believe you until we see Allah openly." Then the earthquake seized them, which is the thunderbolt, and their souls were separated, and they all died. Musa stood pleading with his Lord, supplicating and imploring Him, saying: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾ "They have acted foolishly. Will You destroy those behind me from the Children of Israel?"

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, from Umarah ibn Abd al-Sululi, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Musa, Harun, Shabbar and Shabir set out and went to the foot of a mountain. Harun lay down on a couch and Allah took his soul (tawaffahu). When Musa returned to the Children of Israel they said to him: "Where is Harun?" He said: "Allah took his soul." They said: "You killed him, out of envy for his character and gentleness," or words similar to that. He said: "Then choose whomever you wish." So they chose seventy men. He said: "That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men﴾." When they reached Harun they said: "O Harun, who killed you?" He said: "No one killed me, but Allah took my soul." They said: "O Musa, you will not be disobeyed after today." Then the earthquake seized them. Musa, peace be upon him, began turning right and left and said: "O my Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will." He said: Then Allah revived them and made them all prophets.

This is a very strange report, and I do not know this Umarah ibn Abd (in some copies: Ubayd) al-Salum... [the original text here reads: "وَعِمَارَةُ بْنُ عَبْدٍ هَذَا لَا أَعْرِفُهُ"]. That is: I do not know this Umarah ibn Abd. Shu'bah narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from a man of the Banu Salul, from Ali, and he mentioned it.
[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/142). Its chain includes Umarah ibn Abd al-Sululi. Al-Dhahabi said in Mizan al-I'tidal: "Umarah ibn Abd, from Ali, is unknown and is not to be used as evidence; Abu Hatim said so. Ahmad said: he is of sound narration; only Abu Ishaq narrates from him."]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: The earthquake seized them only because they had not separated themselves from their people in their worship of the calf, nor had they forbidden them. This view is supported by Musa's words: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾

* *

As for His saying ﴿It is only Your trial﴾, meaning Your testing, Your examination, and Your probation. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Aliyah, Rabi' ibn Anas, and many others among the scholars of the early and later generations. It has no meaning other than this; the meaning is: the matter is only Your matter, the judgement belongs only to You. Whatever You will, comes to be. You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. None can guide the one You have led astray, and none can lead astray the one You have guided. None can give what You have withheld, and none can withhold what You have given. Sovereignty belongs entirely to You, and judgement belongs entirely to You. Creation and command are Yours.

* *

As for His saying ﴿You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers﴾: al-Ghafr (forgiveness) is concealment and not holding the sin to account. When mercy is joined with forgiveness, what is intended is that He does not let him fall into the like of it in the future. ﴿And You are the best of forgivers﴾ means: none forgives sins except You. ﴿And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter﴾: the first part of the supplication is the averting of what is feared, and this part is the attainment of what is sought. ﴿Ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter﴾ means: make it obligatory for us and establish for us good in both. This has already been explained in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿Indeed we have turned back to You﴾ means: we repented, returned, and turned in penitence to You. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Taymi, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and others. It is also the linguistic meaning.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, from my father, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Nujayy, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Jews were only named (Yahud) because they said: ﴿Indeed we have turned back to You﴾.
Jabir (he is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi) is weak.

Allah, responding to Musa in his statement ﴿It is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will﴾, said, the verse: ﴿My punishment I inflict upon whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things; so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me﴾. That is: I do what I will, and I judge what I desire, and to Me belong wisdom and justice in all of that. Glory be to Him; there is no god but He.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, it is a verse of great comprehensiveness and generality, like His saying, reporting about the bearers of the Throne and those around it, that they say: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Abdullah al-Jushami, from Jundub ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A Bedouin came, made his mount kneel, tied it, and then prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he went to his mount, untied its rope, mounted it, and then called out: "O Allah, have mercy on me and on Muhammad, and do not share our mercy with anyone." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you say this is more astray, or his camel? Did you not hear what he said?" They said: "Yes." He said: "He has restricted a wide mercy. Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, created one hundred mercies, and He sent down one mercy by which creation shows compassion to one another, its jinn, its humans, and its animals, and He kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. Do you say he is more astray, or his camel?"

It was narrated by Abu Dawud from Ali ibn Nasr, from Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, with this chain.
[Al-Musnad (4/312) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4885.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Uthman, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, has one hundred mercies, of which one mercy is that by which creatures show mercy to one another, and by which wild animals show tenderness to their young; and He delayed ninety-nine until the Day of Resurrection."

Muslim alone transmitted it, narrating it through the hadith of Sulayman, who is Ibn Tarkhan, and Dawud ibn Abi Hind, both from Abu Uthman, whose name is Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull, from Salman al-Farisi, from the Prophet ﷺ, with this wording.
[Al-Musnad (5/439) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2753.]

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has one hundred mercies; with Him are ninety-nine, and He placed with you one, by which you show mercy to one another, between the jinn and mankind and between creation. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will gather it to Himself." Ahmad alone transmitted it through this route.
[Al-Musnad (3/55).]

Ahmad also said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has one hundred mercies; He distributed one part of them among creation, and by it people, wild beasts, and birds show mercy to one another."

Ibn Majah transmitted it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with this wording.
[Al-Musnad (3/55) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4294.]

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Sa'd Abu Ghaylan al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the wicked in his religion will enter Paradise, and the fool in his livelihood. By Him in whose hand is my soul, one whom the Fire has burned for his sin will enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah will forgive on the Day of Resurrection a forgiveness at which Iblis will stretch his neck, hoping that it will reach him."

This is a very strange hadith, and this Sa'd I do not know.
[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/168). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/216): "Sa'id ibn Talib Abu Ghaylan was declared trustworthy by Abu Zur'ah and Ibn Hibban, and there is some weakness in him, while the rest of his narrators are trustworthy."]

* *

As for His saying ﴿So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me﴾, meaning: I will make the attainment of My mercy obligatory as a favour from Me and a kindness to them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 54]. His saying ﴿for those who fear Me﴾ means: I will assign it to those who possess these qualities, and they are the community of Muhammad ﷺ, those who fear (yattaqun), that is, who avoid shirk and the grave sins.

﴿And who give zakah﴾: it was said: the purification of souls. It was also said: the purification of wealth. It is possible that it includes both, since the verse is Meccan. ﴿And who believe in Our signs﴾, meaning: they affirm them.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse: God had commanded Musa to choose seventy men from his people, and he chose seventy men and went out with them to supplicate their Lord. Among what they asked God was: "O Allah, give us what You have not given anyone before us, and do not give it to anyone after us." God disliked this request, so the earthquake (al-Rajfah) seized them. Musa said: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Al-Suddi said: God commanded Musa to come to Him with some men of the Children of Israel, who would apologise to Him for the worship of the calf, and He set them an appointed time. Musa chose seventy men from his people by his own eye, then went with them so that they might apologise. When they reached that place they said: "We will not believe you, O Musa, until we see Allah openly, for you have spoken to Him, so show Him to us." Then the thunderbolt (al-Sa'iqah) seized them and they died. Musa stood weeping and supplicating to Allah, saying: "My Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I meet them, after You have destroyed their best?" ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Musa chose from the Children of Israel seventy men, the best of the best, and said: "Go to Allah and repent to Him for what you have done, and ask Him to accept the repentance of those you have left behind among your people. Fast, purify yourselves, and purify your garments." He went out with them to Mount Sinai, at the appointed time his Lord had set for him, and he would not come to Him except by His permission and knowledge. The seventy said to him, as it is related to me, when they had done what he commanded them and set out with him to meet their Lord: "Ask for us, so that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." When Musa approached the mountain, a column of cloud descended upon it until it covered the whole mountain. Musa drew near and entered into it, and he said to the people: "Come near." Whenever Allah spoke to Musa, a bright light would fall upon Musa's forehead, such that no son of Adam could look at it, so a veil was placed between them. The people drew near until, when they entered, they fell prostrate and heard Him speaking to Musa, commanding and forbidding him: "Do this, and do not do that." When the matter was finished, the cloud withdrew from Musa and he came to them. They said to Musa: "We will not believe you until we see Allah openly." Then the earthquake seized them, which is the thunderbolt, and their souls were separated, and they all died. Musa stood pleading with his Lord, supplicating and imploring Him, saying: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too﴾ "They have acted foolishly. Will You destroy those behind me from the Children of Israel?"

Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, from Umarah ibn Abd al-Sululi, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Musa, Harun, Shabbar and Shabir set out and went to the foot of a mountain. Harun lay down on a couch and Allah took his soul (tawaffahu). When Musa returned to the Children of Israel they said to him: "Where is Harun?" He said: "Allah took his soul." They said: "You killed him, out of envy for his character and gentleness," or words similar to that. He said: "Then choose whomever you wish." So they chose seventy men. He said: "That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men﴾." When they reached Harun they said: "O Harun, who killed you?" He said: "No one killed me, but Allah took my soul." They said: "O Musa, you will not be disobeyed after today." Then the earthquake seized them. Musa, peace be upon him, began turning right and left and said: "O my Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me too. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will." He said: Then Allah revived them and made them all prophets.

This is a very strange report, and I do not know this Umarah ibn Abd (in some copies: Ubayd) al-Salum... [the original text here reads: "وَعِمَارَةُ بْنُ عَبْدٍ هَذَا لَا أَعْرِفُهُ"]. That is: I do not know this Umarah ibn Abd. Shu'bah narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from a man of the Banu Salul, from Ali, and he mentioned it.
[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/142). Its chain includes Umarah ibn Abd al-Sululi. Al-Dhahabi said in Mizan al-I'tidal: "Umarah ibn Abd, from Ali, is unknown and is not to be used as evidence; Abu Hatim said so. Ahmad said: he is of sound narration; only Abu Ishaq narrates from him."]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: The earthquake seized them only because they had not separated themselves from their people in their worship of the calf, nor had they forbidden them. This view is supported by Musa's words: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾

* *

As for His saying ﴿It is only Your trial﴾, meaning Your testing, Your examination, and Your probation. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Aliyah, Rabi' ibn Anas, and many others among the scholars of the early and later generations. It has no meaning other than this; the meaning is: the matter is only Your matter, the judgement belongs only to You. Whatever You will, comes to be. You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. None can guide the one You have led astray, and none can lead astray the one You have guided. None can give what You have withheld, and none can withhold what You have given. Sovereignty belongs entirely to You, and judgement belongs entirely to You. Creation and command are Yours.

* *

As for His saying ﴿You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers﴾: al-Ghafr (forgiveness) is concealment and not holding the sin to account. When mercy is joined with forgiveness, what is intended is that He does not let him fall into the like of it in the future. ﴿And You are the best of forgivers﴾ means: none forgives sins except You. ﴿And ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter﴾: the first part of the supplication is the averting of what is feared, and this part is the attainment of what is sought. ﴿Ordain for us good in this world and in the Hereafter﴾ means: make it obligatory for us and establish for us good in both. This has already been explained in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿Indeed we have turned back to You﴾ means: we repented, returned, and turned in penitence to You. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Taymi, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and others. It is also the linguistic meaning.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, from my father, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Nujayy, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Jews were only named (Yahud) because they said: ﴿Indeed we have turned back to You﴾.
Jabir (he is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi) is weak.

Allah, responding to Musa in his statement ﴿It is only Your trial, by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will﴾, said, the verse: ﴿My punishment I inflict upon whom I will, and My mercy encompasses all things; so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me﴾. That is: I do what I will, and I judge what I desire, and to Me belong wisdom and justice in all of that. Glory be to Him; there is no god but He.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, it is a verse of great comprehensiveness and generality, like His saying, reporting about the bearers of the Throne and those around it, that they say: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Abdullah al-Jushami, from Jundub ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A Bedouin came, made his mount kneel, tied it, and then prayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he went to his mount, untied its rope, mounted it, and then called out: "O Allah, have mercy on me and on Muhammad, and do not share our mercy with anyone." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you say this is more astray, or his camel? Did you not hear what he said?" They said: "Yes." He said: "He has restricted a wide mercy. Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, created one hundred mercies, and He sent down one mercy by which creation shows compassion to one another, its jinn, its humans, and its animals, and He kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. Do you say he is more astray, or his camel?"

It was narrated by Abu Dawud from Ali ibn Nasr, from Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, with this chain.
[Al-Musnad (4/312) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4885.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Uthman, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, has one hundred mercies, of which one mercy is that by which creatures show mercy to one another, and by which wild animals show tenderness to their young; and He delayed ninety-nine until the Day of Resurrection."

Muslim alone transmitted it, narrating it through the hadith of Sulayman, who is Ibn Tarkhan, and Dawud ibn Abi Hind, both from Abu Uthman, whose name is Abd al-Rahman ibn Mull, from Salman al-Farisi, from the Prophet ﷺ, with this wording.
[Al-Musnad (5/439) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2753.]

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has one hundred mercies; with Him are ninety-nine, and He placed with you one, by which you show mercy to one another, between the jinn and mankind and between creation. When the Day of Resurrection comes, He will gather it to Himself." Ahmad alone transmitted it through this route.
[Al-Musnad (3/55).]

Ahmad also said: Affan narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has one hundred mercies; He distributed one part of them among creation, and by it people, wild beasts, and birds show mercy to one another."

Ibn Majah transmitted it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with this wording.
[Al-Musnad (3/55) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4294.]

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Sa'd Abu Ghaylan al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the wicked in his religion will enter Paradise, and the fool in his livelihood. By Him in whose hand is my soul, one whom the Fire has burned for his sin will enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah will forgive on the Day of Resurrection a forgiveness at which Iblis will stretch his neck, hoping that it will reach him."

This is a very strange hadith, and this Sa'd I do not know.
[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/168). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/216): "Sa'id ibn Talib Abu Ghaylan was declared trustworthy by Abu Zur'ah and Ibn Hibban, and there is some weakness in him, while the rest of his narrators are trustworthy."]

* *

As for His saying ﴿So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me﴾, meaning: I will make the attainment of My mercy obligatory as a favour from Me and a kindness to them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 54]. His saying ﴿for those who fear Me﴾ means: I will assign it to those who possess these qualities, and they are the community of Muhammad ﷺ, those who fear (yattaqun), that is, who avoid shirk and the grave sins.

﴿And who give zakah﴾: it was said: the purification of souls. It was also said: the purification of wealth. It is possible that it includes both, since the verse is Meccan. ﴿And who believe in Our signs﴾, meaning: they affirm them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 157 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾. This is the description of Muhammad ﷺ in the books of the prophets. They gave their nations glad tidings of his coming (ba'th) and commanded them to follow him. His attributes have remained present in their books, known to their scholars (ulama') and rabbis (ahbar), as Imam Ahmad said:

Ahmad related: Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Juraypiri, from Abu Sakhr al-'Uqayli, who said: A man of the Bedouins told me: "I brought a caravan (jalubah) to Madinah during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When I finished my sale (bay'ah), I said: 'I will certainly meet this man and listen to him directly.' He said: So I encountered him between Abu Bakr and 'Umar, walking, and I followed them from behind until they came upon a Jewish man displaying the Torah, reading it, consoling himself with it over a son of his who was dying, a young man as handsome and beautiful as could be. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I adjure you by the One who revealed the Torah: do you find in this book of yours my description and my emigration (makhraji)?' He shook his head like this, meaning: No. His son said: 'Yes, by the One who revealed the Torah, we indeed find in our book your description and your emigration, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Remove the Jew from your brother.' Then he took charge of his shroud (kafan) and the prayer over him."

Its chain (musnad) is: this is a good, strong hadith, and it has a supporting report (shahid) in the Sahih from Anas.

Al-Hakim, author of al-Mustadrak, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Baghawi informed us: Ibrahim ibn al-Haytham al-Baladi narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim ibn Idris narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Shurahbil ibn Muslim, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, from Hisham ibn al-'As al-Umawi, who said: "I and another man were sent to Heraclius, the ruler of the Romans, inviting him to Islam. We set out until we reached al-Ghuta, meaning the Ghuta of Damascus, and we alighted with Jabalah ibn al-Ayham al-Ghassani. We entered upon him and found him on a couch of his, so he sent his messenger to us to speak with him. We said: 'By Allah, we will not speak to a messenger; we were sent only to the king. If he permits us, we will speak to him; otherwise we will not speak to the messenger.' The messenger returned to him and informed him of this. He said: So he permitted us and said: 'Speak.' Hisham ibn al-'As spoke to him and invited him to Islam, and he was wearing black garments. Hisham said to him: 'What is this you are wearing?' He said: 'I put it on and swore not to take it off until I expel you from al-Sham.' We said: 'By Allah, we will certainly take this seat of yours from you, and we will take the kingdom of the Greatest King, if Allah wills; our Prophet, our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, informed us of that.' He said: 'You are not of them; rather they are a people who fast by day and stand in prayer by night. So how is your fasting?' We informed him, and his face filled with blackness. He said: 'Stand up.' He sent a messenger with us to the king. We set out, and when we were near Madinah, the one with us said: 'These beasts of yours will not enter the king's city; if you wish, we will carry you on mules and asses.' We said: 'By Allah, we will not enter except upon them.' They sent word to the king that they refused that. So we entered upon our mounts, our swords hung at our sides, until we reached a chamber (ghurfah) and we made our mounts kneel at its base while he was looking at us. We said: 'La ilaha illallah, and Allahu akbar.' By Allah, the Lord knows, the chamber shook until it became like a palm cluster shaken by the winds. He sent to us: 'You are not permitted to proclaim your religion openly before us.' He sent to us: 'Enter.' We entered upon him while he was on his bed, with his commanders from the Romans around him, everything in his assembly was red, and what surrounded him was red, and he was wearing red garments. We drew near him, and he laughed and said: 'What would have prevented you from greeting me with your greeting among yourselves?' There was a man beside him, eloquent in Arabic and abundant in speech. We said: 'Our greeting among ourselves is not lawful for you, and your greeting by which you are greeted is not lawful for us to return to you.' He said: 'How is your greeting among yourselves?' We said: 'Al-salamu 'alayk.' He said: 'And how do you greet your king?' We said: 'With it.' He said: 'And how does he return it to you?' We said: 'With it.' He said: 'What is the greatest of your speech?' We said: 'La ilaha illallah, and Allahu akbar.' When we spoke these words, and Allah knows, the chamber shook until he raised his head toward it. He said: 'This word you have uttered, when the chamber shook: whenever you utter it in your houses, do your chambers shake over you?' We said: 'No, we have never seen it do this except in your presence.' He said: 'I wish that whenever you say it, everything would shake over you. And I have come out of half my kingdom.' We said: 'Why?' He said: 'Because it was easier for its matter, and more fitting that it not be from the affair of prophethood, and that it be from the tricks of men.' Then he asked us about what he wanted, and we informed him. Then he said: 'How are your prayer and your fasting?' We informed him, and he said: 'Stand up,' and we stood. He ordered a good dwelling and abundant provisions for us, and we stayed three days."

He sent for us at night, and we entered upon him, and he asked us to repeat our words, and we repeated them. Then he called for something like a great gilded box (rab'ah), in which were small chambers with doors. He opened one chamber and a lock, and brought out black silk, and spread it out, and in it was a red figure, and in it a man, large of eyes, great of buttocks, I had never seen such length of neck, with no beard, and two braids, the finest of what Allah created. He said: "Do you recognize this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Adam, peace be upon him," and he had the most hair of people.

Then he opened another door and brought out black silk, and in it was a white figure, with hair like the curls of the qitat, red eyes, large head, beautiful beard. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Nuh, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out black silk, and in it was a man exceedingly white, beautiful of eyes, broad of forehead, long of cheek, white-bearded, as if smiling. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Ibrahim, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door, and in it was a white figure, and behold, by Allah, it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "Do you recognize this?" We said: "Yes, Muhammad, Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: We wept. He said: Allah knows that he stood up, then sat down, and said: "By Allah, is it truly him?" We said: "Yes, it is truly him, as if you were looking at him." He remained silent for a while looking at it, then said: "Indeed, he was the last of the houses, but I hastened it for you so that I might see what you have."

Then he opened another door and brought out black silk, and in it was a brown, wheat-colored, dark figure, a man with curly hair, sunken eyes, sharp gaze, frowning, with closely set teeth, lips drawn in, as if angry. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Musa, peace be upon him." And beside him was a figure resembling him, except that his head was oily, broad of forehead, and in his eyes was squint. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Harun ibn 'Imran, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, and in it was the figure of a man, brown, straight-haired, of medium height, as if angry. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Lut, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, and in it was the figure of a man white tinged with red, aquiline-nosed, light of whiskers, handsome of face. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Ishaq, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, and in it was a figure resembling Ishaq, except that on his lip was a mole. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." [He said] "This is Ya'qub, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out black silk, in which was the figure of a white man, handsome of face, aquiline-nosed, of good stature, upon whose face shone a light, in whose face humility was recognized, tending toward redness. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Isma'il, the grandfather of your Prophet, upon them both be peace."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, in which was a figure as if it were Adam, peace be upon him, its face like the sun. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Yusuf, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, in which was the figure of a red man, thin of shins, weak-eyed, large of belly, of medium height, girded with a sword. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Dawud, peace be upon him."

Then he opened another door and brought out white silk, in which was the figure of a man large of buttocks, long of legs, riding a horse. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both."

Then he opened another door and brought out black silk, in which was a white figure, and behold, a young man, intensely black-bearded, abundant of hair, beautiful of eyes, beautiful of face. He said: "Do you know this?" We said: "No." He said: "This is 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him."

We said: "From where do you have these figures? For we know that they are as the prophets, peace be upon them, were portrayed, for we have seen the figure of our Prophet, peace be upon him, like him." He said: "Indeed, Adam, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to show him the prophets from his offspring, so He sent down their likenesses to him, and they were in the treasury of Adam, peace be upon him, at the sunset. Dhu al-Qarnayn took them out from the west of the sun and gave them to Daniel." Then he said: "Indeed, by Allah, my soul is content to come out of my kingdom, and I was a servant so that I might be more honorable in my rule, until I die." Then he rewarded us, bestowing a fine reward, and sent us off. When we came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, we related to him what he had shown us, what he had said to us, and what he had given us. He said: Abu Bakr wept and said: "Poor man! If Allah had intended good for him, He would have guided him." Then he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us that they and the Jews find the description of Muhammad ﷺ with them."

Thus al-Hafiz al-Kabir Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, may Allah have mercy on him, related it in the book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from al-Hakim by ijazah, and he mentioned it. Its isnad is not objectionable (la ba'sa bih).

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Fulayh narrated to us, from Hilal ibn ʿAli, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, who said: I met ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr and said: "Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Tawrah (Torah)."
