He said: "Yes, by Allah, he is indeed described in the Tawrah just as he is described in the Qur'an: 'O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, a warner, and a guardian for the unlettered. You are My servant and My messenger. I have named you al-Mutawakkil (the one who relies upon Allah). He is not harsh or coarse, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he pardons and overlooks. Allah will not take him until he has set right the crooked community, by their saying, "There is no god but Allah," and by him He will open hearts that are veiled, ears that are deaf, and eyes that are blind.'" ʿAta' said: "Then I met Kaʿb and asked him about that, and he did not differ in a single letter, except that Kaʿb said it in his own language: 'qulūban ghulūfiyyan wa-ādhānan ṣumūmiyyan wa-aʿyunan ʿumūmiyyan' (hearts veiled, ears deaf, and eyes blind)."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fulayh, from Hilal ibn ʿAli, with a chain similar to it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/164) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2125).]] and he added after his saying, "not harsh or coarse," the words: "nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he pardons and overlooks."

It occurs in the speech of many of the early scholars (salaf) to apply the term "Tawrah" to the books of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab). Something similar to this has also occurred in some hadiths, and Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Idris, the copyist of al-Humaydi, narrated to us [[In MS h: "Muhammad ibn Idras ibn al-Humaydi"; in the other copies: "Muhammad ibn Idris ibn Warraq ibn al-Humaydi." The reading adopted is from al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil 20/204, as cited in the margin of the Shaʿb edition.]] Muhammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Ibrahim, from the descendants of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, narrated to us, who said: Umm ʿUthman bint Saʿid, who is my grandmother, narrated to me, from her father Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from his father Muhammad ibn Jubayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "I set out as a merchant to al-Sham (Syria). When I was in the lower parts of al-Sham, a man from the People of the Book met me and said: 'Do you have a man among you who is a prophet?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you know his form if you see it?' I said: 'Yes.' He brought me into a room containing images, but I did not see the image of the Prophet (ﷺ). While I was like that, a man from among them entered upon us and said: 'What are you doing?' We informed him, and he took us to his house. The moment I entered, I looked at the image of the Prophet (ﷺ), and there was a man holding the heel of the Prophet (ﷺ). I said: 'Who is this man holding his heel?' He said: 'There has been no prophet except that after him there was another prophet, except this Prophet, for there is no prophet after him. This is the caliph after him,' and there was the description of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/125). He also narrated it in al-Awsat, no. (3496), Majma' al-Bahrayn, and said: "It is not narrated from Jubayr except by this chain; Muhammad ibn Idris alone transmitted it." al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/233): "In its chain are people whom I do not know."]]

Abu Dawud said: Hafs ibn ʿUmar Abu ʿUmar al-Darir narrated to us [[In all copies: "ʿUmar ibn Hafs Abu ʿUmar al-Darir," but the reading adopted is from Sunan Abi Dawud.]] Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, that Saʿid ibn Iyas al-Jurayri informed them, from ʿAbdullah ibn Shaqiq al-ʿUqayli, from al-Aqra', the muezzin of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, who said: ʿUmar sent me to the bishop, so I called him. ʿUmar said to him: "Do you find me in the Book?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How do you find me?" He said: "I find you a horn (qarn)." ʿUmar raised his whip and said: "A horn of what?" He said: "A horn of iron, a stern ruler." He said: "How do you find the one after me?" He said: "I find him a righteous caliph, except that he gives preference to his relatives." ʿUmar said: "May Allah have mercy on Uthman," three times. He said: "How do you find the one after him?" He said: "I find him the rust of iron." So ʿUmar placed his hand on his head and said: "Woe to me, woe to me!" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, he is a righteous caliph, but he will be made caliph when the sword is drawn and blood is shed." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4656). "Al-dafar" means foulness.]]

* *

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿He enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong﴾: this is the description of the Messenger (ﷺ) in the earlier scriptures, and such was his state, peace and blessings be upon him. He commanded only what is good and forbade only what is evil, as ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "When you hear Allah say, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then give it your attentive hearing, for it is either a good He is commanding or an evil He is forbidding." Among the most important and greatest of these is what Allah [may He be exalted] sent him with: commanding the worship of Him alone, with no partner, and forbidding the worship of anything other than Him, just as He sent all the messengers before him. As Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl: 36].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu ʿAmir, namely al-ʿAqadi ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr, narrated to us; Sulayman, namely Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Rabiʿah ibn Abi ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿid, from Abu Humayd and Abu Usayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you hear a hadith from me that your hearts recognise, and your hair and skins soften towards it, and you see that it is close to you, then I am the closest of you to it. And when you hear a hadith from me that your hearts deny, and your hair and skins recoil from it, and you see that it is far from you, then I am the farthest of you from it." [[al-Musnad, from the hadith of Abu Usayd (3/497) and from the hadith of Abu Humayd (5/425).]]

This [hadith] is of good chain (jayyid al-isnad), but none of the authors of the Six Books (al-Kutub al-Sittah) narrated it. [The word "al-Sittah" is an addition from copy A.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "If you are narrated a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then think of it in the best, most guiding, most wholesome, and most pious way." [[al-Musnad (1/122).]]

Then he narrated it from Yahya, from Ibn Saʿid, from Misʿar, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "If you are narrated a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then think of it in the one that is most guiding, most wholesome, and most pious." [[al-Musnad (1/130).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And He makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the evil things﴾: that is, He makes lawful for them what they had made unlawful for themselves, such as the baheerah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah, the ham, and similar things by which they had constricted themselves, and He makes unlawful for them the evil things.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: such as the flesh of swine and usury, and what they used to consider lawful of the forbidden foods that Allah, may He be exalted, had prohibited.

Some scholars said: Everything that Allah, may He be exalted, has made lawful is good and beneficial for the body and the religion, and everything He has made unlawful is evil and harmful for the body and the religion.

Those who hold the view that goodness and badness are known by reason (al-tahsin wa-al-taqbih al-ʿaqliyyan) have relied upon this noble verse, and a response to that has been given which this place cannot accommodate.

Likewise, those scholars who held that the reference in determining the permissibility of foods not expressly declared lawful or unlawful is what the Arabs found pleasant in their state of ease, and similarly in the matter of prohibition, what they found repugnant, have also cited this verse as evidence. There is a lengthy discussion about this as well.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾: that is, He came with ease and tolerance, as the hadith has been narrated through several chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been sent with the upright, tolerant religion (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah)." He also said to his two governors, Muʿadh and Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, when he sent them to Yemen: "Give good news and do not repel, make things easy and do not make them difficult, and cooperate and do not differ." His companion Abu Barzah al-Aslami said: "I accompanied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and witnessed his ease."

The nations who came before us had constraints in their laws, so Allah widened and facilitated matters for this Ummah. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has overlooked for my Ummah what its souls whisper about, so long as it does not speak or act upon it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5269), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (127), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] And he said: "Error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do have been lifted from my Ummah." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (2045), from the hadith of Abu Dhar, may Allah be pleased with him, and its takhrij and supporting narrations have been mentioned previously.]] For this reason Allah guided this Ummah to say: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make errors. Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286]. It is established in Sahih Muslim that Allah, may He be exalted, said after each of these requests: "I have done it, I have done it." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (126), from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿So those who believed in him, honoured him, supported him, and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾: that is, they esteemed him and revered him; ﴿and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾: that is, the Qur'an and the revelation that he brought, conveying it to the people; ﴿those are the successful﴾: that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

Allah says to His Prophet and Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ): **"Say"**, O Muhammad, **"O mankind"**. This is an address to the red and the black, and to the Arab and the non-Arab: **"Indeed, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all"**, i.e., to all of you. This is part of his nobility and greatness: that he is the Seal of the Prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin), and that he was sent to mankind in its entirety, as Allah says: **"Say: 'Allah is sufficient as Witness between me and you, and this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches'"** [al-An'am: 19]. And Allah says: **"And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place"** [Hud: 17]. And Allah says: **"And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, 'Have you embraced Islam?' If they embrace Islam, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance [of the message]"** [Al 'Imran: 20]. The verses on this are numerous, just as the ahadith on this are too many to be enumerated, and it is known by necessity (ḍarūrah) from the religion of Islam that he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is the Messenger of Allah to all of mankind.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the tafsir of this verse: Abdullah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman and Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Ala' ibn Zabr [in A: "Zayd"] narrated to us, Bisr [in A: "Bishr"] ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to me, Abu Idris al-Khawlani narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, say: There was an exchange between Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Abu Bakr angered Umar. Umar departed from him angry, so Abu Bakr followed him, asking him to seek forgiveness for him, but he did not do so until he shut his door in his face. Abu Bakr then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while we were with him. Abu al-Darda' said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for your companion here, he has been reckless (qad ghamara)" – i.e., he became angry and resentful. He said: Umar regretted what had happened from him, so he came, greeted, and sat with the Prophet ﷺ, and related the story to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abu al-Darda' said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry, and Abu Bakr began to say: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I was the one who was more unjust." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you leave my companion for me? I said: 'O mankind, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all,' and you said: 'You are lying,' while Abu Bakr said: 'You have spoken the truth.'" Al-Bukhari alone narrated it.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas [may Allah be pleased with him] [addition from A] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things that no prophet before me was given – and I say it not in boasting: I have been sent to mankind in its entirety: the red and the black; I have been aided with terror (al-ru'b) over a distance of a month's journey; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur); and I have been given intercession, and I have deferred it for my nation, so it is for whoever does not associate anything with Allah." Its chain is good, and they (the compilers of the six books) did not narrate it.

Imam Ahmad also said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us, from Abu al-Hadd, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the year of the Battle of Tabuk, got up at night to pray, and some men from among his companions [in A: "from the Ansar"] gathered behind him, guarding him. When he finished the prayer, he turned toward them and said: "I have been given five things tonight that no one before me has been given. As for me, I have been sent to all of mankind universally [in K: "kafffah"], whereas those before me were sent only to their own people. I have been aided against the enemy with terror, and even if there were a month's distance between me and them, they would be filled with terror of me. Spoils of war have been made lawful for me, to eat from them [in A: "all of them"], whereas those before me considered eating them a great matter; they used to burn them. The earth has been made for me a place of prostration [in K: "mosque"] and a means of purification; wherever the prayer overtakes me, I perform tayammum and pray. Those before me considered that a great matter; they only prayed in their churches and synagogues. And the fifth – what is it! It was said to me: Ask, for every prophet has asked. So I deferred my request until the Day of Resurrection, and it is for you and for whoever bears witness that there is no god but Allah." Its chain is good and strong, and they did not narrate it.

He also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever among my nation, or a Jew or a Christian, hears of me and does not believe in me, will not enter Paradise."

This hadith is in Sahih Muslim by another route, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one of this nation who hears of me – a Jew or a Christian – then dies without believing in me, except that he will enter the Fire." [This is the wording of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which Muslim narrated in his Sahih, no. 153; and the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari with this wording was narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11241.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu Yunus narrated to us – he is Sulaym ibn Jubayr – from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one of this nation hears of me – a Jew or a Christian – then dies without believing in what I have been sent with, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire." Ahmad alone narrated it.

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things: I have been sent to the red and the black; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been aided with terror for a month; and I have been given intercession – there is no prophet except that he has asked for intercession, but I have kept my intercession hidden, and I have made it for whoever of my nation dies without associating anything with Allah."

This chain is also sound, and I have not seen them (the compilers of the six books) narrate it, and Allah knows best. This hadith is also firmly established in the two Sahihs from the narration of Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things that none of the prophets before me was given: I have been aided with terror over a distance of a month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whichever man of my nation the prayer overtakes, let him pray; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given intercession; and every prophet was sent only to his people, whereas I have been sent to mankind in general." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 335; Sahih Muslim no. 521.]

* *

As for His saying: **"He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; there is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death"**, this is an attribute of Allah, the Exalted, in His saying **"the Messenger of Allah"**. That is: the One who sent me is the Creator of everything, its Lord and its Sovereign, in whose hand is the dominion, the giving of life and the causing of death, and to whom belongs the judgment.

* *

As for His saying: **"So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet"**, He informed them that he is the Messenger of Allah to them, then commanded them to follow him and believe in him. **"The unlettered Prophet"**, i.e., the one whom you were promised and given glad tidings of in the earlier Scriptures, for he is described with this in their books. Therefore He said: **"The unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words"**, i.e., his deeds confirm his speech, and he believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord. **"And follow him"**, i.e., take his path and follow his footsteps, **"that you may be guided"**, i.e., to the Straight Path.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the Children of Israel, that among them is a group who follow the truth and act justly by it, as He said: ﴿Among the People of the Scripture is a steadfast community who recite the verses of Allah during the night hours while they prostrate.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 113] And He said: ﴿And among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah. They do not exchange the signs of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 199] And He said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it." Those will be given their reward twice, for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 52-54] [[Addition from M; in H: "the verse".]] And He said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture recite it with its proper recitation. Those believe in it.﴾ and the rest of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 121]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, they fall down on their faces in prostration, and they say, "Exalted is our Lord; indeed, the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled." And they fall down on their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.﴾ [Al-Isra: 107-109]

Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir of it a remarkable report, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it they act justly.﴾ He said: It has reached me that the Children of Israel, when they killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes, one tribe among them disassociated itself from what they had done, and made excuse, and asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel in the earth, and they traveled through it until they emerged from beyond China. There, they are upright Muslims, facing our qibla. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: That is His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude."﴾ [Al-Isra: 104], and "the promise of the Hereafter" is 'Isa ibn Maryam. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/173).]] Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: They traveled through the tunnel for a year and a half.

Ibn 'Uyaynah said, from Sadaqah Abu al-Hudhayl, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it they act justly.﴾ He said: "A people between you and them is a river of honey." [[In A: "sahl" (plain).]]

The explanation of all of this has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah (the Chapter of the Cow), which is Madani (revealed in Madinah), whereas this context is Makki (revealed in Makkah). We have pointed out the difference between this context and that one, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. [Surah al-Baqarah verse: 60.]

The explanation of all of this has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah (the Chapter of the Cow), which is Madani (revealed in Madinah), whereas this context is Makki (revealed in Makkah). We have pointed out the difference between this context and that one, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. [Surah al-Baqarah verse: 60.]

The explanation of all of this has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah (the Chapter of the Cow), which is Madani (revealed in Madinah), whereas this context is Makki (revealed in Makkah). We have pointed out the difference between this context and that one, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. [Surah al-Baqarah verse: 60.]

This passage elaborates on the Almighty's words: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed concerning the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus did We test them because they were defiant.﴾ [7:163]

﴿And you have certainly known those among you who transgressed concerning the Sabbath, so We said to them: Be apes, despised and driven away.﴾ [2:65]

God Almighty says to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him: ﴿And ask them﴾, meaning: ask these Jews who are in your presence about the story of their forefathers who opposed God's command, so that His retribution overtook them for their deeds, their transgression, and their cunning in disobeying. Warn these people against concealing your description, which they find in their books, lest there befall them what befell their brethren and predecessors. This town is "Aylah," which lies on the shore of the Red Sea (Bahr al-Qulzum).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾. He said: It is a town called "Aylah," between Madyan and al-Tur. Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi also said likewise.

Abdullah ibn Kathir al-Qari said: We have heard that it is Aylah. It was also said: It is Madyan, and this is a report from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: It is a town called "Muqna," between Madyan and Ayduni.

* *

His words ﴿when they transgressed concerning the Sabbath﴾ mean: they committed transgression in it and opposed God's command concerning it, which had enjoined them to observe it at that time. ﴿When their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day﴾. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas: meaning, appearing visibly upon the water.

Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿openly﴾ means from every direction.

Ibn Jarir said: His words ﴿and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾ mean: He tests them by making the fish appear to them on the surface of the water on the day when hunting it is forbidden for them, and hiding it from them on the day when hunting it is permitted for them. ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, meaning We try them ﴿because they were defiant﴾, that is, because of their disobedience to God's obedience and their departure from it.

These were a people who devised tricks to violate God's prohibitions, through the outward means they adopted, whose inner meaning was the pursuit of what is unlawful.

The jurist and imam Abu Abdullah ibn Battah, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Za'farani narrated to us; Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Do not commit what the Jews committed, lest you make lawful the prohibitions of God through the slightest of tricks." [Juz' fi al-Khul' wa Ibtal al-Hiyal li-Ibn Battah (42)]

This is a good chain of narration, for Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim here was mentioned by al-Khatib in his History [in Tarikh Baghdad (5/98, 99), Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Baghdadi is mentioned, but al-Khatib did not comment on him nor declare him trustworthy], and he declared him trustworthy, and the rest of its narrators are well known and reliable. al-Tirmidhi often authenticates a chain like this one.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah al-A'raf (7), verses 164–166:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the people of this town that they divided into three groups. One group [[In K, M, A: "So a group".]] committed what was forbidden and devised stratagems to catch fish on the Sabbath, as already explained in Surah al-Baqarah. Another group forbade that and [denounced it] [[Addition from K, M, A.]] and separated itself from them. A third group remained silent, neither doing nor forbidding, but said to those who denounced: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ That is: why do you forbid these people, when you know that they have been destroyed and deserve punishment from Allah? There is no benefit in your forbidding them. The denouncers said to them: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord﴾. Some read it in the nominative (raf'), as if the sense were: "This is an excuse." Others read it in the accusative (nasb), meaning: "We do this as an excuse to your Lord" ﴿as an excuse to your Lord﴾, that is, concerning what He has enjoined upon us of commanding right and forbidding wrong ﴿and that perhaps they may fear Allah﴾. They meant: perhaps through this denunciation they will refrain from and abandon what they are engaged in, and return to Allah repentant. When they repent, Allah will accept their repentance and have mercy on them.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, that is, when the wrongdoers refused to accept the advice, ﴿We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong﴾, that is, those who committed the disobedience, ﴿with a wretched punishment.﴾ He explicitly mentioned the salvation of those who forbade and the destruction of the wrongdoers, and He was silent about the silent ones, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. They do not deserve praise so as to be praised, nor did they commit a grave sin so as to be blamed. Nevertheless, the scholars (a'immah) differed concerning them: were they among those who perished or among those who were saved? There are two opinions.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning: ﴿And when a community among them said: Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ He said: It is a town on the seashore between Egypt and Medina, called "Aylah." Allah forbade them the fish on their Sabbath day. The fish would come to them on their Sabbath in great numbers on the seashore, but when the Sabbath day passed they could not get them. This continued for as long as Allah willed. Then a group of them took fish on their Sabbath day, and another group forbade them, saying: "Do you take them when Allah has forbidden them to you on your Sabbath day?" They did not increase except in error and rebellion. Another group kept admonishing them. When this lasted long for them, a group of the admonishers said: "You know that these are a people against whom the punishment is certain," ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish [with a severe punishment]﴾ [[Addition from A.]] and they were more zealous for Allah than the other group? They said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord, and that perhaps they may fear Allah.﴾ All of them had been forbidding. When the anger of Allah descended upon them, the two groups that said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy﴾ and those who said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord﴾ were saved, and Allah destroyed the people of disobedience who took the fish, and He made them apes.

Al-'Awfi narrated something similar to this from Ibn 'Abbas.

Hammad ibn Zayd narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾

He said: I do not know whether those who said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy," were saved or not. [Ibn 'Abbas] said: I did not stop with him until I made him know that they were saved, and he clothed me with a garment.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Juraij informed us: a man narrated to me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas one day while he was weeping, with the Mushaf in his lap. I was reluctant to approach him, but I kept on until I went forward and sat down. I said: "What makes you weep, O Abu 'Abbas? May Allah make me your ransom." He said: "These pages." He said: It was in "Surah al-A'raf." He said: "Do you know Aylah?" I said: "Yes." He said: "There was a tribe of Jews there to whom fish were brought on the Sabbath day, and then they submerged and they could not get them except after great toil and hardship. They would come to them on the Sabbath day in large numbers, white and fat, like pregnant she-camels, their backs lying flat upon their bellies in their courtyards. They remained so for a period of time. Then Satan inspired them, saying: 'You have only been forbidden to eat them on the Sabbath day, so take them on it and eat them on other days.' A group of them said this, and another group said: 'Rather, you have been forbidden to eat them, to take them, and to hunt them on the Sabbath day.' They remained so until the following Friday. One group went out with themselves, their sons and their women, another group withdrew to the right, and another group withdrew to the left and remained silent. The right-hand group said: 'Woe to you! Allah, Allah! We forbid you lest you expose yourselves to the punishment of Allah.' The left-hand group said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ The right-hand group said: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord, and that perhaps they may fear Allah.﴾ If they desist, that is more beloved to us, that they not be afflicted and not perish; and if they do not desist, then it is an excuse to your Lord. They persisted in the sin. The right-hand group said: 'You have done it, O enemies of Allah! By Allah, we will not spend the night with you in your city tonight. By Allah, we do not think you will see the morning before Allah makes you see it with a sinking into the earth, or a hurling of stones, or some of what He has of punishment.' When they got up in the morning, they struck the gate and called out, but they were not answered. So they placed a ladder and raised a man over the city wall. He looked at them and said: 'O servants of Allah, apes! By Allah, they have tails swinging!' So they opened and entered upon them. The apes recognized their kin from among mankind, but mankind did not recognize their kin among the apes. The apes began to come to their relatives from mankind, sniffing their garments and weeping, and saying: 'Did we not forbid you from such-and-such?' and they would nod their heads, meaning 'yes.'" Then Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment.﴾ He said: I see that those who forbade were saved, and I do not see that the others were mentioned. Yet we see things that we disapprove of and do not speak about them? He said: I said: "May Allah make me your ransom, do you not see that they disliked what they were doing, and opposed them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?﴾" He said: He ordered for me, and I was clothed in two thick garments.

Mujahid also narrated this from him.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to us, Ashhab ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, from Malik, who said: Ibn Rumman claimed that the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Their fish come to them on their Sabbath day in large numbers, but on the day they do not observe the Sabbath, they do not come to them﴾ means: They used to come to them on the Sabbath day, and when evening came they would leave, and nothing of them would be seen until the next Sabbath day. A man therefore took a line and a peg, and tied a fish in the water on the Sabbath day, and when they had reached the night of Sunday he took it and roasted it. ﴿تَأَذَّنَ﴾ is on the pattern *tafa''ala* (تَفَعَّل) from *al-idhn* (الْإِذْن), meaning he made it known, i.e. "declared." This is the view of Mujahid. Others said it means "commanded."

The sense of the sentence conveys the meaning of an oath (qasam) through this word. For this reason it is followed by the emphatic lam in His words ﴿He will surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who will afflict them with a terrible torment﴾, meaning against the Jews, because of their disobedience, their defiance of God's commands and His law, and their scheming against the things He has forbidden.

It is said that Musa (peace be upon him) imposed on them the kharaj (land tax) for seven years, and it was said for thirteen years, and he was the first to impose the kharaj. Then they were under the domination of kings from the Yunaniyyin (Greeks), the Kashdaniyyin (Kashdanites), and the Kaldaniyyin (Chaldeans). Then they came under the domination of the Christians, who humiliated them and took from them the jizyah (poll tax) and the kharaj. Then Islam came, and Muhammad (ﷺ), and they were under his protection and his dhimmah (covenant of protection), paying the kharaj and the jizyah.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the interpretation of this verse, that he said: "It is the humiliation (maskanah) and the taking of the jizyah from them."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from him: "It is the jizyah, and those who will afflict them with a terrible torment are Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and his community, until the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Jurayj, al-Suddi, and Qatadah.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "It is recommended that the Anbat (peasant farmers) be sent to collect the jizyah."

I say: Ultimately, their final fate is that they will come out as supporters of the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and the Muslims will kill them along with 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him), and that will be at the end of time.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾, meaning for whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command and His law, ﴿and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning for whoever turns back to Him in repentance and returns to Him.

This is from the pattern of coupling mercy with punishment, lest despair arise. Therefore God Most High often couples encouragement (tarhib... al-targhib) with warning (al-tarhib), so that souls remain between hope and fear.

He mentions that He scattered them across the earth as communities (ummam), meaning groups and divisions, as He said: ﴿And We said to the Children of Israel after him, "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed throng."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:104]

﴿Among them are the righteous, and among them are others than that﴾ means: among them are the righteous and others who are not. This is like what the jinn said: ﴿And among us are the righteous, and among us are those beneath that; we were sects of various paths.﴾ [al-Jinn 72:11] ﴿And We tested them﴾, meaning We examined them, ﴿with good times and bad﴾, meaning with ease and hardship, desire and fear, well-being and affliction, ﴿that they might return.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a later generation who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower world and saying, "It will be forgiven us." And if the offer of such goods came to them again, they would take it.﴾ He says: after that generation, among whom were the righteous and the wicked, there came another successor generation with no good in them. They inherited the study of this Book, which is the Torah. Mujahid said: they are the Christians. It may also be broader than that. ﴿Taking the goods of this lower world﴾ means they accept in exchange for giving up the truth and spreading it the goods of the life of this world. They commit excesses against themselves and promise themselves repentance, and whenever something similar to the first presents itself to them, they fall into it. For this reason He said: ﴿And if the offer of such goods came to them again, they would take it.﴾ As Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they commit a sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah for it, and if that sin is offered again, they take it.

Mujahid's statement regarding His words ﴿taking the goods of this lower world﴾: he said: nothing of the world is offered to them except that they take it, whether it is lawful or unlawful, and they wish for forgiveness and say, ﴿It will be forgiven us,﴾ and if they find goods like it, they take it.

Qatadah said regarding ﴿Then there succeeded them a later generation﴾: that is, by Allah, an evil succession. They inherited the Book after their prophets and messengers. Allah made them inheritors and entrusted them with it. And Allah said in another verse: ﴿Then there succeeded them a later generation who neglected the prayer and followed their desires.﴾ [Maryam 19:59] He said: ﴿taking the goods of this lower world and saying, "It will be forgiven us"﴾; they wished for things from Allah as mere wishes, and were deceived by delusions with which they deceived themselves. ﴿And if the offer of such goods came to them again, they would take it﴾: nothing occupies them from anything else, and nothing restrains them from that. Whenever some of the world's affairs came to them, they consumed it, and they did not care whether it was lawful or unlawful.

As-Suddi said regarding His words ﴿Then there succeeded them a later generation﴾ up to His words ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾: The Children of Israel would not appoint a judge except that he would take bribes in the ruling. Their best people gathered and took covenants from one another not to do this and not to accept bribes. Then whenever one of them was appointed judge, he would take a bribe. It would be said to him: "What is your matter, taking bribes in judgment?" He would say: "It will be forgiven me." The rest of the Children of Israel would then criticise what he had done. When he died or was removed, a man from among those who had criticised him would be put in his place, and he would take a bribe. He says: "And if the others were offered the goods of this world, they would take it."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they studied what is in it?﴾ He says, rebuking them for this conduct of theirs, despite the covenant taken from them that they would certainly make the truth clear to the people and would not conceal it, as in His words: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it," but they cast it behind their backs and bartered it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchase.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:187]

Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth﴾: this refers to their making it obligatory upon Allah to forgive their sins, which they kept committing again and again without repenting from them.

Sufyan ath-Thawri narrated from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "The angels lifted it up over their heads."

Al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Then Musa (peace be upon him) traveled with them, heading toward the Holy Land, and he took the Tablets after his anger had subsided. He commanded them with what Allah the Exalted had commanded him to convey of the duties, but these weighed heavily upon them, and they refused to accept them until Allah uprooted [naqa] the mountain over them as though it were a canopy." He said: "The angels lifted it up over their heads." This was related by an-Nasa'i in full [in his Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11326], and it is the hadith of al-Futun, and it will come, Allah willing, in Surah Ta-Ha.

Sunayd ibn Dawud narrated in his Tafsir, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, who said: "This is a Book; will you accept it with what is in it, for indeed in it is the explanation of what is lawful for you and what is unlawful for you, and what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you?" They said: "Recite to us what is in it. If its obligations are light and its limits are gentle, we will accept it." He said: "Accept it with what is in it." They said: "No, not until we know what is in it, how its limits and obligations are." So they returned to Musa many times, and Allah revealed to the mountain, and it was uprooted and rose into the sky until it was between their heads and the sky. Musa said to them: "Do you not see what my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, is saying? If you do not accept the Torah with what is in it, I will surely crush you with this mountain." He said: Al-Hasan al-Basri related to me: "When they looked at the mountain, every man fell down prostrate upon his left brow, and looked at the mountain with his right eye, fearing that it would fall upon him. Therefore, today there is no Jew on earth who prostrates except upon his left brow; they say: 'This is the prostration by which the punishment was lifted.'" Abu Bakr said: "When he spread out the Tablets, in which was the Book of Allah which he had written with his own hand, there remained on the face of the earth no mountain, nor tree, nor stone, except that it shook. Today there is no Jew on the face of the earth, young or old, over whom the Torah is recited, except that he shakes and nods his head for it [ay: haraka (moved), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they will shake their heads at you﴾ [Al-Isra: 51], i.e., they move them]."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 172–174 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, informs us that He brought forth the offspring of the children of Adam from their loins, making them bear witness against themselves that Allah is their Lord and Sovereign, and that there is no god but Him. Just as He, may He be exalted, created them upon this and instilled it in their natures, He said: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He has created mankind. There is no altering of the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. In the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah," and in another narration, "upon this religion (millah). Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Himar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah [Exalted] says: 'I created My servants as hunafa' (upright in faith), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2865; its chain and the preceding one were cited under verse 30.]].

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan narrated to them, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' of the Banu Sa'd, who said: I fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in four campaigns. He said: The people targeted the offspring after they had killed the combatants. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it displeased him greatly. Then he said: "What is the matter with people that they target the offspring?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not the children of polytheists?" He said: "Indeed, the best of you are the children of polytheists! Verily, there is no soul born except that it is born upon the fitrah, and it remains upon it until its tongue speaks for it. Then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has indeed said in His Book: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves [and made them bear witness over themselves]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], and so on [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/321).]]. Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (3/435).]]. Al-Nasa'i also recorded it in his Sunan from the narration of Hushaim, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "al-Aswad ibn Sari' narrated to us," and so he mentioned it, but he did not mention al-Hasan's statement or his recollection of the verse at that point [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8616.]].

Traditions have been related about the taking of the offspring from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and their separation into the people of the right and the people of the left. In some of them there is the call to witness against them that Allah is their Lord.

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to a man of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: 'Tell me, if you had all that is on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will be told: 'You were asked for something easier than that, when you were in the loins of Adam: that you should not associate anything with Me. But you refused except to associate.'"

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs, from the narration of Shu'bah with the same chain [[al-Musnad (3/127); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3334; Sahih Muslim, no. 2805.]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Jarir (meaning Ibn Hazim) narrated to us, from Kulthum ibn Jabir [[In K and M: "Jabr"; in A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah took the covenant from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, at Nu'man, meaning [[In K, M and A: "on the day of".]] Arafah. He brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him. Then He spoke to them directly, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify﴾ ... [up to] ﴿the falsifiers﴾" [[Lit.: the wrongdoers; the verse ends with the word al-mubtilun, "the falsifiers" or "those who nullify (the truth)."]].

Al-Nasa'i also recorded this hadith in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/272); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11191; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/222). Al-Nasa'i said: "Kulthum here is not strong, and his hadith is not preserved."]]. However, Ibn Abi Hatim made it a mawquf (a narration ending with a Companion). Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad and others, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, with the same chain, and said: "Its chain is sahih, but they did not record it." He also said: "Muslim relied on Kulthum ibn Jubayr." Thus he said [[In K and M: "Jabr".]] [[al-Mustadrak (1/27).]]. But Abd al-Warith narrated it from Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and stopped it at Ibn Abbas [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/172).]]. Likewise, Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and Waki' narrated it from Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum, from Jubayr, from his father, with the same wording [[Al-Tabari, Tafsir (13/224) via Ibn Ulayyah, and (13/229) via Waki'.]]. Likewise, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ali ibn Badhimah narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, as his own statement [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/227–229).]]. Likewise, al-Awfi and Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated it from Ibn Abbas [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/236–237).]]. This is more widespread and more firmly established, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Jamrah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], who said: Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam [[Addition from A.]], from his back, like the particles (al-dharr), while they were in a pool of water.

He also said: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, Abu Mas'ud narrated to us, from Jubayr, who said: A son of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim died, and he was six days old. He said: "O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, uncover his face and loosen his knots, for my son will be questioned and asked." So I did what he commanded. When I had finished, I said: "May Allah have mercy on you, about what will your son be questioned? And who will ask him?" He said: "He will be asked about the covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam." I said: "O Abu al-Qasim, and what is this covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam?" He said: "Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me that Allah passed His hand over the loins of Adam and brought forth from them every soul He would create until the Day of Resurrection. He took from them the covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them their provision. Then He returned them to his loins. So the Hour will not be established until those who gave the covenant on that day are born. Whoever among them reaches the later covenant and fulfils it, the first covenant benefits him. And whoever reaches the later covenant and does not fulfil it, the first covenant does not benefit him. Whoever dies young before reaching the later covenant dies upon the first covenant, upon the fitrah" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/230).]].

All these routes strengthen the view that this report is a statement of Ibn Abbas, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak and from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ He said: "He took from his back as the comb is drawn through the hair of the head. Then He said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes.﴾" The angels said: ﴿We testify﴾ [[In A: "lest you say"; the text reads "lest they say".]] on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/232). Al-Tabari said: "I do not know it to be sound, because the trustworthy narrators whose memory and precision are relied upon narrated this hadith from al-Thawri and made it end with Abd Allah ibn Amr, not raising it to the Prophet, and they did not mention in it this phrase that Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah reported from him."]].

Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah is Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, judge of Qumis. He was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa'i recorded from him in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "His hadith is written down." Ibn Adi said: "He narrated hadiths, most of which are gharib (rare, singular narrations)" [[In K, M and A: "many".]].

This hadith was also narrated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, as his own statement. Likewise Jarir narrated it from Mansur with the same chain. This is more sound, and Allah knows best [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh, that is Ibn Ubadah, narrated to us, Malik narrated to us; and Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah: that Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani: that Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes"﴾, and so on. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: 'Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, then passed His hand over his back with His right hand, and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for Paradise, and they will act with the deeds of the people of Paradise." Then He passed His hand over his back again and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for the Fire, and they will act with the deeds of the people of the Fire."'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire because of it."

This was narrated in the same way by Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, and al-Tirmidhi from Ishaq ibn Musa, from Ma'n. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Rawh ibn Ubadah and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hibban recorded it in his Sahih from the narration of Abu Mus'ab al-Zubayri. All of them narrated it from Imam Malik ibn Anas with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/44); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4703; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11190; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3075; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear (directly) from Umar." Likewise said Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah. Abu Hatim added: "Between them is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah."

What Abu Hatim said was also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, from Baqiyyah, from Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi [[In A: "Amr ibn Khath'am".]], from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I was with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾," and then he mentioned it [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4704. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir (13/235) from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, with the same chain.]].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 7, verses 172–174 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni said: Abu Farwa al-Rahawi also followed 'Umar ibn Ju'thum ibn Zayd ibn Sinan, and their version is closer to the correct one than Malik's version. And Allah knows best. [[al-'Ilal of al-Daraqutni (2/221–223).]]

I say: It appears that Imam Malik deliberately omitted the mention of "Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah," because he did not know his condition and did not recognize him, for he is not known except in this hadith. Likewise, he omits the mention of a group of narrators whom he does not approve of. For this reason, he often cites hadiths as mursal (with a missing companion) and cuts short many connected (mawsul) chains. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: At-Tirmidhi, in his commentary on this verse, said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from A.]] created Adam, He wiped over his back, and from his back there fell every soul He would create from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection. He placed between the eyes of each of them a gleam of light. Then He presented them to Adam, and [Adam] said: 'O Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' He saw among them a man whose gleam between his eyes impressed him, and he said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is a man from the last of the nations from your descendants; his name is Dawud (David).' He said: 'Lord, how long have You made his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'O Lord, add to his life forty years from mine.' When the life of Adam had ended, the Angel of Death came to him. He said: 'Have not forty years of my life remained?' He said: 'Have you not given them to your son Dawud?' He said: So Adam denied it, and his descendants denied it; Adam forgot, and his descendants forgot; Adam erred, and his descendants erred."

Then at-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak, through the hadith of Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, with the same chain. He said: Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3076), and al-Mustadrak (2/325).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir (exegesis), through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that he related to him from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning something similar to what came before, until he said: "Then He presented them to Adam and said: 'O Adam, these are your descendants.' And among them were the leprous, the lepers, the blind, and various kinds of illnesses. Adam said: 'O Lord, why have You done this to my descendants?' He said: 'So that My blessing may be thanked.' Adam said: 'O Lord, among these whom You have shown me, who are the people with the most light?' He said: 'These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.'" Then he mentioned the story of Dawud, similar to what came before. [[Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (1015), through the route of Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Another hadith: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatadah al-Nasri [[In A: "al-Basri."]] narrated from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim [may Allah be pleased with him], that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, are deeds begun (decided anew), or has the decree already been determined?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then He scattered them into His two palms." Then he said: "These are in Paradise and these are in the Fire. The people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various routes from him. [[Tafsir at-Tabari (13/244). Shaykh Mahmud Shakir has discussed it at length in the footnote, sufficient to not repeat it here.]]

Another hadith: Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, who is weak, narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation and decreed the decree, He took the people of the right with His right hand and the people of the left with His left hand. He said: 'O people of the right!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O people of the left!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' Then He mixed them together. A speaker said: 'O Lord, why did You mix them together?' He said: 'For them are deeds other than that, which they will perform, so that they may say on the Day of Resurrection: We were indeed unaware of this.' Then He returned them into the loins of Adam [peace be upon him] [[Addition from A.]]." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/287) through the route of Uthman ibn al-Haytham, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, with it. Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr is very weak, but he has a follower: Bishr ibn Numayr narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with something similar. Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (228), and al-Uqayli in ad-Du'afa al-Kabir (1/51). However, one should not rejoice in this follow-up, for Bishr ibn Numayr is abandoned (matruk) and accused (muttaham).]]

Another report: Abu Ja'far ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ and the verse that follows, he said: "He gathered them for Him on that day, all of them, all that would exist from them until the Day of Resurrection. He made them into spirits, then fashioned them, then made them speak, and He took from them the covenant and the pledge, and He made them testify against themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes,' and so on." He said: "I call upon the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call upon your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We did not know of this.' Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, so do not associate anything with Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you My books." They said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord but You, and no god but You." So they acknowledged to Him on that day their obedience. And their father Adam was raised up, and he looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and those below that. He said: "O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?" He said: "I have loved to be thanked." He saw among them the prophets like lamps, upon whom was light, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning messengership and prophethood. This is what Allah, Exalted is He, means by: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 7]. And this is what He means: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30], and from this He said: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [An-Najm: 56], and from this He said: ﴿And We found most of them not upholding any covenant; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-A'raf: 102].

Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad of his father, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in their exegeses (tafasir), through the narration of Ibn Ja'far ar-Razi, with it. It is also narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, as-Suddi, and many other scholars of the early generations, with accounts that agree with these hadiths. We have contented ourselves with citing them rather than lengthening discussion of all those reports. And from Allah we seek help.

These hadiths indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. As for the making of them testify there that He is their Lord, this appears only in the hadith of Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr."]] from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]], and in the hadith of Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]]. We have already explained that both of these are mawquf (ending with a companion), not marfu' (attributed to the Prophet), as previously mentioned. For this reason, some scholars of the early and later generations have said that the intended meaning of this testimony is only their being created upon monotheism (tawhid), as mentioned earlier in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, and in the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from al-Aswad ibn Sari'. Al-Hasan al-Basri explained the verse in this way. They said: That is why He said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam﴾ and did not say "from Adam"; ﴿from their loins﴾ and did not say "from his loin"; ﴿their descendants﴾, meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ [Al-An'am: 165], and He said: ﴿And makes you successors upon the earth﴾ [An-Naml: 62], and He said: ﴿As He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾ [Al-An'am: 133].

Then He said: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ That is, He caused them to be witnesses to this, speaking to Him through their state and their words. Testimony is sometimes by speech, as He said: ﴿They will say, "We testify against ourselves"﴾ [Al-An'am: 130], and sometimes it is by state, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief﴾ [At-Tawbah: 17]; that is, their condition bears witness against them, not that they are speaking that. Likewise is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [Al-'Adiyat: 7]. Just as a question is sometimes by speech and sometimes by state, as in His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

They said: Among what indicates that this is the intended meaning is that He made this testimony a proof against them in associating partners with Him. If this had happened as the one who said it claimed, then everyone would remember it, so that it would be a proof against them. If it is said: The Messenger's informing about it is sufficient to establish its existence. The answer: The polytheists who deny the truth reject everything the messengers brought them, including this and other things. This was made an independent proof against them, which indicates that it is the natural disposition (fitrah) upon which they were created, which is the acknowledgment of monotheism. That is why He said: ﴿lest you say﴾, that is, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, we were of this (tawhid) unaware,﴾ or ﴿say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were only descendants after them..."﴾, and so on.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 172–174 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, informs us that He brought forth the offspring of the children of Adam from their loins, making them bear witness against themselves that Allah is their Lord and Sovereign, and that there is no god but Him. Just as He, may He be exalted, created them upon this and instilled it in their natures, He said: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He has created mankind. There is no altering of the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. In the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah," and in another narration, "upon this religion (millah). Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Himar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah [Exalted] says: 'I created My servants as hunafa' (upright in faith), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2865; its chain and the preceding one were cited under verse 30.]].

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan narrated to them, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' of the Banu Sa'd, who said: I fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in four campaigns. He said: The people targeted the offspring after they had killed the combatants. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it displeased him greatly. Then he said: "What is the matter with people that they target the offspring?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not the children of polytheists?" He said: "Indeed, the best of you are the children of polytheists! Verily, there is no soul born except that it is born upon the fitrah, and it remains upon it until its tongue speaks for it. Then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has indeed said in His Book: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves [and made them bear witness over themselves]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], and so on [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/321).]]. Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (3/435).]]. Al-Nasa'i also recorded it in his Sunan from the narration of Hushaim, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "al-Aswad ibn Sari' narrated to us," and so he mentioned it, but he did not mention al-Hasan's statement or his recollection of the verse at that point [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8616.]].

Traditions have been related about the taking of the offspring from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and their separation into the people of the right and the people of the left. In some of them there is the call to witness against them that Allah is their Lord.

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to a man of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: 'Tell me, if you had all that is on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will be told: 'You were asked for something easier than that, when you were in the loins of Adam: that you should not associate anything with Me. But you refused except to associate.'"

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs, from the narration of Shu'bah with the same chain [[al-Musnad (3/127); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3334; Sahih Muslim, no. 2805.]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Jarir (meaning Ibn Hazim) narrated to us, from Kulthum ibn Jabir [[In K and M: "Jabr"; in A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah took the covenant from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, at Nu'man, meaning [[In K, M and A: "on the day of".]] Arafah. He brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him. Then He spoke to them directly, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify﴾ ... [up to] ﴿the falsifiers﴾" [[Lit.: the wrongdoers; the verse ends with the word al-mubtilun, "the falsifiers" or "those who nullify (the truth)."]].

Al-Nasa'i also recorded this hadith in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/272); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11191; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/222). Al-Nasa'i said: "Kulthum here is not strong, and his hadith is not preserved."]]. However, Ibn Abi Hatim made it a mawquf (a narration ending with a Companion). Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad and others, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, with the same chain, and said: "Its chain is sahih, but they did not record it." He also said: "Muslim relied on Kulthum ibn Jubayr." Thus he said [[In K and M: "Jabr".]] [[al-Mustadrak (1/27).]]. But Abd al-Warith narrated it from Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and stopped it at Ibn Abbas [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/172).]]. Likewise, Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and Waki' narrated it from Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum, from Jubayr, from his father, with the same wording [[Al-Tabari, Tafsir (13/224) via Ibn Ulayyah, and (13/229) via Waki'.]]. Likewise, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ali ibn Badhimah narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, as his own statement [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/227–229).]]. Likewise, al-Awfi and Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated it from Ibn Abbas [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/236–237).]]. This is more widespread and more firmly established, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Jamrah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], who said: Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam [[Addition from A.]], from his back, like the particles (al-dharr), while they were in a pool of water.

He also said: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, Abu Mas'ud narrated to us, from Jubayr, who said: A son of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim died, and he was six days old. He said: "O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, uncover his face and loosen his knots, for my son will be questioned and asked." So I did what he commanded. When I had finished, I said: "May Allah have mercy on you, about what will your son be questioned? And who will ask him?" He said: "He will be asked about the covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam." I said: "O Abu al-Qasim, and what is this covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam?" He said: "Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me that Allah passed His hand over the loins of Adam and brought forth from them every soul He would create until the Day of Resurrection. He took from them the covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them their provision. Then He returned them to his loins. So the Hour will not be established until those who gave the covenant on that day are born. Whoever among them reaches the later covenant and fulfils it, the first covenant benefits him. And whoever reaches the later covenant and does not fulfil it, the first covenant does not benefit him. Whoever dies young before reaching the later covenant dies upon the first covenant, upon the fitrah" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/230).]].

All these routes strengthen the view that this report is a statement of Ibn Abbas, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak and from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ He said: "He took from his back as the comb is drawn through the hair of the head. Then He said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes.﴾" The angels said: ﴿We testify﴾ [[In A: "lest you say"; the text reads "lest they say".]] on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/232). Al-Tabari said: "I do not know it to be sound, because the trustworthy narrators whose memory and precision are relied upon narrated this hadith from al-Thawri and made it end with Abd Allah ibn Amr, not raising it to the Prophet, and they did not mention in it this phrase that Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah reported from him."]].

Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah is Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, judge of Qumis. He was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa'i recorded from him in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "His hadith is written down." Ibn Adi said: "He narrated hadiths, most of which are gharib (rare, singular narrations)" [[In K, M and A: "many".]].

This hadith was also narrated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, as his own statement. Likewise Jarir narrated it from Mansur with the same chain. This is more sound, and Allah knows best [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].
