Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh, that is Ibn Ubadah, narrated to us, Malik narrated to us; and Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah: that Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani: that Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes"﴾, and so on. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: 'Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, then passed His hand over his back with His right hand, and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for Paradise, and they will act with the deeds of the people of Paradise." Then He passed His hand over his back again and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for the Fire, and they will act with the deeds of the people of the Fire."'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire because of it."

This was narrated in the same way by Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, and al-Tirmidhi from Ishaq ibn Musa, from Ma'n. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Rawh ibn Ubadah and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hibban recorded it in his Sahih from the narration of Abu Mus'ab al-Zubayri. All of them narrated it from Imam Malik ibn Anas with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/44); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4703; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11190; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3075; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear (directly) from Umar." Likewise said Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah. Abu Hatim added: "Between them is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah."

What Abu Hatim said was also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, from Baqiyyah, from Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi [[In A: "Amr ibn Khath'am".]], from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I was with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾," and then he mentioned it [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4704. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir (13/235) from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, with the same chain.]].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 7, verses 172–174 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni said: Abu Farwa al-Rahawi also followed 'Umar ibn Ju'thum ibn Zayd ibn Sinan, and their version is closer to the correct one than Malik's version. And Allah knows best. [[al-'Ilal of al-Daraqutni (2/221–223).]]

I say: It appears that Imam Malik deliberately omitted the mention of "Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah," because he did not know his condition and did not recognize him, for he is not known except in this hadith. Likewise, he omits the mention of a group of narrators whom he does not approve of. For this reason, he often cites hadiths as mursal (with a missing companion) and cuts short many connected (mawsul) chains. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: At-Tirmidhi, in his commentary on this verse, said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from A.]] created Adam, He wiped over his back, and from his back there fell every soul He would create from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection. He placed between the eyes of each of them a gleam of light. Then He presented them to Adam, and [Adam] said: 'O Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' He saw among them a man whose gleam between his eyes impressed him, and he said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is a man from the last of the nations from your descendants; his name is Dawud (David).' He said: 'Lord, how long have You made his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'O Lord, add to his life forty years from mine.' When the life of Adam had ended, the Angel of Death came to him. He said: 'Have not forty years of my life remained?' He said: 'Have you not given them to your son Dawud?' He said: So Adam denied it, and his descendants denied it; Adam forgot, and his descendants forgot; Adam erred, and his descendants erred."

Then at-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak, through the hadith of Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, with the same chain. He said: Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3076), and al-Mustadrak (2/325).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir (exegesis), through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that he related to him from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning something similar to what came before, until he said: "Then He presented them to Adam and said: 'O Adam, these are your descendants.' And among them were the leprous, the lepers, the blind, and various kinds of illnesses. Adam said: 'O Lord, why have You done this to my descendants?' He said: 'So that My blessing may be thanked.' Adam said: 'O Lord, among these whom You have shown me, who are the people with the most light?' He said: 'These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.'" Then he mentioned the story of Dawud, similar to what came before. [[Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (1015), through the route of Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Another hadith: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatadah al-Nasri [[In A: "al-Basri."]] narrated from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim [may Allah be pleased with him], that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, are deeds begun (decided anew), or has the decree already been determined?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then He scattered them into His two palms." Then he said: "These are in Paradise and these are in the Fire. The people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various routes from him. [[Tafsir at-Tabari (13/244). Shaykh Mahmud Shakir has discussed it at length in the footnote, sufficient to not repeat it here.]]

Another hadith: Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, who is weak, narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation and decreed the decree, He took the people of the right with His right hand and the people of the left with His left hand. He said: 'O people of the right!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O people of the left!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' Then He mixed them together. A speaker said: 'O Lord, why did You mix them together?' He said: 'For them are deeds other than that, which they will perform, so that they may say on the Day of Resurrection: We were indeed unaware of this.' Then He returned them into the loins of Adam [peace be upon him] [[Addition from A.]]." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/287) through the route of Uthman ibn al-Haytham, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, with it. Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr is very weak, but he has a follower: Bishr ibn Numayr narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with something similar. Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (228), and al-Uqayli in ad-Du'afa al-Kabir (1/51). However, one should not rejoice in this follow-up, for Bishr ibn Numayr is abandoned (matruk) and accused (muttaham).]]

Another report: Abu Ja'far ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ and the verse that follows, he said: "He gathered them for Him on that day, all of them, all that would exist from them until the Day of Resurrection. He made them into spirits, then fashioned them, then made them speak, and He took from them the covenant and the pledge, and He made them testify against themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes,' and so on." He said: "I call upon the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call upon your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We did not know of this.' Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, so do not associate anything with Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you My books." They said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord but You, and no god but You." So they acknowledged to Him on that day their obedience. And their father Adam was raised up, and he looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and those below that. He said: "O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?" He said: "I have loved to be thanked." He saw among them the prophets like lamps, upon whom was light, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning messengership and prophethood. This is what Allah, Exalted is He, means by: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 7]. And this is what He means: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30], and from this He said: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [An-Najm: 56], and from this He said: ﴿And We found most of them not upholding any covenant; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-A'raf: 102].

Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad of his father, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in their exegeses (tafasir), through the narration of Ibn Ja'far ar-Razi, with it. It is also narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, as-Suddi, and many other scholars of the early generations, with accounts that agree with these hadiths. We have contented ourselves with citing them rather than lengthening discussion of all those reports. And from Allah we seek help.

These hadiths indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. As for the making of them testify there that He is their Lord, this appears only in the hadith of Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr."]] from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]], and in the hadith of Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]]. We have already explained that both of these are mawquf (ending with a companion), not marfu' (attributed to the Prophet), as previously mentioned. For this reason, some scholars of the early and later generations have said that the intended meaning of this testimony is only their being created upon monotheism (tawhid), as mentioned earlier in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, and in the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from al-Aswad ibn Sari'. Al-Hasan al-Basri explained the verse in this way. They said: That is why He said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam﴾ and did not say "from Adam"; ﴿from their loins﴾ and did not say "from his loin"; ﴿their descendants﴾, meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ [Al-An'am: 165], and He said: ﴿And makes you successors upon the earth﴾ [An-Naml: 62], and He said: ﴿As He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾ [Al-An'am: 133].

Then He said: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ That is, He caused them to be witnesses to this, speaking to Him through their state and their words. Testimony is sometimes by speech, as He said: ﴿They will say, "We testify against ourselves"﴾ [Al-An'am: 130], and sometimes it is by state, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief﴾ [At-Tawbah: 17]; that is, their condition bears witness against them, not that they are speaking that. Likewise is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [Al-'Adiyat: 7]. Just as a question is sometimes by speech and sometimes by state, as in His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

They said: Among what indicates that this is the intended meaning is that He made this testimony a proof against them in associating partners with Him. If this had happened as the one who said it claimed, then everyone would remember it, so that it would be a proof against them. If it is said: The Messenger's informing about it is sufficient to establish its existence. The answer: The polytheists who deny the truth reject everything the messengers brought them, including this and other things. This was made an independent proof against them, which indicates that it is the natural disposition (fitrah) upon which they were created, which is the acknowledgment of monotheism. That is why He said: ﴿lest you say﴾, that is, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, we were of this (tawhid) unaware,﴾ or ﴿say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were only descendants after them..."﴾, and so on.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 172–174 (part 1 of 2):

He, may He be exalted, informs us that He brought forth the offspring of the children of Adam from their loins, making them bear witness against themselves that Allah is their Lord and Sovereign, and that there is no god but Him. Just as He, may He be exalted, created them upon this and instilled it in their natures, He said: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He has created mankind. There is no altering of the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30]. In the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah," and in another narration, "upon this religion (millah). Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Himar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah [Exalted] says: 'I created My servants as hunafa' (upright in faith), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2865; its chain and the preceding one were cited under verse 30.]].

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan narrated to them, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' of the Banu Sa'd, who said: I fought alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in four campaigns. He said: The people targeted the offspring after they had killed the combatants. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it displeased him greatly. Then he said: "What is the matter with people that they target the offspring?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not the children of polytheists?" He said: "Indeed, the best of you are the children of polytheists! Verily, there is no soul born except that it is born upon the fitrah, and it remains upon it until its tongue speaks for it. Then its parents make it a Jew or a Christian." Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, Allah has indeed said in His Book: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves [and made them bear witness over themselves]﴾ [[Addition from A.]], and so on [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/321).]]. Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (3/435).]]. Al-Nasa'i also recorded it in his Sunan from the narration of Hushaim, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "al-Aswad ibn Sari' narrated to us," and so he mentioned it, but he did not mention al-Hasan's statement or his recollection of the verse at that point [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 8616.]].

Traditions have been related about the taking of the offspring from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and their separation into the people of the right and the people of the left. In some of them there is the call to witness against them that Allah is their Lord.

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It will be said to a man of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: 'Tell me, if you had all that is on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will be told: 'You were asked for something easier than that, when you were in the loins of Adam: that you should not associate anything with Me. But you refused except to associate.'"

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs, from the narration of Shu'bah with the same chain [[al-Musnad (3/127); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3334; Sahih Muslim, no. 2805.]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Jarir (meaning Ibn Hazim) narrated to us, from Kulthum ibn Jabir [[In K and M: "Jabr"; in A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah took the covenant from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, at Nu'man, meaning [[In K, M and A: "on the day of".]] Arafah. He brought forth from his loins every offspring He had created, and scattered them before Him. Then He spoke to them directly, saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes, we testify﴾ ... [up to] ﴿the falsifiers﴾" [[Lit.: the wrongdoers; the verse ends with the word al-mubtilun, "the falsifiers" or "those who nullify (the truth)."]].

Al-Nasa'i also recorded this hadith in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, with the same chain. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/272); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11191; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/222). Al-Nasa'i said: "Kulthum here is not strong, and his hadith is not preserved."]]. However, Ibn Abi Hatim made it a mawquf (a narration ending with a Companion). Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak from the narration of Husayn ibn Muhammad and others, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Kulthum ibn Jabr, with the same chain, and said: "Its chain is sahih, but they did not record it." He also said: "Muslim relied on Kulthum ibn Jubayr." Thus he said [[In K and M: "Jabr".]] [[al-Mustadrak (1/27).]]. But Abd al-Warith narrated it from Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, and stopped it at Ibn Abbas [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/172).]]. Likewise, Isma'il ibn Ulayyah and Waki' narrated it from Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum, from Jubayr, from his father, with the same wording [[Al-Tabari, Tafsir (13/224) via Ibn Ulayyah, and (13/229) via Waki'.]]. Likewise, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, Habib ibn Abi Thabit and Ali ibn Badhimah narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, as his own statement [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/227–229).]]. Likewise, al-Awfi and Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated it from Ibn Abbas [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/236–237).]]. This is more widespread and more firmly established, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abu Hilal, from Abu Jamrah al-Duba'i, from Ibn Abbas [[Addition from A.]], who said: Allah brought forth the offspring of Adam [[Addition from A.]], from his back, like the particles (al-dharr), while they were in a pool of water.

He also said: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, Abu Mas'ud narrated to us, from Jubayr, who said: A son of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim died, and he was six days old. He said: "O Jabir, when you place my son in his grave, uncover his face and loosen his knots, for my son will be questioned and asked." So I did what he commanded. When I had finished, I said: "May Allah have mercy on you, about what will your son be questioned? And who will ask him?" He said: "He will be asked about the covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam." I said: "O Abu al-Qasim, and what is this covenant that he affirmed in the loins of Adam?" He said: "Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to me that Allah passed His hand over the loins of Adam and brought forth from them every soul He would create until the Day of Resurrection. He took from them the covenant that they would worship Him and not associate anything with Him, and He guaranteed them their provision. Then He returned them to his loins. So the Hour will not be established until those who gave the covenant on that day are born. Whoever among them reaches the later covenant and fulfils it, the first covenant benefits him. And whoever reaches the later covenant and does not fulfil it, the first covenant does not benefit him. Whoever dies young before reaching the later covenant dies upon the first covenant, upon the fitrah" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/230).]].

All these routes strengthen the view that this report is a statement of Ibn Abbas, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dahhak and from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ He said: "He took from his back as the comb is drawn through the hair of the head. Then He said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿Yes.﴾" The angels said: ﴿We testify﴾ [[In A: "lest you say"; the text reads "lest they say".]] on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/232). Al-Tabari said: "I do not know it to be sound, because the trustworthy narrators whose memory and precision are relied upon narrated this hadith from al-Thawri and made it end with Abd Allah ibn Amr, not raising it to the Prophet, and they did not mention in it this phrase that Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah reported from him."]].

Ahmad ibn Abi Tayyibah is Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani, judge of Qumis. He was one of the ascetics. Al-Nasa'i recorded from him in his Sunan. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "His hadith is written down." Ibn Adi said: "He narrated hadiths, most of which are gharib (rare, singular narrations)" [[In K, M and A: "many".]].

This hadith was also narrated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, as his own statement. Likewise Jarir narrated it from Mansur with the same chain. This is more sound, and Allah knows best [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh, that is Ibn Ubadah, narrated to us, Malik narrated to us; and Ishaq narrated to us, Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah: that Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani: that Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes"﴾, and so on. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being asked about it, and he said: 'Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, then passed His hand over his back with His right hand, and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for Paradise, and they will act with the deeds of the people of Paradise." Then He passed His hand over his back again and brought forth from him offspring. He said: "I have created these for the Fire, and they will act with the deeds of the people of the Fire."'" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and so He admits him to Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire, until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and so He admits him to the Fire because of it."

This was narrated in the same way by Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, and al-Tirmidhi from Ishaq ibn Musa, from Ma'n. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Rawh ibn Ubadah and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far. Ibn Hibban recorded it in his Sahih from the narration of Abu Mus'ab al-Zubayri. All of them narrated it from Imam Malik ibn Anas with the same chain [[al-Musnad (1/44); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4703; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11190; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3075; Tafsir al-Tabari (13/233).]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear (directly) from Umar." Likewise said Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah. Abu Hatim added: "Between them is Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah."

What Abu Hatim said was also narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, from Baqiyyah, from Umar ibn Ju'thum al-Qurashi [[In A: "Amr ibn Khath'am".]], from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn al-Khattab, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah, who said: "I was with Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was asked about this verse: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾," and then he mentioned it [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4704. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir (13/235) from Muhammad ibn Musaffa, with the same chain.]].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 7, verses 172–174 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hafiz al-Daraqutni said: Abu Farwa al-Rahawi also followed 'Umar ibn Ju'thum ibn Zayd ibn Sinan, and their version is closer to the correct one than Malik's version. And Allah knows best. [[al-'Ilal of al-Daraqutni (2/221–223).]]

I say: It appears that Imam Malik deliberately omitted the mention of "Nu'aym ibn Rabi'ah," because he did not know his condition and did not recognize him, for he is not known except in this hadith. Likewise, he omits the mention of a group of narrators whom he does not approve of. For this reason, he often cites hadiths as mursal (with a missing companion) and cuts short many connected (mawsul) chains. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: At-Tirmidhi, in his commentary on this verse, said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah [Mighty and Majestic] [[Addition from A.]] created Adam, He wiped over his back, and from his back there fell every soul He would create from his descendants until the Day of Resurrection. He placed between the eyes of each of them a gleam of light. Then He presented them to Adam, and [Adam] said: 'O Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' He saw among them a man whose gleam between his eyes impressed him, and he said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is a man from the last of the nations from your descendants; his name is Dawud (David).' He said: 'Lord, how long have You made his life?' He said: 'Sixty years.' He said: 'O Lord, add to his life forty years from mine.' When the life of Adam had ended, the Angel of Death came to him. He said: 'Have not forty years of my life remained?' He said: 'Have you not given them to your son Dawud?' He said: So Adam denied it, and his descendants denied it; Adam forgot, and his descendants forgot; Adam erred, and his descendants erred."

Then at-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Hakim narrated it in his al-Mustadrak, through the hadith of Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, with the same chain. He said: Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3076), and al-Mustadrak (2/325).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his tafsir (exegesis), through the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that he related to him from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning something similar to what came before, until he said: "Then He presented them to Adam and said: 'O Adam, these are your descendants.' And among them were the leprous, the lepers, the blind, and various kinds of illnesses. Adam said: 'O Lord, why have You done this to my descendants?' He said: 'So that My blessing may be thanked.' Adam said: 'O Lord, among these whom You have shown me, who are the people with the most light?' He said: 'These are the prophets, O Adam, from your descendants.'" Then he mentioned the story of Dawud, similar to what came before. [[Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (1015), through the route of Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, with it. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is weak.]]

Another hadith: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qatadah al-Nasri [[In A: "al-Basri."]] narrated from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim [may Allah be pleased with him], that a man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, are deeds begun (decided anew), or has the decree already been determined?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah took the descendants of Adam from their backs, then made them testify against themselves, then He scattered them into His two palms." Then he said: "These are in Paradise and these are in the Fire. The people of Paradise are made easy for the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are made easy for the deeds of the people of the Fire."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various routes from him. [[Tafsir at-Tabari (13/244). Shaykh Mahmud Shakir has discussed it at length in the footnote, sufficient to not repeat it here.]]

Another hadith: Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, who is weak, narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation and decreed the decree, He took the people of the right with His right hand and the people of the left with His left hand. He said: 'O people of the right!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'O people of the left!' They said: 'Here we are, at Your service and Your pleasure!' He said: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes.' Then He mixed them together. A speaker said: 'O Lord, why did You mix them together?' He said: 'For them are deeds other than that, which they will perform, so that they may say on the Day of Resurrection: We were indeed unaware of this.' Then He returned them into the loins of Adam [peace be upon him] [[Addition from A.]]." Ibn Mardawayh narrated it. [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/287) through the route of Uthman ibn al-Haytham, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, with it. Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr is very weak, but he has a follower: Bishr ibn Numayr narrated from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, with something similar. Abu ash-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, no. (228), and al-Uqayli in ad-Du'afa al-Kabir (1/51). However, one should not rejoice in this follow-up, for Bishr ibn Numayr is abandoned (matruk) and accused (muttaham).]]

Another report: Abu Ja'far ar-Razi narrated from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ and the verse that follows, he said: "He gathered them for Him on that day, all of them, all that would exist from them until the Day of Resurrection. He made them into spirits, then fashioned them, then made them speak, and He took from them the covenant and the pledge, and He made them testify against themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes,' and so on." He said: "I call upon the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call upon your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We did not know of this.' Know that there is no god but Me, and no lord but Me, so do not associate anything with Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you My books." They said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; we have no lord but You, and no god but You." So they acknowledged to Him on that day their obedience. And their father Adam was raised up, and he looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and those below that. He said: "O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?" He said: "I have loved to be thanked." He saw among them the prophets like lamps, upon whom was light, and they were singled out with another covenant concerning messengership and prophethood. This is what Allah, Exalted is He, means by: ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 7]. And this is what He means: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the natural disposition (fitrah) of Allah upon which He created mankind; there is no alteration in the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30], and from this He said: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [An-Najm: 56], and from this He said: ﴿And We found most of them not upholding any covenant; indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-A'raf: 102].

Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad of his father, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in their exegeses (tafasir), through the narration of Ibn Ja'far ar-Razi, with it. It is also narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, as-Suddi, and many other scholars of the early generations, with accounts that agree with these hadiths. We have contented ourselves with citing them rather than lengthening discussion of all those reports. And from Allah we seek help.

These hadiths indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam from his loins and distinguished between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. As for the making of them testify there that He is their Lord, this appears only in the hadith of Kulthum ibn Jabr [[In A: "Jubayr."]] from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]], and in the hadith of Abd Allah ibn 'Amr [may Allah be pleased with both of them] [[Addition from A.]]. We have already explained that both of these are mawquf (ending with a companion), not marfu' (attributed to the Prophet), as previously mentioned. For this reason, some scholars of the early and later generations have said that the intended meaning of this testimony is only their being created upon monotheism (tawhid), as mentioned earlier in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, and in the narration of al-Hasan al-Basri from al-Aswad ibn Sari'. Al-Hasan al-Basri explained the verse in this way. They said: That is why He said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam﴾ and did not say "from Adam"; ﴿from their loins﴾ and did not say "from his loin"; ﴿their descendants﴾, meaning He made their offspring generation after generation and century after century, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ [Al-An'am: 165], and He said: ﴿And makes you successors upon the earth﴾ [An-Naml: 62], and He said: ﴿As He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾ [Al-An'am: 133].

Then He said: ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ That is, He caused them to be witnesses to this, speaking to Him through their state and their words. Testimony is sometimes by speech, as He said: ﴿They will say, "We testify against ourselves"﴾ [Al-An'am: 130], and sometimes it is by state, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief﴾ [At-Tawbah: 17]; that is, their condition bears witness against them, not that they are speaking that. Likewise is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [Al-'Adiyat: 7]. Just as a question is sometimes by speech and sometimes by state, as in His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

They said: Among what indicates that this is the intended meaning is that He made this testimony a proof against them in associating partners with Him. If this had happened as the one who said it claimed, then everyone would remember it, so that it would be a proof against them. If it is said: The Messenger's informing about it is sufficient to establish its existence. The answer: The polytheists who deny the truth reject everything the messengers brought them, including this and other things. This was made an independent proof against them, which indicates that it is the natural disposition (fitrah) upon which they were created, which is the acknowledgment of monotheism. That is why He said: ﴿lest you say﴾, that is, lest they say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Indeed, we were of this (tawhid) unaware,﴾ or ﴿say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were only descendants after them..."﴾, and so on.

And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them...

Abd al-Razzaq related from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash and Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them [and Satan pursued him]﴾ [[Addition from MS K.]] "...to the end of the verse." He said: "He was a man from the Children of Israel, called Bal'am ibn Abar." Shu'bah and others also related this from Mansur, with the same wording.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both [[Addition from MS A.]]: "He was Sayfi ibn al-Rahib."

Qatadah said: Ka'b said: "He was a man from the people of al-Balqa', who knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-akbar), and he resided in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) among the Jabbarin (the tyrannical giants)."

al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was a man from the people of Yemen, called Bal'am. Allah gave him His signs, but he abandoned them."

Malik ibn Dinar said: "He was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel, and his supplication was answered (mujab al-da'wah). They would put him forward in times of hardship. The Prophet of Allah, Musa, sent him to the king of Madyan to invite him to Allah. [The king] bribed him and gave him gifts, so he followed the king's religion and abandoned the religion of Musa, peace be upon him."

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, from Husayn, from Imran ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was Bal'am ibn Ba'ir." Mujahid and Ikrimah also said the same.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: al-Harith related to me, from Abd al-Aziz, from Israil, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "He was Bil'am." [And Thaqif said: "He was Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."]

Shu'bah said, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from Nafi' ibn Asim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our [signs]﴾ [[Addition from MSS K, M, A.]] He said: "He is your companion, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."

It has been reported through more than one channel from him [Ibn Amr], and it is sound as far as him. It seems that he only meant that Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt resembles him, for a great deal of knowledge of the earlier revealed laws had reached him. But he did not benefit from his knowledge, for he lived to see the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His signs, indications and miracles reached him and became manifest to everyone who had insight. Despite this, he met him but did not follow him. He sided with the polytheists, supported them and praised them, and he composed an eloquent elegy for the polytheists who fell at Badr. May Allah disfigure him [[Addition from MS A.]]. [[See: al-Aqidah fi al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham (2/30).]] It has come in some hadiths: "He was among those whose tongues professed faith but whose hearts did not believe." For he had divinely inspired verses, wise sayings and eloquence, but Allah did not open his heart to Islam.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-A'war, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them﴾. He said: "He was a man given three supplications which would be answered for him. He had a wife by whom he had a child. She said: 'Make one of them for me.' He said: 'For you, one. What do you want?' She said: 'Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel.' So he prayed to Allah, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she became averse to him and wanted something else. So he prayed to Allah to make her a female dog, and she became a female dog. Thus two supplications were gone. Her sons came and said: 'We cannot bear this situation. Our mother has become a female dog, and people taunt us with her. Pray to Allah to return her to the state she was in.' So he prayed to Allah, and she returned as she had been. Thus the three supplications were gone, and she was named al-Basus." [[Related by Abu al-Shaykh in his Tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/608).]] This is gharib (a rare report, transmitted through a weak or single channel).

As for what is well known concerning the occasion of revelation of this noble verse, it is a man from among the earlier people of the time of the Children of Israel, as Ibn Mas'ud and others among the early scholars (al-salaf) said.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "He was a man from the city of the Jabbarin, called Bal'am, and he knew the Greatest Name of Allah."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others among the early scholars said: "[He was a man] whose supplication was answered; he never asked Allah for anything without being given it."

Whoever said that he had been given prophethood and then drew away from it is strange, rather far off, rather mistaken. Al-Tabari transmitted this from some of them, but it is not sound.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "When Musa encamped with them, meaning with the Jabbarin, and those with him, Bal'am's kinsmen and people came to him and said: 'Musa is a formidable man, and he has many soldiers with him. If he prevails over us, he will destroy us. So pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him from us.' He said: 'If I pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him, I will lose my worldly life and my hereafter.' They kept at him until he prayed against them, so Allah stripped from him what he had. This is the words of Allah: ﴿Then he drew away from them, and Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided﴾."

Al-Suddi said: "When the forty years which Allah mentioned, ﴿So it is forbidden to them for forty years﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 26], ended, Allah sent Yusha' ibn Nun as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet and that Allah had commanded him to fight the Jabbarin. So they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am set out. He was a scholar who knew the hidden Greatest Name. He disbelieved, may Allah curse him, came to the Jabbarin and said to them: 'Do not fear the Children of Israel. When you go out to fight them, I will invoke a curse upon them and they will perish!' He had among them whatever worldly things he wished, except that he could not approach women, so he would marry a she-donkey of his." He is the one of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then he drew away from them﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he took control of him and overpowered him in his affairs, so whatever [Satan] commanded him, he obeyed and submitted to. Therefore He said: ﴿And he became of the misguided﴾, meaning of those who perished, bewildered, and ruined.

A hadith has come concerning the meaning of this verse, which al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, from al-Salt ibn Bahram, al-Hasan related to us, Jundub al-Bajali related to us in this mosque, that Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, related to him, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among what I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur'an, until when its splendour is seen upon him and he has become a supporter of Islam, he is struck by [something] as Allah wills, and he draws away from it, casts it behind his back, pursues his neighbour with the sword, and accuses him of polytheism." He [Hudhayfah] said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, which of them is more deserving of polytheism, the accused or the accuser?" He said: "Rather, the accuser."

This is a good chain of narration [[Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (175), by the route: Muhammad ibn Marzuq and al-Hasan ibn Abi Kabshah related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Barsani related to us with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/188): "Its chain is hasan (good)."]]. Al-Salt ibn Bahram was among the trustworthy Kufans, and he was accused of nothing except Irja' (the doctrine of postponement). Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy.

* *

And His words: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them﴾, meaning We would have raised him above the defilement of the filth of this world by the signs which We had given him. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾, meaning he inclined towards the adornment and splendour of this world, turned to its pleasures and luxuries, and was deluded by it as it deluded others who were not people of insight and intellect.

Abu al-Zahiriyyah said, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾: "Satan appeared to him at a distance of a bowshot from the bridge of Banyas, and the she-donkey prostrated to Allah while Bal'am prostrated to Satan." Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others also said the same.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: From the story of this man is what Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, from al-Mu'tamir, from his father, that he was asked about this verse: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, [but he drew away from them]﴾ [[Addition from MS A.]]. He related from Sayyar that he was a man called Bal'am, who had been given prophethood and was one whose supplication was answered. He said: "Musa came with the Children of Israel, intending the land where Bal'am was, or he said: Syria. The people were struck with terrible fear of him. They came to Bal'am and said: 'Pray to Allah against this man and his army!' He said: 'Until I consult my Lord,' or 'until I consult [Him].' So he consulted about praying against them, and it was said to him: 'Do not pray against them, for they are My servants, and their Prophet is among them.' So he said to his people: 'I have consulted my Lord about praying against them, and I have been forbidden.' They presented him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: 'Pray against them!' He said: 'Until I consult.' So he consulted, but no reply came to him. He said: 'I have consulted, but nothing has come back to me!' They said: 'If your Lord disliked that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time.' So he began to pray against them, but whenever he prayed against them, the prayer against his own people came upon his tongue, and whenever he wanted to pray that victory be granted to his people, he prayed that victory be granted to Musa and his army, or something similar, if Allah wills." He said: [The people] said to him: "We see you pray only against us." He said: "Nothing flows upon my tongue except in this way. Even if I prayed against him, it would not be answered for me. But I will direct you to a matter by which their destruction may come about. Allah hates fornication, and if they fall into fornication they will perish, and I hope that Allah will destroy them. So send out the women to meet them, for they are a travelling people, and perhaps they will commit fornication and perish." He said: "They did so, and they sent out the women to meet them." He said: "The king had a daughter, and [the narrator] mentioned of her greatness what only Allah knows!" He said: "Her father, or Bal'am, said: 'Do not let yourself be given to anyone except Musa!'" He said: "And they fell into fornication. And a leader of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her, and he wanted her for himself. She said: 'I will not give myself except to Musa.' He said: 'My rank is such-and-such, and my position is such-and-such.' She sent to her father seeking his advice. He told her: 'Let him have her.'" He said: "A man from the descendants of Harun came with a spear and thrust it through both of them." He said: "Allah strengthened him with power. He pierced them both together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them, or as he related." He said: "Allah sent the plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 175–177 (part 2 of 2):

Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar narrated to me that Balam rode his donkey until, when he reached al-'Alawla (or he said: a road from al-'Alawla), he began to strike her and she would not move forward. She stood up against him and said: "Why are you striking me? Do you not see what is before you?" Then the Satan was in front of him. He said: So he dismounted and prostrated to it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾.

He said: Sayyar narrated this to me, and I do not know whether something from the narration of others has entered into it.

I say: He is Balam, also called Bulam, the son of Ba'ura', the son of Abar. It is also said: the son of Ba'ur, the son of Shuhum, the son of Qushtum, the son of Mab, the son of Lut, the son of Haran (also said: the son of Haran), the son of Azar. He used to live in a village from the villages of al-Balqa'.

Ibn 'Asakir said: He is the one who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, but he detached himself from his religion. He is mentioned in the Qur'an. Then he related from his story something similar to what we have mentioned here, and he related it from Wahb and others. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Salim Abi al-Nadr that he related: When Musa, peace be upon him, descended into the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balam came to him and said to him: "This is Musa ibn 'Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us, and to make them lawful to the Children of Israel. We are your people, and we have no dwelling place, and you are a man whose supplication is answered. So go out and invoke Allah against them." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah is with him, with the angels and the believers. How can I go to invoke against them, when I know from Allah what I know?!" They said to him: "We have no dwelling!" They kept on at him, softening him and humbling themselves before him, until they tempted him, and he was tempted. He mounted his she-donkey heading toward the mountain from which he could overlook the army of the Children of Israel, which is the mountain of Husban. When she had carried him not far, she knelt down with him, so he dismounted and struck her until he had worn her out, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far with him before she knelt down with him again, and he struck her until he had worn her out. Then Allah permitted her to speak, as a proof against him, and she said: "Woe to you, O Balam! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me back from this direction? Are you going to the Prophet of Allah and the believers so that you may invoke against them?" But he did not desist from striking her, so Allah released her when he did that to her. She set off with him until, when she brought him up over the top of Husban, overlooking the army of Musa and the Children of Israel, he began to invoke against them, but whenever he invoked against them with evil, Allah turned his tongue toward his own people, and whenever he invoked for his people with good, he turned his tongue toward the Children of Israel. His people said to him: "Do you know, O Balam, what you are doing? You are invoking for them and invoking against us!" He said: "This is what I do not control; this is a matter over which Allah has prevailed!" He said: His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest. He said to them: "Now the world and the Hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deception and trickery. I will devise a plan for you and scheme. Adorn the women and give them merchandise, then send them to the army to sell it there, and instruct them that no woman should refuse herself to a man who desires her, for if one man of them commits fornication, you will be rid of them." They did so. When the women entered the army, a woman of the Kan'anites named "Kasbi daughter of Sur, the chief of her people," passed by a man from the great men of the Children of Israel, who was "Zamri ibn Shalum," the chief of the tribe of the Banu Sam'an ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them. He went to her, took her hand when her beauty pleased him, then brought her and stood with her before Musa, peace be upon him, and said: "I suppose you will say this is forbidden to you?" He said: "Yes, she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and had intercourse with her. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the plague upon the Children of Israel. Finhas ibn al-'Ayzar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, had been absent when Zamri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel, and he was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was entirely of iron, then entered the tent while they were lying together, and he pierced them both with his spear. Then he carried them out raised up toward the sky, with the spear still in his grip, having taken hold of it with his forearm, leaning with his elbow on his side, and resting the spear against his jaw. He was the firstborn of al-'Ayzar. He kept saying: "O Allah, this is how we deal with those who disobey You." The plague was lifted. The number of those among the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the moment Zamri struck the woman until Finhas killed him, was counted, and they found that seventy thousand had died, though the one who gave the lesser figure said twenty thousand, in a single hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel have given the descendants of Finhas the forequarter, the foreleg and the jaw of every sacrificial animal they slaughter, and the firstborn of all their property and their persons, because he was the firstborn of his father al-'Ayzar. Concerning Balam ibn Ba'ura', Allah revealed: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them [then Satan followed him]﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/264).]

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So his likeness is like that of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾, the exegetes differed concerning its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, from Salim ibn Abi al-Nadr, that Balam's tongue hung out upon his chest, the comparison to the dog is in its panting in both of its states, whether it is driven away or left alone. It was also said: its meaning is that he became like that in his error and his persistence in it, and in his not benefiting from being called to faith or from not being called, like the dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack it or if you leave it, it pants in both conditions. Likewise, this man does not benefit from admonition and the call to faith, nor from its absence, as the Exalted said: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 6], and ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 80], and similar to that.

It was also said: its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the misguided is weak, empty of guidance, and so it pounds constantly; so this was expressed by that. This has been transmitted in similar terms from al-Hasan al-Basri and others.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: perhaps the Children of Israel, who know the condition of Balam and what happened to him, when Allah misguided him and removed him from His mercy, because he used the blessing of Allah upon him, in teaching him the Greatest Name, by which when one asks, He gives, and when one calls upon Him, He responds, in other than the obedience of his Lord. Rather, he invoked by it against the party of the Most Merciful and the branch of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger in that time, Musa ibn 'Imran, the one who spoke with Allah, peace be upon him. Therefore He said: ﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: that they may beware of becoming like him. For Allah has given them knowledge and distinguished them over all others among the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), which they recognize just as they recognize their own sons. So they are the most deserving of people and the most entitled to follow him, support him and aid him, just as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to it. Therefore, whoever among them opposes what is in His Book and conceals it, not informing the servants of it, Allah will inflict upon him humiliation in this world, joined with the humiliation of the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and used to wrong themselves﴾, the Exalted says: evil is the example, the likeness of the people who denied Our signs; that is, evil is their likeness in being compared to dogs, which have no concern except obtaining a morsel or a desire. Whoever departs from the sphere of knowledge and guidance and turns to the desire of his self, following his whims, becomes like the dog, and evil is the likeness of him. Therefore it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no such evil likeness: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that returns to its vomit." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2622).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they used to wrong themselves﴾, meaning: Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, inclining toward the abode of decay and turning to the attainment of pleasures and the pursuit of desire.

And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them...

Abd al-Razzaq related from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash and Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them [and Satan pursued him]﴾ [[Addition from MS K.]] "...to the end of the verse." He said: "He was a man from the Children of Israel, called Bal'am ibn Abar." Shu'bah and others also related this from Mansur, with the same wording.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both [[Addition from MS A.]]: "He was Sayfi ibn al-Rahib."

Qatadah said: Ka'b said: "He was a man from the people of al-Balqa', who knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-akbar), and he resided in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) among the Jabbarin (the tyrannical giants)."

al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was a man from the people of Yemen, called Bal'am. Allah gave him His signs, but he abandoned them."

Malik ibn Dinar said: "He was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel, and his supplication was answered (mujab al-da'wah). They would put him forward in times of hardship. The Prophet of Allah, Musa, sent him to the king of Madyan to invite him to Allah. [The king] bribed him and gave him gifts, so he followed the king's religion and abandoned the religion of Musa, peace be upon him."

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, from Husayn, from Imran ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was Bal'am ibn Ba'ir." Mujahid and Ikrimah also said the same.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: al-Harith related to me, from Abd al-Aziz, from Israil, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "He was Bil'am." [And Thaqif said: "He was Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."]

Shu'bah said, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from Nafi' ibn Asim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our [signs]﴾ [[Addition from MSS K, M, A.]] He said: "He is your companion, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."

It has been reported through more than one channel from him [Ibn Amr], and it is sound as far as him. It seems that he only meant that Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt resembles him, for a great deal of knowledge of the earlier revealed laws had reached him. But he did not benefit from his knowledge, for he lived to see the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His signs, indications and miracles reached him and became manifest to everyone who had insight. Despite this, he met him but did not follow him. He sided with the polytheists, supported them and praised them, and he composed an eloquent elegy for the polytheists who fell at Badr. May Allah disfigure him [[Addition from MS A.]]. [[See: al-Aqidah fi al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham (2/30).]] It has come in some hadiths: "He was among those whose tongues professed faith but whose hearts did not believe." For he had divinely inspired verses, wise sayings and eloquence, but Allah did not open his heart to Islam.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-A'war, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them﴾. He said: "He was a man given three supplications which would be answered for him. He had a wife by whom he had a child. She said: 'Make one of them for me.' He said: 'For you, one. What do you want?' She said: 'Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel.' So he prayed to Allah, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she became averse to him and wanted something else. So he prayed to Allah to make her a female dog, and she became a female dog. Thus two supplications were gone. Her sons came and said: 'We cannot bear this situation. Our mother has become a female dog, and people taunt us with her. Pray to Allah to return her to the state she was in.' So he prayed to Allah, and she returned as she had been. Thus the three supplications were gone, and she was named al-Basus." [[Related by Abu al-Shaykh in his Tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/608).]] This is gharib (a rare report, transmitted through a weak or single channel).

As for what is well known concerning the occasion of revelation of this noble verse, it is a man from among the earlier people of the time of the Children of Israel, as Ibn Mas'ud and others among the early scholars (al-salaf) said.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "He was a man from the city of the Jabbarin, called Bal'am, and he knew the Greatest Name of Allah."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others among the early scholars said: "[He was a man] whose supplication was answered; he never asked Allah for anything without being given it."

Whoever said that he had been given prophethood and then drew away from it is strange, rather far off, rather mistaken. Al-Tabari transmitted this from some of them, but it is not sound.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "When Musa encamped with them, meaning with the Jabbarin, and those with him, Bal'am's kinsmen and people came to him and said: 'Musa is a formidable man, and he has many soldiers with him. If he prevails over us, he will destroy us. So pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him from us.' He said: 'If I pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him, I will lose my worldly life and my hereafter.' They kept at him until he prayed against them, so Allah stripped from him what he had. This is the words of Allah: ﴿Then he drew away from them, and Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided﴾."

Al-Suddi said: "When the forty years which Allah mentioned, ﴿So it is forbidden to them for forty years﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 26], ended, Allah sent Yusha' ibn Nun as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet and that Allah had commanded him to fight the Jabbarin. So they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am set out. He was a scholar who knew the hidden Greatest Name. He disbelieved, may Allah curse him, came to the Jabbarin and said to them: 'Do not fear the Children of Israel. When you go out to fight them, I will invoke a curse upon them and they will perish!' He had among them whatever worldly things he wished, except that he could not approach women, so he would marry a she-donkey of his." He is the one of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then he drew away from them﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he took control of him and overpowered him in his affairs, so whatever [Satan] commanded him, he obeyed and submitted to. Therefore He said: ﴿And he became of the misguided﴾, meaning of those who perished, bewildered, and ruined.

A hadith has come concerning the meaning of this verse, which al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, from al-Salt ibn Bahram, al-Hasan related to us, Jundub al-Bajali related to us in this mosque, that Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, related to him, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among what I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur'an, until when its splendour is seen upon him and he has become a supporter of Islam, he is struck by [something] as Allah wills, and he draws away from it, casts it behind his back, pursues his neighbour with the sword, and accuses him of polytheism." He [Hudhayfah] said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, which of them is more deserving of polytheism, the accused or the accuser?" He said: "Rather, the accuser."

This is a good chain of narration [[Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (175), by the route: Muhammad ibn Marzuq and al-Hasan ibn Abi Kabshah related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Barsani related to us with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/188): "Its chain is hasan (good)."]]. Al-Salt ibn Bahram was among the trustworthy Kufans, and he was accused of nothing except Irja' (the doctrine of postponement). Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy.

* *

And His words: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them﴾, meaning We would have raised him above the defilement of the filth of this world by the signs which We had given him. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾, meaning he inclined towards the adornment and splendour of this world, turned to its pleasures and luxuries, and was deluded by it as it deluded others who were not people of insight and intellect.

Abu al-Zahiriyyah said, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾: "Satan appeared to him at a distance of a bowshot from the bridge of Banyas, and the she-donkey prostrated to Allah while Bal'am prostrated to Satan." Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others also said the same.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: From the story of this man is what Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, from al-Mu'tamir, from his father, that he was asked about this verse: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, [but he drew away from them]﴾ [[Addition from MS A.]]. He related from Sayyar that he was a man called Bal'am, who had been given prophethood and was one whose supplication was answered. He said: "Musa came with the Children of Israel, intending the land where Bal'am was, or he said: Syria. The people were struck with terrible fear of him. They came to Bal'am and said: 'Pray to Allah against this man and his army!' He said: 'Until I consult my Lord,' or 'until I consult [Him].' So he consulted about praying against them, and it was said to him: 'Do not pray against them, for they are My servants, and their Prophet is among them.' So he said to his people: 'I have consulted my Lord about praying against them, and I have been forbidden.' They presented him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: 'Pray against them!' He said: 'Until I consult.' So he consulted, but no reply came to him. He said: 'I have consulted, but nothing has come back to me!' They said: 'If your Lord disliked that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time.' So he began to pray against them, but whenever he prayed against them, the prayer against his own people came upon his tongue, and whenever he wanted to pray that victory be granted to his people, he prayed that victory be granted to Musa and his army, or something similar, if Allah wills." He said: [The people] said to him: "We see you pray only against us." He said: "Nothing flows upon my tongue except in this way. Even if I prayed against him, it would not be answered for me. But I will direct you to a matter by which their destruction may come about. Allah hates fornication, and if they fall into fornication they will perish, and I hope that Allah will destroy them. So send out the women to meet them, for they are a travelling people, and perhaps they will commit fornication and perish." He said: "They did so, and they sent out the women to meet them." He said: "The king had a daughter, and [the narrator] mentioned of her greatness what only Allah knows!" He said: "Her father, or Bal'am, said: 'Do not let yourself be given to anyone except Musa!'" He said: "And they fell into fornication. And a leader of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her, and he wanted her for himself. She said: 'I will not give myself except to Musa.' He said: 'My rank is such-and-such, and my position is such-and-such.' She sent to her father seeking his advice. He told her: 'Let him have her.'" He said: "A man from the descendants of Harun came with a spear and thrust it through both of them." He said: "Allah strengthened him with power. He pierced them both together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them, or as he related." He said: "Allah sent the plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 175–177 (part 2 of 2):

Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar narrated to me that Balam rode his donkey until, when he reached al-'Alawla (or he said: a road from al-'Alawla), he began to strike her and she would not move forward. She stood up against him and said: "Why are you striking me? Do you not see what is before you?" Then the Satan was in front of him. He said: So he dismounted and prostrated to it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾.

He said: Sayyar narrated this to me, and I do not know whether something from the narration of others has entered into it.

I say: He is Balam, also called Bulam, the son of Ba'ura', the son of Abar. It is also said: the son of Ba'ur, the son of Shuhum, the son of Qushtum, the son of Mab, the son of Lut, the son of Haran (also said: the son of Haran), the son of Azar. He used to live in a village from the villages of al-Balqa'.

Ibn 'Asakir said: He is the one who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, but he detached himself from his religion. He is mentioned in the Qur'an. Then he related from his story something similar to what we have mentioned here, and he related it from Wahb and others. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Salim Abi al-Nadr that he related: When Musa, peace be upon him, descended into the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balam came to him and said to him: "This is Musa ibn 'Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us, and to make them lawful to the Children of Israel. We are your people, and we have no dwelling place, and you are a man whose supplication is answered. So go out and invoke Allah against them." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah is with him, with the angels and the believers. How can I go to invoke against them, when I know from Allah what I know?!" They said to him: "We have no dwelling!" They kept on at him, softening him and humbling themselves before him, until they tempted him, and he was tempted. He mounted his she-donkey heading toward the mountain from which he could overlook the army of the Children of Israel, which is the mountain of Husban. When she had carried him not far, she knelt down with him, so he dismounted and struck her until he had worn her out, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far with him before she knelt down with him again, and he struck her until he had worn her out. Then Allah permitted her to speak, as a proof against him, and she said: "Woe to you, O Balam! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me back from this direction? Are you going to the Prophet of Allah and the believers so that you may invoke against them?" But he did not desist from striking her, so Allah released her when he did that to her. She set off with him until, when she brought him up over the top of Husban, overlooking the army of Musa and the Children of Israel, he began to invoke against them, but whenever he invoked against them with evil, Allah turned his tongue toward his own people, and whenever he invoked for his people with good, he turned his tongue toward the Children of Israel. His people said to him: "Do you know, O Balam, what you are doing? You are invoking for them and invoking against us!" He said: "This is what I do not control; this is a matter over which Allah has prevailed!" He said: His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest. He said to them: "Now the world and the Hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deception and trickery. I will devise a plan for you and scheme. Adorn the women and give them merchandise, then send them to the army to sell it there, and instruct them that no woman should refuse herself to a man who desires her, for if one man of them commits fornication, you will be rid of them." They did so. When the women entered the army, a woman of the Kan'anites named "Kasbi daughter of Sur, the chief of her people," passed by a man from the great men of the Children of Israel, who was "Zamri ibn Shalum," the chief of the tribe of the Banu Sam'an ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them. He went to her, took her hand when her beauty pleased him, then brought her and stood with her before Musa, peace be upon him, and said: "I suppose you will say this is forbidden to you?" He said: "Yes, she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and had intercourse with her. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the plague upon the Children of Israel.
