Finhas ibn al-'Ayzar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, had been absent when Zamri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel, and he was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was entirely of iron, then entered the tent while they were lying together, and he pierced them both with his spear. Then he carried them out raised up toward the sky, with the spear still in his grip, having taken hold of it with his forearm, leaning with his elbow on his side, and resting the spear against his jaw. He was the firstborn of al-'Ayzar. He kept saying: "O Allah, this is how we deal with those who disobey You." The plague was lifted. The number of those among the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the moment Zamri struck the woman until Finhas killed him, was counted, and they found that seventy thousand had died, though the one who gave the lesser figure said twenty thousand, in a single hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel have given the descendants of Finhas the forequarter, the foreleg and the jaw of every sacrificial animal they slaughter, and the firstborn of all their property and their persons, because he was the firstborn of his father al-'Ayzar. Concerning Balam ibn Ba'ura', Allah revealed: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them [then Satan followed him]﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/264).]

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So his likeness is like that of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾, the exegetes differed concerning its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, from Salim ibn Abi al-Nadr, that Balam's tongue hung out upon his chest, the comparison to the dog is in its panting in both of its states, whether it is driven away or left alone. It was also said: its meaning is that he became like that in his error and his persistence in it, and in his not benefiting from being called to faith or from not being called, like the dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack it or if you leave it, it pants in both conditions. Likewise, this man does not benefit from admonition and the call to faith, nor from its absence, as the Exalted said: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 6], and ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 80], and similar to that.

It was also said: its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the misguided is weak, empty of guidance, and so it pounds constantly; so this was expressed by that. This has been transmitted in similar terms from al-Hasan al-Basri and others.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: perhaps the Children of Israel, who know the condition of Balam and what happened to him, when Allah misguided him and removed him from His mercy, because he used the blessing of Allah upon him, in teaching him the Greatest Name, by which when one asks, He gives, and when one calls upon Him, He responds, in other than the obedience of his Lord. Rather, he invoked by it against the party of the Most Merciful and the branch of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger in that time, Musa ibn 'Imran, the one who spoke with Allah, peace be upon him. Therefore He said: ﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: that they may beware of becoming like him. For Allah has given them knowledge and distinguished them over all others among the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), which they recognize just as they recognize their own sons. So they are the most deserving of people and the most entitled to follow him, support him and aid him, just as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to it. Therefore, whoever among them opposes what is in His Book and conceals it, not informing the servants of it, Allah will inflict upon him humiliation in this world, joined with the humiliation of the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and used to wrong themselves﴾, the Exalted says: evil is the example, the likeness of the people who denied Our signs; that is, evil is their likeness in being compared to dogs, which have no concern except obtaining a morsel or a desire. Whoever departs from the sphere of knowledge and guidance and turns to the desire of his self, following his whims, becomes like the dog, and evil is the likeness of him. Therefore it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no such evil likeness: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that returns to its vomit." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2622).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they used to wrong themselves﴾, meaning: Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, inclining toward the abode of decay and turning to the attainment of pleasures and the pursuit of desire.

And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them...

Abd al-Razzaq related from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash and Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them [and Satan pursued him]﴾ [[Addition from MS K.]] "...to the end of the verse." He said: "He was a man from the Children of Israel, called Bal'am ibn Abar." Shu'bah and others also related this from Mansur, with the same wording.

Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah said, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both [[Addition from MS A.]]: "He was Sayfi ibn al-Rahib."

Qatadah said: Ka'b said: "He was a man from the people of al-Balqa', who knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-akbar), and he resided in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) among the Jabbarin (the tyrannical giants)."

al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was a man from the people of Yemen, called Bal'am. Allah gave him His signs, but he abandoned them."

Malik ibn Dinar said: "He was one of the scholars of the Children of Israel, and his supplication was answered (mujab al-da'wah). They would put him forward in times of hardship. The Prophet of Allah, Musa, sent him to the king of Madyan to invite him to Allah. [The king] bribed him and gave him gifts, so he followed the king's religion and abandoned the religion of Musa, peace be upon him."

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, from Husayn, from Imran ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was Bal'am ibn Ba'ir." Mujahid and Ikrimah also said the same.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: al-Harith related to me, from Abd al-Aziz, from Israil, from Mughirah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "He was Bil'am." [And Thaqif said: "He was Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."]

Shu'bah said, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from Nafi' ibn Asim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our [signs]﴾ [[Addition from MSS K, M, A.]] He said: "He is your companion, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt."

It has been reported through more than one channel from him [Ibn Amr], and it is sound as far as him. It seems that he only meant that Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt resembles him, for a great deal of knowledge of the earlier revealed laws had reached him. But he did not benefit from his knowledge, for he lived to see the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His signs, indications and miracles reached him and became manifest to everyone who had insight. Despite this, he met him but did not follow him. He sided with the polytheists, supported them and praised them, and he composed an eloquent elegy for the polytheists who fell at Badr. May Allah disfigure him [[Addition from MS A.]]. [[See: al-Aqidah fi al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah by Ibn Hisham (2/30).]] It has come in some hadiths: "He was among those whose tongues professed faith but whose hearts did not believe." For he had divinely inspired verses, wise sayings and eloquence, but Allah did not open his heart to Islam.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sa'id al-A'war, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he drew away from them﴾. He said: "He was a man given three supplications which would be answered for him. He had a wife by whom he had a child. She said: 'Make one of them for me.' He said: 'For you, one. What do you want?' She said: 'Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel.' So he prayed to Allah, and He made her the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she became averse to him and wanted something else. So he prayed to Allah to make her a female dog, and she became a female dog. Thus two supplications were gone. Her sons came and said: 'We cannot bear this situation. Our mother has become a female dog, and people taunt us with her. Pray to Allah to return her to the state she was in.' So he prayed to Allah, and she returned as she had been. Thus the three supplications were gone, and she was named al-Basus." [[Related by Abu al-Shaykh in his Tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (3/608).]] This is gharib (a rare report, transmitted through a weak or single channel).

As for what is well known concerning the occasion of revelation of this noble verse, it is a man from among the earlier people of the time of the Children of Israel, as Ibn Mas'ud and others among the early scholars (al-salaf) said.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "He was a man from the city of the Jabbarin, called Bal'am, and he knew the Greatest Name of Allah."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others among the early scholars said: "[He was a man] whose supplication was answered; he never asked Allah for anything without being given it."

Whoever said that he had been given prophethood and then drew away from it is strange, rather far off, rather mistaken. Al-Tabari transmitted this from some of them, but it is not sound.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: "When Musa encamped with them, meaning with the Jabbarin, and those with him, Bal'am's kinsmen and people came to him and said: 'Musa is a formidable man, and he has many soldiers with him. If he prevails over us, he will destroy us. So pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him from us.' He said: 'If I pray to Allah to repel Musa and those with him, I will lose my worldly life and my hereafter.' They kept at him until he prayed against them, so Allah stripped from him what he had. This is the words of Allah: ﴿Then he drew away from them, and Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided﴾."

Al-Suddi said: "When the forty years which Allah mentioned, ﴿So it is forbidden to them for forty years﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 26], ended, Allah sent Yusha' ibn Nun as a prophet. He called the Children of Israel and informed them that he was a prophet and that Allah had commanded him to fight the Jabbarin. So they pledged allegiance to him and believed him. A man from the Children of Israel called Bal'am set out. He was a scholar who knew the hidden Greatest Name. He disbelieved, may Allah curse him, came to the Jabbarin and said to them: 'Do not fear the Children of Israel. When you go out to fight them, I will invoke a curse upon them and they will perish!' He had among them whatever worldly things he wished, except that he could not approach women, so he would marry a she-donkey of his." He is the one of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then he drew away from them﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he took control of him and overpowered him in his affairs, so whatever [Satan] commanded him, he obeyed and submitted to. Therefore He said: ﴿And he became of the misguided﴾, meaning of those who perished, bewildered, and ruined.

A hadith has come concerning the meaning of this verse, which al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, from al-Salt ibn Bahram, al-Hasan related to us, Jundub al-Bajali related to us in this mosque, that Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, related to him, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Among what I fear for you is a man who recites the Qur'an, until when its splendour is seen upon him and he has become a supporter of Islam, he is struck by [something] as Allah wills, and he draws away from it, casts it behind his back, pursues his neighbour with the sword, and accuses him of polytheism." He [Hudhayfah] said: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, which of them is more deserving of polytheism, the accused or the accuser?" He said: "Rather, the accuser."

This is a good chain of narration [[Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, no. (175), by the route: Muhammad ibn Marzuq and al-Hasan ibn Abi Kabshah related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Barsani related to us with it. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/188): "Its chain is hasan (good)."]]. Al-Salt ibn Bahram was among the trustworthy Kufans, and he was accused of nothing except Irja' (the doctrine of postponement). Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Yahya ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy.

* *

And His words: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them, but he clung to the earth and followed his desire﴾. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them﴾, meaning We would have raised him above the defilement of the filth of this world by the signs which We had given him. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾, meaning he inclined towards the adornment and splendour of this world, turned to its pleasures and luxuries, and was deluded by it as it deluded others who were not people of insight and intellect.

Abu al-Zahiriyyah said, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾: "Satan appeared to him at a distance of a bowshot from the bridge of Banyas, and the she-donkey prostrated to Allah while Bal'am prostrated to Satan." Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr and others also said the same.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: From the story of this man is what Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, from al-Mu'tamir, from his father, that he was asked about this verse: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, [but he drew away from them]﴾ [[Addition from MS A.]]. He related from Sayyar that he was a man called Bal'am, who had been given prophethood and was one whose supplication was answered. He said: "Musa came with the Children of Israel, intending the land where Bal'am was, or he said: Syria. The people were struck with terrible fear of him. They came to Bal'am and said: 'Pray to Allah against this man and his army!' He said: 'Until I consult my Lord,' or 'until I consult [Him].' So he consulted about praying against them, and it was said to him: 'Do not pray against them, for they are My servants, and their Prophet is among them.' So he said to his people: 'I have consulted my Lord about praying against them, and I have been forbidden.' They presented him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: 'Pray against them!' He said: 'Until I consult.' So he consulted, but no reply came to him. He said: 'I have consulted, but nothing has come back to me!' They said: 'If your Lord disliked that you pray against them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time.' So he began to pray against them, but whenever he prayed against them, the prayer against his own people came upon his tongue, and whenever he wanted to pray that victory be granted to his people, he prayed that victory be granted to Musa and his army, or something similar, if Allah wills." He said: [The people] said to him: "We see you pray only against us." He said: "Nothing flows upon my tongue except in this way. Even if I prayed against him, it would not be answered for me. But I will direct you to a matter by which their destruction may come about. Allah hates fornication, and if they fall into fornication they will perish, and I hope that Allah will destroy them. So send out the women to meet them, for they are a travelling people, and perhaps they will commit fornication and perish." He said: "They did so, and they sent out the women to meet them." He said: "The king had a daughter, and [the narrator] mentioned of her greatness what only Allah knows!" He said: "Her father, or Bal'am, said: 'Do not let yourself be given to anyone except Musa!'" He said: "And they fell into fornication. And a leader of one of the tribes of the Children of Israel came to her, and he wanted her for himself. She said: 'I will not give myself except to Musa.' He said: 'My rank is such-and-such, and my position is such-and-such.' She sent to her father seeking his advice. He told her: 'Let him have her.'" He said: "A man from the descendants of Harun came with a spear and thrust it through both of them." He said: "Allah strengthened him with power. He pierced them both together and raised them on his spear, and the people saw them, or as he related." He said: "Allah sent the plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 175–177 (part 2 of 2):

Abu al-Mu'tamir said: Sayyar narrated to me that Balam rode his donkey until, when he reached al-'Alawla (or he said: a road from al-'Alawla), he began to strike her and she would not move forward. She stood up against him and said: "Why are you striking me? Do you not see what is before you?" Then the Satan was in front of him. He said: So he dismounted and prostrated to it. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾.

He said: Sayyar narrated this to me, and I do not know whether something from the narration of others has entered into it.

I say: He is Balam, also called Bulam, the son of Ba'ura', the son of Abar. It is also said: the son of Ba'ur, the son of Shuhum, the son of Qushtum, the son of Mab, the son of Lut, the son of Haran (also said: the son of Haran), the son of Azar. He used to live in a village from the villages of al-Balqa'.

Ibn 'Asakir said: He is the one who knew the Greatest Name of Allah, but he detached himself from his religion. He is mentioned in the Qur'an. Then he related from his story something similar to what we have mentioned here, and he related it from Wahb and others. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Salim Abi al-Nadr that he related: When Musa, peace be upon him, descended into the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balam came to him and said to him: "This is Musa ibn 'Imran among the Children of Israel. He has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us, and to make them lawful to the Children of Israel. We are your people, and we have no dwelling place, and you are a man whose supplication is answered. So go out and invoke Allah against them." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah is with him, with the angels and the believers. How can I go to invoke against them, when I know from Allah what I know?!" They said to him: "We have no dwelling!" They kept on at him, softening him and humbling themselves before him, until they tempted him, and he was tempted. He mounted his she-donkey heading toward the mountain from which he could overlook the army of the Children of Israel, which is the mountain of Husban. When she had carried him not far, she knelt down with him, so he dismounted and struck her until he had worn her out, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far with him before she knelt down with him again, and he struck her until he had worn her out. Then Allah permitted her to speak, as a proof against him, and she said: "Woe to you, O Balam! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me back from this direction? Are you going to the Prophet of Allah and the believers so that you may invoke against them?" But he did not desist from striking her, so Allah released her when he did that to her. She set off with him until, when she brought him up over the top of Husban, overlooking the army of Musa and the Children of Israel, he began to invoke against them, but whenever he invoked against them with evil, Allah turned his tongue toward his own people, and whenever he invoked for his people with good, he turned his tongue toward the Children of Israel. His people said to him: "Do you know, O Balam, what you are doing? You are invoking for them and invoking against us!" He said: "This is what I do not control; this is a matter over which Allah has prevailed!" He said: His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest. He said to them: "Now the world and the Hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deception and trickery. I will devise a plan for you and scheme. Adorn the women and give them merchandise, then send them to the army to sell it there, and instruct them that no woman should refuse herself to a man who desires her, for if one man of them commits fornication, you will be rid of them." They did so. When the women entered the army, a woman of the Kan'anites named "Kasbi daughter of Sur, the chief of her people," passed by a man from the great men of the Children of Israel, who was "Zamri ibn Shalum," the chief of the tribe of the Banu Sam'an ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them. He went to her, took her hand when her beauty pleased him, then brought her and stood with her before Musa, peace be upon him, and said: "I suppose you will say this is forbidden to you?" He said: "Yes, she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and had intercourse with her. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent the plague upon the Children of Israel. Finhas ibn al-'Ayzar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, had been absent when Zamri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel, and he was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was entirely of iron, then entered the tent while they were lying together, and he pierced them both with his spear. Then he carried them out raised up toward the sky, with the spear still in his grip, having taken hold of it with his forearm, leaning with his elbow on his side, and resting the spear against his jaw. He was the firstborn of al-'Ayzar. He kept saying: "O Allah, this is how we deal with those who disobey You." The plague was lifted. The number of those among the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the moment Zamri struck the woman until Finhas killed him, was counted, and they found that seventy thousand had died, though the one who gave the lesser figure said twenty thousand, in a single hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel have given the descendants of Finhas the forequarter, the foreleg and the jaw of every sacrificial animal they slaughter, and the firstborn of all their property and their persons, because he was the firstborn of his father al-'Ayzar. Concerning Balam ibn Ba'ura', Allah revealed: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them [then Satan followed him]﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so that they may reflect﴾. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/264).]

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So his likeness is like that of a dog: if you drive him away, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants﴾, the exegetes differed concerning its meaning. According to the context of Ibn Ishaq, from Salim ibn Abi al-Nadr, that Balam's tongue hung out upon his chest, the comparison to the dog is in its panting in both of its states, whether it is driven away or left alone. It was also said: its meaning is that he became like that in his error and his persistence in it, and in his not benefiting from being called to faith or from not being called, like the dog in its panting in both its states: if you attack it or if you leave it, it pants in both conditions. Likewise, this man does not benefit from admonition and the call to faith, nor from its absence, as the Exalted said: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 6], and ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 80], and similar to that.

It was also said: its meaning is that the heart of the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the misguided is weak, empty of guidance, and so it pounds constantly; so this was expressed by that. This has been transmitted in similar terms from al-Hasan al-Basri and others.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: perhaps the Children of Israel, who know the condition of Balam and what happened to him, when Allah misguided him and removed him from His mercy, because he used the blessing of Allah upon him, in teaching him the Greatest Name, by which when one asks, He gives, and when one calls upon Him, He responds, in other than the obedience of his Lord. Rather, he invoked by it against the party of the Most Merciful and the branch of faith, the followers of His servant and Messenger in that time, Musa ibn 'Imran, the one who spoke with Allah, peace be upon him. Therefore He said: ﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾, meaning: that they may beware of becoming like him. For Allah has given them knowledge and distinguished them over all others among the Arabs, and He placed in their hands the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), which they recognize just as they recognize their own sons. So they are the most deserving of people and the most entitled to follow him, support him and aid him, just as their prophets informed them of that and commanded them to it. Therefore, whoever among them opposes what is in His Book and conceals it, not informing the servants of it, Allah will inflict upon him humiliation in this world, joined with the humiliation of the Hereafter.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and used to wrong themselves﴾, the Exalted says: evil is the example, the likeness of the people who denied Our signs; that is, evil is their likeness in being compared to dogs, which have no concern except obtaining a morsel or a desire. Whoever departs from the sphere of knowledge and guidance and turns to the desire of his self, following his whims, becomes like the dog, and evil is the likeness of him. Therefore it is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no such evil likeness: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that returns to its vomit." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2622).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they used to wrong themselves﴾, meaning: Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, by turning away from following guidance and obeying their Master, inclining toward the abode of decay and turning to the attainment of pleasures and the pursuit of desire.

He, Exalted is He, says: Whomever Allah guides, there is no one to misguide him. Whomever He misguides, he has certainly been ruined, lost, and gone astray without doubt. Whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. For this reason, in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud it is narrated: "Indeed, all praise is for Allah. We praise Him, seek His help, seek His guidance, and seek His forgiveness. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from the bad consequences of our deeds. Whomever Allah guides, there is none to misguide him, and whomever Allah leaves to stray, there is none to guide him. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger."

The hadith in its entirety was related by Imam Ahmad, and the authors of the Sunan (collections of hadith arranged by legal topic), and others [[Al-Musnad (1/392) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1097, and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/89), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1892.]]

Allah, the Exalted, says: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind" (﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا﴾), meaning: We created and made. "For Hell many of the jinn and mankind" means: We prepared them for it, and they do the deeds of its people. When Allah, the Exalted, willed to create the creatures, He knew what they would do before their existence, so He recorded that with Him in a Book fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, as is related in Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah decreed the measures of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was upon the water." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2653).]

Also in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Aisha bint Talha, from her maternal aunt Aisha, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was invited to the funeral of a child of the Ansar. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, blessed is he, a sparrow from the sparrows of Paradise, who did no evil and did not live to reach it." He said: "Or is it other than that, O Aisha? Allah created Paradise and created for it its people while they were in their fathers' loins, and He created the Fire and created for it [[In d, k, m: "for the Fire."]] its people while they were in their fathers' loins." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2662).]

And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: "Then the angel is sent to it, and he is commanded with four words: he writes its provision, its term, its deed, and whether it is wretched or happy."

It has preceded that when Allah, the Exalted, brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins and divided them into two groups, the People of the Right and the People of the Left, He said: "These are for Paradise and I do not mind; these are for the Fire and I do not mind."

The hadiths on this are many, and the matter of predestination (qadar) is a great one, and this is not the place to expound it.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: "They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear" means: they do not benefit from any of these organs which Allah made a means to guidance, as He says: "And We made for them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts availed them nothing, since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them what they used to mock" [Al-Ahqaf: 26]. And He says: "Deaf, dumb, blind; so they will not return" [Al-Baqarah: 18], which is said regarding the hypocrites, and regarding the disbelievers He says: "Deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not reason" [Al-Baqarah: 171]. And they were not deaf, dumb and blind except in regard to guidance, as He says: "And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse" [Al-Anfal: 23]. And He says: "Indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind" [Al-Hajj: 46]. And He says: "And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion. And indeed they avert them from the way, while they think that they are guided" [Az-Zukhruf: 36-37].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: "They are like livestock; rather, they are further astray." That is: these are the ones who do not hear the truth nor retain it, and do not see guidance, like grazing livestock, which gain nothing from these senses except in what sustains them of the worldly life, as He says: "And the likeness of those who disbelieve is like one who calls out to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry: deaf, dumb, blind" [Al-Baqarah: 171]. That is: their likeness, in the state of being called to faith, is like the likeness of livestock when their shepherd calls them, they hear only his voice and do not understand what he says. For this reason He said of these: "Rather, they are further astray," that is, than the beasts, because beasts may still respond to their shepherd when he calls to them, even if they do not understand his speech, unlike these people. Also, beasts understand what they were created for, either by their nature or by being subjected to it, unlike the disbeliever, who was created only to worship Allah and affirm His oneness, yet he disbelieved in Allah and associated others with Him. For this reason, whoever among mankind obeys Allah is more honoured in his return than the angels of his like, and whoever among mankind disbelieves in Him, the beasts are more complete than him. Thus Allah, the Exalted, said: "They are like livestock; rather, they are further astray. They are the heedless."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 180:

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise, and He is Witr (One, Single) and loves the witr (odd number)."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from him [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6410) and Sahih Muslim no. (2677).]] Al-Bukhari narrated it from Abu al-Yaman, from Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Zinad, with the same [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7392).]] Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from al-Jawzajani, from Safwan ibn Salih, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Shu'ayb, and he mentioned its chain like it, and he added after his saying "He loves the witr": He is Allah, other than whom there is no god, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the King, the Most Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner, the Ever-Forgiving, the Subduer, the Bestower, the Provider, the Opener, the All-Knowing, the Restrainer, the Expander, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Giver of Honour, the Giver of Humiliation, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the Judge, the Just, the Subtle, the All-Aware, the Forbearing, the Magnificent, the Ever-Forgiving, the Most Appreciative, the Most High, the Most Great, the Preserver, the Sustainer, the Reckoner, the Majestic, the Generous, the Watchful, the Responsive, the All-Encompassing, the Wise, the Loving, the Glorious, the Resurrector, the Witness, the Truth, the Trustee, the Strong, the Firm, the Protecting Friend, the Praiseworthy, the Counter, the Originator, the Restorer, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Finder, the Glorious, the One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal Refuge, the Capable, the Omnipotent, the Expediter, the Delayer, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Governor, the Exalted, the Benign, the Oft-Returning, the Avenger, the Pardoner, the Kind, the Owner of Sovereignty, Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the Equitable, the Gatherer, the Self-Sufficient, the Enricher, the Preventer, the Harmer, the Benefactor, the Light, the Guide, the Originator, the Everlasting, the Inheritor, the Guide to Right Conduct, the Patient. [[In M, after this: "There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing."]]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a gharib (strange) hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from A.]], and we do not know, in most of the narrations, the mention of the names except in this hadith.

Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, through the route of Safwan, with it [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3507).]]. Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan through another route [[In A: "another".]], from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3861). Al-Busiri said: "The chain of Ibn Majah's route is weak due to the weakness of Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani."]], and he listed the names similar to what preceded, with additions and omissions.

What a group of the memorizers of hadith relied upon is that the enumeration of the names in this hadith is an interpolation (mudraj) into it. Rather, it is as narrated by al-Walid ibn Muslim and Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-San'ani, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad: that it reached him from more than one of the people of knowledge that they said that, i.e., that they collected them from the Qur'an, as narrated [[In K, M, A: "narrated".]] from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah and Abu Zayd al-Lughawi. And Allah knows best.

Then it should be known that the Most Beautiful Names are not confined to the ninety-nine, on the evidence of what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Abu Salamah al-Juhani, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "No person has ever been struck by distress or grief and then said: 'O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment over me is executed, Your decree over me is just. I ask You by every name that You have named Yourself with, or taught to any of Your creation, or revealed in Your Book, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Qur'an the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the departure of my grief, and the banisher of my distress,' except that Allah will remove his distress and grief and replace them with joy." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not learn them?" He said: "Yes, it is fitting for everyone who hears them to learn them."

Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban al-Busti, the Imam, also narrated it in his Sahih with the same [[Al-Musnad (1/392), and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (2372), "Mawarid".]].

The jurist and Imam Abu Bakr Ibn al-'Arabi, one of the imams of the Malikis, mentioned in his book "al-Ahwadhi fi Sharh al-Tirmidhi" that some people collected from the Book and the Sunnah a thousand names of Allah, and Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, he said: The deviation of the deviators is that they call "al-Lat" [[In A: "al-Lat and al-'Uzza".]] among the names of Allah.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, he said: They derived "al-Lat" from Allah, and they derived "al-'Uzza" from al-'Aziz.

Qatadah said: ﴿yulhidun﴾ means they associate partners (with Allah). Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-ilhad is denial (takdhib). The root meaning of ilhad in the speech of the Arabs is turning away from the right course, inclining, wrongdoing and deviation, and from it comes al-lahd in the grave, because it deviates toward the direction of the qiblah away from the straight line of the pit.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿And among those We created is a community﴾, meaning, among the nations, ﴿a community﴾ standing upright in the truth, in speech and in action, ﴿who guide by the truth﴾, saying it and calling to it, ﴿and by it act justly﴾, acting and judging by it.

It has come in the narrations (al-athar) that the intended community mentioned in this verse is this Muhammadan community.

Sa'id reported from Qatadah concerning the tafsir (exegesis) of this verse: "It has reached us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say when he recited this verse: 'This is for you, and the people before you were given a like of it: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly﴾ [Al-A'raf: 159].'" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (13/286), and it is mursal.]]

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, concerning the words of Allah Most High: ﴿And among those We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, among my ummah there will be a people upon the truth, until 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) descends, whenever he descends." [[Narrated by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (1/474).]]

In the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A group from my ummah will continue to be dominant upon the truth; those who forsake them will not harm them, nor will those who oppose them, until the Hour is established." In another narration: "Until the command of Allah comes while they are upon that." In another narration: "And they are in al-Sham (the Levant)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3641), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1037).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 182–183:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those who deny Our signs, We will lead them step by step (from where they do not know)﴾. Its meaning is that He opens for them the doors of provision and the means of livelihood in this world, until they become deluded by what they have and believe that they are upon something [[In A: "and they believe".]], as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the wrongdoing people was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-An'am: 44, 45]. For this reason He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And I will give them respite﴾, meaning: "And I will give them respite; I will prolong for them what they are in." ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: strong and mighty.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 182–183:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those who deny Our signs, We will lead them step by step (from where they do not know)﴾. Its meaning is that He opens for them the doors of provision and the means of livelihood in this world, until they become deluded by what they have and believe that they are upon something [[In A: "and they believe".]], as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things, until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair. So the last remnant of the wrongdoing people was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-An'am: 44, 45]. For this reason He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And I will give them respite﴾, meaning: "And I will give them respite; I will prolong for them what they are in." ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: strong and mighty.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do they not reflect?﴾ These deniers of Our signs, ﴿that there is no madness in their companion﴾, meaning Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In A: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace"]]. ﴿There is no madness in him﴾, i.e., he has no insanity; rather, he is truly the Messenger of Allah, who calls to the truth. ﴿He is only a clear warner﴾, i.e., manifest to whoever has a heart and intellect by which he understands and comprehends. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Your companion is not a madman﴾ [At-Takwir: 22]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say, "I only advise you of one thing: that you stand before Allah in pairs and individually and then reflect. There is no madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."﴾ [Saba': 46] He says: I only ask of you that you stand for Allah, standing sincerely for Allah, with no partisanship or obstinacy in it. ﴿In pairs and individually﴾, i.e., together and separately. ﴿Then reflect﴾ upon this one who has come to you with the message from Allah: Is there madness in him or not? For if you do that, it will become clear to you and it will be manifest that he is truly and genuinely the Messenger [of Allah].

Qatadah ibn Di'amah said: It was related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was on as-Safa, and he called the Quraysh, and began to address them clan by clan, "O Banu so-and-so, O Banu so-and-so," warning them of the punishment of Allah and the days of Allah's vengeance. One of them said: "Indeed, this companion of yours is surely mad. He kept shouting until morning" – or: "until he woke up." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Do they not reflect that there is no madness in their companion? He is only a clear warner.﴾ [[Narrated by at-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/289).]]

Allah says: ﴿Have they not looked﴾ — these deniers of Our signs — ﴿into the dominion of Allah and His sovereignty over the heavens and the earth, and at whatever thing Allah has created [[addition from manuscript M.]] within them,﴾ so that they would reflect upon that and take a lesson from it, and know that it belongs to the One who has no equal and no like, and to the action of One who is not deserving of worship. And true religion is for Him alone. So they would believe in Him, affirm His Messenger, turn in obedience to Him, renounce the rivals and idols, and be wary lest their terms have drawn near, so that they die in their disbelief and come to the punishment of Allah and His painful retribution.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ He means: in what warning, admonition and intimidation — after the warning and intimidation of Muhammad, which he brought to them from Allah in the verses of His Book — will they believe, if they do not believe in this message which Muhammad brought to them from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?!

Imam Ahmad narrated from Hasan ibn Musa, ʿAffan [[in A: "Uthman".]] ibn Muslim, and ʿAbd al-Samad ibn ʿAbd al-Warith, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, when we reached the seventh heaven, I looked above me and saw thunder, lightning and thunderbolts." He said: "I came upon a people whose bellies were like houses, in which there were snakes visible from outside their bellies. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the consumers of usury.' Then when I descended to the lowest heaven and looked below me, I saw dust, smoke and voices [[in M: "and loud voices".]]. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the devils, who cast confusion over the eyes of the children of Adam, so that they do not reflect on the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and were it not for that, they would have seen the wonders.'"

ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has objectionable narrations (Musnad 2/353).

Then He said, Exalted is He:

Allah says: Whoever Allah has decreed to be misguided, no one can guide him, and even if he looks into his own affairs in whatever way he looks, it will not avail him anything. ﴿And whoever Allah intends for trial, you cannot avail him anything against Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:41]. He also says: ﴿Say: "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe."﴾ [Yunus 10:101]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿They ask you about the Hour⟩, as He said elsewhere: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour⟩ [al-Ahzab 33:63]. It was said: it was revealed concerning the Quraysh. It was also said: concerning a group of the Jews. The first is more likely, because the verse is Meccan, and they used to ask about the time of the Hour, deeming its occurrence unlikely and denying its existence, as He said: ﴿And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?"⟩ [al-Anbiya' 21:38], and He said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error⟩ [al-Shura 42:18].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When is its appointed time?⟩ ('Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "its endpoint", i.e., when is its arrival? And "ayyan" means the end of the duration of the world, which is the first time of the Hour?)

﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time except Him."⟩ Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet ﷺ, when he was asked about the time of the Hour, to refer its knowledge to Allah the Exalted, for it is He who will reveal it at its time, meaning He knows the clear manifestation of its matter and when it will occur precisely, and none knows that except Him, exalted is He. Therefore He said: ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth.⟩

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth⟩, he said: its knowledge became burdensome for the people of the heavens and the earth, in that they do not know it. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan said: when it comes, it will be heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth; he means, it will be grievous to them.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth⟩, he said: there is no creature except that it will suffer some harm on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Juraij said: ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth⟩: when it comes, the sky will be split, the stars will scatter, the sun will be wound up, the mountains will be set in motion, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said will come to pass; that is its heaviness.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that what is meant is: the knowledge of its time became heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth, as Qatadah said.

And this is as they both said, like His saying: ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly⟩, and that does not negate the heaviness of its coming upon the people of the heavens and the earth. And Allah knows best.

As-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿It has become heavy upon the heavens and the earth⟩: it is hidden in the heavens and the earth, so no one knows when it will rise, not an angel brought near, nor a prophet sent.

﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly⟩ [he said]: its establishment will surprise them; it will come upon them while they are heedless.

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly⟩: Allah decreed that it ﴿will not come upon you except suddenly⟩. He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "The Hour will come upon the people while a man is repairing his pond, and a man is watering his livestock, and a man is displaying his merchandise in the market and lowering and raising his scale." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/297) and al-Tha'labi in his Tafsir as cited in Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (1/475), and it is mursal.]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Hour will not be established until the sun rises from its west. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, but that is the time when faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before or earned no good through its faith. The Hour will surely come while two men have spread their garment between them, and they will neither sell it nor fold it. The Hour will surely come while a man has departed with the milk of his she-camel and will not drink it. The Hour will surely come while a man is plastering his pond and will not water in it. The Hour will surely come while a man has raised his morsel to his mouth and will not eat it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6506).]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The Hour will come while a man is milking the she-camel, and the vessel will not reach his mouth before the Hour comes. And two men will be trading a garment, but they will not finish trading it before the Hour comes. And a man will be plastering his pond, but he will not finish drinking from it before the Hour comes." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2954).]

* *

As for His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it⟩, the commentators differed about its meaning. It was said: its meaning is as al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it⟩, he says: as if there were affection between you and them, as if you were a friend to them. Ibn 'Abbas said: When the people asked Muhammad ﷺ about the Hour, they asked him in the manner of people who think that Muhammad is well-informed about them, so Allah revealed to him: "Its knowledge is only with Him; He has kept its knowledge exclusive to Himself, and Allah has not informed any angel brought near or any messenger of it."

Qatadah said: The Quraysh said to Muhammad ﷺ: "Indeed there is kinship between us and you, so disclose to us when the Hour will be." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it⟩.

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Abu Malik and as-Suddi, and this is one view. The sound report from Mujahid—through the narration of Ibn Abi Najih and others—is: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it⟩, he said: you have exhausted asking about it until you knew its time.

Likewise al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it⟩, he says: as if you knew it, though you do not know it. ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah."⟩

Ma'mar said, from some of them: ﴿As if you were well-informed about it⟩: as if you knew it.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿As if you were well-informed about it⟩: as if you knew it, and Allah has concealed its knowledge from His creation. And he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour⟩ [Luqman 31:34], to the end of the verse.

This second meaning is more preferable than the first, and Allah knows best; therefore He said: ﴿Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know."⟩

Likewise, when Gabriel, peace be upon him, came in the form of a Bedouin to teach people the matters of their religion, he sat before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the manner of an inquirer seeking guidance, and asked him about Islam, then about faith, then about excellence (ihsan), then said: "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "The one asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the asker," meaning: I do not know it better than you, and no one knows it better than anyone. Then the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour⟩ to the end of the verse. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (50), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (9).]

In another narration: he asked him about the signs of the Hour, then said: "Five things no one knows except Allah," and he recited this verse. In all of this, after every answer he would say: "You have spoken the truth." Therefore the Companions marvelled at this questioner who asks him and then confirms him. Then when he left, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This was Gabriel; he came to you to teach you your religion." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (50), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (9).]

In another narration he said: "He did not come to me in any form except that I recognised him in it, except this form of his."

I have mentioned this hadith with its chains and wordings from the Sahihs, the Hasans and the Musnads at the beginning of my commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. [See this discussion in: Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari (1/114).]

When that Bedouin asked him and called out to him with a loud voice, saying: "O Muhammad!", the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Hā" (in a tone similar to his) — he said: "O Muhammad, when is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Woe to you! The Hour is coming; what have you prepared for it?" He said: "I have not prepared much prayer or fasting, but I love Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "A person is with the one he loves." The Muslims rejoiced at nothing as they rejoiced at this hadith. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2639), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This has multiple chains in the Two Sahihs and others, from a group of the Companions, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "A person is with the one he loves." [It has come from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, Safwan ibn 'Assal, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: As for the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, it is the one mentioned above. As for the hadith of Safwan ibn 'Assal, it is narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (3535). As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, it is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6169), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2640). As for the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, it is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6170), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2641).] It is mutawatir according to many meticulous hadith scholars.

In it there is that he, peace be upon him, when asked about that which they did not need to know, guided them to what was more important for them, which is preparing for its occurrence and readiness for it before it comes, even if they did not know its precise time.

Therefore Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they would ask him about the Hour: "When is the Hour?" He would look at the youngest person among them and say: "If this one lives, old age will not reach him before your Hour comes upon you." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2952).] He meant by that their death, which leads them to enter the barzakh of the Hereafter.

Then Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas: that a man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Hour, and with him was a boy of the Ansar called Muhammad. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If this boy lives, perhaps old age will not reach him before the Hour comes." Muslim alone narrated it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2953).]

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ma'bad ibn Hilal al-'Anazi [in the other copies: Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal al-Misri] narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "When is the Hour?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent for a while, then looked at a boy before him from the Azd Shanu'ah, and said: "If this one's life is prolonged, old age will not reach him before the Hour comes." Anas said: that boy was one of my contemporaries. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2953).]

He also said: Harun ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, who said: A boy of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah passed by—and he was one of my contemporaries—and the Prophet ﷺ said: "If this one is delayed, old age will not reach him until the Hour comes." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2953).] Al-Bukhari narrated it in the Book of Adab of his Sahih, from 'Amr ibn 'Asim, from Hammam ibn Yahya, from Qatadah, from Anas: that a man from the people of the desert said: "O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour?" and he mentioned the hadith, and at its end: "Then a boy of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah passed by," and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6167).]

This general wording in these narrations is to be understood as restricted by "your Hour" in the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, a month before he died: 'You ask me about the Hour, but its knowledge is with Allah alone. And I swear by Allah, there is not on the face of the earth today any soul that has been created, upon which a hundred years will pass.'" Related by Muslim.[1]

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Umar, the same. Ibn Umar said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only meant the ending of that generation."

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, al-Awwam informed us, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn Afazah, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Ibrahim, Musa and Isa." He said: "They discussed the matter of the Hour." He said: "They referred their matter to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' They then referred their matter to Musa, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' They then referred their matter to Isa, and Isa said: 'As for its appointed time, no one knows it except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And among what my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has covenanted to me is that the Dajjal will emerge.'" He said: "And with me will be two staffs. When he sees me, he will melt as lead melts." He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will destroy him when he sees me, so much so that the stone and the tree will say: 'O Muslim, there is a disbeliever beneath me, come and kill him.'" He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands." He said: "At that time Gog and Magog will emerge, and they are from every high ground they descend. They will trample their lands, leaving nothing they pass over without destroying it, and they will not pass by any water without drinking it." He said: "Then the people will return to me and complain of them, so I will supplicate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, against them, and He will destroy them and cause them to die, until the earth becomes foul from their stench, that is: it stinks." He said: "Then Allah will send down rain, which will sweep away their bodies until it casts them into the sea."

Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun said: "Then the mountains will be blown away and the earth will be stretched out like a hide." Then he returned to the narration of Hushaym, who said: "Among what my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has covenanted to me is that when that happens, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman at full term, whose family does not know when it will surprise them with its birth, by night or by day."[2]

Ibn Majah related it, from Bundar, from Yazid ibn Harun, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, with its chain, similarly.[3]

These are the greatest of the steadfast messengers (ulu al-azm), and none of them had knowledge of the exact time of the Hour. They referred the matter to Isa, peace be upon him, and he spoke about its signs, because he will descend at the end of this Ummah, implementing the rulings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and will kill the Masih al-Dajjal, and Allah will make the destruction of Gog and Magog come through the blessing of his supplication. So he informed them of what Allah, the Exalted, had made him know.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit narrated to us, saying: I heard my father mention from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the Hour, and he said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord; none will reveal its time except Him. But I will inform you of its signs and what will precede it: Before it there will be fitnah and harj." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we know what fitnah is, so what is harj?" He said, in the language of Abyssinia: "Killing." He said: "And mutual disowning will spread among the people, so that hardly anyone will recognise anyone."[4] It was not related by anyone from the authors of the Six Books by this route.

Waki' said: Ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept mentioning matters of the Hour until there was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when will be its arrival?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42], the verse.[5]

Al-Nasa'i related it from the narration of Isa ibn Yunus, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with it. This is a good, strong chain.[6]

So this Prophet, the unlettered, the master of the messengers and their seal [Muhammad], may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is the Prophet of mercy, the Prophet of repentance, the Prophet of the great battle, the one who comes last and after whom none come, and the Gatherer, at whose feet people will be gathered. Along with his saying, as established in the Sahih from the hadith of Anas and Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I was sent, and the Hour is like these two," and he joined his index and middle fingers.[7] Despite all of this, Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to return the knowledge of the time of the Hour to Him when he was asked about it, so He said: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.﴾
