Allah commanded him to entrust all matters to Him, and to declare about himself that he does not know the unseen, and has no knowledge of any of it except what Allah makes him know, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Knower of the unseen, He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has chosen; and indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards﴾ [al-Jinn: 26, 27] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A.]] And His saying: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of the good﴾. ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of the good﴾ — he said: "If I knew when I would die, I would do righteous deeds."

Similarly, Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, and Ibn Jurayj said the same.

But this is open to scrutiny, because the deeds of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were constant. In another narration: when he did a deed, he would keep to it [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (783), from the hadith of ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

So all his deeds were of one pattern, as if he were looking at Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in all his states — unless the intent is to guide others to prepare for that. And Allah knows best.

The best explanation in this regard is what al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of the good﴾, meaning: of wealth. In another narration: "I would have known, when I bought something, what would profit me in it, so I would never sell anything without profiting from it, and misfortune would never touch me." He said: "Poverty would not afflict me."

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: the meaning of that is: "Had I known the unseen, I would have prepared for the barren year during the fertile one, and I would have known high prices from low prices, so I would have stocked up at the low price."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding ﴿And misfortune would never touch me﴾: "I would have avoided evil before it happened, and guarded against it."

Then He informed that he is only a warner and a bringer of good tidings — that is, a warner of punishment, and a bringer of good tidings to the believers of the Gardens, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people﴾ [Maryam: 97].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah draws attention to the fact that He created all of mankind from Adam (peace be upon him), and that from him He created his spouse Hawwa' (Eve), and then people spread out from the two of them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you into nations and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ [Al-Hujurat 49:13] And He the Exalted says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women.﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:1]

In this noble verse He says: ﴿And made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her.﴾ That is, that he might become familiar with her and find rest with her, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:21] There is no closer familiarity between two spouses than that between the married pair. For this reason, Allah the Exalted mentioned that the sorcerer may, through his scheming, reach the separation between a man and his wife.

﴿So when he covered her﴾ that is, had intercourse with her, ﴿she conceived a light burden﴾ and that is the beginning of pregnancy, in which the woman feels no pain; it is only the sperm-drop, then the clinging clot, then the lump of flesh.

* *

As for His words ﴿and she carried it about⁠﴾, Mujahid said: she continued carrying it. The like of this was narrated from al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Suddi.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: from his father: she felt it to be light (istakhaffathu).

Ayyub said: I asked al-Hasan about His words ﴿and she carried it about⁠﴾, and he said: "If you were an Arab man, you would know what it means. It means: she continued with it (fa-istamarrat bihi)."

Qatadah said: ﴿and she carried it about⁠﴾ and her pregnancy became evident.

Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: she continued with the water (in her womb), she stood with it and sat with it.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: she continued with it, and she doubted whether she had conceived or not.

﴿So when she became heavy﴾ that is, became burdened with her pregnancy.

Al-Suddi said: the child grew large in her womb.

﴿They both called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous (child)⁠﴾ that is, a sound human being, as al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: they feared that it would be an animal.

Likewise Abu al-Bakhtari and Abu Malik said: they feared that it would not be a human.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "If You give us a boy."

﴿We will surely be among the grateful.⁠ But when He gave them a righteous (child), they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. Exalted is Allah above what they associate.⁠﴾ The commentators have mentioned here reports and hadiths which I shall cite and then explain what is in them, and then follow that with the correct explanation of this, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Umar ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When Hawwa' gave birth, Iblis came to her—and no child of hers would survive—and said: 'Name him Abd al-Harith, for he will live.' So she named him Abd al-Harith, and he lived. That was from the inspiration and command of Satan."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it in this way, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar (Bundar), from Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, with the same chain.

At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir for this verse from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abd al-Samad, with the same, and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of Umar ibn Ibrahim, from Qatadah. Some of them narrated it from Abd al-Samad without raising it (to the Prophet)."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abd al-Samad, raised, and then said: "This hadith has a sahih isnad, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."

Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir, from Abu Zur'ah al-Razi, from Hilal ibn Fayyad, from Umar ibn Ibrahim, with the same, raised.

Likewise Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Shadh ibn Fayyad, from Umar ibn Ibrahim, with the same, raised.

I say: "Shadh" here is Hilal, and Shadh is his laqab (epithet). The point is that this hadith is defective (ma'lul) in three respects:

First: this Umar ibn Ibrahim is al-Basri, and Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy, but Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "He is not to be used as evidence." However, Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of al-Mu'tamir, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, raised. Allah knows best.

Second: it has been narrated as the saying of Samurah himself, not raised, as Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father. And Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu al-'Ala' ibn al-Shikhkhir, from Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: "Adam named his son 'Abd al-Harith."

Third: al-Hasan himself explained the verse otherwise, and had this been with him from Samurah raised, he would not have turned away from it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan: ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them﴾ He said: "This was in some of the People of the Religions, and it was not in Adam."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said: "He meant by it the offspring of Adam and whoever among them associated partners after him"—meaning His words ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾. Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "They are the Jews and the Christians; Allah gave them children, and they made them Jews and Christians."

These are sahih chains from al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, that he explained the verse in this way, and it is among the best of explanations and the most fitting meaning of the verse. Had this hadith been preserved with him from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, neither he nor anyone else would have turned away from it, especially given his piety toward Allah and his scrupulousness. This shows you that it is a statement halted at the Companion (mawquf). It is also possible that he received it from some of the People of the Book who had embraced Islam, such as Ka'b or Wahb ibn Munabbih and others, as will be explained, Allah willing. Nevertheless, we are absolved of the responsibility of the raised report. Allah knows best.

As for the reports: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Hawwa' used to bear children to Adam, peace be upon him, and he would make them servants of Allah and name them "Abd Allah" and "Ubayd Allah" and the like, but they would die. Iblis came to him and Adam and said: "If you do not name him with the name you name him, he will live." She bore a boy and he named him "Abd al-Harith," and concerning this Allah revealed: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ to His words ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning Adam: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ to His words ﴿and she carried it about⁠﴾ — she doubted whether she had conceived or not. ﴿So when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous (child), we will surely be among the grateful."⁠﴾ Then Satan came to them and said: "Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know what will become of it? Will it be an animal or not?" And he adorned falsehood for them; indeed he is a clear enemy. Before that she had borne two sons who died. Satan said to them: "If you do not name him after me, he will not come out sound, and he will die as the first two died." So they named their son "Abd al-Harith," and that is Allah's saying ﴿But when He gave them a righteous (child), they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sharik, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿But when He gave them a righteous (child), they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ he said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. So when he covered her⁠﴾ — Adam — ﴿she conceived a light burden﴾. Then Iblis came to them—may Allah curse him—and said: "I am your companion who expelled you from Paradise. Obey me, or I will make for it (the child) two horns of a deer, and it will come out from your belly and split it open, and I will do, and I will do," frightening them. So they named him "Abd al-Harith," but they refused to obey him, and the child came out dead. Then she conceived a second time, and he came to them again and said: "I am your companion who did what I did. You will do it or I will do it," frightening them. They refused to obey him, and it came out dead. Then she conceived a third time, and he came to them again and reminded them, and love for the child overcame them, so they named him "Abd al-Harith." That is His saying ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

This report was received from Ibn 'Abbas by a group of his companions, such as Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah. From the second generation: Qatadah, al-Suddi, and many of the early scholars, and a group of later scholars, and among the later commentators there are countless groups. It seems—Allah knows best—that its origin was taken from the People of the Book, for Ibn 'Abbas narrated it from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated:

Abi narrated to us, Abu al-Jamahir narrated to us, Sa'id (i.e., Ibn Bashir) narrated to us, from 'Uqbah, from Qatadah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "When Hawwa' conceived, Satan came to her and said: 'Will you obey me and your child will be safe? Name him Abd al-Harith.' She did not do it, and she gave birth and he died. Then she conceived again and he said to her the same, and she did not do it. Then she conceived a third time, and he came to her and said: 'If you obey me he will be safe, otherwise he will be an animal.' So he (Satan) made them fearful, and they obeyed him."

These reports, Allah knows best, clearly appear to be from the reports of the People of the Book. The hadith has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "When the People of the Book tell you something, do not believe them and do not disbelieve them." Then their reports are of three categories: First, what we know to be true by the evidence of the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Second, what we know to be false, by what contradicts it from the Book and the Sunnah as well. Third, what is silent on, which is permitted to be narrated, by his saying, peace be upon him: "Narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no harm," and this is what is neither believed nor disbelieved, due to his saying: "Do not believe them and do not disbelieve them." As for this report: is it from the second or the third category? There is room for consideration. As for those who narrate it from a Companion or Follower, they regard it as of the third category. As for us, we follow the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, in this, and that the intended subject of this context is not Adam and Hawwa', but rather the polytheists from among his offspring. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate.⁠﴾ Then he said:

As for the reports: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Hawwa' used to bear children to Adam, peace be upon him, and he would make them servants of Allah and name them "Abd Allah" and "Ubayd Allah" and the like, but they would die. Iblis came to him and Adam and said: "If you do not name him with the name you name him, he will live." She bore a boy and he named him "Abd al-Harith," and concerning this Allah revealed: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ to His words ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ to the end of the verse.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning Adam: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ to His words ﴿and she carried it about⁠﴾ — she doubted whether she had conceived or not. ﴿So when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord: "If You give us a righteous (child), we will surely be among the grateful."⁠﴾ Then Satan came to them and said: "Do you know what will be born to you? Or do you know what will become of it? Will it be an animal or not?" And he adorned falsehood for them; indeed he is a clear enemy. Before that she had borne two sons who died. Satan said to them: "If you do not name him after me, he will not come out sound, and he will die as the first two died." So they named their son "Abd al-Harith," and that is Allah's saying ﴿But when He gave them a righteous (child), they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sharik, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿But when He gave them a righteous (child), they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾ he said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. So when he covered her⁠﴾ — Adam — ﴿she conceived a light burden﴾. Then Iblis came to them—may Allah curse him—and said: "I am your companion who expelled you from Paradise. Obey me, or I will make for it (the child) two horns of a deer, and it will come out from your belly and split it open, and I will do, and I will do," frightening them. So they named him "Abd al-Harith," but they refused to obey him, and the child came out dead. Then she conceived a second time, and he came to them again and said: "I am your companion who did what I did. You will do it or I will do it," frightening them. They refused to obey him, and it came out dead. Then she conceived a third time, and he came to them again and reminded them, and love for the child overcame them, so they named him "Abd al-Harith." That is His saying ﴿they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them⁠﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

This report was received from Ibn 'Abbas by a group of his companions, such as Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah. From the second generation: Qatadah, al-Suddi, and many of the early scholars, and a group of later scholars, and among the later commentators there are countless groups. It seems—Allah knows best—that its origin was taken from the People of the Book, for Ibn 'Abbas narrated it from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated:

Abi narrated to us, Abu al-Jamahir narrated to us, Sa'id (i.e., Ibn Bashir) narrated to us, from 'Uqbah, from Qatadah, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: "When Hawwa' conceived, Satan came to her and said: 'Will you obey me and your child will be safe? Name him Abd al-Harith.' She did not do it, and she gave birth and he died. Then she conceived again and he said to her the same, and she did not do it. Then she conceived a third time, and he came to her and said: 'If you obey me he will be safe, otherwise he will be an animal.' So he (Satan) made them fearful, and they obeyed him."

These reports, Allah knows best, clearly appear to be from the reports of the People of the Book. The hadith has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "When the People of the Book tell you something, do not believe them and do not disbelieve them." Then their reports are of three categories: First, what we know to be true by the evidence of the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Second, what we know to be false, by what contradicts it from the Book and the Sunnah as well. Third, what is silent on, which is permitted to be narrated, by his saying, peace be upon him: "Narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no harm," and this is what is neither believed nor disbelieved, due to his saying: "Do not believe them and do not disbelieve them." As for this report: is it from the second or the third category? There is room for consideration. As for those who narrate it from a Companion or Follower, they regard it as of the third category. As for us, we follow the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him, in this, and that the intended subject of this context is not Adam and Hawwa', but rather the polytheists from among his offspring. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate.⁠﴾ Then he said:

This is a denunciation from Allah of the polytheists who worshipped others besides Allah, namely the rivals (andad), idols (asnam) and images (awthan). These are created by Allah, made to be ordered and fashioned. They possess nothing of the affair, they neither harm nor benefit, [and do not help] [[added from manuscripts د، ك، م، أ.]] nor can they defend their worshippers. Rather they are inert matter that does not move, hear or see, while their worshippers are more complete than they are in hearing, sight and striking. For this reason He said: ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾ That is: do you associate with Him, among the objects of worship, what creates nothing and is not able to do so? As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, a parable is struck, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Hajj 22:73–74]. He informed that even if all their gods gathered, they could not create a fly. Indeed, if the fly snatched away some trifling food and flew off, they could not rescue it from it. So how can one who has this attribute and condition be worshipped to provide sustenance or be sought for help? For this reason He said: ﴿They create nothing, while they are themselves created.﴾ That is: rather, they are created and fashioned, as the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim) said: ﴿He said: Do you worship what you carve? And Allah created you and what you do.﴾ [as-Saffat 37:95–96]

Then He said: ﴿And they are not able to help them﴾, that is, their worshippers, ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾, meaning: nor can they help themselves against whoever wishes them harm. Like the Friend, upon him be peace, who broke the idols of his people and humiliated them to the utmost degree, as Allah related about him in His saying: ﴿So he turned upon them, striking with the right hand.﴾ [as-Saffat 37:93] And He said: ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it.﴾ [al-Anbiya 21:58] Likewise Mu'adh ibn 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with them both, were young men who had embraced Islam when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah. They would go out at night against the idols of the polytheists, breaking and destroying them, and using them as firewood for widows, so that their people might take warning from this and reflect for themselves. 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a chief among his people, had an idol that he worshipped and perfumed. The two would come at night and turn it upside down on its head and smear it with filth. 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh would come, see what had been done to it, wash it, perfume it, place a sword beside it, and say to it: "Defend yourself." They would return to the same thing, and he would return to his practice again, until they took it once and tied with it the carcass of a dead dog's puppy, and let it down with a rope into a well there. When 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh came and saw this, he looked and knew that the religion he had been upon was false, and said:

By Allah, if you were a god, you would not be
Together with a dog in one well.

Then he embraced Islam, and his Islam was good, and he was killed as a martyr on the day of Uhud. May Allah be pleased with him and content him, and make the Garden of Firdaws his abode.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent.﴾ [[added from أ.]] That is: these idols do not hear the supplication of whoever calls upon them, and it is the same to them whether one calls them or is silent, as Ibrahim said: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, and does not avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam 19:42]

Then He mentioned that they are servants like their worshippers, that is, creatures like them. Rather, humans are more complete than they are, because they hear, see and strike, whereas those do none of that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.﴾ [[added from د، ك، م، أ.]] That is: seek their help against me, do not delay me for the blink of an eye, and exert your utmost effort! ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes care of the righteous.﴾ That is: Allah is my sufficiency and my protector, He is my helper, I rely upon Him, I take refuge in Him, He is my guardian in this world and the Hereafter, and He is the guardian of every righteous person after me. This is like what Hud, upon him be peace, said when his people said to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾ He said: ﴿I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free from what you associate, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ [Hud 11:54–56] And like the words of the Friend [upon him be peace] [[added from أ.]]: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and guides me, and who feeds me and gives me drink, and when I am ill, it is He who cures me.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 26:75–80] etc. And like His saying to his father and his people: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who originated me, for He will guide me.﴾ And He made it a word remaining among his descendants, that they might return. [az-Zukhruf 43:26–28]

* *

His saying: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾ to the end of the verse, confirms what preceded, except that it is in the form of address, whereas that was in the form of the third person. For this reason He said: ﴿They are not able to help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see.﴾ This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you call them, they do not hear your supplication; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. On the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association, and none can inform you like One who is Acquainted.﴾ [[added from أ.]] [Fatir 35:14]

* *

'Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a chief among his people, had an idol that he worshipped and perfumed. The two would come at night and turn it upside down on its head and smear it with filth. 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh would come, see what had been done to it, wash it, perfume it, place a sword beside it, and say to it: "Defend yourself." They would return to the same thing, and he would return to his practice again, until they took it once and tied with it the carcass of a dead dog's puppy, and let it down with a rope into a well there. When 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh came and saw this, he looked and knew that the religion he had been upon was false, and said:

By Allah, if you were a god, you would not be
Together with a dog in one well.

Then he embraced Islam, and his Islam was good, and he was killed as a martyr on the day of Uhud. May Allah be pleased with him and content him, and make the Garden of Firdaws his abode.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent.﴾ [[added from أ.]] That is: these idols do not hear the supplication of whoever calls upon them, and it is the same to them whether one calls them or is silent, as Ibrahim said: ﴿O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, and does not avail you at all?﴾ [Maryam 19:42]

Then He mentioned that they are servants like their worshippers, that is, creatures like them. Rather, humans are more complete than they are, because they hear, see and strike, whereas those do none of that.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.﴾ [[added from د، ك، م، أ.]] That is: seek their help against me, do not delay me for the blink of an eye, and exert your utmost effort! ﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes care of the righteous.﴾ That is: Allah is my sufficiency and my protector, He is my helper, I rely upon Him, I take refuge in Him, He is my guardian in this world and the Hereafter, and He is the guardian of every righteous person after me. This is like what Hud, upon him be peace, said when his people said to him: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾ He said: ﴿I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free from what you associate, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ [Hud 11:54–56] And like the words of the Friend [upon him be peace] [[added from أ.]]: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and guides me, and who feeds me and gives me drink, and when I am ill, it is He who cures me.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 26:75–80] etc. And like His saying to his father and his people: ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who originated me, for He will guide me.﴾ And He made it a word remaining among his descendants, that they might return. [az-Zukhruf 43:26–28]

* *

His saying: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him﴾ to the end of the verse, confirms what preceded, except that it is in the form of address, whereas that was in the form of the third person. For this reason He said: ﴿They are not able to help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you, yet they do not see.﴾ This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you call them, they do not hear your supplication; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. On the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association, and none can inform you like One who is Acquainted.﴾ [[added from أ.]] [Fatir 35:14]

* *

His saying: ﴿And you see them looking at you, yet they do not see.﴾ He said "looking at you" only in that they face you with fashioned eyes as if they were looking, though they are inert. For this reason He dealt with them as with one who understands, since they are in fashioned forms like a human being. So He said: ﴿and you see them looking at you﴾, expressing them with the pronoun used for rational beings.

As-Suddi said: what is meant by this is the polytheists, and something similar is related from Mujahid. But the first view is preferable, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and Qatadah also said it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verses 199–200:

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿Take what is easy﴾, that it means: take what comes to you of their wealth easily, and whatever they bring you of anything, take it. This was before Surah Barāʾah came down with the obligatory rules of charity (ṣadaqāt) and their details, and the limit to which charity reached. This was said by al-Suddī.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Take the ʿafw﴾, spend the surplus. And Saʿīd [in M: "Ḥumayd"] ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: it means the surplus.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His words: ﴿Take the ʿafw﴾, Allah commanded him to pardon and forgive the polytheists for ten years, then He commanded him to be harsh toward them. Ibn Jarīr chose this view.

Other than one narrator said, from Mujāhid regarding His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Take the ʿafw﴾, he said: [take] from the characters and deeds of people without spying [in D, K, M: "taḥassus"; in A: "tajassus"].

Hishām ibn ʿUrwa said, from his father: Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to take the ʿafw from the characters of people. In another narration he said: take what is pardoned for you of their characters.

In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from Hishām, from his father ʿUrwa, from his brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Allah only revealed ﴿Take the ʿafw﴾ regarding the characters of people [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, nos. 4643, 4644]. In another narration from someone else: from Hishām, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar. In another narration: from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, that they both said the same. [The Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Fatḥ al-Bārī (8/305): "ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said, from Hishām, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar; it was narrated by al-Bazzār and al-Ṭabarānī, and it is shādh (anomalous); likewise the narration of Ḥammād ibn Salama, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, in Ibn Mardawayh."] And Allah knows best.

In the narration of Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, from Abū Muʿāwiya, from Hishām, from Wahb ibn Kaysān, from Ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿Take the ʿafw﴾, he said: from the characters of people; by Allah, I will certainly take it from them as long as I keep their company. This is the most well-known of the views, and what Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim both narrated supports it: Yūnus told us, Sufyān (that is, Ibn ʿUyayna) told us, from Umayy, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Take the ʿafw, and enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is this, O Jibrīl?" He said: "Allah has commanded you to pardon those who wrong you, give to those who deprive you, and join ties with those who cut you off."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it, from Abū Yazīd al-Qarāṭīsī in writing, from Aṣbagh ibn al-Faraj, from Sufyān, from Umayy, from al-Shaʿbī, similar to it. This is, in any case, a mursal (narration), but a supporting report has been transmitted through other routes. It has been narrated as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) from Jābir and Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda, from the Prophet (ﷺ); Ibn Mardawayh recorded both.

Imam Aḥmad said: Abū al-Mughīra told us, Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿa told us, ʿAlī ibn Yazīd told me, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī, from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I took the initiative, took hold of his hand, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of the most excellent deeds." He said: "O ʿUqba, join ties with those who cut you off, give to those who deprive you, and turn away from those who wrong you."

Al-Tirmidhī narrated similarly, through ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zaḥr [in M: "Aḥmad"; in A: "Naḥr"] from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, with it. And he said: it is ḥasan.

I say: However, ʿAlī ibn Yazīd and his teacher al-Qāsim Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān are both weak.

Al-Bukhārī said regarding His words: ﴿Take the ʿafw and enjoin al-ʿurf and turn away from the ignorant﴾: "al-ʿurf" means al-maʿrūf (what is known as good). Abū al-Yamān told us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba informed me that Ibn ʿAbbās said: ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfa came and stayed with his nephew al-Ḥurr ibn Qays, who was among those whom ʿUmar brought close, and the reciters (qurrāʾ) were the companions of ʿUmar's gatherings and his consultations, whether elderly or young. ʿUyayna said to his nephew: "O nephew, you have standing with this leader, so ask permission for me to see him." He said: "I will ask permission for you." Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-Ḥurr asked permission for ʿUyayna, and ʿUmar [raḍiya Allāh ʿanhu] granted it. When he entered upon him, he said: "Hey, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb! By Allah, you do not give us abundantly, nor do you judge between us with justice." ʿUmar became angry until he was about to strike him, but al-Ḥurr said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Take the ʿafw, and enjoin al-ʿurf, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, and this man is one of the ignorant." By Allah, ʿUmar did not go beyond it once he recited it to him, and he was one who stopped at the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Bukhārī alone transmitted it [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, no. 4642].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us by reading, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mālik ibn Anas informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, that Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar passed by a caravan of the people of Syria in which there was a bell, and he said: "This is forbidden." They said: "We know better about this than you; only the large bell is disliked, but something like this is not objectionable." Sālim fell silent and recited: ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾.

Al-Bukhārī's statement "al-ʿurf: al-maʿrūf" was explicitly affirmed by ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, al-Suddī, Qatāda, Ibn Jarīr, and others. Ibn Jarīr relates that it is said: "awlaytuhu ʿurfan," "ʿārifan," and "ʿārifatan," all with the meaning of "al-maʿrūf." He said: Allah has commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to command His servants to what is known as good, which includes all acts of obedience, and to turn away from the ignorant. Although this is a command to His Prophet (ﷺ), it is a training of his character in bearing with those who wrong and transgress against them, not turning away from one who is ignorant of the right due to Allah's rights, nor pardoning one who disbelieves in Allah and is ignorant of His oneness, and who is at war with the Muslims.

Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba said, from Qatāda regarding His words: ﴿Take the ʿafw, and enjoin al-ʿurf, and turn away from the ignorant﴾: he said: These are characters which Allah [ʿazza wa-jall] commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) with, and guided him to.

Some wise men took up this meaning and cast it in two verses containing paronomasia (jinās):

Take the ʿafw, and enjoin what is known as Your Lord commanded,
And turn away from the ignorant...

And gentleness in speech is for all people,
So it is praiseworthy from those of rank who are gentle...

Some scholars said: People are of two kinds. A person who does good: take from his goodness what is pardoned for you, and do not burden him beyond his capacity or what would embarrass him. And a person who does evil: command him to what is known, and if he persists in his misguidance, disobeys you, and continues in his ignorance, then turn away from him, for perhaps that will repel his scheming, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe. And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, My Lord, lest they be present with me."﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 96–98]. And He said: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 34–35] — that is, this advice. And: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 36]. And He said in this noble surah also: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ So these three verses are in al-Aʿrāf, al-Muʾminūn, and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, with no fourth. For in them He, the Exalted, guides to dealing with the disobedient among mankind with what is known and what is better, for that restrains him from his rebellion by His permission. Therefore He said: ﴿then the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Then He, the Exalted, guides to seeking refuge in Him from the devil of the jinn, for kindness does not restrain him from you; he only wants your destruction and complete ruin, for he is a clear enemy to you and to your father before you.

Ibn Jarīr, in explaining His words: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you﴾, said: "And if Satan incites you to anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant and drives you to repay them" — ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾: he says: then seek protection in Allah from his incitement — ﴿Hearing, Knowing﴾: he says: indeed Allah, whom you seek refuge in from the incitement of Satan, hears the ignorance of the ignorant toward you, and your seeking refuge in Him from his incitement, and other speech of His creatures; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He knows what will remove from you the incitement of Satan, and other matters of His creation.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When it was revealed: ﴿Take the ʿafw, and enjoin al-ʿurf, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Lord, what about anger?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī (13/333)].

I say: The hadith of the two men who reviled each other in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) has already been mentioned at the beginning of the discussion of seeking refuge, when one of them became so angry that his nose began to swell with rage, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I know a word which, if he said it, what he feels would leave him: 'I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed.'" It was said to him, and he said: "Am I mad?" [See the hadith and its takhrīj in the discussion of seeking refuge.]

The root of "al-nazgh" is corruption, whether by anger or otherwise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And say to My servants that they should say that which is best. Indeed, Satan incites [dissension] among them﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 53]. And "al-ʿiyādh" is seeking refuge, relying upon, and seeking protection from evil; whereas "al-malādh" is in seeking good. As Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ] [addition from K, M, A] al-Mutanabbī said:

O You to whom I turn for what I hope for,
And from whom I seek refuge from what I fear...

No people mend a bone that You have broken,
Nor do they break a bone that You have mended.

[Dīwān al-Mutanabbī (2/272).]

[The Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr said in al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya (11/275): "It has reached me from our teacher, the scholar Shaykh al-Islām Aḥmad ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, that he used to object to al-Mutanabbī's exaggeration regarding a created being, saying: it is only appropriate for the majesty of Allah, Glorified and Exalted. And the scholar Shams al-Dīn ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me that he heard the aforementioned Shaykh Taqī al-Dīn say: 'I have perhaps recited these two verses in prostration, supplicating Allah with what they contain of humility and submission.'"]

...

We have already presented the hadiths on seeking refuge at the beginning of the tafsir, which suffices so that they need not be repeated here.

And a person who does evil: command him to what is known, and if he persists in his misguidance, disobeys you, and continues in his ignorance, then turn away from him, for perhaps that will repel his scheming, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe. And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, My Lord, lest they be present with me."﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 96–98]. And He said: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 34–35] — that is, this advice. And: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 36]. And He said in this noble surah also: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ So these three verses are in al-Aʿrāf, al-Muʾminūn, and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, with no fourth. For in them He, the Exalted, guides to dealing with the disobedient among mankind with what is known and what is better, for that restrains him from his rebellion by His permission. Therefore He said: ﴿then the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Then He, the Exalted, guides to seeking refuge in Him from the devil of the jinn, for kindness does not restrain him from you; he only wants your destruction and complete ruin, for he is a clear enemy to you and to your father before you.

Ibn Jarīr, in explaining His words: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you﴾, said: "And if Satan incites you to anger that prevents you from turning away from the ignorant and drives you to repay them" — ﴿then seek refuge in Allah﴾: he says: then seek protection in Allah from his incitement — ﴿Hearing, Knowing﴾: he says: indeed Allah, whom you seek refuge in from the incitement of Satan, hears the ignorance of the ignorant toward you, and your seeking refuge in Him from his incitement, and other speech of His creatures; nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He knows what will remove from you the incitement of Satan, and other matters of His creation.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: When it was revealed: ﴿Take the ʿafw, and enjoin al-ʿurf, and turn away from the ignorant﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Lord, what about anger?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And if an evil from Satan should touch you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing.﴾ [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī (13/333)].

I say: The hadith of the two men who reviled each other in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) has already been mentioned at the beginning of the discussion of seeking refuge, when one of them became so angry that his nose began to swell with rage, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I know a word which, if he said it, what he feels would leave him: 'I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed.'" It was said to him, and he said: "Am I mad?" [See the hadith and its takhrīj in the discussion of seeking refuge.]

The root of "al-nazgh" is corruption, whether by anger or otherwise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And say to My servants that they should say that which is best. Indeed, Satan incites [dissension] among them﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 53]. And "al-ʿiyādh" is seeking refuge, relying upon, and seeking protection from evil; whereas "al-malādh" is in seeking good. As Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ] [addition from K, M, A] al-Mutanabbī said:

O You to whom I turn for what I hope for,
And from whom I seek refuge from what I fear...

No people mend a bone that You have broken,
Nor do they break a bone that You have mended.

[Dīwān al-Mutanabbī (2/272).]

[The Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Kathīr said in al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya (11/275): "It has reached me from our teacher, the scholar Shaykh al-Islām Aḥmad ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, that he used to object to al-Mutanabbī's exaggeration regarding a created being, saying: it is only appropriate for the majesty of Allah, Glorified and Exalted. And the scholar Shams al-Dīn ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me that he heard the aforementioned Shaykh Taqī al-Dīn say: 'I have perhaps recited these two verses in prostration, supplicating Allah with what they contain of humility and submission.'"]

...

We have already presented the hadiths on seeking refuge at the beginning of the tafsir, which suffices so that they need not be repeated here.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 7, verse 201–202:

He (Exalted is He) informs about the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) among His servants, those who obeyed Him in what He commanded and abandoned what He forbade, that "when an evil suggestion from Satan (ṭayf) touches them" (idhā massahum), that is, befalls them. Others read it as "ṭā'if," and a hadith has been transmitted concerning it. Both are well-known recitations. It is said they have one meaning. It is also said there is a difference between them. Some interpreted this as anger, some as the touch of Satan causing epilepsy (ṣar') and the like, and some as the desire to commit a sin (al-hamm bil-dhanb), and some as actually committing a sin.

* *

His saying, "they remember" (tadhakkarū), that is, the punishment of Allah and His abundant reward, and His promise and His warning, so they repent, turn back in penitence, seek refuge in Allah, and return to Him promptly. "Then they see clearly" (fa-idhā hum mubṣirūn), that is, they have become upright and have awakened from what they were in.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh has narrated here the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and she had a ṭayf, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah that He cure me." He said: "If you wish, I will pray to Allah and He will cure you, and if you wish, be patient, and there is no reckoning upon you." She said: "Rather, I will be patient, and there is no reckoning upon me."

More than one of the people of the Sunan have narrated it, and in their version: She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am afflicted with fits and I uncover myself, so pray to Allah that He cure me." He said: "If you wish, I will pray to Allah to cure you, and if you wish, be patient and you will have Paradise?" She said: "Rather I will be patient, and I will have Paradise, but pray to Allah that I do not uncover myself." So he prayed for her, and she would no longer uncover herself.

Al-Hakim also transmitted it in his Mustadrak and said: "It is sound according to the condition of Muslim," though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it. (Al-Mustadrak 4/218.)

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in the biography of "'Amr ibn Jami'" in his History that a young man used to worship in the mosque, and a woman fell in love with him, invited him to herself, and kept at him until he almost entered the house with her. He then recalled this verse: "Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an evil suggestion from Satan touches them, remember [Allah], and then they see clearly" (Q. 7:201). He fell unconscious, then recovered and repeated it, and died. 'Umar came and offered condolences to his father, and he had been buried at night, so he went and prayed over his grave with those who were with him. Then 'Umar called out to him, saying: "O young man! 'And for he who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens'" (Q. 55:46). The young man answered him from within the grave: "O 'Umar, my Lord has given me both of them in Paradise, twice." (Tarikh Dimashq li-Ibn 'Asakir 13/411, 412, manuscript section; and Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq li-Ibn Manzur 19/190, 191.)

* *

His saying, "and their brothers" (wa-ikhwānuhum), that is, the brothers of the devils from among mankind, as in His saying: "Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils" (Q. 17:27). They are their followers, who listen to them and comply with their commands. "They are drawn on by them into error" (yamuddūnahum fi'l-ghayy), that is, the devils assist them in committing sins, make them easy for them, and beautify them for them.

Ibn Kathir said: al-madd means increase. That is, they increase them in error (al-ghayy), meaning ignorance and foolishness.

"Then they do not hold back" (thumma lā yuqṣirūn). It is said its meaning is that the devils extend (their support), and mankind does not refrain in their deeds because of that. As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "And their brothers draw them on into error; then they do not hold back" (Q. 7:202), he said: Neither do humans refrain from the evil deeds they do, nor do the devils withhold from them.

It is said its meaning is as al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "They draw them on into error, then they do not hold back," he said: They are the jinn, who inspire their allies among mankind, "then they do not hold back," meaning they do not tire.

Likewise al-Suddi and others said: that is, the devils extend support to their allies among mankind, and they do not weary of supporting them in evil, because that is their nature and disposition, in which they neither slacken nor cease, as He (Exalted is He) said: "Have you not seen that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with strong incitement?" (Q. 19:83). Ibn 'Abbas and others said: they urge them to sins with urging.

As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "And their brothers draw them on into error; then they do not hold back" (Q. 7:202), he said: Neither do humans refrain from the evil deeds they do, nor do the devils withhold from them.

(Q. 19:83). Ibn 'Abbas and others said: they urge them to sins with urging.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying, ﴿Why do you not make it up?﴾: he said, "Why did you not receive it (talaqqaytaha)?" And on another occasion he said: "Why did you not innovate it and bring it into being?"

Ibn Jarir [in some manuscripts: "Jurayj"] narrated from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid regarding His saying, ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why do you not make it up?"﴾: he said, "Why did you not demand it (iqtadaytaha)?" They say, "You bring it out of yourself." Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas [may Allah be pleased with him] regarding ﴿Why do you not make it up?﴾: he said, "You received it from Allah, Mighty and Majestic [in some manuscripts: "Most High"]."

Al-Dahhak said regarding ﴿Why do you not make it up?﴾: "Why did you not take it yourself, and bring it from the sky?"

The meaning of His saying, ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign﴾, i.e., a miracle and an extraordinary event, is as He said: ﴿If We wish, We send down upon them a sign from the sky, so their necks would remain bowed before it﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:4]. They say to the Messenger (ﷺ): "Will you not exert yourself in seeking signs from Allah until we see them and believe in them?" Allah the Exalted said to him: ﴿Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾ That is: I do not go ahead of Him, the Exalted, in anything; rather I only follow what He commands me, and I comply with what He reveals to me. If He sends a sign, I accept it, and if He withholds it, I do not ask Him to begin giving it, unless He gives me permission for that, for He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

Then He guided them to the fact that this Qur'an is the greatest of miracles, the clearest of proofs, and the most truthful of arguments and evidences, so He said: ﴿This is insights from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.﴾

When Allah, may He be exalted, mentioned that the Qur'an is "insights for mankind, and guidance and mercy," He commanded listening attentively when it is recited, out of glorification and reverence for it. This is not the way the disbelieving idolaters of Quraysh behaved, as they said: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, that perhaps you may overcome.﴾ [Fussilat: 26] [[In A: "al-mushrikin" (the idolaters).]] [[Addition from D: "that perhaps you may overcome."]]

This command is especially emphasized in the obligatory prayer when the imam recites aloud, as is reported in the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The imam is appointed only to be followed. So when he says the takbir, say the takbir, and when he recites, then listen attentively." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (404).]] Likewise, the compilers of the Sunan (collections of hadith) narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (12/141), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (846).]], and Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj also authenticated it, but he did not include it in his book. [[See the discussion of this addition in the commentary on Surat al-Fatihah.]]

Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri said, from Abu Iyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "They used to speak during the prayer. Then when this verse was revealed: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾ [[Addition from M: "and remain silent."]] and the other verse, they were commanded to be silent." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (13/345).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Musayyab ibn Rafi', who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "We used to greet one another during the prayer, saying: 'Peace be upon so-and-so, and peace be upon so-and-so.' Then the Qur'an came: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent, that perhaps you may receive mercy.﴾"

He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Bashir ibn Jabir, who said: Ibn Mas'ud prayed, and he heard some people reciting along with the imam. When he finished, he said: "Has the time not yet come for you to understand? Has the time not yet come for you to use your reason? ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾, as Allah has commanded you." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/346).]]

He said: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Zuhri, who said: This verse was revealed concerning a young man of the Ansar. Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited something, he would recite it along with him, so this verse was revealed: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent.﴾

Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan also narrated, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Abu Ukaymidah al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished a prayer in which he had recited aloud, and said: "Did any of you recite with me just now?" A man said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I was thinking, why is the Qur'an being disputed with me?" So the people refrained from reciting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in those prayers in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited aloud, once they heard that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [[Al-Musnad (2/301); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (826); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (312); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/140); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (848).]] [[In D: "al-salah" (the prayer).]] [[In K and M: "fa-qala" (then he said).]]

al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan (sound-good) hadith." Abu Hatim al-Razi also authenticated it.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: "One should not recite behind the imam in what the imam recites aloud. The recitation of the imam suffices them, even if he does not make his voice audible to them. But they should recite silently to themselves in what is recited quietly. It is not permissible for anyone behind him to recite along with him in what is recited aloud, whether silently or openly, for Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent, that perhaps you may receive mercy.﴾"

I say: This is the view of a group of scholars: that the follower (ma'mum) is not obligated to recite anything in an audible prayer when the imam recites aloud, neither al-Fatihah nor anything else. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, namely the older one (al-qadim), and it is the position of Malik, and a narration from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, on the basis of the evidences we have already mentioned. In his newer opinion (al-jadid), al-Shafi'i said: one recites only al-Fatihah during the imam's pauses. This is also the view of a group of the Companions, the Successors, and those after them. Abu Hanifah and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: the follower is not obligated to recite at all, neither in silent nor in audible prayers, based on what has come in the hadith: "Whoever has an imam, the imam's recitation is his recitation." This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, from Jabir, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report, and it is in the Muwatta' of Malik from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Jabir, as a mawquf (ending with a Companion) report, and this latter is more authentic. This issue is discussed at length elsewhere. [[See the full discussion in the introduction to Surat al-Fatihah.]] Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bukhari also wrote a separate work on it [[Titled "Juz' al-Qira'ah Khalf al-Imam" (The Section on Reciting Behind the Imam), published by Mu'assasat al-Risalah in Beirut.]], and he chose the obligation of reciting behind the imam in both silent and audible prayers as well. And Allah knows best.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas his statement about: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾, that it means: during the obligatory prayer. Similarly it is narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal.

Ibn Jarir said: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz, who said: "I saw 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah talking while a storyteller was telling stories. I said: 'Will you not listen to the remembrance and earn the promised reward?' He said: They looked at me, then turned back to their conversation. He said: I repeated it, and they looked at me and turned back to their conversation. He said: I repeated it a third time, and they looked at me and said: 'That applies only in prayer: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent.﴾'"

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Hashim Isma'il ibn Kathir, from Mujahid concerning His statement: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾, he said: "In the prayer." Similarly, more than one narrator reported it from Mujahid.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "There is no harm if a man speaks outside of prayer while the Qur'an is being recited."

Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Qatadah, al-Sha'bi, al-Suddi, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said that what is meant by this is the prayer.

Shu'bah said, from Mansur: I heard Ibrahim ibn Abi Hurrah narrate that he heard Mujahid say concerning this verse: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾, "It refers to the prayer and to the sermon on Friday."

Ibn Jurayj likewise narrated from 'Ata' something similar.

Hushaym said, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, from al-Hasan, who said: "It refers to the prayer and to when the remembrance (dhikr) is being recited."

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Baqiyyah: I heard Thabit ibn 'Ajlan say: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say concerning His statement: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and remain silent﴾: "The silence is required on the day of al-Adha, the day of al-Fitr, the day of Friday, and during what the imam recites aloud in the prayer."

This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, that what is meant is silence during the prayer and during the sermon, because of what has come in the hadiths about the command to be silent behind the imam and during the sermon.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, that he disliked that when the imam passes over a verse of fear or a verse of mercy, anyone behind him should say anything; he said: "Silence."

Mubarak ibn Fadalah said, from al-Hasan: "When you sit with the Qur'an, be silent for it."

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of Allah, a multiplied good deed is recorded for him, and whoever recites it, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (2/341); in its chain is 'Abbad ibn Maysarah, who is weak.]] May Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, commands remembrance of Him at the beginning and at the end of the day, just as He commanded worship of Him at these two times in His saying: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Qaf 50:39]. This was before the five prayers were prescribed on the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey), and this verse is Meccan.

He said here "al-ghuww" (morning), which is the early part of the day, and "wal-asal", the plural of "asil" (evening), just as "al-aiman" is the plural of "yamin" (oath/right hand).

As for His saying: ﴿with humility and fear﴾, meaning: remember your Lord within yourself, with awe and hope, and with speech, but not aloud. For this reason He said: ﴿and without loudness in speech﴾. Thus it is recommended that remembrance not be by calling out or by loud, excessive shouting. For this reason, when they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "Is our Lord near, so that we whisper to Him, or is He far, so that we call out to Him?", Allah revealed: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:186].

[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (3/480) through the route of 'Abdah al-Sijistani, from al-Salt ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, and it has been discussed under verse 186 of Surat al-Baqarah.]

In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "The people raised their voices with supplication during some journey, so the Prophet ﷺ said to them: 'O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; indeed, the One you call upon is All-Hearing, near.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4205 and Sahih Muslim no. 2704.]

This verse may also mean what is found in His saying: ﴿And do not recite your prayer aloud or silently, but seek between that a middle way﴾ [Al-Isra' 17:110]. The polytheists, whenever they heard the Qur'an, would revile it, revile the One who revealed it, and revile the one who brought it. So Allah commanded him not to recite it aloud, lest the polytheists harm him, and not to recite it silently so that his companions would not hear him, but to take a path between loudness and secrecy. Likewise He said in this noble verse: ﴿and without loudness in speech, in the mornings and evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾.

Ibn Jarir and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam before him claimed that the meaning of this verse is the command to the listener of the Qur'an, during his listening, to remember Allah in this manner. But this is far-fetched and contradicts the attentive silence that is commanded. Furthermore, the intended meaning is, as previously mentioned, during prayer, or during prayer and the sermon, and it is well known that silent attentiveness at that time is better than remembrance by the tongue, whether secret or aloud. So what these two said has not been followed by others. Rather, the intended meaning is to urge the servants to increase remembrance in the mornings and evenings, lest they be among the heedless. For this reason He praised the angels who glorify Him night and day without slackening, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord are not too proud to worship Him, and they glorify Him and prostrate to Him﴾ [Allah's words]. He mentioned this to them so that they might be emulated in their abundant obedience and worship. For this reason prostration was prescribed for us here when their prostration to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was mentioned, as came in the hadith: "Will you not line up as the angels line up before their Lord? They complete the first rows and close up the ranks in the row." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. 430, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This is the first prostration in the Qur'an, and by consensus it is prescribed for its reciter and listener to prostrate. It has also been reported in a hadith narrated by Ibn Majah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ, that he counted it among the prostrations of the Qur'an. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1056.]

End of the commentary on Surat al-A'raf, and all praise and grace are due to Allah.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, commands remembrance of Him at the beginning and at the end of the day, just as He commanded worship of Him at these two times in His saying: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Qaf 50:39]. This was before the five prayers were prescribed on the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey), and this verse is Meccan.

He said here "al-ghuww" (morning), which is the early part of the day, and "wal-asal", the plural of "asil" (evening), just as "al-aiman" is the plural of "yamin" (oath/right hand).

As for His saying: ﴿with humility and fear﴾, meaning: remember your Lord within yourself, with awe and hope, and with speech, but not aloud. For this reason He said: ﴿and without loudness in speech﴾. Thus it is recommended that remembrance not be by calling out or by loud, excessive shouting.
